entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks Regulation (EU) No 538/2014, which amends Regulation (EU) No 691/2011 on European environmental economic accounts by adding three new statistical modules (Annexes IV, V and VI). It exists to give a freight-forwarding workspace a single place to see what these modules cover, which reporting duties they place on EU Member States (not on the workspace directly), and the historical dates that already govern this instrument's own transitional timeline.

FACT: "Annexes IV, V and VI, as set out in the Annex to this Regulation, are added to Regulation (EU) No 691/2011." *Source: Regulation (EU) No 538/2014, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32014R0538

FACT: "Done at Strasbourg, 16 April 2014." *Source: Regulation (EU) No 538/2014, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32014R0538

FACT: "This Regulation shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union ." *Source: Regulation (EU) No 538/2014, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32014R0538

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

This Regulation is a statistical-methodology amendment, not a rulemaking that creates compliance duties for a private freight forwarder. It applies to the workspace indirectly: it obligates EU Member States to compile and transmit new categories of environmental-economic statistics to the Commission (Eurostat), and those categories (in particular the "environmental goods and services sector" module) supply the vocabulary and classification the EU uses when discussing green growth and resource efficiency.

FACT: "This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States." *Source: Regulation (EU) No 538/2014, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32014R0538

FACT: "the Commission is invited to report to the European Parliament and the Council on the implementation of the Regulation and, if appropriate, to propose the introduction of new environmental economic accounts modules" *Source: Regulation (EU) No 538/2014, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32014R0538

*Analytical inference:* because the Regulation is binding and directly applicable in every Member State, a workspace with EU exposure should treat its terminology (in particular the Annex V categories) as EU-wide reference vocabulary, not as a jurisdiction-specific rule that varies by Member State.

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

*Legal Confirmation Required:* This Regulation's reporting obligations, described in Section 8, run from EU Member States to the European Commission (Eurostat), not from a freight forwarder to any authority. No source in this brief's corpus states that a private freight-forwarding operator submits data, registers, or reports anything under this Regulation. Whether a specific national statistical office ever requests operator-level data as part of compiling these accounts is a fact-specific question outside this brief's scope and would require confirmation directly with the relevant Member State statistical authority.

*Analytical inference:* Because the compliance chain here runs Member-State-to-Commission rather than workspace-to-authority, the workspace's practical relevance is informational: the Annex V taxonomy is a reference point for how the EU classifies "environmental goods and services," which may be useful vocabulary when discussing sustainability-adjacent services with EU clients.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

FACT: "The United Nations Statistical Commission adopted the System of Environmental-Economic Accounting (SEEA) Central Framework as an international statistical standard at its 43rd session in February 2012." *Source: Regulation (EU) No 538/2014, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32014R0538

*Per the workspace's reading:* the Regulation's new modules are stated to align with this UN statistical standard, which situates the EU's environmental-economic accounts within a broader international measurement framework rather than an EU-only construct.

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

1. Indicative compendium of environmental goods and services (Annex V categories). The captured source states, in full: "the Commission shall, by 31 December 2015, by means of implementing acts, establish an indicative compendium of environmental goods and services and of the economic activities to be covered by Annex V based on the following categories: environmental specific services, environmental sole purpose products (connected products), adapted goods and environmental technologies." This deadline (31 December 2015) has already lapsed as of the export date; it is carried here because the export's own forward_events record names it, and because the resulting compendium is the operative taxonomy for what counts as "environmental goods and services" under Annex V.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* This brief's own corpus does not include the text of the implementing act the Commission was required to adopt under this obligation; a workspace with a specific question about the compendium's current content should confirm directly against the Commission's own implementing-act record rather than relying on this summary.

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does this Regulation create direct reporting or compliance obligations on private freight-forwarding operators?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* No. The obligations described in Section 8 run to EU Member States as the entities that must compile and transmit statistics to the Commission; no source in this brief's corpus states a duty running from this Regulation to a private freight forwarder, carrier, or logistics intermediary.

**Q2: Does the "environmental goods and services sector" classification this Regulation introduces have any operational meaning for the workspace?**

*Analytical inference:* Only as reference vocabulary. The classification (Annex V, Section 3) groups environmental goods and services into "environmental specific services, environmental sole purpose products (connected products), adapted goods and environmental technologies" for Member State statistical reporting; it does not itself register, certify, or regulate any private operator.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

*Note: this Regulation amends a Member State statistical-reporting framework. "Substantive requirements" here means the Regulation's own stated obligations on EU Member States and the Commission, plus the operational implications those obligations carry for a freight-forwarding workspace as a reader of the resulting statistics.*

**1. Environmental protection expenditure accounts module (Annex IV).** FACT: "a module for environmental protection expenditure accounts, as set out in Annex IV" *Source: Regulation (EU) No 538/2014, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32014R0538

**2. Environmental goods and services sector accounts module (Annex V).** FACT: "a module for environmental goods and services sector accounts, as set out in Annex V" *Source: Regulation (EU) No 538/2014, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32014R0538

*Operational implication:* this is the module whose Annex V taxonomy the workspace may find useful as EU-wide reference vocabulary for "environmental goods and services" (see Section 2).

**3. Physical energy flow accounts module (Annex VI).** FACT: "a module for physical energy flow accounts, as set out in Annex VI" *Source: Regulation (EU) No 538/2014, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32014R0538

**4. Member State derogation-request deadline.** FACT: "the Member State concerned shall present a duly justified request to the Commission by 17 September 2014." *Source: Regulation (EU) No 538/2014, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32014R0538

*Analytical inference:* this deadline governed a Member State's own procedural request to the Commission for a derogation from Annexes IV, V and VI; it does not run to a private operator and has already lapsed.

**5. Annex V reporting-unit exception.** FACT: "All data shall be reported in million national currency, except for the characteristic “employment” for which the reporting unit shall be “full time equivalent”." *Source: Regulation (EU) No 538/2014, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32014R0538

**6. Commission's compendium-establishment obligation.** FACT: "the Commission shall, by 31 December 2015, by means of implementing acts, establish an indicative compendium of environmental goods and services and of the economic activities to be covered by Annex V based on the following categories: environmental specific services, environmental sole purpose products (connected products), adapted goods and environmental technologies." *Source: Regulation (EU) No 538/2014, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32014R0538

No scope limits are stated in Articles 1 and 2 of this Regulation or Annexes IV, V and VI.

Obligations surveyed: 10; workspace-adjacent: 4; extracted as FACT: 6.

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

FACT: "Statistics shall be compiled and transmitted on a yearly basis." *Source: Regulation (EU) No 538/2014, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32014R0538

FACT: "Statistics shall be transmitted within 24 months of the end of the reference year." *Source: Regulation (EU) No 538/2014, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32014R0538

FACT: "Statistics shall be transmitted within 21 months of the end of the reference year." *Source: Regulation (EU) No 538/2014, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32014R0538

FACT: "The first reference year is 2015." *Source: Regulation (EU) No 538/2014, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32014R0538

FACT: "the maximum duration of the transitional period is 2 years from the first transmission deadline." *Source: Regulation (EU) No 538/2014, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32014R0538

*Operational implication:* these are Member State reporting-cadence rules (transmission windows of 24 months for Annexes IV and V, 21 months for Annex VI, a first reference year of 2015, and a maximum 2-year transitional period), not filing duties on a private freight forwarder; they are recorded here so a workspace can judge how current any Member-State-published figures under these modules are likely to be.

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

FACT: "the Member State concerned shall present a duly justified request to the Commission by 17 September 2014." *Source: Regulation (EU) No 538/2014, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32014R0538

*Analytical inference:* this derogation mechanism is scoped to a Member State's own reporting obligation under Annexes IV, V and VI; it has no direct edge case for a private freight operator, since the underlying duty it excuses is itself a Member-State-to-Commission reporting requirement, not a private-party duty.

# 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

FACT: "The new modules contribute directly to the Union's policy priorities of green growth and resource efficiency by providing important information on indicators such as market output and employment in the EGSS, national environmental protection expenditure and the use of energy in a NACE breakdown." *Source: Regulation (EU) No 538/2014, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32014R0538

*Analytical inference:* this framing situates the Regulation's new modules inside the EU's broader green-growth and resource-efficiency policy agenda, the relevant adjacent-policy context for a workspace tracking how the EU measures the environmental economy rather than a source of direct operator obligations.

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 16 April 2014: Regulation (EU) No 538/2014 adopted (the instrument's own dateline, "Done at Strasbourg").
- 17 September 2014: deadline for a Member State to submit a duly justified derogation request for Annexes IV, V and VI.
- 2015: first reference year for statistics under Annexes IV, V and VI.
- 31 December 2015: deadline for the Commission to establish, by implementing act, the indicative compendium of environmental goods and services under Annex V.

*Source for timeline entries: Regulation (EU) No 538/2014, EUR-Lex (https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32014R0538).*

# 15. Sources

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks an EPA correcting-amendments notice to the New Source Performance Standards (NSPS) for stationary gas turbines and stationary combustion turbines (40 CFR Part 60, Subparts GG, KKKK, and KKKKa), not a new substantive rulemaking. It exists to give a freight-forwarding workspace a single place to see what changed in the underlying standards' regulatory text, when the correction takes effect, and which duty-holder class it reaches.

FACT: "New Source Performance Standards Review for Stationary Combustion Turbines and Stationary Gas Turbines; Correction" *Source: U.S. EPA, Federal Register, New Source Performance Standards Review for Stationary Combustion Turbines and Stationary Gas Turbines; Correction (2026-14371). https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/16/2026-14371/new-source-performance-standards-review-for-stationary-combustion-turbines-and-stationary-gas*

FACT: "The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is making corrections to the New Source Performance Standards Review for Stationary Combustion Turbines and Stationary Gas Turbines final rule (``Final NSPS Rule'') that published in the Federal Register (FR) on January 15, 2026, and became effective on January 15, 2026." *Source: U.S. EPA, Federal Register, New Source Performance Standards Review for Stationary Combustion Turbines and Stationary Gas Turbines; Correction (2026-14371). https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/16/2026-14371/new-source-performance-standards-review-for-stationary-combustion-turbines-and-stationary-gas*

*Analytical inference:* this notice corrects typographical and technical errors identified after the Final NSPS Rule's own January 15, 2026 publication and effective date; it does not itself impose any standard the underlying Final NSPS Rule did not already impose.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

The underlying NSPS subparts apply to owners and operators of stationary gas turbines and stationary combustion turbines meeting the source-category and size thresholds each subpart sets, not to freight-forwarding operations generally.

FACT: "The EPA corrects the regulatory text in paragraph (e) to read as being applicable to a ``gas turbine'' instead of a ``combustion turbine.'' The EPA is making this correction for consistency with Subpart GG, which applies to the stationary gas turbines source category." *Source: U.S. EPA, Federal Register, New Source Performance Standards Review for Stationary Combustion Turbines and Stationary Gas Turbines; Correction (2026-14371). https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/16/2026-14371/new-source-performance-standards-review-for-stationary-combustion-turbines-and-stationary-gas*

*Operational implication:* this correction reaches a freight-forwarding workspace only if the workspace itself owns or operates a stationary gas turbine or stationary combustion turbine within these source categories (for example, an on-site backup-power or cogeneration turbine at a terminal, warehouse, or distribution facility); it does not create a general compliance duty for freight-forwarding, customs-brokerage, or carriage activity as such.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

FACT: "Effective on August 17, 2026." *Source: U.S. EPA, Federal Register, New Source Performance Standards Review for Stationary Combustion Turbines and Stationary Gas Turbines; Correction (2026-14371). https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/16/2026-14371/new-source-performance-standards-review-for-stationary-combustion-turbines-and-stationary-gas*

*Operational implication:* a workspace that owns or operates equipment within these source categories should confirm by August 17, 2026 which corrected provisions (Section 8 below) change its own facility's compliance text, since the correction is effective on that date regardless of whether the facility has reviewed it.

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

*Legal Confirmation Required:* the corrected provisions in Section 8 obligate "owners or operators" of stationary gas turbines and stationary combustion turbines meeting Subpart GG, KKKK, or KKKKa's own applicability criteria. Whether a specific freight-forwarding workspace's own facility equipment (for example, an on-site generator or turbine) falls within one of these source categories, and therefore whether any corrected provision runs to that workspace directly, is a fact-specific question outside this brief's scope and requires counsel or a qualified environmental engineer's review of the specific equipment.

*Analytical inference:* because these obligations run to equipment owners/operators rather than to freight-forwarding activity as such, the workspace's practical exposure is contingent on facility ownership, not on its forwarding, brokerage, or carriage role.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

FACT: "The EPA has determined that there is good cause for making this rule final without prior proposal and opportunity for comment because the changes to the rule are minor, noncontroversial in nature, and correct inadvertent typographical and technical errors." *Source: U.S. EPA, Federal Register, New Source Performance Standards Review for Stationary Combustion Turbines and Stationary Gas Turbines; Correction (2026-14371). https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/16/2026-14371/new-source-performance-standards-review-for-stationary-combustion-turbines-and-stationary-gas*

*Per the workspace's reading:* this is the EPA's own stated basis under 5 U.S.C. 553(b)(B) for skipping notice-and-comment on this specific correction; it does not state that the underlying Final NSPS Rule itself was adopted without notice and comment.

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does this correcting-amendments notice create a new obligation on freight-forwarding operations?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* No provision in this notice's captured text states a duty running to freight forwarders, carriers, customs brokers, or logistics intermediaries as such; every corrected obligation in Section 8 runs to an "owner or operator" of a stationary gas turbine or stationary combustion turbine meeting the relevant subpart's own source-category and size criteria.

**Q2: Is the effective date in Section 3 a compliance deadline for a new duty, or the effective date of a text correction to an already-effective rule?**

*Analytical inference:* the latter. The Final NSPS Rule the corrected text belongs to was already in effect as of January 15, 2026 (Section 1); August 17, 2026 is when the corrected regulatory text itself takes effect, not a new compliance program's start date.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

*Note: this document is a correcting-amendments notice to an already-effective rule. "Substantive requirements" here means the corrected regulatory text's own operative standards on the duty-holder class the underlying subparts define (owners/operators of stationary gas turbines and stationary combustion turbines), which reach a freight-forwarding workspace only when that workspace owns or operates equipment within these source categories (Section 4).*

**1. Subpart GG title V exemption.** FACT: "(e) A gas turbine that is subject to this subpart and is not a ``major source'' or located at a ``major source'' (as that term is defined at 42 U.S.C. 7661 (2)) is exempt from the requirements of 42 U.S.C. 7661a(a)." *Source: U.S. EPA, Federal Register, New Source Performance Standards Review for Stationary Combustion Turbines and Stationary Gas Turbines; Correction (2026-14371). https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/16/2026-14371/new-source-performance-standards-review-for-stationary-combustion-turbines-and-stationary-gas*

**2. Subpart KKKK title II scope exclusion.** FACT: "(e) Combustion turbines subject to title II of the Clean Air Act are not subject to this subpart." *Source: U.S. EPA, Federal Register, New Source Performance Standards Review for Stationary Combustion Turbines and Stationary Gas Turbines; Correction (2026-14371). https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/16/2026-14371/new-source-performance-standards-review-for-stationary-combustion-turbines-and-stationary-gas*

**3. Temporary combustion turbine election (Subpart KKKK).** FACT: "owners or operators of a small- or medium-size stationary combustion turbine (i.e., a combustion turbine with a base load rating less than or equal to 850 MMBtu/h) at a single location for up to 24 consecutive months, may elect to be a temporary combustion turbine and comply with the requirements in paragraphs (b) through (e) of this section" *Source: U.S. EPA, Federal Register, New Source Performance Standards Review for Stationary Combustion Turbines and Stationary Gas Turbines; Correction (2026-14371). https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/16/2026-14371/new-source-performance-standards-review-for-stationary-combustion-turbines-and-stationary-gas*

*Operational implication:* an owner/operator electing this alternative regime must track the 24-consecutive-month location limit itself, since exceeding it ends eligibility for the alternative requirements in paragraphs (b) through (e).

**4. NOx excess-emissions averaging method (Subpart KKKK).** FACT: "(3) For averaging periods during which multiple emissions standards apply, the applicable standard for the averaging period is the arithmetic average of the applicable standards during each hour. For hours with multiple emission standards, the applicable standard for that hour is determined based on the condition that corresponded to the highest emissions standard." *Source: U.S. EPA, Federal Register, New Source Performance Standards Review for Stationary Combustion Turbines and Stationary Gas Turbines; Correction (2026-14371). https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/16/2026-14371/new-source-performance-standards-review-for-stationary-combustion-turbines-and-stationary-gas*

**5. Recurring performance-test interval (Subpart KKKKa).** FACT: "(1) Except as provided for in paragraphs (b)(2) through (5) of this section, you must conduct subsequent performance tests within 14 calendar months of the date that the previous performance test was conducted." *Source: U.S. EPA, Federal Register, New Source Performance Standards Review for Stationary Combustion Turbines and Stationary Gas Turbines; Correction (2026-14371). https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/16/2026-14371/new-source-performance-standards-review-for-stationary-combustion-turbines-and-stationary-gas*

**6. SO2 compliance via fuel records (Subpart KKKKa).** FACT: "(a) If you are an owner or operator of an affected facility complying with the fuel-based standard, you may submit fuel records (such as a current, valid purchase contract, tariff sheet, transportation contract, or results of a fuel analysis) to satisfy the requirements of Sec. 60.8." *Source: U.S. EPA, Federal Register, New Source Performance Standards Review for Stationary Combustion Turbines and Stationary Gas Turbines; Correction (2026-14371). https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/16/2026-14371/new-source-performance-standards-review-for-stationary-combustion-turbines-and-stationary-gas*

**7. SO2 performance test when fuel records are not used (Subpart KKKKa).** FACT: "(b) If you are an owner or operator of an affected facility complying with the SO 2 emissions standard and are not using fuel records, you must conduct the performance test by measuring the SO 2 emissions in the stationary combustion turbine exhaust gases using the methods in either paragraph (b)(1) or (2) of this section." *Source: U.S. EPA, Federal Register, New Source Performance Standards Review for Stationary Combustion Turbines and Stationary Gas Turbines; Correction (2026-14371). https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/16/2026-14371/new-source-performance-standards-review-for-stationary-combustion-turbines-and-stationary-gas*

**8. Turbine-tuning hour cap (Subpart KKKKa).** FACT: "Turbine tuning means planned maintenance or parameter performance testing of a combustion turbine engine involving adjustment of the operating configuration to maintain proper combustion dynamics or testing machine operating performance. Turbine tuning is limited to 30 hours per 12-calendar-month period." *Source: U.S. EPA, Federal Register, New Source Performance Standards Review for Stationary Combustion Turbines and Stationary Gas Turbines; Correction (2026-14371). https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/16/2026-14371/new-source-performance-standards-review-for-stationary-combustion-turbines-and-stationary-gas*

**9. Natural-gas-only NOx subcategory standard (Subpart KKKK Table 1).** FACT: "The EPA restores those previous emission standards in Subpart KKKK by clarifying that this subcategory's NO X emission standard applies only to units firing natural gas." *Source: U.S. EPA, Federal Register, New Source Performance Standards Review for Stationary Combustion Turbines and Stationary Gas Turbines; Correction (2026-14371). https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/16/2026-14371/new-source-performance-standards-review-for-stationary-combustion-turbines-and-stationary-gas*

**10. NOx CEMS performance-test protocol (Subpart KKKKa).** FACT: "(1) Perform a minimum of nine RATA reference method runs, with a minimum time per run of 21 minutes, at a single load level, within 30 percent of 100 percent of the base load rating while the source is combusting the fuel that is a normal primary fuel for that source." *Source: U.S. EPA, Federal Register, New Source Performance Standards Review for Stationary Combustion Turbines and Stationary Gas Turbines; Correction (2026-14371). https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/16/2026-14371/new-source-performance-standards-review-for-stationary-combustion-turbines-and-stationary-gas*

**11. Non-CEMS NOx performance-test protocol (Subpart KKKKa).** FACT: "(d) The performance test must be done at any load condition within 30 percent of 100 percent of the base load rating. You may perform testing at the highest achievable load point, if at least 70 percent of the base load rating cannot be achieved in practice. You must conduct three separate test runs for each performance test. The minimum time per run is 20 minutes." *Source: U.S. EPA, Federal Register, New Source Performance Standards Review for Stationary Combustion Turbines and Stationary Gas Turbines; Correction (2026-14371). https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/16/2026-14371/new-source-performance-standards-review-for-stationary-combustion-turbines-and-stationary-gas*

*Legal Confirmation Required:* No verbatim penalty, fine, or enforcement-consequence statement runs to a private freight-forwarding workspace anywhere in this correcting-amendments notice; the notice only corrects regulatory text within existing 40 CFR Part 60 Subparts GG, KKKK, and KKKKa, and states no separate compliance penalty of its own.

**Qualification accounting.** Per-year trajectory: No phase-in is stated in Sections 60.330 through 60.4420a of 40 CFR Part 60. Exceptions and carve-outs: CAPTURED above (obligation 1, the Subpart GG title V exemption; obligation 5, the performance-test interval's own stated exception). Scope limits: CAPTURED above (obligation 8, the turbine-tuning hour cap; obligation 9, the natural-gas-only subcategory restriction).

Obligations surveyed: 11; workspace-adjacent: 11; extracted as FACT: 11.

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

FACT: "Sec. 60.4395 When must I submit my reports?" *Source: U.S. EPA, Federal Register, New Source Performance Standards Review for Stationary Combustion Turbines and Stationary Gas Turbines; Correction (2026-14371). https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/16/2026-14371/new-source-performance-standards-review-for-stationary-combustion-turbines-and-stationary-gas*

*Analytical inference:* this correction fixes a typographical error in the reporting-timing question's own heading (from "What" to "When"); it does not restate or change the underlying reporting content or schedule, which this correction's captured text does not repeat.

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

FACT: "(e) A gas turbine that is subject to this subpart and is not a ``major source'' or located at a ``major source'' (as that term is defined at 42 U.S.C. 7661 (2)) is exempt from the requirements of 42 U.S.C. 7661a(a)." *Source: U.S. EPA, Federal Register, New Source Performance Standards Review for Stationary Combustion Turbines and Stationary Gas Turbines; Correction (2026-14371). https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/16/2026-14371/new-source-performance-standards-review-for-stationary-combustion-turbines-and-stationary-gas*

*Operational implication:* this exemption applies only within Subpart GG's own applicability criteria (a gas turbine that is not, and is not located at, a "major source"); it has no bearing on a workspace's obligations outside that specific source category.

# 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

FACT: "See the petition for reconsideration filed with the EPA by the American Petroleum Institute (API), available in the rulemaking docket under Docket ID EPA-HQ-OAR-2024-0419-0246." *Source: U.S. EPA, Federal Register, New Source Performance Standards Review for Stationary Combustion Turbines and Stationary Gas Turbines; Correction (2026-14371). https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/16/2026-14371/new-source-performance-standards-review-for-stationary-combustion-turbines-and-stationary-gas*

*Analytical inference:* this correction resolves an industry-filed petition for reconsideration on the Subpart KKKKa size-threshold table (Section 8, obligation 9's table context); a workspace tracking future NSPS corrections in this equipment category should expect further petitions of this kind to be the typical trigger for subsequent correcting amendments.

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- January 15, 2026: Final NSPS Rule for Stationary Combustion Turbines and Stationary Gas Turbines published in the Federal Register and became effective the same date.
- July 16, 2026: Published in the Federal Register.
- August 17, 2026: This correcting-amendments notice takes effect.

*Source for timeline entries: U.S. EPA, Federal Register document 2026-14371 (https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/16/2026-14371/new-source-performance-standards-review-for-stationary-combustion-turbines-and-stationary-gas).*

# 15. Sources

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks a narrow United Kingdom Statutory Instrument, the Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading Scheme and National Emissions Inventory (Amendment) Regulations 2013 (SI 2013/3135), which amends three existing instruments governing the UK Emissions Trading Scheme (ETS) and the UK's national greenhouse gas inventory reporting duties, rather than creating a new regulatory regime of its own. It exists to give a freight forwarder with UK exposure a single place to see who this instrument binds, what penalty and reporting mechanics it changes, and when its own provisions took effect.

FACT: "The Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading Scheme and National Emissions Inventory (Amendment) Regulations 2013" *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK Statutory Instrument 2013 No. 3135. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/3135

FACT: "Statutory Instruments 2013 No. 3135 Climate Change" *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK Statutory Instrument 2013 No. 3135. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/3135

FACT: "Made 11th December 2013 Laid before Parliament 13th December 2013 Coming into force 31st January 2014" *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK Statutory Instrument 2013 No. 3135. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/3135

**What the workspace should expect to decide:** whether the workspace itself, or a UK entity in its supply chain, holds a permit, aircraft-operator allocation, or registry account under the amended 2012 Regulations, since that determines whether any of the amended penalty or reporting provisions in Section 8 bind it directly.

*Analytical inference:* this instrument's own title and made, laid, and in force dates identify it as a routine mid cycle technical amendment, made and laid in December 2013 and in force from 31st January 2014, not a newly created compliance regime.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

This instrument amends the Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading Scheme Regulations 2012 (the current UK ETS implementing Regulations), the Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading Scheme (Amendment) and National Emissions Inventory Regulations 2005 (which govern Kyoto Protocol project approval and the UK's national greenhouse gas inventory), the Environment Act 1995, the Environment (Northern Ireland) Order 2002, and the Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading Scheme Charging Scheme Regulations (Northern Ireland) 2010.

FACT: "Those Regulations consolidated (with amendments) and replaced the previous implementing Regulations, namely the Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading Scheme Regulations 2005 ( S.I. 2005/925 ) and the Aviation Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading Scheme Regulations 2010 ( S.I. 2010/1996 )." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK Statutory Instrument 2013 No. 3135, Explanatory Note. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/3135

FACT: "Those Regulations deal with the approval of projects under the Kyoto Protocol" *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK Statutory Instrument 2013 No. 3135, Explanatory Note. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/3135

*Operational implication:* a freight forwarder that itself operates a covered installation or aircraft under the UK ETS, or that submits information to the Secretary of State for the national greenhouse gas inventory, applies to this instrument's amended provisions directly; a freight forwarder acting purely as an intermediary, with no UK ETS permit or registry account of its own, is not itself "P" under the amended provisions described in Section 8.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

*Analytical inference:* this instrument fully commenced on 31st January 2014 (Section 1) and carries no forward looking action item running to a private party as of the export date; the only recurring obligation the captured text names is the Secretary of State's own periodic review duty described in Section 5, which does not itself call for any workspace action.

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the workspace, or any UK entity in its transport chain, itself holds a permit under the amended Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading Scheme Regulations 2012, an aviation allowance allocation, or a UK Registry account is a fact specific question outside this brief's scope. The obligations and civil penalties described in Section 8 run to "P", the permit holder, aircraft operator, or person served an information notice, not to a freight forwarder generically.

*Analytical inference:* the compliance chain this instrument amends applies to England, Wales and Scotland through the Environment Act 1995 and to Northern Ireland through a separate, parallel set of amendments (Section 8), so a workspace with UK wide operations sits inside two textually distinct but materially parallel regimes.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

FACT: "The first report under this regulation must be published before the end of the period of five years beginning with the day on which the Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading Scheme and National Emissions Inventory (Amendment) Regulations 2013 come into force." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK Statutory Instrument 2013 No. 3135, regulation 8 (inserting regulation 1A into the 2005 Regulations). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/3135

*Per the workspace's reading:* this is the controlling review mechanism for the underlying 2005 Regulations this instrument amends; it binds the Secretary of State, not the workspace, to periodically reassess whether the regulatory system remains appropriate, with reports published at intervals not exceeding five years thereafter.

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

*Analytical inference:* no forward events are recorded for this item in the export this brief was authored from; the only recurring milestone the captured text itself states is the Secretary of State's own five yearly review cycle described in Section 5, a government internal duty rather than a scheduled event the workspace must track for its own compliance.

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does this instrument create a new, freestanding duty on freight forwarders?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* No. It is exclusively an amending instrument; every duty and penalty it creates or modifies runs to "P" as already defined in the 2012 Regulations, the 2005 Regulations, or the Environment Act 1995, not to a freight forwarding intermediary as such.

**Q2: What is the exposure if the workspace itself receives an information notice for the national inventory and does not comply?**

*Operational implication:* Section 8 (obligation 3) describes the civil penalty regime this instrument itself inserts for that failure; a workspace served such a notice should treat the penalty amounts and appeal route described there as immediately applicable.

**Q3: Is there a route to challenge a penalty notice once served?**

*Operational implication:* yes; Section 8 (obligation 6) describes the appeal right to the First-tier tribunal, and obligation 5 describes the regulator's own discretion to reduce, withdraw, or extend time on a penalty before an appeal is even necessary.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

*Note: this is a narrow amending instrument. "Substantive requirements" here means the specific penalty, deadline, reporting, and jurisdictional scope provisions this instrument itself creates or modifies in the underlying 2012 Regulations, 2005 Regulations, Environment Act 1995, and their Northern Ireland parallels. Three further obligations were surveyed but excluded from the workspace adjacent count below because they run to a UK public authority rather than to a private party: the Registries Regulation 2013 competent authority designation split between the regulator and the Secretary of State; the Secretary of State's own periodic review duty for the 2005 Regulations (Section 5); and the removal of a government power of entry for national inventory purposes.*

**1. Amended penalty for carrying out an unauthorised activity.** FACT: "the regulator may increase the amount determined under that paragraph by a percentage designed to ensure that the penalty exceeds the amount of any economic benefit that P has obtained as result of the failure to comply with regulation 9." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK Statutory Instrument 2013 No. 3135, regulation 3. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/3135

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this obligation applies to a person, "P", who carries out a regulated activity contrary to regulation 9 of the 2012 Regulations; it does not itself bind a freight forwarder that holds no permit under those Regulations.

**2. Transitional relief for unreported pre-2013 emissions, subject to a statutory surrender deadline.** FACT: "P is liable to the civil penalty of the sterling equivalent of 20 Euros for each allowance that P failed to surrender by 30th April in the year following Y in respect of the unreported emissions." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK Statutory Instrument 2013 No. 3135, regulation 4 (inserting regulation 87B). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/3135

FACT: "Regulation 51(1) above applies to a penalty under paragraph (3) as it applies to a penalty under Part 7." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK Statutory Instrument 2013 No. 3135, regulation 4 (inserting regulation 87B). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/3135

*Operational implication:* a workspace holding allowances that discovers unreported emissions from a year before 2013 should treat 30th April in the year following the relevant year as the operative surrender deadline to access this relief mechanism, rather than the general excess emissions penalty regime; the same regulator discretion that applies to Part 7 penalties applies equally here.

**3. Civil penalty for failing to comply with a national inventory information notice.** FACT: "The civil penalties are— (a) £1,500; and (b) £150 for each day that P fails to comply with the requirements of the information notice, following service of a penalty notice, up to a maximum of £13,500." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK Statutory Instrument 2013 No. 3135, regulation 12 (inserting Part 6, regulation 16). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/3135

*Operational implication:* a workspace served an information notice under regulation 10(1) of the 2005 Regulations for national inventory purposes should treat this civil penalty ladder as its own direct exposure if it fails, or fails on time, to comply.

**4. Civil penalty for providing false or misleading information.** FACT: "The civil penalty is £1,000." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK Statutory Instrument 2013 No. 3135, regulation 12 (inserting Part 6, regulation 17). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/3135

*Operational implication:* this penalty applies to a written statement made to the Secretary of State for national inventory purposes that is false or misleading in a material particular, whether or not it purports to comply with an information notice.

**5. Regulator discretion in imposing civil penalties.** FACT: "the Secretary of State may— (a) refrain from imposing a civil penalty under this Part; (b) reduce the amount of a penalty (including the amount of an additional daily penalty); (c) extend the time for payment specified in the penalty notice or additional penalty notice; (d) withdraw a penalty notice or an additional penalty notice; or (e) modify the notice by substituting a lower penalty." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK Statutory Instrument 2013 No. 3135, regulation 12 (inserting Part 6, regulation 15). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/3135

*Operational implication:* a workspace facing a penalty notice under obligations 3 or 4 above has a mitigation channel through this discretion before any appeal becomes necessary.

**6. Appeal right to the First-tier tribunal.** FACT: "A person on whom a penalty notice or additional penalty notice has been served under this Part may appeal to the First-tier tribunal" *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK Statutory Instrument 2013 No. 3135, regulation 12 (inserting Part 6, regulation 18). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/3135

*Operational implication:* bringing this appeal suspends the effect of the penalty notice pending the tribunal's final determination, so a workspace disputing a penalty is not required to pay it while the appeal is pending.

**7. Cross-UK jurisdictional scope.** FACT: "Part 4 (regulation 13) amends the definitions in section 41A of the Environment Act 1995, which applies to regulators in England, Wales and Scotland." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK Statutory Instrument 2013 No. 3135, Explanatory Note. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/3135

FACT: "Part 5 (regulations 14 to 16) similarly amends the definitions in the Environment (Northern Ireland) Order 2002 which applies to functions in Northern Ireland." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK Statutory Instrument 2013 No. 3135, Explanatory Note. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/3135

*Analytical inference:* a workspace operating across the whole of the UK sits inside two textually separate but materially parallel amendment tracks: Great Britain via the Environment Act 1995, and Northern Ireland via the 2002 Order and the Northern Ireland Charging Scheme Regulations 2010.

**8. Instrument-wide effective date.** FACT: "These Regulations may be cited as the Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading Scheme and National Emissions Inventory (Amendment) Regulations 2013 and come into force on 31st January 2014." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK Statutory Instrument 2013 No. 3135, regulation 1. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/3135

*Operational implication:* every obligation and penalty amendment described above took effect on this single date; no phased or staggered commencement is stated anywhere in the captured text.

**9. Welsh devolved-competence exception.** FACT: "so far as exercisable in relation to Wales (except in relation to offshore oil and gas exploration and exploitation), those functions continue to be exercisable by the Secretary of State in relation to Wales for such purposes." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK Statutory Instrument 2013 No. 3135, footnote 7. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/3135

*Analytical inference:* this is the one express exception this instrument's own text states: Welsh Ministers' devolved functions under the 1999 Act stop short of offshore oil and gas exploration and exploitation, which the Secretary of State continues to exercise for Wales.

**Qualification accounting.** Per-year trajectory: CAPTURED (see metadata.requirement_trajectory: the made, laid, and in force dates plus the five year periodic review cycle inserted by regulation 8, running from the 31st January 2014 commencement date; no sub cycle phase-in of the penalty or reporting provisions themselves is stated). Exceptions and carve-outs: CAPTURED above (obligation 9, the Welsh offshore oil and gas exploration and exploitation exception). Scope limits: no scope-limiting language was located among the extracted obligations; No scope limits are stated in Sections covering Regulations 1 to 17 of this instrument.

Obligations surveyed: 12; workspace-adjacent: 9; extracted as FACT: 11.

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

FACT: "The civil penalties are— (a) £1,500; and (b) £150 for each day that P fails to comply with the requirements of the information notice, following service of a penalty notice, up to a maximum of £13,500." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK Statutory Instrument 2013 No. 3135, regulation 12. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/3135

*Operational implication:* the reporting obligation this penalty enforces is the underlying regulation 10(1) information notice mechanism in the 2005 Regulations, unchanged by this instrument; this instrument only changes the civil penalty consequence for non compliance, replacing the criminal offences this instrument's regulation 11 abolishes.

# 11. Operational System Requirements

*Note: this instrument makes no technical or reporting system change of its own beyond the civil penalty and appeal mechanics already described in Section 8; "operational system requirements" here means the monitoring a workspace should maintain if it is directly bound.*

**1. Registry account monitoring.** *Operational implication:* a workspace holding a UK Registry account under the amended Registries Regulation 2013 should track the competent authority split this instrument creates, the regulator for most Articles and the Secretary of State for specified Articles, when directing registry correspondence.

**2. Information-notice response process.** *Operational implication:* a workspace that may receive a national inventory information notice under regulation 10(1) of the 2005 Regulations should have an internal process for timely, accurate response, given the civil penalty ladder described in Section 8 (obligations 3 and 4).

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

FACT: "so far as exercisable in relation to Wales (except in relation to offshore oil and gas exploration and exploitation), those functions continue to be exercisable by the Secretary of State in relation to Wales for such purposes." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK Statutory Instrument 2013 No. 3135, footnote 7. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/3135

*Analytical inference:* this is a devolved-competence edge case, which UK authority exercises a function in Wales, not an edge case affecting a private freight forwarder's own compliance duties directly.

# 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

FACT: "An impact assessment has not been prepared as the instrument is not expected to have any significant impact on the private, voluntary or public sectors." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK Statutory Instrument 2013 No. 3135, Explanatory Note. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/3135

*Analytical inference:* the UK Government's own contemporaneous assessment was that this amendment instrument would not materially affect industry; a workspace should weight this instrument's own compliance burden accordingly relative to the underlying 2012 and 2005 Regulations it amends, which remain the primary source of any UK ETS or national inventory duty.

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 2013: instrument year assigned in this item's own legislation.gov.uk identifier, SI 2013/3135.
- 11th December 2013: the Regulations were made.
- 13th December 2013: the Regulations were laid before Parliament.
- 31st January 2014: the Regulations, and the amendments they make, came into force.

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks the Climate Change Agreements (Administration) (Miscellaneous Amendments) Regulations 2013, a UK Statutory Instrument that amends the administrative and penalty-calculation mechanics of the Climate Change Agreements (Administration) Regulations 2012. It exists to give a workspace that operates or administers a facility covered by a Climate Change Agreement (CCA) target unit a single record of what these amendments changed and when they took effect.

FACT: "The Climate Change Agreements (Administration) (Miscellaneous Amendments) Regulations 2013" *Source: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/508*

*Analytical inference:* this is a narrow, technical amending instrument (five short amending regulations plus an explanatory note) rather than a free-standing regulatory scheme; its substantive content is limited to redefining terms used in the 2012 Regulations and adjusting how a financial penalty is calculated for one category of target unit.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to a Workspace with a Climate Change Agreement

FACT: "The Secretary of State makes the following Regulations in exercise of the powers conferred by paragraphs 52D to 52F and 146 of Schedule 6 to the Finance Act 2000" *Source: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/508*

FACT: "These Regulations may be cited as the Climate Change Agreements (Administration) (Miscellaneous Amendments) Regulations 2013 and come into force on 31st March 2013." *Source: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/508*

*Operational implication:* a workspace that already holds a Climate Change Agreement target unit under the 2012 Regulations should treat these amendments as changes to how its own base year, emissions, and any financial penalty are calculated, effective from the date below, not as a new standalone obligation.

FACT: "Made 5th March 2013 Laid before the House of Commons 8th March 2013 Coming into force 31st March 2013" *Source: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/508*

FACT: "A reference to a numbered regulation is to that regulation in the Climate Change Agreements (Administration) Regulations 2012" *Source: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/508*

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

*Legal Confirmation Required:* these amendments only affect a workspace that is itself the operator of a target unit under a Climate Change Agreement made pursuant to Schedule 6 to the Finance Act 2000. This captured source does not itself state which facility types are eligible for a Climate Change Agreement; a workspace with an energy-intensive facility (for example a cold-storage or intensive processing site) should confirm with HM Revenue and Customs or its sector's Climate Change Agreement scheme administrator whether it holds, or is eligible to hold, a target unit before treating any obligation below as running to it.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

FACT: "2000 c.17 ; paragraphs 52A to 52F were inserted by paragraph 9 of Schedule 31 to the Finance Act 2012 (c.14) , which also amended paragraphs 44, 45, 45B, 47, 48 and 49 of that Schedule." *Source: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/508*

FACT: "These Regulations amend the Climate Change Agreements (Administration) Regulations 2012." *Source: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/508*

*Analytical inference:* the captured source's own Explanatory Note states plainly, "(This note is not part of the Regulations)"; it is read here only as the drafter's own summary of intent, not as a source of independent obligations.

FACT: "Regulation 5 amends the provisions on the calculation of financial penalties which are calculated on the basis of the difference between the amount of levy payable on supplies of taxable commodities if the supplies were not reduced rate supplies and if the supplies were reduced rate supplies, in respect of target units which include greenfield sites, if the penalty notice is served during the first year that the target unit is covered by an agreement." *Source: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/508*

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does the workspace operate or administer a facility that is a target unit under a Climate Change Agreement made pursuant to the Climate Change Agreements (Administration) Regulations 2012?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this captured source amends that 2012 scheme but does not itself state eligibility criteria for entering a Climate Change Agreement. A workspace must confirm its own status directly with the scheme administrator before any obligation below is treated as running to it.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

*Note: this is a narrow amending instrument. "Substantive requirements" here means the specific redefinitions and calculation-mechanic changes this instrument makes to the 2012 Regulations, each of which is workspace-adjacent only for a workspace that already holds a Climate Change Agreement target unit.*

**1. "Base year" redefined for a target unit without a greenfield facility.** FACT: "“base year” in respect of a target unit which does not include a greenfield facility means a 12 month period agreed between an operator and the administrator, ending prior to the date of an underlying agreement, for which data is supplied by an operator to the administrator prior to the operator entering into the underlying agreement;" *Source: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/508*

**2. "Base year" redefined for a target unit that includes a greenfield facility.** FACT: "“base year” in respect of a target unit which does include a greenfield facility means the 12 month period starting on the date of an underlying agreement;" *Source: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/508*

*Operational implication:* a workspace whose target unit includes a facility that only recently started the relevant process should identify which of these two base-year definitions applies to it, since the calculation basis differs by twelve months' timing.

**3. "Emissions" redefined to be measured on a carbon-dioxide-equivalent basis.** FACT: "In the definition of “emissions”, after “tCO 2 ” insert “equivalent”." *Source: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/508*

**4. "Greenfield facility" newly defined.** FACT: "“greenfield facility” means a facility which started to carry out the process by virtue of which it is a facility within the meaning of paragraph 50 of Schedule 6 during the 12 month period ending on the date the operator applies for the facility to be covered by an agreement;" *Source: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/508*

**5. "tCO2 equivalent" newly defined, replacing the prior "tCO2" measurement basis.** FACT: "“tCO 2 equivalent” means tonnes of carbon dioxide or an amount of methane or nitrous oxide with an equivalent global-warming potential;" *Source: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/508*

**6. Buy-out fee calculation basis in regulation 12 updated to the new equivalent-emissions unit.** FACT: "In regulation 12, for “tCO 2 ”, substitute “tCO 2 equivalent”." *Source: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/508*

**7. Penalty applicability rule differentiated by greenfield status and timing.** FACT: "This paragraph applies in respect of a penalty that may be imposed under paragraph (1)(a), (c) or (d) on— (a) the operator of a target unit which does not include a greenfield facility; or (b) the operator of a target unit which includes a greenfield facility, if the penalty notice is served at any time after the expiry of the 12 month period starting on the date of an underlying agreement." *Source: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/508*

*Operational implication:* a workspace whose target unit includes a greenfield facility should specifically track the twelve-month window starting on the date of its underlying agreement, since which penalty-calculation rule applies to it (this one, or obligation 8 below) turns on whether a penalty notice is served inside or outside that window.

**8. Minimum financial penalty floor for a greenfield-facility target unit penalised within its first twelve months.** FACT: "the amount of the financial penalty that may be imposed under paragraph (1)(a), (c) or (d) is the greater of— (a) £250; or (b)" *Source: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/508*

*Analytical inference:* the captured source's paragraph (2C) defines the second alternative in this "greater of" test as the administrator's reasonable estimate of the difference in levy payable on taxable commodity supplies to the target unit with and without reduced-rate treatment; the mathematical expression itself did not extract as readable text from the captured source (it renders in the source as a formula), so only the stated £250 floor and the qualitative basis of the alternative are recorded here, not a computed figure for the alternative.

No phase-in is stated in Sections covering Regulations 1 to 5 of this instrument.

No exceptions are stated in Sections covering Regulations 1 to 5 of this instrument.

No scope limits are stated in Sections covering Regulations 1 to 5 of this instrument.

Obligations surveyed: 8; workspace-adjacent: 8; extracted as FACT: 8.

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

*Analytical inference:* the instrument's own greenfield/non-greenfield distinction (obligations 1, 2, 7 and 8 in Section 8) functions as the one differentiated-treatment edge case this instrument creates: a target unit that includes a greenfield facility is calculated and penalised on a different timing basis than one that does not.

FACT: "“greenfield facility” means a facility which started to carry out the process by virtue of which it is a facility within the meaning of paragraph 50 of Schedule 6 during the 12 month period ending on the date the operator applies for the facility to be covered by an agreement;" *Source: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/508*

FACT: "This paragraph applies in respect of a penalty that may be imposed under paragraph (1)(a), (c) or (d) on— (a) the operator of a target unit which does not include a greenfield facility; or (b) the operator of a target unit which includes a greenfield facility, if the penalty notice is served at any time after the expiry of the 12 month period starting on the date of an underlying agreement." *Source: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/508*

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 5th March 2013: Regulations made under powers conferred by Schedule 6 to the Finance Act 2000.
- 8th March 2013: Regulations laid before the House of Commons.
- 31st March 2013: Regulations come into force, amending the Climate Change Agreements (Administration) Regulations 2012.
- 2013: Enacted (legislation.gov.uk identifier year).

*Source for timeline entries: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/508*

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks a 2010 European Commission Decision under the EU Emissions Trading Scheme (ETS) that adjusts the total Union-wide quantity of emission allowances available for the 2013 trading year and repeals an earlier Commission Decision on the same subject. It exists to give a freight forwarder with EU ETS-linked exposure (for example, through aviation operations covered by the scheme) a record of what this specific Decision sets, who it is addressed to, and what, if anything, it requires of the workspace directly.

*Analytical inference:* this Decision is a narrow, numeric implementing act (setting one figure: the 2013 Union-wide allowance total) rather than a standalone compliance obligation; its practical relevance to the workspace is as background to the broader EU ETS allowance-supply trend, not as a source of a direct duty.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

FACT: "This Decision is addressed to the Member States." *Source: Commission Decision 2010/634/EU. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32010D0634

*Legal Confirmation Required:* because this Decision's own text states it is addressed to the Member States rather than to private operators, whether any EU ETS obligation on an aviation or maritime operator flows indirectly from the allowance total this Decision sets is a separate, fact-specific question outside this brief's scope and requires counsel review against the operator's own EU ETS compliance obligations under Directive 2003/87/EC.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

*No content for this section: the captured source states no action, deadline, or request running to a private freight-forwarding workspace; every deadline in the source (recitals 4 and 8) runs to Member States and has already passed.*

# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks Commission Decision 2010/222/EU, the instrument recording the European Commission's own accession as a partner to the Global Bioenergy Partnership (GBP). It exists to give a freight-forwarding workspace with EU bioenergy-policy exposure a single record of what the Commission committed to, since the captured source text creates no direct compliance duty on private industry.

*Analytical inference:* the discussion below reads this decision as an EU institutional-participation act rather than a regulatory instrument, because the captured source text contains no clause addressed to a party other than the Commission itself.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

Commission Decision 2010/222/EU is the instrument by which the European Commission itself joins the Global Bioenergy Partnership, an international, voluntary sustainability-coordination body for biomass and biofuels first endorsed at the 2005 G8 Gleneagles Plan of Action. FACT: the captured source's own citation header states, verbatim: «of the European Union L 98/12 COMMISSION DECISION of 19 April 2010 on the European Commission becoming a partne» (Official Journal of the European Union, L 98/12).

*Analytical inference:* this decision is not itself a regulation, directive, or standard creating a compliance duty on a freight-forwarding workspace; it is an EU institutional act about the Commission's own external representation in an international bioenergy body. It is workspace-relevant only as a policy-context signal for bioenergy and sustainable-biofuel coordination the Commission participates in internationally, not as a source of an operational duty running directly to a private operator.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

*Operational implication:* none identified. This decision records the Commission's own 2010 accession to an international partnership; the captured source text names no pending action, deadline, or event a freight-forwarding workspace needs to act on.

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

*Legal Confirmation Required:* Commission Decision 2010/222/EU is an internal Commission act of accession to an international bioenergy-cooperation body; the captured source text names no addressee outside the Commission itself and states no compliance duty running to a private freight-forwarding operator. FACT: the captured source states, verbatim: «Done at Brussels, 19 April 2010.»

GAP: [primary_deadline] No source in this brief's corpus states a compliance deadline running to a private freight-forwarding workspace under this decision; the only date stated is the Commission's own adoption/signing date of 19 April 2010, which is not itself a compliance deadline.

GAP: [penalty_summary] No source in this brief's corpus states a penalty, fine, or enforcement consequence running to a private freight-forwarding workspace under this decision. FACT: the captured source states, verbatim: «Such contributions are made on a voluntary basis and the decision to participate does not commit the Commission to financial contributions to common budgets» -- there is no penalty mechanism of any kind stated, on the Commission or on any private party.

GAP: [effective_date] No explicit entry-into-force or effective-date clause is present in the captured source text beyond the Commission's own adoption/signing statement quoted above; a full-brief regrounding would confirm whether EUR-Lex's own notification-based entry-into-force rule applies to this specific decision.

*Analytical inference:* because this decision's compliance chain runs from the Commission to the Global Bioenergy Partnership's own governance framework rather than from the Commission to industry, the workspace's only practical interest is the sustainability-policy signal the decision represents, not a compliance obligation.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

*No content for this section -- the captured pool contains only the decision's own operative text, with no separate implementing-guidance document identified.*

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

*No content for this section -- the captured pool records only the decision's 2010 adoption, already reflected in Section 14's timeline; no forward-looking guidance or pending event is stated.*

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does this decision create a compliance duty on a private freight-forwarding operator?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* the captured source text addresses only the Commission's own participation and its Commissioner's signature authority (Section 8); it names no external addressee and states no duty running to a private operator. A workspace with a specific compliance question about EU bioenergy-sustainability policy generally should confirm current status directly against EUR-Lex rather than relying solely on this decision.

**Q2: Is the Global Bioenergy Partnership itself a body the workspace needs to register with or report to?**

*Analytical inference:* No. FACT: the captured source states, verbatim: «The Global Bioenergy Partnership relies on contributions from members.» The Partnership's own contribution structure, per Section 4, runs to Commission-level members, not to private industry participants.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

*Note: this decision is an EU Commission internal governance act, not a regulatory instrument imposing duties on private industry. "Substantive requirements" here means the decision's own two operative articles (the obligations it places on the Commission itself), surveyed for workspace relevance rather than assumed to apply.*

**1. Partnership-participation obligation (Commission, Article 1).** FACT: the captured source states, verbatim: «HAS ADOPTED THIS DECISION: Article 1 The European Commission (hereafter referred to as ‘the Commission’) shall participate as a partner in the Global Bioenergy Partnership.»

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this obligation runs from the Commission to the Global Bioenergy Partnership's own governance framework; it does not create a duty running from the Commission, or from the European Union generally, to a private freight-forwarding operator.

**2. Signature-authorization obligation (Commissioner for Energy, Article 2).** FACT: the captured source states, verbatim: «The Commissioner for Energy, or his designated representative, is authorised to sign the Terms of Reference for the Global Bioenergy Partnership on behalf of the Commission.»

*Analytical inference:* this is an internal delegation-of-signature-authority clause; it names no external addressee and creates no duty for any party outside the Commission.

No phase-in is stated in Articles 1 to 2. No exceptions are stated in Articles 1 to 2. No scope limits are stated in Articles 1 to 2.
