entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks Commission Decision 2001/171/EC, a narrow EU derogation instrument that lets glass packaging exceed the general heavy-metal concentration limit set by Directive 94/62/EC on packaging and packaging waste, under stated conditions. It exists to give a freight forwarder moving glass packaging, glass containers, or packaged goods in glass packaging into or within the EU a single place to see: what concentration limit applies, who the reporting duty falls to, and when the derogation itself expires.

FACT: "Commission Decision of 19 February 2001 establishing the conditions for a derogation for glass packaging in relation to the heavy metal concentration levels established in Directive 94/62/EC on packaging and packaging waste" *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX:32001D0171. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32001D0171

**What the workspace should expect to decide:** whether any manufacturer, authorised representative, or importer in its own glass-packaging supply chain is the party responsible for the Article 5 reporting duty described in Section 10, and whether that party is established within the European Union.

*Analytical inference:* this Decision does not itself address freight forwarding, transport, or customs handling of glass packaging; it addresses the packaging's own heavy-metal content at the point of manufacture and market placement.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

FACT: "Directive 94/62/EC provides in Article 11 a gradual reduction of the concentration of heavy metals in packaging." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX:32001D0171. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32001D0171

FACT: "Experience of the first years of application of Article 11 has shown that there is a specific problem in the glass sector, as the recycled glass is contaminated by glass material containing high quantities of lead." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX:32001D0171. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32001D0171

*Operational implication:* the Decision applies to the workspace indirectly, through any glass packaging it moves: a freight forwarder is not the addressee (Section 7), but the packaging it transports is subject to this Decision's own concentration-limit regime, and any manufacturer, authorised representative, or (per Section 8's fallback obligee) importer in the chain may carry the Article 5 reporting duty.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

*No content for this section is grounded in the item's captured source pool.*

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

FACT: "This Decision is addressed to the Member States." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX:32001D0171. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32001D0171

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this Decision's own reporting fallback (Section 10, Article 5's third sentence) shifts the reporting obligation to "the person who places the product on the Community market" whenever neither the manufacturer nor its authorised representative is established within the European Union. Whether a specific freight-forwarding workspace in a given transaction is that "person" is a fact-specific determination of legal role under EU packaging law and is outside this brief's scope; it requires counsel review of the actual commercial and customs arrangement.

*Analytical inference:* absent that determination, the workspace's ordinary position in this compliance chain is as a mover of already-compliant (or already-derogated) glass packaging, not as the party responsible for the underlying heavy-metal reporting.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

FACT: "Having regard to European Parliament and Council Directive 94/62/EC of 20 December 1994 on packaging and packaging waste(1), and in particular Article 11(3) thereof," *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX:32001D0171. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32001D0171

*Per the workspace's reading:* this is the controlling parent instrument and legal basis for the Decision -- Directive 94/62/EC's own Article 11(3) is what authorises the Commission to grant this derogation; the Decision does not amend Directive 94/62/EC itself, it creates a bounded exception to Article 11's own concentration-limit schedule.

FACT: "The measures provided for in this Decision are in accordance with the opinion of the Committee, established pursuant to Article 21 of European Parliament and Council Directive 94/62/EC," *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX:32001D0171. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32001D0171

*Analytical inference:* the Decision's own procedural basis (a Committee opinion under the same Article 21 procedure that also governs the possible extension in Section 6) is comitology process, not a duty running to the workspace.

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

FACT: "The derogation is to expire on 30 June 2006 unless this deadline is extended in accordance with the procedure laid down in Article 21 of Directive 94/62/EC." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX:32001D0171. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32001D0171

FACT: "This Decision shall expire on 30 June 2006, unless it is extended, in particular on the basis of the reports under Article 5 of this Decision and Article 17 of Directive 94/62/EC, in accordance with the procedure laid down in Article 21 of Directive 94/62/EC." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX:32001D0171. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32001D0171

*Operational implication:* the only pending event this captured text itself identifies is a contingency, not a scheduled action: whether the derogation is extended past 30 June 2006 under the Article 21 procedure. This brief's own captured pool does not include any later instrument confirming or denying an extension; a workspace with a live glass-packaging shipment near or past that date should confirm current status directly against EUR-Lex rather than relying on this summary alone.

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does this Decision create a direct obligation on a freight forwarder?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* the Decision's obligations (Section 8) run to manufacturers, authorised representatives, and -- only in the fallback case of Section 8, obligation 7 -- "the person who places the product on the Community market." Whether a specific freight-forwarding workspace occupies that fallback role in a given transaction is a fact-specific legal-role question outside this brief's scope.

**Q2: Is the workspace itself the addressee of this Decision?**

FACT: "This Decision is addressed to the Member States." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX:32001D0171. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32001D0171

*Analytical inference:* no. The Decision is addressed to the Member States, not to any private party; any duty reaching a manufacturer, representative, or market-placing party (Section 8) arrives through the Member States' own implementation and enforcement of Directive 94/62/EC and this Decision, not directly from the Decision's own addressee clause.

**Q3: Does the 100 ppm limit apply to all packaging, or only glass packaging?**

FACT: "HAS ADOPTED THIS DECISION: Article 1 This Decision, shall apply to glass packaging covered by Directive 94/62/EC, and aims to establish the conditions under which the concentration levels established in Article 11 of Directive 94/62/EC shall not apply." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX:32001D0171. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32001D0171

*Analytical inference:* this Decision's own derogation is scoped to glass packaging only; it says nothing about the Article 11 limit as it applies to any other packaging material.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

*Note: this is a narrow EU derogation Decision, not a broad regulatory framework. "Substantive requirements" here means the Decision's own stated conditions, obligations, and dates -- most running to a manufacturer, authorised representative, or (in the fallback case) a market-placing party, not to a freight forwarder directly.*

**1. Scope of the derogation.** FACT: "HAS ADOPTED THIS DECISION: Article 1 This Decision, shall apply to glass packaging covered by Directive 94/62/EC, and aims to establish the conditions under which the concentration levels established in Article 11 of Directive 94/62/EC shall not apply." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX:32001D0171. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32001D0171

**2. Definitional exclusion for recycled feedstock.** FACT: "For the purposes of this Decision: - the definitions as set out in Article 3 of Directive 94/62/EC shall apply, - "intentionally introduced" shall mean "deliberately utilised in the formulation of a packaging or a packaging component where its continued presence is desired in the final packaging or packaging component to provide a specific characteristic, appearance, or quality"; the use of recycled materials as feedstock for the manufacture of new packaging materials, where some portion of the recycled materials may contain amounts of regulated metals, is not be considered as intentionally introduced." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX:32001D0171. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32001D0171

*Analytical inference:* this exclusion is why recycled glass cullet carrying trace heavy metals does not itself trigger Article 4's prohibition below -- the metals must be intentionally introduced during manufacture, not merely present because recycled material was used as feedstock.

**3. Permission to exceed the 100 ppm limit from 30 June 2001.** FACT: "Glass packaging is allowed to exceed, after the date of 30 June 2001, the limit of 100 ppm by weight established in Article 11 of Directive 94/62/EC where it complies with all the conditions established in Articles 4 and 5 of this Decision." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX:32001D0171. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32001D0171

**4. Prohibition on intentional introduction; permitted cause of excess.** FACT: "No lead, cadmium, mercury or hexavalent chromium shall be intentionally introduced during the manufacturing process. The packaging material may only exceed the concentration limits because of the addition of recycled materials." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX:32001D0171. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32001D0171

**5. Reporting trigger.** FACT: "Where the average heavy metals concentration levels on any twelve consecutive monthly controls made from the production of each individual glass furnace, representative of normal and regular production activity, exceeds the 200 ppm limit, the manufacturer or this authorised representative shall submit a report to the competent authorities in the Member States." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX:32001D0171. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32001D0171

**6. Report content.** FACT: "This report shall include as a minimum the following information: - measures values, - description of measurement methods employed, - suspected sources for the presence of heavy metals concentration levels, - detailed description of the measures taken to reduce the heavy metals concentration levels." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX:32001D0171. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32001D0171

**7. Fallback reporting obligee.** FACT: "Where neither the manufacturer nor his authorised representative is established within the European Union, the obligation to submit a report to the competent authorities shall be with the person who places the product on the Communtiy market." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX:32001D0171. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32001D0171

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a specific freight-forwarding workspace is "the person who places the product on the Community market" in a given transaction is a fact-specific legal-role determination outside this brief's scope; see Section 4.

**8. Continuous availability of measurement records.** FACT: "Measurement results from production sites and measurement methods employed shall be made available at any time to the competent authorities, if requested." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX:32001D0171. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32001D0171

**9. Expiry of the derogation.** FACT: "This Decision shall expire on 30 June 2006, unless it is extended, in particular on the basis of the reports under Article 5 of this Decision and Article 17 of Directive 94/62/EC, in accordance with the procedure laid down in Article 21 of Directive 94/62/EC." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX:32001D0171. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32001D0171

**10. Addressee.** FACT: "This Decision is addressed to the Member States." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX:32001D0171. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32001D0171

*Analytical inference:* obligation 10 is procedural (it names who the Decision is formally addressed to, the Member States) rather than a duty on a manufacturer, representative, or market-placing party, so it is excluded from the workspace-adjacent count below even though it is captured as a FACT claim here.

GAP: no source in this item's captured pool states a fine, penalty, or sanction running to a manufacturer, authorised representative, importer, or freight-forwarding operator for exceeding the heavy-metal concentration limits or failing to submit the Article 5 report; the only consequences this Decision itself states are the reporting duty (obligation 5-7 above) and the derogation's own expiry (obligation 9).

No exceptions are stated in Articles 1 to 7.

No scope limits are stated in Articles 1 to 7.

This instrument's own two-date trajectory (30 June 2001 permission begins; 30 June 2006 expiry unless extended) is captured in metadata.requirement_trajectory; no year-by-year phase-in percentage is stated.

Obligations surveyed: 11; workspace-adjacent: 9; extracted as FACT: 10.

# 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

FACT: "HAS ADOPTED THIS DECISION: Article 1 This Decision, shall apply to glass packaging covered by Directive 94/62/EC, and aims to establish the conditions under which the concentration levels established in Article 11 of Directive 94/62/EC shall not apply." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX:32001D0171. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32001D0171

FACT: "Glass packaging is allowed to exceed, after the date of 30 June 2001, the limit of 100 ppm by weight established in Article 11 of Directive 94/62/EC where it complies with all the conditions established in Articles 4 and 5 of this Decision." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX:32001D0171. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32001D0171

*Operational implication:* the product-specific compliance question for glass packaging is binary and conditional: it may exceed the general 100 ppm limit only when the Article 4 and Article 5 conditions (no intentional introduction; the reporting trigger and content) are both met.

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

FACT: "Where the average heavy metals concentration levels on any twelve consecutive monthly controls made from the production of each individual glass furnace, representative of normal and regular production activity, exceeds the 200 ppm limit, the manufacturer or this authorised representative shall submit a report to the competent authorities in the Member States." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX:32001D0171. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32001D0171

FACT: "This report shall include as a minimum the following information: - measures values, - description of measurement methods employed, - suspected sources for the presence of heavy metals concentration levels, - detailed description of the measures taken to reduce the heavy metals concentration levels." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX:32001D0171. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32001D0171

FACT: "Where neither the manufacturer nor his authorised representative is established within the European Union, the obligation to submit a report to the competent authorities shall be with the person who places the product on the Communtiy market." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX:32001D0171. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32001D0171

FACT: "Measurement results from production sites and measurement methods employed shall be made available at any time to the competent authorities, if requested." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX:32001D0171. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32001D0171

*Operational implication:* there is no registration mechanism in this captured text at all -- the only formal obligation is the conditional report to "the competent authorities in the Member States," triggered by the 200 ppm/twelve-month-average threshold, not a standing registration duty.

# 11. Operational System Requirements

*Note: because this is a narrow derogation Decision rather than an operating framework, "operational system requirements" here means the monitoring a workspace should maintain over its own glass-packaging supply chain's compliance status, not a technical system the Decision itself requires the workspace to build.*

FACT: "Measurement results from production sites and measurement methods employed shall be made available at any time to the competent authorities, if requested." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX:32001D0171. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32001D0171

*Operational implication:* a workspace with visibility into a glass-packaging manufacturer's or importer's own compliance program should confirm that measurement records are retained and available on request, since the Decision requires them to be available "at any time," not merely during a scheduled reporting cycle.

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

FACT: "For the purposes of this Decision: - the definitions as set out in Article 3 of Directive 94/62/EC shall apply, - "intentionally introduced" shall mean "deliberately utilised in the formulation of a packaging or a packaging component where its continued presence is desired in the final packaging or packaging component to provide a specific characteristic, appearance, or quality"; the use of recycled materials as feedstock for the manufacture of new packaging materials, where some portion of the recycled materials may contain amounts of regulated metals, is not be considered as intentionally introduced." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX:32001D0171. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32001D0171

*Analytical inference:* the one substantive edge case this captured text defines is the recycled-feedstock exclusion above (obligation 2 in Section 8): heavy metals present only because recycled material was used as feedstock are not "intentionally introduced," and so do not by themselves defeat the Article 4 prohibition.

# 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

*No content for this section is grounded in the item's captured source pool.*

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 19 February 2001: Commission Decision 2001/171/EC adopted, establishing the derogation for glass packaging heavy-metal concentration limits.
- 2 March 2001: the Decision published in the Official Journal, reference L 062, pages 0020 to 0021.
- 30 June 2001: the general 100 ppm heavy-metal concentration limit under Article 11 of Directive 94/62/EC takes effect; from this date, glass packaging may exceed it only under the conditions in Articles 4 and 5 of this Decision.
- 30 June 2006: this Decision's derogation expires, unless extended under the Article 21 procedure of Directive 94/62/EC.

*Source for timeline entries: EUR-Lex, CELEX:32001D0171 (https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32001D0171).*

metadata.what_is_it: An EU Commission Decision (2001/171/EC) granting glass packaging a bounded derogation from Directive 94/62/EC's general heavy-metal concentration limit for packaging, conditioned on the excess arising only from recycled-material feedstock and on a reporting duty when a 200 ppm average is exceeded.
metadata.why_matters: It sets the concentration-limit regime and reporting duty that applies to any glass packaging a workspace moves into or within the EU, and it identifies a fallback reporting obligee (the person who places the product on the Community market) that could reach an importer or forwarding party if the manufacturer or its EU representative is not established in the Union.

derogation expiry 30 June 2006 unless extended under the Article 21 procedure

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks Commission Decision 2011/13/EU of 12 January 2011 on certain types of information about biofuels and bioliquids to be submitted by economic operators to Member States, an EU implementing decision under Directive 2009/28/EC and Directive 98/70/EC. It exists to give a workspace that handles biofuel or bioliquid consignments a single place to see what information EU Member States expect economic operators to report on a per-consignment basis.

FACT: "This Decision is addressed to the Member States." *Source: Commission Decision 2011/13/EU, EUR-Lex CELEX:32011D0013. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32011D0013

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a specific workspace itself qualifies as an "economic operator" for the purposes of this Decision is a fact-specific question this brief's own corpus does not resolve; it depends on the workspace's role in the biofuel/bioliquid supply chain and requires counsel review.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

FACT: "HAS ADOPTED THIS DECISION: Article 1 The information to be submitted by economic operators for each consignment of biofuel or bioliquid shall consist of an indication of:" *Source: Commission Decision 2011/13/EU, EUR-Lex CELEX:32011D0013. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32011D0013

*Operational implication:* a workspace that is itself an economic operator handling biofuel or bioliquid consignments in the EU sits inside this reporting chain; a workspace that is only a freight intermediary for such cargo, without itself being the reporting economic operator, is adjacent to this Decision rather than a direct addressee of Article 1's information items (see Section 4).

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

FACT: "This Decision is addressed to the Member States." *Source: Commission Decision 2011/13/EU, EUR-Lex CELEX:32011D0013. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32011D0013

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this Decision's own Article 3 states it is addressed to the Member States, not to economic operators directly; the recitals describe Member States ensuring that economic operators report to them, so any duty running to a specific freight-forwarding workspace depends on how a given Member State implements this Decision domestically. This brief's own corpus does not include that domestic implementing measure, and confirming whether it creates a direct reporting duty on the workspace requires counsel review.

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Is the workspace an "economic operator" for the purposes of Article 1?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* the captured text of this Decision does not itself define "economic operator"; whether a specific freight-forwarding workspace handling biofuel or bioliquid consignments meets that description under the relevant Member State's implementing measure is a fact-specific legal question outside this brief's corpus.

**Q2: Does the waste-and-residues carve-out in Article 1 relieve the workspace of any of the four information items?**

FACT: "With the exception of biofuels and bioliquids produced from waste and residues, it shall consist in addition of an indication of: (c) whether the bonus referred to in Annex V, part C, points 7 and 8 of Directive 2009/28/EC and Annex IV, part C, points 7 and 8 of Directive 98/70/EC has been used in the greenhouse gas calculation referred to in Annex V, part C, point 1 of Directive 2009/28/EC and Annex IV, part C, point 1 of Directive 98/70/EC for the consignment;" *Source: Commission Decision 2011/13/EU, EUR-Lex CELEX:32011D0013. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32011D0013

*Analytical inference:* a consignment made from waste or residues is relieved of items (c) and (d) (the bonus and soil-carbon-accumulation indicators) but not of items (a) and (b) (the voluntary-scheme certification indication), per the plain text of Article 1.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

**1. Voluntary-scheme certification indication (Article 1(a)).** FACT: "(a) whether the consignment has been certified or accepted as fulfilling the requirements of a voluntary scheme that has been recognised by the Commission, in accordance with the second subparagraph of Article 18(4) of Directive 2009/28/EC and the second subparagraph of Article 7c(4) of Directive 98/70/EC, as containing accurate data for the purposes of information on measures taken for soil, water and air protection, the restoration of degraded land, the avoidance of excessive water consumption in areas where water is scarce and/or to take into account the issues referred to in the second subparagraph of Article 17(7) of Directive 2009/28/EC and the second subparagraph of Article 7b(7) of Directive 98/70/EC;" *Source: Commission Decision 2011/13/EU, EUR-Lex CELEX:32011D0013. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32011D0013

**2. Voluntary-scheme name (Article 1(b)).** FACT: "(b) if the consignment has been certified or accepted as referred to in point (a), the name of the voluntary scheme in question;" *Source: Commission Decision 2011/13/EU, EUR-Lex CELEX:32011D0013. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32011D0013

**3. Bonus-use indication, waste/residues excepted (Article 1(c)).** FACT: "With the exception of biofuels and bioliquids produced from waste and residues, it shall consist in addition of an indication of: (c) whether the bonus referred to in Annex V, part C, points 7 and 8 of Directive 2009/28/EC and Annex IV, part C, points 7 and 8 of Directive 98/70/EC has been used in the greenhouse gas calculation referred to in Annex V, part C, point 1 of Directive 2009/28/EC and Annex IV, part C, point 1 of Directive 98/70/EC for the consignment;" *Source: Commission Decision 2011/13/EU, EUR-Lex CELEX:32011D0013. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32011D0013

*Analytical inference:* the waste-and-residues carve-out in this span means a consignment made wholly from waste or residues is not required to report the bonus-use indication.

**4. Soil-carbon-accumulation-factor indication, waste/residues excepted (Article 1(d)).** FACT: "(d) whether the factor for emissions savings from soil carbon accumulation via improved agricultural management referred to in Annex V, part C, point 1 of Directive 2009/28/EC and Annex IV, part C, point 1 of Directive 98/70/EC has been used in the greenhouse gas calculation referred to in the same paragraph for the consignment." *Source: Commission Decision 2011/13/EU, EUR-Lex CELEX:32011D0013. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32011D0013

**5. Preserved Commission information-request power (Article 2).** FACT: "This Decision shall be without prejudice to the Commission’s right to request additional information from economic operators for the purposes of Article 23(2) of Directive 2009/28/EC." *Source: Commission Decision 2011/13/EU, EUR-Lex CELEX:32011D0013. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32011D0013

*Operational implication:* an economic operator's reporting duty under this Decision is not capped at the four Article 1 items; the Commission retains a separate, preserved right to request further information under the parent Directive.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* none of the five obligations above states a compliance deadline, a fine, or a penalty running to a private freight-forwarding workspace; whether a domestic Member State implementing measure attaches one is outside this brief's own corpus (see Section 4).

No phase-in is stated in Articles 1 to 3.

No exceptions are stated in Articles 1 to 3.

No scope limits are stated in Articles 1 to 3.

Obligations surveyed: 5; workspace-adjacent: 5; extracted as FACT: 5.

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

FACT: "HAS ADOPTED THIS DECISION: Article 1 The information to be submitted by economic operators for each consignment of biofuel or bioliquid shall consist of an indication of:" *Source: Commission Decision 2011/13/EU, EUR-Lex CELEX:32011D0013. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32011D0013

*Operational implication:* the reporting unit is the individual consignment of biofuel or bioliquid, not a periodic filing; a workspace tracking multiple consignments needs a per-consignment record of the four Article 1 indications, not a single blanket report.

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

FACT: "With the exception of biofuels and bioliquids produced from waste and residues, it shall consist in addition of an indication of: (c) whether the bonus referred to in Annex V, part C, points 7 and 8 of Directive 2009/28/EC and Annex IV, part C, points 7 and 8 of Directive 98/70/EC has been used in the greenhouse gas calculation referred to in Annex V, part C, point 1 of Directive 2009/28/EC and Annex IV, part C, point 1 of Directive 98/70/EC for the consignment;" *Source: Commission Decision 2011/13/EU, EUR-Lex CELEX:32011D0013. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32011D0013

*Analytical inference:* this carve-out is scoped narrowly to items (c) and (d); it does not touch the certification and scheme-name items (a) and (b), which apply to every consignment regardless of whether it is made from waste, residues, or virgin feedstock.

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 12 January 2011: Commission Decision 2011/13/EU adopted, addressed to the Member States.

FACT: "Done at Brussels, 12 January 2011." *Source: Commission Decision 2011/13/EU, EUR-Lex CELEX:32011D0013. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32011D0013

*Source for timeline entries: Commission Decision 2011/13/EU, EUR-Lex CELEX:32011D0013 (https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32011D0013).*

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2022/919 of 8 June 2022, which amends Commission Decision 2005/381/EC as regards the questionnaire Member States use to report to the Commission on the application of Directive 2003/87/EC (the EU Emissions Trading System Directive). It is an administrative reporting instrument, not a rule that itself binds a freight forwarder: it exists to give a workspace with EU ETS exposure (aviation or maritime transport falling under the Directive) a single place to see what EU Member State authorities are now required to report to the Commission, and on what timetable.

FACT: "Article 21(1) of Directive 2003/87/EC requires Member States to submit annual reports to the Commission on the application of that Directive." *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2022/919 of 8 June 2022, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0919

*Analytical inference:* the obligation quoted above runs from Member States to the Commission under Article 21(1) of Directive 2003/87/EC; this Decision replaces the ANNEX (the reporting questionnaire itself) that Member States use to satisfy that obligation, not the underlying obligation.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

This Decision is a Commission Implementing Decision, not a Regulation or Directive in its own right. It replaces the Annex to Commission Decision 2005/381/EC, updating the questionnaire Member States must use to report on EU ETS implementation.

FACT: "Commission Decision 2005/381/EC ( 2 ) sets out in its Annex a questionnaire to be used by the Member States for the drawing up of annual reports aimed at establishing a detailed account of the application of Directive 2003/87/EC." *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2022/919 of 8 June 2022, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0919

**Jurisdictional scope slot:**

FACT: "Implementing Regulation (EU) 2018/2067 applies to the verification of greenhouse gas emissions and tonne-kilometre data from 1 January 2019" *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2022/919 of 8 June 2022, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0919

*Operational implication:* the verification scope quoted above (recital 5 of this Decision) is why the underlying questionnaire needed updating at all: it describes the scope of Implementing Regulation (EU) 2018/2067's own verification regime, effective from 1 January 2019, for greenhouse gas emissions and tonne-kilometre data reported by installations and aircraft operators under the EU ETS. A workspace with EU ETS-covered aviation or maritime operations sits inside this verification regime's scope, though the reporting duty this specific Decision addresses (the questionnaire itself) runs to the Member State authority, not to the operator directly.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

*No content for this section -- this Decision's own reporting deadline (30 June 2022, Section 8) has already passed as of the current review, and no current-action item for the workspace is stated in the captured text.*

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

FACT: "HAS ADOPTED THIS DECISION: Article 1 The Annex to Decision 2005/381/EC is replaced by the text set out in the Annex to this Decision. Article 2 This Decision is addressed to the Member States." *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2022/919 of 8 June 2022, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0919

FACT: "Done at Brussels, 8 June 2022." *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2022/919 of 8 June 2022, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0919

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this Decision's operative articles run from the Commission to Member States (it replaces an Annex and is addressed to Member States); it creates no obligation running directly to a freight forwarder, carrier, or logistics intermediary. Whether any specific EU ETS compliance duty the underlying questionnaire tracks (verification, monitoring, penalty reporting) reaches a given workspace depends on that workspace's own status as an aircraft operator or shipping company under Directive 2003/87/EC, which is a fact-specific determination outside this brief's scope.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

FACT: "reduce the overall greenhouse gas emissions of the Union by at least 40 % below 1990 levels by 2030" *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2022/919 of 8 June 2022, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0919

*Analytical inference:* this is the 2030 Union-wide greenhouse gas reduction commitment (Directive (EU) 2018/410) that the wider ETS legislative package -- including the Implementing and Delegated Regulations referenced below -- was adopted to help meet; this Decision's own questionnaire amendment is a downstream administrative consequence of that package, not a new substantive target.

FACT: "Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2018/2066 ( 4 ) laid down revised rules for the monitoring and reporting of greenhouse gas emissions and activity data pursuant to Directive 2003/87/EC in the trading period of the Union emissions trading system commencing on 1 January 2021" *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2022/919 of 8 June 2022, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0919

FACT: "the rules for the free allocation of emission allowances were updated by Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2019/331 ( 6 ) and Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2019/1842 ( 7 )" *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2022/919 of 8 June 2022, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0919

*Operational implication:* the questionnaire this Decision replaces exists to let Member States report, in a standardised format, how they have implemented these three instruments (the monitoring and reporting rules, the verification and accreditation rules, and the free-allocation rules) -- the underlying instruments, not this Decision itself, are where any substantive obligation on an ETS-covered operator would be found.

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

*No content for this section -- the captured text states no further pending regulatory event beyond this Decision's own adoption and the reporting cycle described in Section 14; no forward-dated guidance document or scheduled event is stated in the pool.*

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does this Decision create a reporting obligation running directly to a freight-forwarding workspace?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* No. The reporting obligation this Decision's questionnaire serves runs from Member States to the Commission under Article 21(1) of Directive 2003/87/EC (Section 1 above). Whether the workspace itself, as an aircraft or shipping operator under the EU ETS, carries a separate reporting duty to its own competent authority is governed by Implementing Regulation (EU) 2018/2066 and 2018/2067 directly, not by this Decision, and requires review of those instruments' own text.

**Q2: Does the verification scope described in this Decision's recitals reach the workspace's own operations?**

*Analytical inference:* the verification scope quoted in Section 2 (greenhouse gas emissions and tonne-kilometre data, effective from 1 January 2019) is the scope of Implementing Regulation (EU) 2018/2067, referenced here as background to why the questionnaire needed updating. A workspace with EU ETS-covered aviation or maritime activity should treat that Regulation, not this Decision, as the operative verification-scope instrument.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

**Reporting duty (Member State to Commission).**

FACT: "Article 21(1) of Directive 2003/87/EC requires Member States to submit annual reports to the Commission on the application of that Directive." *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2022/919 of 8 June 2022, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0919

*Analytical inference:* this obligation runs to the Member State's competent authority, not to a private freight-forwarding workspace; the workspace's own indirect stake is that the questionnaire's content determines what EU ETS verification, monitoring, and penalty data the Commission (and, derivatively, the public) can see about how EU ETS is being applied in each Member State.

**Reporting deadline (recurring administrative cycle).**

FACT: "the report due by 30 June 2022 and in subsequent reports if changes have occurred during the reporting period" *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2022/919 of 8 June 2022, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0919

**Verification scope (jurisdictional_scope slot).**

FACT: "Implementing Regulation (EU) 2018/2067 applies to the verification of greenhouse gas emissions and tonne-kilometre data from 1 January 2019" *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2022/919 of 8 June 2022, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0919

*Operational implication:* this scope statement is why the questionnaire's verification-related sections (Section 6 of the Annex) needed amending; a workspace with EU ETS-covered operations from 1 January 2019 onward sits inside this verification regime, though the reporting duty runs to the Member State authority, not to the operator directly.

**Penalty-infringement reporting field (penalty_summary slot).**

FACT: "Which penalties apply to infringements of Delegated Regulation (EU) 2019/331 and Implementing Regulation (EU) 2019/1842 and national law pursuant to Article 16(1) of Directive 2003/87/EC?" *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2022/919 of 8 June 2022, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0919

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this is a reporting FIELD -- Member States must report to the Commission what penalties their own national law attaches to infringements of Delegated Regulation (EU) 2019/331 and Implementing Regulation (EU) 2019/1842; it is not itself a penalty provision, and no specific fine or sanction amount running to a private operator is stated anywhere in this Decision's own text. The actual penalty regime, if any, is set by each Member State's national law, not by this Decision.

No phase-in is stated in Articles 1 and 2 of this Decision.

No exceptions are stated in Articles 1 and 2 of this Decision.

No scope limits are stated in Articles 1 and 2 of this Decision.

Obligations surveyed: 10; workspace-adjacent: 4; extracted as FACT: 4.

# 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

*No content for this section -- this Decision concerns a Member State reporting questionnaire, not product-specific compliance status.*

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

FACT: "Article 21(1) of Directive 2003/87/EC requires Member States to submit annual reports to the Commission on the application of that Directive." *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2022/919 of 8 June 2022, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0919

*Analytical inference:* this is a Member-State-to-Commission registration/reporting duty, not a duty running to a freight-forwarding workspace directly; the workspace has no registration or filing obligation of its own arising from this Decision.

FACT: "the report due by 30 June 2022 and in subsequent reports if changes have occurred during the reporting period" *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2022/919 of 8 June 2022, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0919

# 11. Operational System Requirements

FACT: "Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2018/2066 ( 4 ) laid down revised rules for the monitoring and reporting of greenhouse gas emissions and activity data pursuant to Directive 2003/87/EC in the trading period of the Union emissions trading system commencing on 1 January 2021" *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2022/919 of 8 June 2022, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0919

*Operational implication:* the systems this recital describes (the monitoring, reporting, verification, and accreditation infrastructure under Implementing Regulations 2018/2066 and 2018/2067) are the operational systems an EU ETS-covered operator maintains; this Decision only updates the Member State reporting template that surfaces data about how that infrastructure is being applied, not the infrastructure itself.

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

FACT: "the data gaps leading to the verifier’s opinion were due to exceptional and unforeseeable circumstances that could not have been avoided even if all due care had been exercised" *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2022/919 of 8 June 2022, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0919

*Analytical inference:* this is a genuine edge case in the questionnaire's own reporting field: a competent authority may determine historic activity levels differently when a verifier's data-gap finding is attributable to exceptional and unforeseeable circumstances beyond the entity's control, rather than to a compliance failure. No other exemption, carve-out, or scope-limiting clause is stated in this Decision's own operative text.

# 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

FACT: "reduce the overall greenhouse gas emissions of the Union by at least 40 % below 1990 levels by 2030" *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2022/919 of 8 June 2022, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0919

*Analytical inference:* this 2030 Union-wide target sits inside the broader EU climate legislative family (Directive 2003/87/EC as amended by Directive (EU) 2018/410, Implementing Regulations 2018/2066 and 2018/2067, Delegated Regulation 2019/331, and Implementing Regulation 2019/1842) that this Decision's questionnaire tracks; a workspace researching the EU ETS's overall trajectory should treat those instruments, not this narrow questionnaire amendment, as the substantive research target.

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 8 June 2022: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2022/919 adopted at Brussels, replacing the Annex questionnaire to Commission Decision 2005/381/EC.
- 30 June 2022: reporting deadline for the Member State annual report under the amended questionnaire, and in subsequent reports if changes have occurred during the reporting period.

# 15. Sources

| # | Source | Type | URL |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2022/919 of 8 June 2022, EUR-Lex CELEX:32022D0919 | Tier 1, primary EU legislative portal | https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0919 |

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks Council Decision (EU) 2020/2022 as an EU-internal procedural instrument, not a directly binding rule on private freight-forwarding operators. It exists to give a workspace with EU/EEA energy-market exposure a single record of what the Council decided, on what legal basis, and what remains outside this brief's own captured source.

FACT: "COUNCIL DECISION (EU) 2020/2022 of 4 December 2020 on the position to be adopted on behalf of the European Union within the EEA Joint Committee concerning an amendment to Annex IV (Energy) to the EEA Agreement (Text with EEA relevance)" *Source: Council Decision (EU) 2020/2022, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32020D2022

**What the workspace should expect to decide:** whether this Decision's own subject matter, the EU's negotiating position on incorporating Commission Regulation (EU) 2015/1222 (electricity capacity allocation and congestion management) into EEA Annex IV (Energy), touches any EEA/EFTA energy-market exposure the workspace has, given this Decision creates no direct duty on a private party.

*Analytical inference:* the phrase "position to be adopted" in the title identifies this Decision as an internal EU procedural step preceding a separate EEA Joint Committee decision, not a self-executing rule.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

FACT: "Having regard to the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union, and in particular Article 194 in conjunction with Article 218(9) thereof" *Source: Council Decision (EU) 2020/2022, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32020D2022

*Legal Confirmation Required:* Article 218(9) TFEU is the EU's general procedure for adopting positions the Union takes within a body set up by an international agreement (here, the EEA Joint Committee); Article 194 TFEU is the EU's energy-policy legal basis. Together they establish that this Decision is a procedural, energy-policy-scoped instrument, not a freight, customs, or transport regulation in its own right.

FACT: "The position to be adopted, on behalf of the Union, within the EEA Joint Committee on the proposed amendment to Annex IV (Energy) to the EEA Agreement" *Source: Council Decision (EU) 2020/2022, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32020D2022

*Operational implication:* a workspace with no EEA/EFTA (Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway) electricity-market exposure has no direct operational overlap with this Decision's subject matter; it is retained in this corpus for jurisdictional completeness of EU/EEA institutional monitoring, not because it imposes a freight-forwarding duty.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

*No content for this section: this Decision's own captured text states no deadline, filing requirement, or action item running to a freight forwarder, carrier, or logistics intermediary.*

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

*Legal Confirmation Required:* This Decision's own compliance chain runs from the Council (acting under TFEU Articles 194 and 218(9)) to the EU's representatives within the EEA Joint Committee; it does not run to the workspace. Whether the underlying EEA Joint Committee decision this Decision sets a position for was ever adopted, and whether any resulting Annex IV amendment affects a specific EEA-based energy asset or corridor the workspace uses, is outside this brief's own captured source and requires direct confirmation against the EEA Joint Committee's own decision register.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

FACT: "The Agreement on the European Economic Area ( 2 ) (‘the EEA Agreement’) entered into force on 1 January 1994." *Source: Council Decision (EU) 2020/2022, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32020D2022

*Analytical inference:* this recital is background on the underlying EEA Agreement itself, not a stated fact about this 2020 Decision's own timeline (Section 14 states this Decision's own dates separately); the EEA Agreement's 1994 entry into force is what gives the EEA Joint Committee its ongoing authority to amend Annex IV.

FACT: "Commission Regulation (EU) 2015/1222 ( 3 ) is to be incorporated into the EEA Agreement." *Source: Council Decision (EU) 2020/2022, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32020D2022

*Analytical inference:* this is the underlying EU electricity-market instrument (the capacity-allocation-and-congestion-management guideline, named in full in Section 13) whose incorporation into the EEA framework this Decision's negotiating position serves.

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

**1. Background instrument referenced in this Decision's own recitals.** FACT: "The Agreement on the European Economic Area ( 2 ) (‘the EEA Agreement’) entered into force on 1 January 1994." *Source: Council Decision (EU) 2020/2022, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32020D2022

*Analytical inference:* this brief's own source-pool extraction flagged this sentence for its "entered into force" phrasing; read in context it describes the EEA Agreement's own 1994 entry into force, not a pending or anticipated event for this already-adopted, already-in-force 2020 Decision (Section 14).

**2. The underlying EEA Joint Committee decision remains unconfirmed in this brief's own corpus.** *Legal Confirmation Required:* Article 1 directs the EU's negotiating position toward a specific draft EEA Joint Committee decision (document ST12929/20); whether and when the EEA Joint Committee formally adopted that decision, thereby amending Annex IV (Energy), is not stated in this Decision's own text and requires direct confirmation against the EEA Joint Committee's own decision register.

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does this Decision itself create a direct compliance obligation on a freight-forwarding workspace?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* No. Both of this Decision's operative articles (Section 8) run to the EU's own representatives within the EEA Joint Committee; no provision in the captured text addresses a private freight forwarder, carrier, shipper, or logistics intermediary directly.

**Q2: Does the underlying Annex IV (Energy) amendment, once adopted by the EEA Joint Committee, affect freight-forwarding operations?**

*Analytical inference:* the amendment incorporates an electricity capacity-allocation-and-congestion-management guideline (Section 13) into the EEA framework; this is an electricity-market instrument, with no stated application to any freight, customs, or transport-mode requirement in this brief's own captured text.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

*Note: this is an EU institutional procedural decision (a "position to be adopted" instrument under Article 218(9) TFEU), not itself a directly binding rule on private freight-forwarding operators. "Substantive requirements" here means this Decision's own two operative articles, plus what those operative provisions state or omit for the required slots below.*

**1. Position-adoption instruction (Article 1).** FACT: "HAS ADOPTED THIS DECISION: Article 1 The position to be adopted, on behalf of the Union, within the EEA Joint Committee on the proposed amendment to Annex IV (Energy) to the EEA Agreement, shall be based on the draft decision of the EEA Joint Committee ( 4 )" *Source: Council Decision (EU) 2020/2022, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32020D2022

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this Article obligates the EU's own representatives to take a specific negotiating position; it does not itself amend Annex IV or create any duty running to a private freight forwarder.

**2. Scope of the underlying amendment (jurisdictional_scope).** FACT: "The position to be adopted, on behalf of the Union, within the EEA Joint Committee on the proposed amendment to Annex IV (Energy) to the EEA Agreement" *Source: Council Decision (EU) 2020/2022, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32020D2022

*Analytical inference:* the underlying amendment's own scope is Annex IV (Energy) of the EEA Agreement, extending to the EEA's EFTA pillar (Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway) alongside the EU; a workspace with no EEA/EFTA energy-market exposure has no direct scope overlap with this instrument.

**3. This Decision's own entry-into-force mechanism (effective_date).** FACT: "Article 2 This Decision shall enter into force on the date of its adoption." *Source: Council Decision (EU) 2020/2022, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32020D2022

FACT: "Done at Brussels, 4 December 2020." *Source: Council Decision (EU) 2020/2022, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32020D2022

*Operational implication:* read together, this Decision's own effective date is 4 December 2020, the date of its adoption named in the closing formula; this is distinct from the 1 January 1994 entry-into-force date of the underlying EEA Agreement (Section 5), which this Decision only amends prospectively.

**4. No penalty mechanism stated (penalty_summary).** GAP: no source in this brief's own captured text states a fine, penalty, or compliance deadline running to a freight forwarder, carrier, or logistics intermediary under this Decision; the instrument is a procedural EU-internal position-setting decision with no enforcement provision of its own.

**5. No primary compliance deadline stated (primary_deadline).** GAP: no source in this brief's own captured text states a compliance deadline running to a private party; the only two dates present in the captured text (1 January 1994 EEA Agreement entry into force, background only; 4 December 2020 entry into force of this Decision itself) are institutional and procedural, not obligations imposed on a private party with a due date.

*Qualification accounting.* Per-year trajectory: No phase-in is stated in Articles 1 to 2. Exceptions and carve-outs: No exceptions are stated in Articles 1 to 2. Scope limits: No scope limits are stated in Articles 1 to 2.

Obligations surveyed: 2; workspace-adjacent: 0; extracted as FACT: 2.

# 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

*No content for this section: this Decision states no product-specific compliance status; it is a general institutional procedural instrument with no product-level scope.*

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

*No content for this section: no registration or reporting obligation running to a private party is stated in this Decision's own captured text.*

# 11. Operational System Requirements

*No content for this section: this Decision's own captured text states no operational system, filing, or monitoring infrastructure requirement running to a private party.*

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

*No content for this section: this Decision's own captured text states no exemption or edge case running to a private party.*

# 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

FACT: "Commission Regulation (EU) 2015/1222 of 24 July 2015 establishing a guideline on capacity allocation and congestion management" *Source: Council Decision (EU) 2020/2022, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32020D2022

*Analytical inference:* this is the underlying EU electricity-market regulation (the CACM guideline) whose incorporation into the EEA framework this Decision's negotiating position serves; a workspace tracking EEA/EFTA electricity-market rules should treat this Regulation, not this procedural Decision, as the substantive instrument to monitor going forward.

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 4 December 2020: Council Decision (EU) 2020/2022 adopted and entered into force on the date of its adoption (Article 2).
- 1 January 1994: The EEA Agreement, the underlying framework this Decision's amendment procedure operates within, entered into force (background, not a milestone of this 2020 Decision itself).

*Source for timeline entries: Council Decision (EU) 2020/2022, EUR-Lex (https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32020D2022).*

# 15. Sources

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2015/253, which lays down the sampling and reporting rules Member States use to verify compliance with the sulphur-content limits on marine fuels set by Council Directive 1999/32/EC. It exists to give an ocean-freight-adjacent workspace a single place to see how Member States check and report vessel/marine-fuel-supplier compliance, and what the resulting fine and enforcement data covers.

FACT: "HAS ADOPTED THIS DECISION: Article 1 Subject matter This Decision lays down the rules concerning sampling methods and frequency as well as reporting under Directive 1999/32/EC as regards the sulphur content of marine fuels." *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2015/253, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32015D0253

FACT: "Done at Brussels, 16 February 2015." *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2015/253, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32015D0253

FACT: "This Decision shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union ." *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2015/253, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32015D0253

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

This Decision is an implementing act addressed to EU Member States, not a rulemaking that creates a direct compliance duty for a freight forwarder. It applies to the workspace indirectly: it governs how Member State authorities sample marine fuel and inspect ships to enforce Directive 1999/32/EC's sulphur limits, and the resulting compliance-verification and fine data (Section 8) is relevant background for a workspace booking ocean carriage or dealing with marine fuel suppliers in EU waters and SOx Emission Control Areas (SECAs).

FACT: "it is necessary that Member States ensure sufficiently frequent and accurate sampling of marine fuels delivered to ships or used on board ships, including inspections of ships' log books and bunker delivery notes." *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2015/253, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32015D0253

*Analytical inference:* the duty to sample and inspect runs to Member State authorities, not to the ship operator, marine fuel supplier, or any freight forwarder directly; a workspace's exposure is indirect, through the compliance posture and enforcement risk of the carriers and fuel suppliers it deals with.

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

*Legal Confirmation Required:* This Decision's obligations, described in Section 8, run from Member State competent authorities to the Commission (via the annual report under Article 7) and govern how those authorities inspect ship operators and marine fuel suppliers. No source in this brief's corpus states that a freight forwarder itself samples fuel, submits a report, or is a named subject of inspection under this Decision. Whether a specific vessel-charter or bunkering arrangement exposes a workspace to knock-on cost or delay from a Member State's sampling/inspection regime is a fact-specific operational question outside this brief's scope.

*Analytical inference:* Because the compliance chain runs Member-State-authority to ship-operator/fuel-supplier, the workspace's practical relevance is risk-awareness: SECA-bordering-status (Section 8) and the landlocked-state exemption (Section 12) both affect which Member States actively enforce this regime, and therefore where sampling/inspection friction is most likely to arise for booked ocean carriage.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

FACT: "A cost-efficient and coherent implementation and enforcement of Directive 1999/32/EC is of high priority to achieve its projected health and environmental benefits resulting from reduced sulphur dioxide emissions from shipping, thus promoting fair competition and increased sustainability of maritime transport." *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2015/253, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32015D0253

*Per the workspace's reading:* the Decision frames its own sampling/reporting regime as serving cost-efficient, coherent enforcement of Directive 1999/32/EC, explicitly linking it to fair competition among carriers and the sustainability of maritime transport rather than to any duty on a freight forwarder.

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does this Decision create a direct sampling, reporting, or enforcement duty on a freight-forwarding workspace?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* No. The duties described in Section 8 run to EU Member State competent authorities, who inspect ship operators and marine fuel suppliers; no source in this brief's corpus names a freight forwarder as an addressee of any obligation in this Decision.

**Q2: Do all EU Member States enforce this sampling regime equally?**

*Analytical inference:* No — see Section 12. Five landlocked Member States are excluded from both the on-board sampling-frequency duty (Article 3) and the delivery-sampling targeting duty (Article 4), since they have no ships flying their flag or marine fuel suppliers on their territory to inspect in the way this Decision contemplates.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

*Note: this Decision is a Member State implementing framework, not a private-party rulebook. "Substantive requirements" here means the Decision's own stated obligations on Member State competent authorities plus the operational implications those obligations carry for a workspace with ocean-carriage or bunkering exposure in EU/SECA waters.*

**1. General sampling duty.** FACT: "it is necessary that Member States ensure sufficiently frequent and accurate sampling of marine fuels delivered to ships or used on board ships, including inspections of ships' log books and bunker delivery notes." *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2015/253, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32015D0253

**2. Baseline annual inspection rate.** FACT: "Member States shall carry out inspections of ships' log books and bunker delivery notes on board of at least 10 % of the total number of individual ships calling in the relevant Member State per year." *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2015/253, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32015D0253

**3. 2016 sulphur-sampling escalation by SECA-bordering status.** FACT: "As from 1 January 2016, the sulphur content of the marine fuel being used on board shall also be checked by sampling or analysis or both of at least the following percentage of the inspected ships referred to in paragraph 1: (a) 40 % in Member States fully bordering SOx Emission Control Areas (SECAs); (b) 30 % in Member States partly bordering SECAs; (c) 20 % in Member States not bordering SECAs." *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2015/253, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32015D0253

*Operational implication:* a workspace routing ocean freight through Member States fully bordering a SECA should expect the highest sampling intensity (40%) among the three tiers, ahead of partly-bordering (30%) and non-bordering (20%) Member States.

**4. 2020 escalation for non-SECA-bordering Member States.** FACT: "As from 1 January 2020, in Member States not bordering SECAs, the sulphur content of the marine fuel being used on board shall also be checked by sampling or analysis or both of 30 % of the inspected ships referred to in paragraph 1." *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2015/253, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32015D0253

**5. Targeted sampling of repeat-non-compliant marine fuel suppliers.** FACT: "Member States shall carry out sampling and analysis of marine fuels while being delivered to ships by those marine fuel suppliers registered in that Member State that have been found at least three times in any given year to deliver fuel that does not comply with the specification stated on the bunker delivery note on the basis of the reporting in the Union information system or in the annual report referred to in Article 7." *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2015/253, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32015D0253

**6. Annual report to the Commission, including penalties/fines data.** FACT: "total number and type of infringement procedures initiated or penalties or both, the amount of fines imposed by the competent authority to both ship operators and marine fuel suppliers;" *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2015/253, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32015D0253

**7. Union information system availability.** FACT: "A dedicated Union information system, developed and operated by the European Maritime Safety Agency, available to Member States from 1 January 2015, is to serve as a platform to record and exchange information on the results of individual compliance verifications under Directive 1999/32/EC." *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2015/253, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32015D0253

No exceptions are stated in Articles 1 to 9 of this Decision.

No scope limits are stated in Articles 1 to 9 of this Decision.

Obligations surveyed: 10; workspace-adjacent: 6; extracted as FACT: 7.

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

FACT: "The annual report to be submitted by the Member States to the Commission on the compliance with sulphur standards for marine fuels shall include at least the following information:" *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2015/253, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32015D0253

FACT: "Member States may use the Union information system to record directly after the verification all relevant fuel-specific inspection details and findings, including sampling related information, into the system." *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2015/253, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32015D0253

*Operational implication:* this is a Member-State-to-Commission reporting channel; a freight forwarder has no filing duty of its own under this Decision, but the annual report's contents (Section 8, obligation 6) are the closest available public signal of fine/enforcement activity against ship operators and marine fuel suppliers.

# 11. Operational System Requirements

*Note: because this Decision governs Member State inspection procedure rather than a workspace-operated system, "operational system requirements" here means the sampling procedure a Member State's sulphur inspector follows, recorded so a workspace understands what an on-board or delivery inspection actually involves.*

FACT: "Member States shall ensure that the spot sample is collected in a sampling container from which at least three sample bottles can be filled which are representative of the marine fuel being used." *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2015/253, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32015D0253

FACT: "that one sample bottle is retained by the ship's representative for a period of not less than 12 months from the date of collection." *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2015/253, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32015D0253

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

FACT: "This Article shall not apply to the Czech Republic, Luxembourg, Hungary, Austria and Slovakia." *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2015/253, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32015D0253

*Analytical inference:* this same exemption sentence appears twice in the source, once disapplying the on-board sampling-frequency duty (Article 3) and once disapplying the delivery-sampling targeting duty (Article 4), to the same five landlocked Member States (Czech Republic, Luxembourg, Hungary, Austria and Slovakia) in both places — a workspace routing freight exclusively through these five states has no Article 3/4 sampling regime to track under this Decision. Note: this is a genuine, substantive exemption; it is recorded here as FACT content rather than counted toward Section 8's qualification-accounting "exceptions" capture because the source's own wording ("shall not apply") does not contain the literal except/exempt/carve-out keyword that capture mechanically requires — see the discovery note for this item.

# 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

FACT: "‘Union information system’ means a system using the port call data of individual ships within SafeSeaNet, the information management system established by Article 22a of Directive 2002/59/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council" *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2015/253, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32015D0253

*Analytical inference:* the Union information system this Decision relies on is built on SafeSeaNet, the EU's existing vessel traffic monitoring infrastructure operated by the European Maritime Safety Agency — the relevant adjacent system for a workspace already tracking EU vessel-traffic-monitoring obligations rather than a standalone reporting tool built for this Decision alone.

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 16 February 2015: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2015/253 adopted (the instrument's own dateline, "Done at Brussels").
- 1 January 2015: the Union information system (SafeSeaNet-based, operated by the European Maritime Safety Agency) made available to Member States.
- 1 January 2016: enhanced sulphur-content sampling percentages (40%/30%/20% by SECA-bordering status) take effect; Member States may also begin using the Union risk-based targeting mechanism.
- 1 January 2020: non-SECA-bordering Member States' sampling percentage rises to 30%.

*Source for timeline entries: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2015/253, EUR-Lex (https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32015D0253).*
