entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks Commission Regulation (EU) No 412/2012, a REACH Annex XVII restriction on dimethylfumarate (DMF) in articles, and gives a freight-forwarding workspace handling furniture or footwear shipments a single place to see what is prohibited, when the prohibition took effect, and which Member States it binds.

FACT: "COMMISSION REGULATION (EU) No 412/2012 of 15 May 2012 amending Annex XVII to Regulation (EC) No 1907/2006 of the European Parliament and of the Council on the Registration, Evaluation, Authorisation and Restriction of Chemicals (REACH) (Text with EEA relevance)" *Source: EUR-Lex, Commission Regulation (EU) No 412/2012 (CELEX 32012R0412). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32012R0412*

FACT: "Furniture and footwear available on the market in several Member States have been identified as the cause of damage to the health of consumers in France, Poland, Finland, Sweden and the United Kingdom." *Source: EUR-Lex, Commission Regulation (EU) No 412/2012 (CELEX 32012R0412). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32012R0412*

*Operational implication:* a workspace forwarding, clearing, or warehousing furniture or footwear consignments moving into or within the EU should treat DMF content as a customs and market-access risk factor for those product categories specifically, not for freight generally.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

FACT: "DMF was most often contained in little pouches fixed inside the furniture or added to the footwear boxes." *Source: EUR-Lex, Commission Regulation (EU) No 412/2012 (CELEX 32012R0412). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32012R0412*

*Analytical inference:* because DMF was used as an anti-mould treatment inside packaging and product pouches rather than as a visible additive, a workspace cannot verify compliance by visual inspection alone; the obligation runs to the article's own composition, which is a manufacturer/importer disclosure and testing question, not a freight-handling one.

FACT: "This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States." *Source: EUR-Lex, Commission Regulation (EU) No 412/2012 (CELEX 32012R0412). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32012R0412*

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

FACT: "This Regulation shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union" *Source: EUR-Lex, Commission Regulation (EU) No 412/2012 (CELEX 32012R0412). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32012R0412*

*Operational implication:* the prohibition in Section 8 has already been binding since the twentieth day after this Regulation's Official Journal publication; there is no future compliance date for a workspace to calendar, only the standing bar on DMF-containing furniture and footwear articles above the stated concentration.

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

FACT: "the Commission has adopted Decision 2009/251/EC of 17 March 2009 requiring Member States to ensure that products containing the biocide dimethylfumarate are not placed or made available on the market" *Source: EUR-Lex, Commission Regulation (EU) No 412/2012 (CELEX 32012R0412). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32012R0412*

FACT: "The prohibition provided by Decision 2009/251/EC was subsequently prolonged by Commission Decision 2010/153/EU" *Source: EUR-Lex, Commission Regulation (EU) No 412/2012 (CELEX 32012R0412). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32012R0412*

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this Regulation replaced a series of Member-State-directed emergency Decisions with a single, permanent, directly applicable EU restriction; whether a specific consignment's own DMF content and concentration triggers the Annex 61 prohibition is a product-testing question for the manufacturer, importer, or brand owner, not a determination this brief's captured text supports for any specific shipment.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

FACT: "if a Member State considers that the manufacture, placing on the market or use of a substance on its own, in a mixture or in an article poses a risk to human health or the environment that is not adequately controlled and needs to be addressed, it shall prepare a dossier after notifying that intention to the European Chemicals Agency (the Agency)." *Source: EUR-Lex, Commission Regulation (EU) No 412/2012 (CELEX 32012R0412). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32012R0412*

*Per the workspace's reading:* this is the REACH Article 68(1) mechanism France used to initiate this specific restriction; it is a Member State's own procedural duty toward the European Chemicals Agency, not an obligation running to a freight-forwarding workspace.

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does this Regulation impose a duty on freight forwarders as such?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* No provision in this captured text names freight forwarders, carriers, or customs brokers as a duty-holder class. The Annex 61 prohibitions (Section 8) are framed as objective bars on the article itself ("shall not be used," "shall not be placed on the market") rather than obligations naming a specific commercial role; whether a specific workspace's own handling of a DMF-affected shipment creates exposure under national enforcement of this Regulation is outside this brief's scope.

**Q2: Does the prohibition apply uniformly across the EU, or does it vary by Member State?**

*Analytical inference:* uniformly. Obligation 4 in Section 8 states the Regulation is binding in its entirety and directly applicable in every Member State, meaning no national transposition step is expected to vary its substantive scope.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

**1. DMF use prohibition (Annex XVII entry 61).** FACT: "Shall not be used in articles or any parts thereof in concentrations greater than 0,1 mg/kg." *Source: EUR-Lex, Commission Regulation (EU) No 412/2012 (CELEX 32012R0412). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32012R0412*

**2. DMF market-placement prohibition (Annex XVII entry 61).** FACT: "Articles or any parts thereof containing DMF in concentrations greater than 0,1 mg/kg shall not be placed on the market." *Source: EUR-Lex, Commission Regulation (EU) No 412/2012 (CELEX 32012R0412). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32012R0412*

*Operational implication:* obligation 2 is the provision most directly relevant to a freight forwarder's own customs and market-access exposure, since it bars placing the affected article on the EU market at all, independent of who placed it there.

**3. Amendment mechanism incorporating the prohibitions.** FACT: "Annex XVII to Regulation (EC) No 1907/2006 is amended in accordance with the Annex to this Regulation." *Source: EUR-Lex, Commission Regulation (EU) No 412/2012 (CELEX 32012R0412). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32012R0412*

**4. EU-wide direct applicability.** FACT: "This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States." *Source: EUR-Lex, Commission Regulation (EU) No 412/2012 (CELEX 32012R0412). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32012R0412*

**5. Entry-into-force timing.** FACT: "This Regulation shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union" *Source: EUR-Lex, Commission Regulation (EU) No 412/2012 (CELEX 32012R0412). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32012R0412*

*Legal Confirmation Required:* No verbatim compliance deadline distinct from the Regulation's own entry-into-force date (Article 2) is stated in the captured source text; the DMF use and market-placement prohibitions (Section 8) bind immediately on entry into force, with no separate phase-in or compliance-by date named.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* No verbatim penalty, fine, or enforcement-consequence statement is located in the captured source text; this Regulation states the substantive prohibition itself (Section 8) but leaves enforcement and penalties to Member States' own national regimes, which this instrument's own text does not restate.

**Qualification accounting.** Per-year trajectory: No phase-in is stated in Articles 1 to 2 and the Annex of this Regulation. Exceptions and carve-outs: No exceptions are stated in Articles 1 to 2 and the Annex of this Regulation. Scope limits: No scope limits are stated in Articles 1 to 2 and the Annex of this Regulation.

Obligations surveyed: 6; workspace-adjacent: 5; extracted as FACT: 5.

Shortfall: none -- K equals M, and the 6,607-character pool is well under the 200,000-character large-pool threshold, so the forced five-claim floor does not apply; the one surveyed-but-excluded item is the REACH Article 68(1) dossier-preparation mechanism (Section 5), which is a Member State's own procedural duty toward the European Chemicals Agency, not an obligation adjacent to freight-forwarding operations.

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 17 March 2009: Commission Decision 2009/251/EC adopted, the predecessor emergency measure on DMF-containing products.
- 15 May 2012: Commission Regulation (EU) No 412/2012 adopted.
- 16 May 2012: Published in the Official Journal of the European Union (L 128/1).
- Twentieth day following publication: This Regulation's Annex XVII DMF prohibitions (Section 8) enter into force.

*Source for timeline entries: EUR-Lex, Commission Regulation (EU) No 412/2012 (https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32012R0412).*

# 15. Sources

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks a short, single-purpose EU Decision, Decision No 1359/2013/EU, which amends one provision of the EU Emissions Trading System's founding Directive (2003/87/EC) to give the European Commission a one-time, capped power to adjust the timing of greenhouse gas allowance auctions. It exists to give a freight forwarder with EU ETS exposure a single place to see what this Decision changes, who it binds, and what the captured text genuinely does and does not state.

FACT: "DECISION No 1359/2013/EU OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL of 17 December 2013 amending Directive 2003/87/EC clarifying provisions on the timing of auctions of greenhouse gas allowances" *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX 32013D1359. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32013D1359

FACT: "19.12.2013 EN Official Journal of the European Union L 343/1" *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX 32013D1359. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32013D1359

FACT: "Done at Brussels, 17 December 2013." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX 32013D1359. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32013D1359

**What the workspace should expect to decide:** whether the workspace, or a client whose cargo the workspace moves, itself holds or trades EU ETS allowances, since only such a party is materially affected by the auction-timetable mechanism described in Section 8.

*Analytical inference:* this Decision's own title and dates identify it as the historical 2013 legal basis for what the market later called "backloading" of EU ETS auction volumes; it was adopted and published in December 2013, over a decade before this brief's own export date.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

This Decision amends Article 10(4) of Directive 2003/87/EC, the founding EU ETS Directive, not the Directive's own coverage of installations or aircraft operators.

FACT: "Directive 2003/87/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council of 13 October 2003 establishing a scheme for greenhouse gas emission allowance trading within the Community and amending Council Directive 96/61/EC" *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX 32013D1359, footnote 3. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32013D1359

*Operational implication:* a freight forwarder applies to this Decision only to the extent it, or an installation or aircraft operator in its chain, is itself covered by Directive 2003/87/EC and participates in EU ETS allowance auctions; a freight-forwarding intermediary with no EU ETS obligations of its own is not itself bound by this Decision.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

*Analytical inference:* this Decision has no forward-looking action item as of the export date; it authorised a single, already-exercised adjustment power for the European Commission over a decade ago, and the captured text states no ongoing or recurring duty running to a private party.

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this Decision does not itself address freight forwarders. FACT: "This Decision is addressed to the Member States." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX 32013D1359, Article 2. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32013D1359

*Analytical inference:* any effect on a private party flows through a Member State's own implementation of the EU ETS auction platform under the amended Article 10(4), not directly from this Decision's own text.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

*Per the workspace's reading:* the controlling instrument for a workspace's own EU ETS obligations is Directive 2003/87/EC itself (footnote 3, Section 2), not this amending Decision; this Decision only clarifies one narrow point, the Commission's power to adapt the auction timetable, within that Directive.

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

*Analytical inference:* no forward events are recorded for this item in the export this brief was authored from, and the captured text states no scheduled future event of its own; the one-time adaptation power this Decision grants (Section 8) was already available for exercise as of this Decision's own 2013 adoption.

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does this Decision itself create a compliance duty on freight forwarders?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* No. It is addressed to the Member States (Section 4) and amends a power held by the European Commission; it does not itself name or bind a freight-forwarding intermediary.

**Q2: Does the captured text state a deadline, fine, or effective date a workspace should calendar?**

*Analytical inference:* No. The captured 2,673-character text states no primary deadline, penalty, or entry-into-force clause of its own; these three required slots are recorded as genuine gaps in Section 8, not omissions.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

*Note: this is a short, single-purpose amending Decision. "Substantive requirements" here means the three obligation-shaped statements the captured text itself contains: the Commission's own auction-timetable adaptation power, the one-time cap on its use, and the Decision's own addressee scope.*

**1. Auction-timetable adaptation power.** FACT: "Where an assessment shows for the individual industrial sectors that no significant impact on sectors or subsectors exposed to a significant risk of carbon leakage is to be expected, the Commission may, in exceptional circumstances, adapt the timetable for the period referred to in Article 13(1) beginning on 1 January 2013 so as to ensure the orderly functioning of the market." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX 32013D1359, Article 1. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32013D1359

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this power runs to the European Commission, exercisable only after the stated carbon-leakage assessment; it does not itself bind a freight forwarder, though its exercise can shift EU ETS allowance auction volumes a workspace's own carbon-exposed clients rely on for planning.

**2. One-time, numerically capped exercise.** FACT: "The Commission shall make no more than one such adaptation for a maximum number of 900 million allowances." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX 32013D1359, Article 1. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32013D1359

*Operational implication:* a workspace tracking EU ETS market conditions should treat this as a historical, already-exhausted ceiling (one adaptation, 900 million allowances) rather than a recurring or renewable power.

**3. Addressee and jurisdictional scope.** FACT: "This Decision is addressed to the Member States." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX 32013D1359, Article 2. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32013D1359

*Analytical inference:* the Decision's own binding force runs to the 27 (at the time, 28) EU Member States as a class, not to private undertakings; a workspace's own EU ETS exposure runs instead through Directive 2003/87/EC itself (Section 2), as implemented by each Member State.

**Qualification accounting.** Per-year trajectory: no phase-in is stated anywhere in this Decision's own two operative Articles; No phase-in is stated in Articles 1 to 2 of this Decision. Exceptions and carve-outs: no exception or carve-out language is stated; No exceptions are stated in Articles 1 to 2 of this Decision. Scope limits: no scope-limiting language beyond the addressee statement above is stated; No scope limits are stated in Articles 1 to 2 of this Decision.

Obligations surveyed: 3; workspace-adjacent: 3; extracted as FACT: 3.

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 17th December 2013: Decision No 1359/2013/EU adopted.
- 19th December 2013: Decision published in the Official Journal of the European Union, L 343/1.

*Source for timeline entries: EUR-Lex, CELEX 32013D1359 (https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32013D1359).*

# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks Commission Regulation (EC) No 729/2009, an EU act that enters a single food product name into the register of protected designations of origin and protected geographical indications. It exists to give a workspace that handles, trades, or transports goods bearing a protected geographical indication (PGI) a record of this specific registration and the EU-wide legal effect it carries.

FACT: "COMMISSION REGULATION (EC) No 729/2009 of 10 August 2009 entering a name in the register of protected designations of origin and protected geographical indications (Ciauscolo (PGI))" *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32009R0729*

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to a Workspace Handling Protected-Name Goods

FACT: "Having regard to Council Regulation (EC) No 510/2006 of 20 March 2006 on the protection of geographical indications and designations of origin for agricultural products and foodstuffs" *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32009R0729*

FACT: "and in particular the first subparagraph of Article 7(4) thereof" *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32009R0729*

FACT: "shall enter into force on the 20th day following its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union" *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32009R0729*

*Analytical inference:* this Regulation is a single-product implementing act under the horizontal PGI protection framework (Regulation (EC) No 510/2006); it does not itself restate that framework's own duties (for example, restrictions on using the protected name for non-conforming products), which are not present in this captured text.

*Operational implication:* a workspace that trades in or transports "Ciauscolo" (an Italian cooked/salted/smoked meat product, see Section 9) should treat this Regulation as the authoritative confirmation that the name carries PGI protection EU-wide, not as a source of its own separate compliance duties.

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this Regulation's own text creates no direct duty running to a freight forwarder, distributor, or other private operator; its only operative effects are entering the name in the Commission's register (Section 8, obligation 1) and making the resulting protection binding and directly applicable across Member States (Section 8, obligation 2). Any duty to avoid marketing a non-conforming product under the protected name arises under Regulation (EC) No 510/2006 itself, which is not captured in this pool; a workspace with a specific labeling or marketing question should confirm current status directly against that framework Regulation.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

FACT: "Pursuant to the first subparagraph of Article 6(2) of Regulation (EC) No 510/2006, Italy’s application to register the name ‘Ciauscolo’ was published in the Official Journal of the European Union" *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32009R0729*

FACT: "As no statement of objection under Article 7 of Regulation (EC) No 510/2006 has been received by the Commission, this name should be entered in the register" *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32009R0729*

*Analytical inference:* these two recitals together show the registration was uncontested (no statement of objection was received under Article 7 of Regulation (EC) No 510/2006), which is why the Commission adopted the entry without further procedural steps appearing in this text.

FACT: "OJ L 93, 31.3.2006, p. 12 ." *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32009R0729*

FACT: "OJ C 328, 23.12.2008, p. 38 ." *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32009R0729*

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does the workspace handle, transport, or trade in a product marketed under the name "Ciauscolo"?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this captured text confirms the name's protected status and its product class (Section 9) but does not itself state labeling, marketing, or transport-handling duties for a workspace; a workspace with an actual "Ciauscolo" shipment should confirm current PGI-compliance requirements against Regulation (EC) No 510/2006 directly.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

*Note: this is a single-product registration act, not a scheme creating ongoing operational duties. "Substantive requirements" here means this Regulation's own two operative Articles, both of which are administrative/legal-effect provisions rather than a compliance checklist.*

**1. Registration effect.** FACT: "The name contained in the Annex to this Regulation is hereby entered in the register." *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32009R0729*

*Analytical inference:* this obligation runs to the Commission's own register, not to any private party; a workspace has no filing or registration action of its own to take under this Article.

**2. Binding, directly applicable, EU-wide legal effect.** FACT: "This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States." *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32009R0729*

*Operational implication:* because this Regulation is directly applicable in all Member States, the "Ciauscolo" PGI protection applies uniformly across the EU without requiring separate national implementing measures; a workspace moving this product between Member States faces the same protected-name status in each.

No phase-in is stated in Articles 1 to 2.

No exceptions are stated in Articles 1 to 2.

No scope limits are stated in Articles 1 to 2.

Obligations surveyed: 2; workspace-adjacent: 2; extracted as FACT: 2.

# 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

FACT: "Agricultural products intended for human consumption listed in Annex I to the Treaty: Class 1.2. — Meat products (cooked, salted, smoked, etc.) ITALY Ciauscolo (PGI)" *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32009R0729*

*Operational implication:* "Ciauscolo" is registered under product Class 1.2 (meat products: cooked, salted, smoked, etc.), originating in Italy; a workspace's shipment documentation for this product should reflect the protected name and its Italian origin designation.

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 10 August 2009: Regulation adopted (Done at Brussels), entering the name Ciauscolo in the PGI register.

FACT: "Done at Brussels, 10 August 2009." *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32009R0729*

*Source for timeline entries: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32009R0729*

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks Regulation (EU) 2021/1056, which establishes the Just Transition Fund (JTF), an EU cohesion-policy fund supporting territories and workers affected by the transition to a climate-neutral economy. It exists to give a freight forwarder with EU exposure a record of what this Regulation funds, what it excludes, and whether it creates any direct duty on a private freight-forwarding workspace.

FACT: "The JTF shall support the Investment for jobs and growth goal in all Member States." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2021/1056. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32021R1056

*Analytical inference:* this Regulation is primarily a funding instrument administered through Member States and the Commission; its relevance to the workspace is as a potential funding source (if the workspace is an eligible SME in an affected territory) and as an exclusion (if the workspace's activities involve fossil fuel transport, storage, or distribution), not as a standalone compliance obligation.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

FACT: "The JTF shall support the Investment for jobs and growth goal in all Member States." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2021/1056. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32021R1056

*Operational implication:* a freight-forwarding workspace operating as an SME in a territory covered by an approved territorial just transition plan may be an eligible beneficiary of JTF support for eligible activities such as local transport decarbonisation; conversely, a workspace whose activities involve fossil fuel production, processing, transport, distribution, storage, or combustion is explicitly excluded from JTF support for those activities (see Section 8, obligation 5, and Section 12).

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

*No content for this section: the only date-bound obligation in the captured text, Article 14's 30 June 2025 review deadline, is a Commission-facing deadline that has already passed as of this brief's authoring date; no other immediate action item running to a private freight-forwarding workspace is stated.*

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

FACT: "This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2021/1056. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32021R1056

*Analytical inference:* as a directly applicable EU Regulation, this instrument requires no national transposition; even so, its own operative provisions administer funding through Member States and approved territorial just transition plans (Article 11), not through direct obligations on private freight-forwarding operators. A workspace's own compliance chain runs through applying to a Member State's JTF-funded programme as a beneficiary, not through a duty this Regulation imposes on it directly.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

*No content for this section: this Regulation does not incorporate a separate authoritative guidance document beyond its own text and the cross-referenced companion Regulations (EU) 2021/1057, (EU) 2021/1058 and (EU) 2021/1060, none of which the captured pool includes.*

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

FACT: "By 30 June 2025, the Commission shall review the implementation of the JTF with regard to the specific objective set out in Article 2" *Source: Regulation (EU) 2021/1056. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32021R1056

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this review deadline, 30 June 2025, has already passed as of this brief's authoring date; this brief's own captured pool does not include the Commission's resulting report, so whether the review changed the JTF's implementation is a separate, fact-specific question requiring a check of the Commission's own published review report.

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does this Regulation create a direct funding-exclusion or funding-eligibility fact relevant to a freight-forwarding workspace?**

FACT: "(d) investment related to the production, processing, transport, distribution, storage or combustion of fossil fuels." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2021/1056. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32021R1056

*Operational implication:* a workspace whose own operations involve fossil fuel transport, distribution, or storage is excluded from JTF support for those specific activities; a workspace seeking JTF support for local transport decarbonisation investments (Section 8, obligation 4) is not affected by this exclusion.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

*Note: this Regulation is primarily an EU cohesion-policy funding instrument. "Substantive requirements" below means the Regulation's own stated funding parameters, eligibility rules, and exclusions, several of which are directly relevant to a freight-forwarding workspace as a potential JTF beneficiary or as an excluded activity.*

**1. Total JTF resources, 2021 to 2027, and Member State coverage.** FACT: "The resources for the JTF under the Investment for jobs and growth goal that are available for budgetary commitment for the period 2021-2027 shall be EUR 7 500 000 000 in 2018 prices" *Source: Regulation (EU) 2021/1056. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32021R1056

*Analytical inference:* this is the JTF's core cohesion-policy funding envelope, available to all Member States; it is background to the fund's overall scale, not a figure the workspace itself reports against.

**2. Recovery Instrument resources, total and annual breakdown.** FACT: "The measures referred to in Article 1(2) of Regulation (EU) 2020/2094 shall be implemented under this Regulation with an amount of EUR 10 000 000 000 in 2018 prices" *Source: Regulation (EU) 2021/1056. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32021R1056

FACT: "— 2021: EUR 2 000 000 000, — 2022: EUR 4 000 000 000, — 2023: EUR 4 000 000 000." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2021/1056. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32021R1056

*Analytical inference:* this is the JTF's separate COVID-19 recovery top-up, committed across 2021 through 2023; see the per-year trajectory captured in this entry's metadata.

**3. Conditional access to 50% of annual allocations.** FACT: "Where a Member State has not made a commitment to implement the objective of achieving a climate-neutral Union by 2050, only 50 % of the annual allocations for that Member State set out in accordance with Articles 3(4) and 4(3) shall be made available for programming and included in the priorities." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2021/1056. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32021R1056

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this condition runs to Member States (whether they have committed to the 2050 climate-neutral objective), not to a private freight-forwarding workspace directly.

**4. Eligible activity: local transport decarbonisation.** FACT: "investments in smart and sustainable local mobility, including decarbonisation of the local transport sector and its infrastructure" *Source: Regulation (EU) 2021/1056. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32021R1056

*Operational implication:* a freight-forwarding workspace investing in decarbonisation of local transport infrastructure or operations may fall within this eligible-activity category if it is an SME in a territory covered by an approved territorial just transition plan.

**5. Excluded activity: fossil fuel production, processing, transport, distribution, storage, or combustion.** FACT: "(d) investment related to the production, processing, transport, distribution, storage or combustion of fossil fuels." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2021/1056. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32021R1056

*Operational implication:* a workspace whose own logistics activities involve fossil fuel transport, distribution, or storage cannot receive JTF support for those specific activities, regardless of its territory or SME status.

**6. Scope of support (Article 9's own heading).** FACT: "Exclusion from the scope of support" *Source: Regulation (EU) 2021/1056. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32021R1056

*Analytical inference:* Article 9 frames the JTF's exclusions as defining the outer boundary of the fund's own scope of support, distinct from the affirmative eligible-activity list in Article 8.

**7. Co-financing rate caps by region type.** FACT: "the co-financing rate, applicable to the region where the territory or territories identified in the territorial just transition plans in accordance with Article 11 of this Regulation are located, for the JTF priority or priorities shall not be higher than: (a) 85 % for less developed regions; (b) 70 % for transition regions; (c) 50 % for more developed regions." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2021/1056. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32021R1056

*Analytical inference:* these caps apply to the programme's own co-financing structure between JTF resources and national contributions; they do not set a workspace's own private co-financing share for any individual project, which is a matter for the specific programme's own call terms.

**8. Financial corrections for programme underachievement (the Regulation's penalty-shaped mechanism).** FACT: "Based on the examination of the final performance report of the programme, the Commission may make financial corrections in accordance with Article 104 of Regulation (EU) 2021/1060 where less than 65 % of the target set out for one or more output indicators is achieved." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2021/1056. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32021R1056

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this financial-correction mechanism applies to programme-level output-indicator underachievement, assessed against the managing programme, not as a fine or penalty against any individual private freight-forwarding beneficiary.

**Required-slot grounding.** FACT: "The JTF shall support the Investment for jobs and growth goal in all Member States." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2021/1056. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32021R1056 FACT: "This Regulation shall enter into force on the day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union" *Source: Regulation (EU) 2021/1056. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32021R1056 FACT: "By 30 June 2025, the Commission shall review the implementation of the JTF with regard to the specific objective set out in Article 2" *Source: Regulation (EU) 2021/1056. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32021R1056

**Qualification accounting.** Per-year trajectory: CAPTURED (see metadata.requirement_trajectory: the Recovery Instrument's EUR 10 000 000 000 committed across 2021, 2022 and 2023 per obligation 2 above). Exceptions and carve-outs: No exceptions are stated in Articles 1 to 15. Scope limits: CAPTURED above (obligation 6, the Article 9 scope-of-support heading, and obligation 5, the fossil fuel exclusion).

Obligations surveyed: 8; workspace-adjacent: 3; extracted as FACT: 8.

# 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

*No content for this section: the captured source addresses fund eligibility categories, not any product-specific compliance status.*

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

*No content for this section: the registration and reporting duties stated in the captured source, Member State territorial just transition plans under Article 11 and programme indicator reporting under Article 12, run from Member States to the European Commission, not from a private freight-forwarding workspace to any authority.*

# 11. Operational System Requirements

*No content for this section: the captured source states no technical or monitoring system requirement running to a private freight-forwarding workspace; indicator reporting, Article 12 and Annex III, is a Member State and programme-level obligation.*

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

FACT: "The JTF shall not support: (a) the decommissioning or the construction of nuclear power stations; (b) the manufacturing, processing and marketing of tobacco and tobacco products;" *Source: Regulation (EU) 2021/1056. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32021R1056

FACT: "(d) investment related to the production, processing, transport, distribution, storage or combustion of fossil fuels." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2021/1056. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32021R1056

*Operational implication:* these four exclusions, nuclear power stations, tobacco manufacturing and marketing, undertakings in difficulty absent temporary State aid authorisation, and fossil fuel production, processing, transport, distribution, storage, or combustion, define the JTF's outer boundary; the fossil fuel exclusion is the one most likely to be directly relevant to a freight-forwarding workspace's own activities.

# 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

*No content for this section: the captured source is a single EU Regulation text with no adjacent industry research, alternative mechanism, or comparative-jurisdiction content.*

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 24 June 2021: This Regulation was adopted, establishing the Just Transition Fund. FACT: "Done at Brussels, 24 June 2021." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2021/1056. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32021R1056

# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks Commission Decision 2010/205/EU, addressed to the EU Member States, which sets the standard reporting questionnaire Member States use to report to the Commission on their national implementation of the European Pollutant Release and Transfer Register (E-PRTR) Regulation (EC) No 166/2006. It exists to give a freight-forwarding workspace with EU exposure a single record of what this reporting-format instrument does and does not create, since the captured source text addresses only Member States, never a private operator directly.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

FACT: the captured source states, verbatim: «Article 16(1) of Regulation (EC) No 166/2006 requires a report on the implementation of the Regulation, based on the information from the last three reporting years, to be established in accordance with the procedure laid down in Article 16(2) of Regulation (EC) No 166/2006.»

FACT: the captured source states, verbatim: «Article 16(2) of Regulation (EC) No 166/2006 requires that the report be drawn up on the basis of a questionnaire drafted by the Commission with the assistance of the Committee set up in Article 19(1) of the Regulation.»

FACT: the captured source states, verbatim: «This Decision is addressed to the Member States.»

*Analytical inference:* this Decision is a Member-State-to-Commission reporting-format instrument, not a rule creating a compliance duty on private industry; its own addressee clause names only the Member States, and both recitals above describe obligations running from Member States to the Commission under Regulation (EC) No 166/2006, not obligations running to a freight-forwarding workspace.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

*Operational implication:* none identified. This decision sets a recurring Member-State reporting questionnaire; the captured source text names no pending action, deadline, or event a freight-forwarding workspace itself needs to act on.

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this Decision's compliance chain runs from Member States to the Commission under Article 16 of Regulation (EC) No 166/2006; the captured source text states no duty running to a private freight-forwarding operator. FACT: the captured source states, verbatim: «Done at Brussels, 31 March 2010.»

GAP: [primary_deadline] No source in this brief's corpus states a reporting deadline by an actual date; the questionnaire (Section 10 below) asks Member States to describe their own national deadlines, but no specific date is itself stated in the captured text.

GAP: [effective_date] No explicit entry-into-force or effective-date clause is present in the captured source text beyond the Commission's own adoption/signing statement quoted above.

*Analytical inference:* a large industrial facility with significant pollutant releases (for example a large port or terminal operation subject to E-PRTR reporting under Regulation (EC) No 166/2006 directly, not under this Decision) could be indirectly affected by the underlying Regulation's own facility-reporting duty, but this Decision itself never states such a duty -- it only prescribes the format Member States use to report to the Commission.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

*No content for this section -- the captured pool contains only this Decision's own operative text and Annex, with no separate implementing-guidance document identified.*

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

*No content for this section -- the captured pool records only the Decision's 2010 adoption, already reflected in Section 14's timeline; no forward-looking guidance or pending event is stated.*

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does this Decision create a compliance duty on a private freight-forwarding operator?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* the captured source text addresses only the Member States (Section 2); it names no other addressee and states no duty running to a private operator. A workspace with a specific compliance question about E-PRTR facility-level reporting under the underlying Regulation (EC) No 166/2006 itself should confirm current status directly against EUR-Lex rather than relying solely on this Decision.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

*Note: this Decision is a Member-State-to-Commission reporting-format instrument, not a rule imposing duties on private industry. "Substantive requirements" here means the Decision's own recitals and Article 1 (the obligations it places on Member States), surveyed for workspace relevance rather than assumed to apply.*

**1. Article 16(1) report requirement (recital).** FACT: «Article 16(1) of Regulation (EC) No 166/2006 requires a report on the implementation of the Regulation, based on the information from the last three reporting years, to be established in accordance with the procedure laid down in Article 16(2) of Regulation (EC) No 166/2006.»

**2. Article 16(2) questionnaire procedure (recital).** FACT: «Article 16(2) of Regulation (EC) No 166/2006 requires that the report be drawn up on the basis of a questionnaire drafted by the Commission with the assistance of the Committee set up in Article 19(1) of the Regulation.»

**3. First reporting period (recital).** FACT: «The first report covers the period 2007 to 2009 inclusive.»

**4. Questionnaire-use obligation (Member States, Article 1).** FACT: «HAS ADOPTED THIS DECISION: Article 1 The Member States shall use the reporting questionnaire set up in Annex to this Decision as a basis for drawing up the report to be submitted to the Commission pursuant to Article 16(1) of Regulation (EC) No 166/2006»

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this obligation runs from Member States to the Commission; it does not create a duty running to a private freight-forwarding operator.

**5. National penalty-regime reporting (Annex, Article 20 of the Regulation).** FACT: the captured source states, verbatim: «penalties are effective, proportionate and dissuasive and what was the experience of their application»

*Analytical inference:* this is not itself a stated penalty amount or mechanism -- it is a reporting requirement asking Member States to describe, to the Commission, whether their OWN national penalty regime for E-PRTR facility reporting is effective, proportionate and dissuasive; the captured text states no specific fine or sanction figure at all.

No phase-in is stated in Articles 1 to 2 of this Decision or Article 16 of Regulation (EC) No 166/2006. No exceptions are stated in Articles 1 to 2 of this Decision or Article 16 of Regulation (EC) No 166/2006. No scope limits are stated in Articles 1 to 2 of this Decision or Article 16 of Regulation (EC) No 166/2006.

Obligations surveyed: 10; workspace-adjacent: 0; extracted as FACT: 5.

# 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

*No content for this section -- this Decision does not create product-specific compliance status; it is a Member-State reporting-format instrument with no product scope.*

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

FACT: the captured source's own Annex states, verbatim: «This questionnaire contains questions Member States are required to answer regarding the implementation of the E-PRTR Regulation during the last three reporting years .»

FACT: the captured source's own Annex states, verbatim: «Deadlines for reporting to the competent authority»

FACT: the captured source's own Annex states, verbatim: «Where any information is kept confidential, give an indication of the types of information, the reason for and the frequency with which it has been withheld.»

*Operational implication:* every reporting obligation named in the Annex questionnaire runs from a Member State's competent authority to the Commission; none of the three items above asks a private freight-forwarding operator to register or report anything directly under this Decision.

# 11. Operational System Requirements

FACT: the captured source's own Annex states, verbatim: «The responses to the questionnaire shall be made available by Member States in an electronic format .»

*Operational implication:* the only system requirement stated is that Member States make their questionnaire responses available electronically; this is a Member-State reporting-channel requirement, not a system a private operator itself must build or maintain.

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

*No content for this section -- no exemption or edge case is stated in the captured source text (see Section 8's qualification accounting).*

# 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

*No content for this section -- the captured pool contains only this single Decision's own text and Annex, with no adjacent research or alternative body referenced.*

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- March 31, 2010: Commission Decision 2010/205/EU was adopted, addressed to the Member States, setting the E-PRTR reporting questionnaire under Regulation (EC) No 166/2006.

*Source for timeline entry: EUR-Lex, CELEX:32010D0205 (Official Journal of the European Union L 88/18).*

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks SI 2020/1540, a UK EU-Exit "fix-up" instrument that replaces European Commission and Member State functions in waste and environmental permitting law with UK and devolved-administration functions, and amends or revokes a long list of retained EU waste instruments. It exists to give a freight forwarder handling waste shipments, hazardous waste consignments, WEEE, or packaging waste in or into the United Kingdom a single place to see: which UK authority now exercises which function, what changed in the underlying permitting regime, and which prior EU reporting-format instruments no longer apply.

FACT: "The Waste and Environmental Permitting etc. (Legislative Functions and Amendment etc.) (EU Exit) Regulations 2020" *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2020/1540. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2020/1540

FACT: "These Regulations may be cited as the Waste and Environmental Permitting etc. (Legislative Functions and Amendment etc.) (EU Exit) Regulations 2020." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2020/1540. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2020/1540

**What the workspace should expect to decide:** whether any specific waste classification, hazardous-waste consignment, or environmental-permit reference it relies on has been renumbered, redefined, or transferred to a different UK authority by this instrument.

*Analytical inference:* this is a technical continuity instrument, not a new substantive duty-creating regulation; its own Explanatory Note (Section 5) states no significant private-sector impact is foreseen.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

FACT: "Part 2 provides for a legislative function of the European Commission under Directive 2008/98/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council on waste to be exercisable instead by public authorities in the United Kingdom." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2020/1540. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2020/1540

FACT: "Part 3 amends primary legislation and Part 4 amends subordinate legislation, including previous instruments made under section 8(1) of the 2018 Act." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2020/1540. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2020/1540

FACT: "Part 5 amends or revokes retained EU tertiary legislation relating to resources and waste." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2020/1540. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2020/1540

*Operational implication:* the instrument applies to the workspace indirectly, through the waste and environmental permitting regime it moves goods under: it does not itself impose a new duty on a freight forwarder, but it changes which UK body classifies waste, and it revokes or amends the underlying EU instruments that formerly set reporting formats and technical rules for waste and packaging.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

FACT: "A full impact assessment has not been produced for this instrument as no, or no significant, impact on the private, voluntary or public sector is foreseen." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2020/1540. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2020/1540

*Analytical inference:* the instrument's own Explanatory Note states no significant private-sector impact is foreseen; nothing in the captured text identifies a near-term action item for a private party beyond confirming, where relevant, which UK authority now exercises a function formerly exercised at EU level (Section 8).

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

FACT: "(3) “ The appropriate authority ” means— (a) for regulations applying in relation to England, the Secretary of State; (b) for regulations applying in relation to Wales, the Welsh Ministers; (c) for regulations applying in relation to Scotland, the Scottish Ministers; (d) for regulations applying in relation to Northern Ireland, the Department of Agriculture, Environment and Rural Affairs." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2020/1540. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2020/1540

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this instrument's duties (Section 8) run mainly to the UK devolved administrations named above (the "appropriate authority") and to specific pieces of primary and subordinate legislation being amended; it does not name a freight forwarder, carrier, or logistics intermediary as a duty-holder anywhere in the captured text. Whether a specific waste-classification or hazardous-waste-consignment obligation, as amended by this instrument, reaches a specific workspace transaction is a fact-specific question outside this brief's scope and requires review of the amended instrument itself (e.g. the Hazardous Waste (England and Wales) Regulations 2005, Section 8 obligation 9).

*Analytical inference:* the workspace's practical position in this compliance chain is as a mover of goods already subject to the underlying waste and permitting regimes this instrument amends, not as a direct addressee of this instrument itself.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

FACT: "A full impact assessment has not been produced for this instrument as no, or no significant, impact on the private, voluntary or public sector is foreseen." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2020/1540. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2020/1540

*Per the workspace's reading:* this Explanatory Note (expressly stated in the source not to be part of the Regulations themselves) is the instrument's own account of its purpose and expected impact, and confirms the instrument is legislative continuity work rather than a new compliance burden.

FACT: "Rebecca Pow Parliamentary Under Secretary of State Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs 16th December 2020" *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2020/1540. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2020/1540

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

FACT: "(3) Regulations 10 to 12 and 14 come into force immediately before IP completion day." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2020/1540. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2020/1540

FACT: "(4) Regulations 13 and 15, and this regulation, come into force immediately before the coming into force of the Environment and Rural Affairs (Amendment) (EU Exit) Regulations 2019( 2 )." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2020/1540. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2020/1540

*Operational implication:* the instrument's own staggered commencement (Section 8, obligation 1) means different Regulations of this SI took effect at different points relative to "IP completion day" and relative to a separate 2019 instrument's own commencement; a workspace reconstructing exactly when a specific amendment took effect should check the specific Regulation number against this staggered schedule rather than assuming a single commencement date for the whole instrument.

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does this instrument create a direct obligation on a freight forwarder?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* no duty-holder in the captured text is described in terms that name a freight forwarder, carrier, or logistics intermediary; the duties identified (Section 8) run to UK devolved administrations and to the specific legislation being amended. Whether an amended provision (for example, the Hazardous Waste Regulations 2005 amendment, Section 8 obligation 9) reaches a specific workspace transaction requires review of that amended instrument directly.

**Q2: Which UK authority now performs the function the European Commission or "Member States" formerly performed for list-of-waste classification?**

FACT: "(3) “ The appropriate authority ” means— (a) for regulations applying in relation to England, the Secretary of State; (b) for regulations applying in relation to Wales, the Welsh Ministers; (c) for regulations applying in relation to Scotland, the Scottish Ministers; (d) for regulations applying in relation to Northern Ireland, the Department of Agriculture, Environment and Rural Affairs." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2020/1540. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2020/1540

*Analytical inference:* the answer depends on which UK nation the waste classification applies in; there is no single UK-wide successor body.

**Q3: Does this instrument itself state a fine or penalty for non-compliance?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* no. See Section 8's own GAP note; this instrument's own captured text contains no penalty, fine, or offence language.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

*Note: this is a UK EU-Exit "fix-up" instrument, not a framework creating new private-party duties. "Substantive requirements" here means the instrument's own stated commencement, extent, authority-transfer, and amendment/revocation provisions -- most running to UK devolved administrations or to the legislation being amended, not to a freight forwarder directly.*

**1. Staggered commencement.** FACT: "(2) These Regulations come into force on IP completion day, except as provided in paragraphs (3) and (4)." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2020/1540. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2020/1540 FACT: "(3) Regulations 10 to 12 and 14 come into force immediately before IP completion day." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2020/1540. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2020/1540 FACT: "(4) Regulations 13 and 15, and this regulation, come into force immediately before the coming into force of the Environment and Rural Affairs (Amendment) (EU Exit) Regulations 2019( 2 )." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2020/1540. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2020/1540

**2. Extent.** FACT: "(5) Parts 1 and 2 extend to the United Kingdom." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2020/1540. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2020/1540 FACT: "(6) An amendment, repeal or revocation made by Part 3, 4 or 5 or the Schedule has the same extent as the provision being amended, repealed or revoked, subject to paragraph (7)." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2020/1540. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2020/1540 FACT: "(7) The revocations in paragraphs 7, 9, 10 and 11 of the Schedule extend to England and Wales and Northern Ireland." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2020/1540. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2020/1540

*Analytical inference:* obligation 2's third element is a genuine geographic scope limit: the Schedule paragraph 7, 9, 10, and 11 revocations extend only to England and Wales and Northern Ireland, not Scotland, while the general Part 1 and 2 provisions extend UK-wide.

**3. Devolved "appropriate authority" replaces EU/Member State functions.** FACT: "(3) “ The appropriate authority ” means— (a) for regulations applying in relation to England, the Secretary of State; (b) for regulations applying in relation to Wales, the Welsh Ministers; (c) for regulations applying in relation to Scotland, the Scottish Ministers; (d) for regulations applying in relation to Northern Ireland, the Department of Agriculture, Environment and Rural Affairs." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2020/1540. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2020/1540

**4. Power to prescribe or amend the list of waste.** FACT: "The appropriate authority may, by regulations, make provision for or in connection with prescribing or amending a list which categorises different types of waste (a “list of waste”)." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2020/1540. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2020/1540

**5. Consultation duty on the appropriate authority.** FACT: "Before making any regulations under regulation 3, the appropriate authority must consult such persons as the appropriate authority considers appropriate." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2020/1540. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2020/1540

**6. Statutory-instrument procedure for list-of-waste regulations.** FACT: "Regulations by the Secretary of State or the Welsh Ministers under regulation 3 are to be made by statutory instrument." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2020/1540. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2020/1540

**7. Power to make consequential provision.** FACT: "Regulations made under regulation 3 may— (a) include consequential, incidental, supplementary, transitional or saving provision (including provision amending, repealing or revoking enactments); (b) make different provision for different purposes." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2020/1540. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2020/1540

**8. Repeal of Environmental Protection Act 1990 section 62A.** FACT: "In the Environmental Protection Act 1990( 9 ), omit section 62A." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2020/1540. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2020/1540

**9. Amendment of the Hazardous Waste (England and Wales) Regulations 2005.** FACT: "In the Hazardous Waste (England and Wales) Regulations 2005( 10 ), omit regulations 6(b), 8(1)(b), 9(1)(b) and 72(3)." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2020/1540. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2020/1540

**10. Amendment of the Marine Licensing (Exempted Activities) Order 2011 and five further 2019 EU-Exit instruments (Regulations 9 to 15).** FACT: "except in relation to a person in Northern Ireland, means supplying or making available, whether in return for payment or free of charge, to a third party within the United Kingdom" *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2020/1540. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2020/1540 FACT: "in paragraph (1), for “EU market” substitute “market of Great Britain”;" *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2020/1540. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2020/1540

*Analytical inference:* the great bulk of this instrument (Regulations 9 to 15) is line-by-line textual substitution across five 2019 EU-Exit instruments -- principally replacing "exit day" with "IP completion day," replacing "EU market" with "market of Great Britain," and adjusting definitions for the Ireland/Northern Ireland Protocol (as obligation 10's Northern Ireland carve-out illustrates) -- rather than new substantive rules.

The same Regulation 10 amendment also states a scope-limiting clause for extractive waste. FACT: "The management of extractive waste is excluded from the scope of this Directive where it falls within the scope of Schedule 20, or paragraph 8(a) or (b) of Schedule 22, to the Environmental Permitting (England and Wales) Regulations 2016." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2020/1540. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2020/1540

**11. Amendment of retained EU list-of-wastes and mining-waste-inspection Decisions.** FACT: "Commission Decision 2000/532/EC replacing Decision 94/3/EC establishing a list of wastes pursuant to Article 1(a) of Council Directive 75/442/EEC on waste and Council Decision 94/904/EC establishing a list of hazardous waste pursuant to Article 1(4) of Council Directive 91/689/EEC on hazardous waste is amended as follows." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2020/1540. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2020/1540 FACT: "(2) Omit Articles 4, 5 and 6." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2020/1540. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2020/1540 FACT: "Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2020/248 laying down technical guidelines for inspections in accordance with Article 17 of Directive 2006/21/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council is amended as follows." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2020/1540. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2020/1540

**12. Revocation of 14 retained EU tertiary instruments.** FACT: "The instruments listed in the Schedule are revoked." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2020/1540. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2020/1540 FACT: "Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2017/699 establishing a common methodology for the calculation of the weight of electrical and electronic equipment (EEE) placed on the market of each Member State and a common methodology for the calculation of the quantity of waste electrical and electronic equipment (WEEE) generated by weight in each Member State." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2020/1540. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2020/1540

*Operational implication:* the revoked instruments (Schedule) include WEEE-weight-calculation methodology, packaging-waste-database format rules, food-waste measurement methodology, and EU Ecolabel criteria; a workspace still citing any of these EU instruments as the current UK rule should confirm whether a replacement UK measure now governs the same subject.

GAP: no source in this item's captured pool states a fine, penalty, or sanction running to a manufacturer, waste operator, importer, or freight-forwarding operator for non-compliance with this instrument's own provisions; the captured text contains no "penalty," "fine," or "offence" language anywhere, consistent with its own Explanatory Note stating no significant private-sector impact is foreseen.

No phase-in is stated in Sections 1 to 18 of this instrument.

Obligations 5, 6, and 7 above (the consultation duty, statutory-instrument procedure, and consequential-provision power) run only to the UK devolved administrations exercising the list-of-waste power and impose no duty reaching a private party; they are excluded from the workspace-adjacent count below, though each is extracted as FACT above for completeness of the instrument's own procedural scheme.

Obligations surveyed: 12; workspace-adjacent: 9; extracted as FACT: 12.

# 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

FACT: "The appropriate authority may, by regulations, make provision for or in connection with prescribing or amending a list which categorises different types of waste (a “list of waste”)." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2020/1540. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2020/1540

FACT: "In the Hazardous Waste (England and Wales) Regulations 2005( 10 ), omit regulations 6(b), 8(1)(b), 9(1)(b) and 72(3)." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2020/1540. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2020/1540

*Operational implication:* product-specific compliance for waste and hazardous-waste shipments continues to turn on classification under the "list of waste" mechanism (now a UK devolved-administration power) and on the amended Hazardous Waste (England and Wales) Regulations 2005, not on any new product test this instrument itself creates.

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

FACT: "The instruments listed in the Schedule are revoked." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2020/1540. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2020/1540

FACT: "Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2017/699 establishing a common methodology for the calculation of the weight of electrical and electronic equipment (EEE) placed on the market of each Member State and a common methodology for the calculation of the quantity of waste electrical and electronic equipment (WEEE) generated by weight in each Member State." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2020/1540. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2020/1540

*Operational implication:* this instrument does not create a new registration or reporting obligation; it revokes the EU-level format rules for existing reporting regimes (WEEE weight-calculation, packaging-waste database formats, food-waste measurement), which a workspace should expect to be replaced, if at all, by a UK-specific format rather than continuing under the revoked EU instrument.

# 11. Operational System Requirements

*Note: because this is a legislative-continuity instrument, "operational system requirements" here means the reference updates a workspace's own compliance tracking should make, not a technical system the instrument itself requires building.*

FACT: "(3) “ The appropriate authority ” means— (a) for regulations applying in relation to England, the Secretary of State; (b) for regulations applying in relation to Wales, the Welsh Ministers; (c) for regulations applying in relation to Scotland, the Scottish Ministers; (d) for regulations applying in relation to Northern Ireland, the Department of Agriculture, Environment and Rural Affairs." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2020/1540. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2020/1540

*Operational implication:* a workspace's own compliance reference material citing "the Secretary of State," "the European Commission," or "Member States" for UK waste-classification purposes should be updated to cite the correct devolved "appropriate authority" for the nation in question.

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

FACT: "except in relation to a person in Northern Ireland, means supplying or making available, whether in return for payment or free of charge, to a third party within the United Kingdom" *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2020/1540. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2020/1540

*Analytical inference:* the one explicit edge case this captured text defines is the Northern Ireland carve-out in the amended "placing on the market" definition (Section 8, obligation 10): a person in Northern Ireland is treated differently from a person elsewhere in the United Kingdom, reflecting the Protocol on Ireland/Northern Ireland in the EU withdrawal agreement.

# 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

*No content for this section is grounded in the item's captured source pool.*

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 16th December 2020: Commission Decision 2000/532/EC amendments and the wider instrument signed by the Parliamentary Under Secretary of State, Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs.
- 2020: The Waste and Environmental Permitting etc. (Legislative Functions and Amendment etc.) (EU Exit) Regulations 2020 made, per the legislation.gov.uk instrument year.
- IP completion day: general commencement date for this instrument, except as provided for specific Regulations (Section 6).

*Source for timeline entries: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2020/1540 (https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2020/1540).*

metadata.why_matters: It determines which UK authority now classifies waste as hazardous or non-hazardous, updates definitions across five 2019 EU-Exit environmental permitting instruments (exit day to IP completion day; EU market to market of Great Britain), and revokes 14 EU instruments that formerly set reporting formats for WEEE, packaging waste, and food waste.

14 retained EU instruments revoked (Regulation 18 and Schedule)
commencement staggered across IP completion day and the 2019 EU Exit Regulations (Regulation 1)
metadata.enforcement_body: the appropriate authority in each UK nation (the Secretary of State for England, the Welsh Ministers, the Scottish Ministers, or the Department of Agriculture, Environment and Rural Affairs for Northern Ireland) per Regulation 2
