entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks Commission Regulation (EU) 2021/341 of 23 February 2021, which amends eight existing ecodesign Regulations (servers and data storage products; electric motors and variable speed drives; refrigerating appliances; light sources and separate control gears; electronic displays; household dishwashers; household washing machines and washer-dryers; and refrigerating appliances with a direct sales function) to add a "declared values" definition, an anti-circumvention prohibition, and verification-tolerance rules for market-surveillance testing. It exists to give a workspace shipping or handling any of these eight product categories a single place to see the compliance-testing rules manufacturers, importers, and authorised representatives now operate under.

*Analytical inference:* this Regulation amends product-compliance testing and verification rules for manufacturers, importers, and authorised representatives; it does not itself address freight, transport, or customs duties. A workspace's interest is in the compliance status of cargo in these eight product categories, not in a direct duty running to the workspace as a freight intermediary (see Section 4).

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

FACT: "The manufacturer, importer or authorised representative shall not place on the market products designed to be able to detect they are being tested (for example by recognising the test conditions or test cycle) and to react specifically by automatically altering their performance during the test with the aim of reaching a more favourable level for any of the parameters in the technical documentation or included in any documentation provided." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2021/341, EUR-Lex CELEX:32021R0341. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32021R0341

*Operational implication:* a workspace shipping servers, electric motors, refrigerating appliances, light sources, electronic displays, dishwashers, or washing machines from the EU market can expect the manufacturer, importer, or authorised representative of record to certify that the product's performance is not artificially altered for test conditions, across all eight product categories this Regulation amends.

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

FACT: "means the values provided by the manufacturer, importer or authorised representative for the stated, calculated or measured technical parameters in accordance with Article 5, for the verification of compliance by the Member State authorities." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2021/341, EUR-Lex CELEX:32021R0341. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32021R0341

*Legal Confirmation Required:* the duties this Regulation creates run to the "manufacturer, importer or authorised representative" of the product, not to a freight-forwarding workspace as such; whether a specific workspace ever acts in one of those three named roles for a given shipment (for example, as an "importer" of record) is a fact-specific question outside this brief's own corpus and requires counsel review.

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Is the workspace ever the "manufacturer, importer or authorised representative" this Regulation names?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* the captured text of this Regulation does not itself define these EU regulatory roles beyond naming them; whether a specific workspace's activity (for example, arranging import clearance) makes it the "importer" for the purposes of the eight amended Regulations is a fact-specific legal question outside this brief's corpus.

**Q2: Does the verification-tolerance rule affect the workspace's own testing of cargo?**

FACT: "The verification tolerances defined in this Annex relate only to the verification by Member State authorities of the declared values and shall not be used by the manufacturer, importer or authorised representative as an allowed tolerance to establish the values in the technical documentation or in interpreting these values with a view to achieving compliance or to communicate better performance by any means." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2021/341, EUR-Lex CELEX:32021R0341. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32021R0341

*Analytical inference:* this tolerance is reserved for Member State market-surveillance authorities' own verification testing; it is not an allowance a workspace or any other party may use to justify a declared value in the product's own technical documentation.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

**1. Anti-circumvention prohibition (cross-product).** FACT: "The manufacturer, importer or authorised representative shall not place on the market products designed to be able to detect they are being tested (for example by recognising the test conditions or test cycle) and to react specifically by automatically altering their performance during the test with the aim of reaching a more favourable level for any of the parameters in the technical documentation or included in any documentation provided." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2021/341, EUR-Lex CELEX:32021R0341. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32021R0341

**2. "Declared values" definition (electric motors and variable speed drives, illustrative of the same definition added across the amended Regulations).** FACT: "means the values provided by the manufacturer, importer or authorised representative for the stated, calculated or measured technical parameters in accordance with Article 5, for the verification of compliance by the Member State authorities." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2021/341, EUR-Lex CELEX:32021R0341. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32021R0341

**3. Verification-tolerance restriction to Member State authorities (servers and data storage products, Annex IV).** FACT: "The verification tolerances defined in this Annex relate only to the verification by Member State authorities of the declared values and shall not be used by the manufacturer, importer or authorised representative as an allowed tolerance to establish the values in the technical documentation or in interpreting these values with a view to achieving compliance or to communicate better performance by any means." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2021/341, EUR-Lex CELEX:32021R0341. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32021R0341

**4. Transitional compliance equivalence (refrigerating appliances).** FACT: "If no unit belonging to the same model or equivalent models was placed on the market before 1 November 2020, the units of models placed on the market between 1 November 2020 and 28 February 2021 which comply with the provisions of this regulation shall be considered compliant with the requirements of Commission Regulation (EC) No 643/2009." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2021/341, EUR-Lex CELEX:32021R0341. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32021R0341

*Operational implication:* a refrigerating-appliance unit already on the market in the November 2020 to February 2021 window is treated as compliant with the prior Regulation (EC) No 643/2009 rather than being retroactively non-compliant, which matters for a workspace holding or shipping inventory from that window.

**5. Staggered application, first wave (1 May 2021).** FACT: "Article 1(3), Article 3(4), Article 5(6), Article 6(3), Article 7(4) and Article 8(3) shall apply from 1 May 2021." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2021/341, EUR-Lex CELEX:32021R0341. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32021R0341

**6. Staggered application, second wave (1 July 2021).** FACT: "Article 2 and Article 4(4) shall apply from 1 July 2021." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2021/341, EUR-Lex CELEX:32021R0341. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32021R0341

**7. Staggered application, third wave (1 September 2021).** FACT: "Article 4(1), (2) and (5) shall apply from 1 September 2021." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2021/341, EUR-Lex CELEX:32021R0341. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32021R0341

**8. Default entry into force.** FACT: "This Regulation shall enter into force on the third day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union ." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2021/341, EUR-Lex CELEX:32021R0341. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32021R0341

*Operational implication:* every provision not named in obligations 5 to 7 above took effect on this default entry-into-force date; the three staggered dates are the exception to, not the whole of, this Regulation's timing.

**9. Scope limit on the ABC power-averaging allowance for HDR display measurement (electronic displays, Annex measurement methodology).** FACT: "An ABC allowance does not apply in HDR display mode." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2021/341, EUR-Lex CELEX:32021R0341. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32021R0341

*Legal Confirmation Required:* none of the nine obligations above states a fine, sanction, or penalty running to a manufacturer, importer, authorised representative, or freight-forwarding workspace; this Regulation's own text is silent on enforcement consequences (see Section 4's own compliance-chain note for where that duty structure sits).

No exceptions are stated in Articles 1 to 9.

Obligations surveyed: 9; workspace-adjacent: 9; extracted as FACT: 9.

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

FACT: "means the values provided by the manufacturer, importer or authorised representative for the stated, calculated or measured technical parameters in accordance with Article 5, for the verification of compliance by the Member State authorities." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2021/341, EUR-Lex CELEX:32021R0341. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32021R0341

*Operational implication:* the "declared values" this definition establishes are what a manufacturer, importer, or authorised representative records in the product's technical documentation; a workspace sourcing technical documentation for customs or compliance purposes should expect to find these declared values referenced by that name across all eight amended Regulations.

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

FACT: "If no unit belonging to the same model or equivalent models was placed on the market before 1 November 2020, the units of models placed on the market between 1 November 2020 and 28 February 2021 which comply with the provisions of this regulation shall be considered compliant with the requirements of Commission Regulation (EC) No 643/2009." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2021/341, EUR-Lex CELEX:32021R0341. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32021R0341

*Analytical inference:* this transitional-equivalence treatment is scoped to refrigerating appliances placed on the market in a specific four-month window (1 November 2020 to 28 February 2021); it does not extend to other product categories or other date ranges.

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 23 February 2021: Commission Regulation (EU) 2021/341 adopted.

FACT: "Done at Brussels, 23 February 2021." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2021/341, EUR-Lex CELEX:32021R0341. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32021R0341
- Third day following publication in the Official Journal of the European Union: default entry into force.
- 1 May 2021: Article 1(3), Article 3(4), Article 5(6), Article 6(3), Article 7(4) and Article 8(3) apply.
- 1 July 2021: Article 2 and Article 4(4) apply.
- 1 September 2021: Article 4(1), (2) and (5) apply.

FACT: "This Regulation shall enter into force on the third day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union ." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2021/341, EUR-Lex CELEX:32021R0341. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32021R0341

FACT: "Article 1(3), Article 3(4), Article 5(6), Article 6(3), Article 7(4) and Article 8(3) shall apply from 1 May 2021." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2021/341, EUR-Lex CELEX:32021R0341. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32021R0341

FACT: "Article 2 and Article 4(4) shall apply from 1 July 2021." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2021/341, EUR-Lex CELEX:32021R0341. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32021R0341

FACT: "Article 4(1), (2) and (5) shall apply from 1 September 2021." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2021/341, EUR-Lex CELEX:32021R0341. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32021R0341

*Source for timeline entries: Commission Regulation (EU) 2021/341, EUR-Lex CELEX:32021R0341 (https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32021R0341).*

metadata.what_is_it: An EU omnibus amendment (Regulation 2021/341) adding a declared-values definition, an anti-circumvention prohibition, and verification-tolerance rules to eight ecodesign Regulations covering servers, motors, refrigerating appliances, light sources, displays, dishwashers, and washing machines.

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2022/2299 of 15 November 2022, which lays down the structure, format, technical details, and process for the biennial integrated national energy and climate progress reports Member States submit under the EU's Governance of the Energy Union Regulation (EU) 2018/1999. It is a REGULATION (directly applicable, unlike a Decision addressed to specific parties), but its own substantive content is Member-State-facing reporting infrastructure across 23 Annexes covering decarbonisation, renewable energy, energy efficiency, energy security, the internal energy market, and fossil-fuel subsidy phase-out.

FACT: "Regulation (EU) 2018/1999 requires Member States to submit to the Commission integrated national energy and climate plans covering a ten-year period and to rely on a two-step approach by, first, setting national objectives, targets and contributions for all the five dimensions of the Energy Union and, second, planning the relevant policies and measures to achieve those." *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2022/2299 of 15 November 2022, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022R2299

*Analytical inference:* this reporting infrastructure is background to the EU's energy and climate trajectory (renewable energy targets, energy efficiency obligation schemes, fossil-fuel subsidy phase-out) that shapes fuel cost and availability conditions a freight-forwarding workspace operates within; the Regulation does not itself impose an obligation on a private operator.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

FACT: "Member States are to submit draft updated integrated national energy and climate plans by 30 June 2023 and final ones by 30 June 2024" *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2022/2299 of 15 November 2022, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022R2299

FACT: "Article 2 Reporting on progress with respect to the decarbonisation dimension 1. Member States shall report the information on progress towards the objectives, including progress towards the Union’s climate-neutrality objective set out in Article 2(1) of Regulation (EU) 2021/1119 of the European Parliament and of the Council" *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2022/2299 of 15 November 2022, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022R2299

**Jurisdictional scope slot:**

FACT: Member States report GHG inventory data using the Global Warming Potential value set that "applies to GHG inventories in the same year" *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2022/2299 of 15 November 2022, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022R2299

*Operational implication:* the decarbonisation reporting obligation quoted above runs to Member States, which must report progress toward the Union's climate-neutrality objective (Regulation (EU) 2021/1119); a freight-forwarding workspace is not itself a reporting party under this Regulation, but the GHG-inventory data it produces is one input to the national statistics this Regulation standardises the reporting format for.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

*No content for this section -- the draft-plan deadline of 30 June 2023 and the final-plan deadline of 30 June 2024 (Section 8) have both already passed as of the current review, and no current-action item for the workspace is stated in the captured text.*

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

FACT: "HAS ADOPTED THIS REGULATION: CHAPTER I DEFINITIONS Article 1 Definitions For the purposes of this Regulation, the following definitions shall apply:" *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2022/2299 of 15 November 2022, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022R2299

FACT: "This Regulation shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union." *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2022/2299 of 15 November 2022, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022R2299

FACT: "This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States." *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2022/2299 of 15 November 2022, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022R2299

FACT: "Done at Brussels, 15 November 2022." *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2022/2299 of 15 November 2022, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022R2299

*Legal Confirmation Required:* as a Regulation, this instrument is binding in its entirety and directly applicable across all Member States without national transposition -- unlike a Decision addressed to named parties. That direct applicability governs Member States' own reporting duty to the Commission; it creates no reporting duty running directly to a freight-forwarding workspace, carrier, or logistics intermediary.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

*No content for this section -- the captured recitals describe the Governance of the Energy Union Regulation (EU) 2018/1999's own reporting cycle rather than a separate authoritative guidance document this Regulation interprets.*

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

*No content for this section -- the captured text states no further pending regulatory event beyond this Regulation's own adoption and reporting cycle described in Section 14; no forward-dated guidance document or scheduled event is stated in the pool.*

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does this Regulation create a reporting obligation running directly to a freight-forwarding workspace?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* No. The biennial progress-report and NECP-update obligations this Regulation standardises the format for run from Member States to the Commission under Regulation (EU) 2018/1999. Whether the workspace, as a large commercial energy consumer or an entity potentially in scope of Article 8(4) of Directive 2012/27/EU's energy-audit obligation (Section 8 below), carries a separate reporting duty of its own is governed by that Directive directly, not by this Regulation.

**Q2: Does the taxation-measures exception to the alternative-policy-measures reporting table (Section 8) affect the workspace?**

*Analytical inference:* the exception is a reporting-scope exclusion for Member States (they need not report taxation measures in that specific table); it does not itself exempt any operator, including a freight-forwarding workspace, from an underlying tax obligation, which would be set by the taxation measure itself, not by this Regulation's reporting table.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

**NECP submission duty (Member State to Commission).**

FACT: "Regulation (EU) 2018/1999 requires Member States to submit to the Commission integrated national energy and climate plans covering a ten-year period and to rely on a two-step approach by, first, setting national objectives, targets and contributions for all the five dimensions of the Energy Union and, second, planning the relevant policies and measures to achieve those." *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2022/2299 of 15 November 2022, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022R2299

**NECP update deadlines (primary_deadline slot).**

FACT: "Member States are to submit draft updated integrated national energy and climate plans by 30 June 2023 and final ones by 30 June 2024" *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2022/2299 of 15 November 2022, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022R2299

**Decarbonisation progress reporting duty.**

FACT: "Article 2 Reporting on progress with respect to the decarbonisation dimension 1. Member States shall report the information on progress towards the objectives, including progress towards the Union’s climate-neutrality objective set out in Article 2(1) of Regulation (EU) 2021/1119 of the European Parliament and of the Council" *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2022/2299 of 15 November 2022, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022R2299

**GHG inventory jurisdictional scope (jurisdictional_scope slot).**

FACT: Member States report GHG inventory data using the Global Warming Potential value set that "applies to GHG inventories in the same year" *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2022/2299 of 15 November 2022, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022R2299

**Penalty-in-case-of-non-compliance reporting field (penalty_summary slot).**

FACT: "Penalties applied in case of non-compliance (and related references, including the law or other legal texts setting the penalties and related conditions)" *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2022/2299 of 15 November 2022, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022R2299

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this is a reporting FIELD under the energy efficiency obligation scheme (EEOS) annex -- Member States report what penalties their own national law attaches to EEOS non-compliance; it is not itself a penalty provision, and no specific fine or sanction amount running to a private operator is stated anywhere in this Regulation's own text.

**Alternative-policy-measures reporting exception (taxation measures excluded).**

FACT: "Alternative policy measures referred to in Article 7b and Article 20(6) of Directive 2012/27/EU) (except taxation measures)" *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2022/2299 of 15 November 2022, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022R2299

**SME scope definition for Article 8(4) energy-audit reporting.**

FACT: "The definition for the enterprises in scope of Article 8(4) of Directive 2012/27/EU follows the Commission’s definition for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs)" *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2022/2299 of 15 November 2022, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022R2299

*Analytical inference:* a freight-forwarding workspace large enough to fall outside the SME definition referenced above could be within the scope of Article 8(4) of Directive 2012/27/EU's mandatory energy-audit obligation; this Regulation only standardises how Member States report on that scheme, it does not itself state the audit obligation's substantive terms.

No phase-in is stated in Articles 1 to 20 of this Regulation.

Obligations surveyed: 12; workspace-adjacent: 7; extracted as FACT: 7.

# 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

*No content for this section -- this Regulation concerns Member State reporting format and process, not product-specific compliance status.*

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

FACT: "Regulation (EU) 2018/1999 requires Member States to submit to the Commission integrated national energy and climate plans covering a ten-year period and to rely on a two-step approach by, first, setting national objectives, targets and contributions for all the five dimensions of the Energy Union and, second, planning the relevant policies and measures to achieve those." *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2022/2299 of 15 November 2022, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022R2299

*Analytical inference:* this is a Member-State-to-Commission registration/reporting duty, not a duty running to a freight-forwarding workspace directly.

FACT: "Member States are to submit draft updated integrated national energy and climate plans by 30 June 2023 and final ones by 30 June 2024" *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2022/2299 of 15 November 2022, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022R2299

# 11. Operational System Requirements

FACT: "Article 2 Reporting on progress with respect to the decarbonisation dimension 1. Member States shall report the information on progress towards the objectives, including progress towards the Union’s climate-neutrality objective set out in Article 2(1) of Regulation (EU) 2021/1119 of the European Parliament and of the Council" *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2022/2299 of 15 November 2022, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022R2299

*Operational implication:* the decarbonisation, renewable-energy, and energy-efficiency reporting systems this Regulation standardises are Member-State statistical infrastructure; a workspace does not itself operate or maintain these systems, though the resulting national statistics inform the EU's broader energy-transition policy trajectory.

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

FACT: "Alternative policy measures referred to in Article 7b and Article 20(6) of Directive 2012/27/EU) (except taxation measures)" *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2022/2299 of 15 November 2022, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022R2299

*Analytical inference:* this is the only word-boundary-clean, unnegated exception clause found in the captured text: Member States reporting alternative policy measures under Directive 2012/27/EU need not report taxation measures in that specific table. No other exemption, carve-out, or scope-limiting clause of comparable substance is stated in this Regulation's own Chapters I to VI.

# 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

FACT: "The definition for the enterprises in scope of Article 8(4) of Directive 2012/27/EU follows the Commission’s definition for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs)" *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2022/2299 of 15 November 2022, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022R2299

*Analytical inference:* this SME-scope reference ties this Regulation's reporting infrastructure back to Directive 2012/27/EU's energy-audit obligation (Article 8(4)) and to the Commission's general SME definition (Commission Recommendation 2003/361/EC); a workspace researching whether it is itself subject to mandatory energy audits should treat those two instruments, not this reporting-format Regulation, as the substantive research target.

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 15 November 2022: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2022/2299 adopted at Brussels.
- 30 June 2023: deadline for Member States to submit draft updated integrated national energy and climate plans.
- 30 June 2024: deadline for Member States to submit final updated integrated national energy and climate plans.

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks The Waste (England and Wales) Regulations 2011 (S.I. 2011/988), the UK statutory instrument implementing the Waste Framework Directive's waste hierarchy, separate-collection, and carrier/broker/dealer registration duties in England and Wales. It exists to give a workspace that transports, collects, or otherwise handles controlled waste in England or Wales a single record of what the Regulations require, on what commencement dates, and what remains outside this brief's own captured source.

FACT: "Statutory Instruments 2011 No. 988 Environmental Protection, England And Wales The Waste (England and Wales) Regulations 2011 Made 28th March 2011 Coming into force in accordance with regulation 1" *Source: The Waste (England and Wales) Regulations 2011, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2011/988

**What the workspace should expect to decide:** whether any part of its own England/Wales operations (waste transport, collection, or brokering as part of reverse logistics, damaged-cargo disposal, or warehouse waste handling) makes it a "carrier," "broker," or "dealer" of controlled waste for the purposes of the Control of Pollution (Amendment) Act 1989, which would trigger the registration duty in Section 10 below.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

FACT: "Citation, commencement and extent U.K. 1. —(1) These Regulations may be cited as the Waste (England and Wales) Regulations 2011. (2) Subject to paragraph (3), they come into force on the day after the day on which they are made. (3) Regulation 12 comes into force at the end of the period of 6 months beginning with the day on which these Regulations are made. (4) These Regulations extend to England and Wales." *Source: The Waste (England and Wales) Regulations 2011, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2011/988

*Operational implication:* the Regulations apply territorially to England and Wales only; a workspace with no England/Wales waste-handling exposure has no direct overlap. Regulation 12 (the waste hierarchy duty, Section 8) was itself commenced later than the rest of the instrument, per its own six-month delay stated above.

FACT: "the waste hierarchy referred to in Article 4 of the Waste Framework Directive is applied to the generation of waste" *Source: The Waste (England and Wales) Regulations 2011, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2011/988

*Analytical inference:* this confirms the Regulations' own lineage as the England/Wales transposition of the EU Waste Framework Directive's Article 4 waste hierarchy, not a freestanding UK domestic policy choice.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

*Legal Confirmation Required:* the Regulation 27 transitional exemption from carrier/broker registration (Section 12) ended at the close of 2013; a workspace relying on that historical exemption to justify not registering as a carrier of controlled waste should confirm its current registration status directly with the Environment Agency (England) or Natural Resources Wales, since the exemption itself no longer applies to any current activity.

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

*Legal Confirmation Required:* Whether the workspace's own activities meet the statutory definition of a "carrier," "broker," or "dealer" of controlled waste (which would trigger the registration duty in Section 10) is a fact-specific question this brief's own captured source does not resolve for any specific workspace; it requires direct assessment against the Control of Pollution (Amendment) Act 1989 and regulation 25 of these Regulations.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

FACT: "Regulations 13 and 14 apply from 1st January 2015 to require the separate collection of waste paper, metal, plastic and glass and prohibit mixing of those wastes once separately collected." *Source: The Waste (England and Wales) Regulations 2011, legislation.gov.uk (Explanatory Note). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2011/988

*Per the workspace's reading:* this is the instrument's own Explanatory Note summarising Regulations 13 and 14's separate-collection duty; the underlying operative regulation text for Regulations 13 and 14 themselves is not independently captured in this brief's own pool beyond this summary sentence.

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

*No content for this section: this record's export carries no forward events, and every future-dated provision in the Regulations' own text captured here (the 1st January 2015 separate-collection application date; Regulation 12's delayed commencement) is already historical relative to today.*

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Is the workspace a "carrier," "broker," or "dealer" of controlled waste under the Control of Pollution (Amendment) Act 1989?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this brief's own captured source states the registration duty (Section 10) and the now-expired transitional exemption (Section 12) but does not itself state which activities make an entity a carrier, broker, or dealer; that determination requires direct legal assessment of the workspace's own operations.

**Q2: Does the workspace already hold a current carrier/broker/dealer registration?**

*Analytical inference:* the Regulation 27 transitional exemption (Section 12) that once excused certain carriers/brokers from registration ended at the close of 2013; any workspace whose registration status was last assessed against that now-expired exemption should re-confirm current status.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

*Note: this instrument mixes obligations running to a private carrier/broker/dealer (registration, the waste hierarchy duty, offences and penalties) with obligations running to public bodies (national waste management plan consultation and publication duties). "Workspace-adjacent" below marks the former, not the latter.*

**1. Waste hierarchy duty (Regulation 12(1)).** FACT: "12. —(1) An establishment or undertaking which imports, produces, collects, transports, recovers or disposes of waste, or which as a dealer or broker has control of waste must, on the transfer of waste, take all such measures available to it as are reasonable in the circumstances to apply the following waste hierarchy as a priority order— (a) prevention; (b) preparing for re-use; (c) recycling; (d) other recovery (for example energy recovery); (e) disposal." *Source: The Waste (England and Wales) Regulations 2011, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2011/988

*Operational implication:* this duty names "transports" and "collects" explicitly; a freight-forwarding workspace that transports or collects waste as part of its England/Wales operations falls within this duty's own wording.

**2. Separate collection duty (Regulations 13 and 14, from 1st January 2015).** FACT: "Regulations 13 and 14 apply from 1st January 2015 to require the separate collection of waste paper, metal, plastic and glass and prohibit mixing of those wastes once separately collected." *Source: The Waste (England and Wales) Regulations 2011, legislation.gov.uk (Explanatory Note). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2011/988

**3. Registration duty for carriers, brokers and dealers (Regulation 29(1)).** FACT: "29. — (1) This regulation applies to— (a) registration of a carrier for the purposes of the Control of Pollution (Amendment) Act 1989; and (b) registration of a broker or dealer for the purposes of regulation 25." *Source: The Waste (England and Wales) Regulations 2011, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2011/988

**4. Authority-production deadline (primary_deadline, within the registration/authority-of-transfer procedure).** FACT: "the authority must be produced at, or sent to, the relevant office no later than 5 working days from when required." *Source: The Waste (England and Wales) Regulations 2011, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2011/988

*Operational implication:* a carrier who cannot produce authority for a waste transfer forthwith when required must still produce or send it to the relevant office within this 5-working-day window.

**5. Offences and penalties (penalty_summary; Regulation 42).** FACT: "42. —(1) A person is guilty of an offence who— (a) if they are not a specified person, fails to comply with regulation 25; or (b) fails to comply with a compliance notice, stop notice or restoration notice." *Source: The Waste (England and Wales) Regulations 2011, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2011/988

FACT: "A person guilty of an offence under— (a) paragraph (1)(a); or (b) paragraph (1)(b) in relation to contravention of regulation 25, is liable on summary conviction to a fine not exceeding level 5 on the standard scale." *Source: The Waste (England and Wales) Regulations 2011, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2011/988

FACT: "A person guilty of an offence under paragraph (1)(b) in relation to contravention of regulation 12(1), [ F82 13(2) ] or 14(1) is liable— (a) on summary conviction, to a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum; (b) on conviction on indictment, to a fine." *Source: The Waste (England and Wales) Regulations 2011, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2011/988

*Operational implication:* the standard-scale level-5 fine applies to a general Regulation 25 breach; a breach of the waste hierarchy duty (Regulation 12(1)) or the separate-collection duty (Regulations 13(2)/14(1)) instead carries an uncapped fine on conviction on indictment.

**6. Corporate and officer liability (Regulation 44).** FACT: "Where a body corporate is guilty of an offence under regulation 42(1), and that offence is proved to have been committed with the consent or connivance of, or to have been attributable to any neglect on the part of— (a) any director, manager, secretary or other similar officer of the body corporate; or (b) any person who was purporting to act in any such capacity, that person, as well as the body corporate, is guilty of the offence." *Source: The Waste (England and Wales) Regulations 2011, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2011/988

*Operational implication:* a director, manager, secretary, or similarly-placed officer of a corporate freight-forwarding workspace can be personally liable alongside the company for an offence committed with their consent, connivance, or attributable neglect.

**7. Transitional exemption from registration, now expired (Regulation 27).** FACT: "27. —(1) Until the end of 2013, a transitionally exempt carrier is not required to be registered as a carrier of controlled waste for the purposes of section 1 of the Control of Pollution (Amendment) Act 1989." *Source: The Waste (England and Wales) Regulations 2011, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2011/988

*Analytical inference:* this exemption expired at the end of 2013; it is surveyed here as historical context for Section 3's threshold flag, not as a currently-available exemption.

**8. National waste management plan consultation, scope exclusion (not workspace-adjacent).** FACT: "This regulation does not apply to a national waste management plan containing only provision relating to paragraph 8, 9, 10 or 11 of Schedule 1." *Source: The Waste (England and Wales) Regulations 2011, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2011/988

*Analytical inference:* this duty runs to the public authority preparing the national waste management plan, not to a private carrier, broker, or dealer; it is surveyed for completeness but is not workspace-adjacent.

Obligations surveyed: 8; workspace-adjacent: 6; extracted as FACT: 8.

# 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

*No content for this section: this instrument's own captured text states no product-specific compliance status; its duties are activity-defined (carrying, collecting, transporting, or disposing of waste), not product-defined.*

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

FACT: "29. — (1) This regulation applies to— (a) registration of a carrier for the purposes of the Control of Pollution (Amendment) Act 1989; and (b) registration of a broker or dealer for the purposes of regulation 25." *Source: The Waste (England and Wales) Regulations 2011, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2011/988

FACT: "the authority must be produced at, or sent to, the relevant office no later than 5 working days from when required." *Source: The Waste (England and Wales) Regulations 2011, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2011/988

*Operational implication:* registration is made to the "appropriate body" (the Environment Agency in England, Natural Resources Wales in Wales) using the form that body provides; this brief's own captured source does not itself state the registration fee or renewal period.

# 11. Operational System Requirements

*Operational implication:* a carrier subject to these Regulations should maintain a process for producing waste-transfer authority documentation to the relevant office within the 5-working-day window (Section 8, item 4), and for applying the waste hierarchy priority order (Section 8, item 1) on every transfer of waste it handles.

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

FACT: "27. —(1) Until the end of 2013, a transitionally exempt carrier is not required to be registered as a carrier of controlled waste for the purposes of section 1 of the Control of Pollution (Amendment) Act 1989." *Source: The Waste (England and Wales) Regulations 2011, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2011/988

*Analytical inference:* no currently-available exemption from the registration duty is stated in this brief's own captured text; the only exemption found (Regulation 27) expired at the end of 2013.

# 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

FACT: "a marine licence is required or would be required but for a marine exemption order for transporting the waste in order to carry out a specified marine operation." *Source: The Waste (England and Wales) Regulations 2011, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2011/988

*Analytical inference:* this marine-licensing cross-reference is the adjacent regime for an ocean-freight workspace considering waste disposal at sea; it sits outside the carrier/broker/dealer registration duty this brief otherwise tracks and is governed by separate marine-licensing legislation.

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 28th March 2011: The Waste (England and Wales) Regulations 2011 made.
- 2011: Regulation 12 (the waste hierarchy duty) comes into force at the end of the six-month period beginning with the day the Regulations were made (Regulation 1(3)).
- 1st January 2015: Regulations 13 and 14 begin requiring separate collection of waste paper, metal, plastic and glass and prohibiting mixing of those wastes once separately collected.
- 2013: The Regulation 27 transitional exemption from carrier/broker registration ends.

*Source for timeline entries: The Waste (England and Wales) Regulations 2011, legislation.gov.uk (https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2011/988).*

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks European Parliament and Council Directive 94/63/EC, which controls volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions from the storage of petrol and its distribution from terminals to service stations, covering terminal storage installations, loading/unloading equipment, and the road tankers, rail tankers and vessels ("mobile containers") used to move petrol between terminals and service stations.

FACT: "European Parliament and Council Directive 94/63/EC of 20 December 1994 on the control of volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions resulting from the storage of petrol and its distribution from terminals to service stations" *Source: Directive 94/63/EC, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:31994L0063

FACT: "Done at Brussels, 20 December 1994." *Source: Directive 94/63/EC, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:31994L0063

FACT: "emissions of volatile organic compounds (VOCs) from petrol and solvents in the Community would be in the order of 10 million tonnes per year if no control measures were taken" *Source: Directive 94/63/EC, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:31994L0063

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

This Directive is addressed to EU Member States, which transpose its requirements into national law; it is not a rulemaking that itself creates a compliance duty for a freight forwarder. It applies to the workspace indirectly and materially: it governs the technical design of terminal storage installations, loading gantries, and the road tanker, rail tanker and vessel equipment used to move petrol, which shapes what infrastructure and vapour-recovery equipment is actually available for petrol logistics in the EU.

FACT: "This Directive is addressed to the Member States." *Source: Directive 94/63/EC, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:31994L0063

FACT: "Scope This Directive shall apply to the operations, installations, vehicles and vessels used for storage, loading and transport of petrol from one terminal to another or from a terminal to a service station." *Source: Directive 94/63/EC, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:31994L0063

*Analytical inference:* because Article 1's own scope names "operations, installations, vehicles and vessels used for storage, loading and transport of petrol," a workspace operating or chartering road tankers, rail tankers or vessels for petrol movements sits inside this Directive's subject matter even though the transposition duty itself runs to Member States, not to the workspace.

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

*Legal Confirmation Required:* This Directive's obligations, described in Section 8, run from EU Member States (which transpose the Directive into national law) to terminal operators and service stations within their territory. No source in this brief's corpus states that a freight forwarder itself is a named addressee of any Article. Whether a specific national transposing measure imposes a duty on a workspace operating road tankers, rail tankers or vessels used for petrol carriage is a fact-specific question outside this brief's scope and would require confirmation against the relevant Member State's own transposing legislation.

*Analytical inference:* Because the compliance chain runs Member-State-to-terminal/service-station, the workspace's practical relevance is equipment and infrastructure awareness: the vapour-recovery and bottom-loading specifications in Section 8 and the Annexes govern what loading/unloading equipment a compliant EU terminal will actually operate.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

FACT: "on grounds of international standardization and of safety during the loading of ships, standards must be drawn up at International Maritime Organization level for vapour control and recovery systems to apply to both loading installations and ships; whereas the Community must therefore endeavour to ensure that the necessary provisions are introduced into the Marpol Convention during the current revision of Marpol due to be completed in 1996" *Source: Directive 94/63/EC, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:31994L0063

*Per the workspace's reading:* the Directive's own recitals tie its vessel-loading vapour-control ambitions to a parallel International Maritime Organization / Marpol Convention process, so a workspace tracking IMO/Marpol developments for vessel loading should treat this Directive's Article 1 scope (which already covers vessels) as the EU-internal counterpart to that international track.

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does this Directive create a direct compliance duty on a freight-forwarding workspace?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* No. The duties described in Section 8 run to EU Member States, which then regulate terminal operators and service stations; no source in this brief's corpus names a freight forwarder as an addressee of any Article.

**Q2: Do all EU Member States apply the same compliance timetable?**

*Analytical inference:* No — see Section 12. Spain and the Kingdom of the Netherlands (and, for a separate throughput tier, Spain and the Portuguese Republic) are each named for their own one-off or restructured derogations from the standard timetables in Articles 4 and 6.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

*Note: this Directive's obligations run principally to EU Member States, which transpose them into national law governing terminal operators and service stations. "Substantive requirements" here means the Directive's own stated obligations plus the operational implications those obligations carry for a workspace operating or chartering the road tankers, rail tankers and vessels this Directive's Article 1 scope names.*

**1. Directive scope.** FACT: "Scope This Directive shall apply to the operations, installations, vehicles and vessels used for storage, loading and transport of petrol from one terminal to another or from a terminal to a service station." *Source: Directive 94/63/EC, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:31994L0063

**2. Storage installation design and target reference value.** FACT: "Storage installations shall be designed and operated in accordance with the technical provisions of Annex I. These provisions are designed to reduce the total annual loss of petrol resulting from loading and storage at each storage installation at terminals to below the target reference value of 0,01 weight by weight (w/w) % of the throughput." *Source: Directive 94/63/EC, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:31994L0063

**3. Storage installation phased compliance timetable.** FACT: "The provisions of paragraph 1 shall apply: (a) from the date referred to in Article 10 for new installations; (b) three years from the date referred to in Article 10 for existing installations if the throughput loaded at a terminal is greater than 50 000 tonnes/year; (c) six years from the date referred to in Article 10 for existing installations if the throughput loaded at a terminal is greater than 25 000 tonnes/year; (d) nine years from the date referred to in Article 10 for all other existing storage installations at terminals." *Source: Directive 94/63/EC, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:31994L0063

*Operational implication:* a workspace should expect the largest-throughput existing terminals to reach compliant vapour-recovery status first among existing installations, with progressively smaller-throughput existing terminals given progressively longer transition windows (see the exact throughput tiers quoted above).

**4. Loading/unloading equipment design and target reference value.** FACT: "Loading and unloading equipment shall be designed and operated in accordance with the technical provisions of Annex II. These provisions are designed to reduce the total annual loss of petrol resulting from loading and unloading of mobile containers at terminals to below the target reference value of 0,005 w/w % of the throughput." *Source: Directive 94/63/EC, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:31994L0063

**5. Loading/unloading phased compliance timetable.** FACT: "The provisions of paragraph 1 shall apply: (a) from the date referred to in Article 10 for new terminals for loading onto road tankers, rail tankers and/or vessels; (b) three years from the date referred to in Article 10 for existing terminals for loading onto road tankers, rail tankers and/or vessels if the throughput is greater than 150 000 tonnes/year; (c) six years from the date referred to in Article 10 for existing terminals for loading onto road tankers and rail tankers if the throughput is greater than 25 000 tonnes/year; (d) nine years from the date referred to in Article 10 for all other existing loading installations at terminals for loading onto road tankers and rail tankers." *Source: Directive 94/63/EC, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:31994L0063

**6. Small-terminal derogation.** FACT: "By way of derogation, paragraphs 1 and 3 shall not apply: (a) to existing terminals with a throughput of less than 10 000 tonnes/year and; (b) to new terminals with a throughput of less than 5 000 tonnes/year located in small remote islands." *Source: Directive 94/63/EC, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:31994L0063

**7. Mobile container (road tanker, rail tanker, vessel) vapour-retention requirement.** FACT: "mobile containers which supply petrol to service stations and terminals shall be designed and operated so as to accept and retain return vapours from the storage installations at the service stations or terminals" *Source: Directive 94/63/EC, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:31994L0063

*Operational implication:* this is the requirement most directly relevant to a workspace operating or chartering the road tankers, rail tankers and vessels used to move petrol between terminals and service stations.

**8. Member State transposition deadline.** FACT: "Member States shall bring into force the laws, regulations and administrative provisions necessary to comply with this Directive by 31 December 1995." *Source: Directive 94/63/EC, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:31994L0063

**9. Petrol definition and its stated exclusion.** FACT: "'petrol` shall mean any petroleum derivative, with or without additives, having a reid vapour pressure of 27,6 kilopascals or more, which is intended for use as a fuel for motor vehicles, except liquefied petroleum gas (LPG);" *Source: Directive 94/63/EC, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:31994L0063

Obligations surveyed: 9; workspace-adjacent: 6; extracted as FACT: 9.

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

FACT: "The reports on the implementation of this Directive shall be established according to the procedure laid down in Article 5 of Council Directive 91/692/EEC of 23 December 1991 standardizing and rationalizing reports on the implementation of certain Directives relating to the environment" *Source: Directive 94/63/EC, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:31994L0063

*Operational implication:* this is a Member-State-to-Commission reporting channel under a separate, standardizing Directive (91/692/EEC); a freight forwarder has no filing duty of its own under Directive 94/63/EC.

# 11. Operational System Requirements

*Note: the technical specifications below (Annex IV) describe the bottom-loading and vapour-collection equipment an EU-compliant terminal gantry actually operates, recorded here so a workspace understands what equipment a compliant loading arrangement for road tankers involves.*

FACT: "mobile containers which supply petrol to service stations and terminals shall be designed and operated so as to accept and retain return vapours from the storage installations at the service stations or terminals" *Source: Directive 94/63/EC, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:31994L0063

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

FACT: "By way of derogation, paragraphs 1 and 3 shall not apply: (a) to existing terminals with a throughput of less than 10 000 tonnes/year and; (b) to new terminals with a throughput of less than 5 000 tonnes/year located in small remote islands." *Source: Directive 94/63/EC, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:31994L0063

FACT: "The Kingdom of Spain may grant a derogation of one year from the time limit set down in paragraph 2 (b)." *Source: Directive 94/63/EC, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:31994L0063

FACT: "This provision does not apply to top-loading tankers as long as that loading system is permitted." *Source: Directive 94/63/EC, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:31994L0063

*Analytical inference:* the Directive names several Member-State-specific derogations beyond the small-terminal carve-out above (a one-year Spanish derogation from the Article 4(2)(b) time limit; a similarly structured one-year derogation for Spain and the Portuguese Republic from the Article 6(2)(b) time limit; and a Netherlands derogation permitting a restructured, nationally-programmed timetable for service stations) — a workspace should not assume a single EU-wide compliance date applies uniformly to every Member State's terminals and service stations.

# 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

FACT: "emissions of volatile organic compounds (VOCs) from petrol and solvents in the Community would be in the order of 10 million tonnes per year if no control measures were taken" *Source: Directive 94/63/EC, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:31994L0063

*Analytical inference:* the Directive's own recitals frame petrol storage/distribution VOC emissions as a meaningful share of this wider Community VOC baseline, situating this Directive as one component of a broader EU air-quality and motor-fuel emissions programme rather than a standalone rule.

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 20 December 1994: Directive 94/63/EC adopted (the instrument's own dateline, "Done at Brussels").
- 31 December 1995: deadline for Member States to bring into force the national laws, regulations and administrative provisions necessary to comply with this Directive.

*Source for timeline entries: Directive 94/63/EC, EUR-Lex (https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:31994L0063).*

# 15. Sources

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks a UK Statutory Instrument amending the UK Emissions Trading Scheme (UK ETS) Order 2020's enforcement, penalty, and Schedule 5A registry-administrator provisions. It gives a freight-forwarding workspace with UK-regulated industrial installations or aircraft operations a single place to see what changed, when it took effect, and what the new penalty exposure is.

FACT: "The Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading Scheme (Amendment) Order 2022" *Source: legislation.gov.uk, The Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading Scheme (Amendment) Order 2022 (UK S.I. 2022/454). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2022/454*

FACT: "The United Kingdom Emissions Trading Scheme (the “UK ETS”) was established by the Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading Scheme Order 2020" *Source: legislation.gov.uk, The Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading Scheme (Amendment) Order 2022 (UK S.I. 2022/454). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2022/454*

FACT: "The UK ETS runs for ten “scheme years” beginning in 2021." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, The Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading Scheme (Amendment) Order 2022 (UK S.I. 2022/454). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2022/454*

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

FACT: "Operators of certain industrial installations and certain aircraft operators are required to monitor, report on, and surrender “allowances” equivalent to, their greenhouse gas emissions in each scheme year." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, The Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading Scheme (Amendment) Order 2022 (UK S.I. 2022/454). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2022/454*

*Operational implication:* a workspace that itself operates a UK-regulated industrial installation, or that operates aircraft within the UK ETS's own scope, sits inside the duty-holder class this Order's amendments reach; a workspace that only forwards or arranges freight without operating such an installation or aircraft does not.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

FACT: "Made 13th April 2022 Coming into force 14th April 2022" *Source: legislation.gov.uk, The Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading Scheme (Amendment) Order 2022 (UK S.I. 2022/454). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2022/454*

*Operational implication:* this Order has already been in force since 14th April 2022; a workspace within the duty-holder class described in Section 2 should treat the Section 8 amendments (new civil penalty amounts, the new obstruction offence, and the registry administrator's own enforcement-notice power) as already binding, not as a future compliance date to calendar.

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

FACT: "The Joint Committee on Statutory Instruments reported the 2020 Amendment Order on the grounds that there is a doubt as to whether it is intra vires in one respect, namely that the amendments were contained in an instrument subject to the negative, rather than the affirmative, resolution procedure" *Source: legislation.gov.uk, The Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading Scheme (Amendment) Order 2022 (UK S.I. 2022/454). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2022/454*

FACT: "(2) Omit articles 24, 26 and 31." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, The Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading Scheme (Amendment) Order 2022 (UK S.I. 2022/454). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2022/454*

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this procedural re-enactment (curing a vires doubt in how the 2020 Amendment Order's enforcement changes were originally made) does not itself change which enforcement and penalty provisions bind a duty holder; it changes only the procedural validity of how those provisions were adopted. Whether a specific workspace's own UK ETS-regulated installation or aircraft operation was affected by this procedural history is outside this brief's scope.

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does this Order create obligations on freight forwarders as such?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* No. Every substantive amendment in Section 8 runs to the UK ETS Order 2020's own duty-holder class -- operators of regulated installations and aircraft operators (Section 2) -- not to freight forwarders, carriers, or customs brokers as such.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

**1. Inspection power extended to an authorised person.** FACT: "In paragraph (1) after “regulator” insert “or an authorised person( 3 )" *Source: legislation.gov.uk, The Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading Scheme (Amendment) Order 2022 (UK S.I. 2022/454). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2022/454*

**2. New obstruction offence.** FACT: "(c) intentionally to obstruct the regulator, or an authorised person, in the exercise of a power referred to in paragraph (1)." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, The Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading Scheme (Amendment) Order 2022 (UK S.I. 2022/454). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2022/454*

**3. Registry administrator's own Schedule 5A enforcement-notice power.** FACT: "Where the registry administrator considers that a person has contravened, is contravening or is likely to contravene a requirement imposed on the person by or under Schedule 5A, the registry administrator may give notice (an “ enforcement notice ”) to the person." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, The Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading Scheme (Amendment) Order 2022 (UK S.I. 2022/454). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2022/454*

**4. Schedule 5A carve-out from the general enforcement-notice provision.** FACT: "in paragraph (i) after “this Order” insert “, except for Schedule 5A" *Source: legislation.gov.uk, The Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading Scheme (Amendment) Order 2022 (UK S.I. 2022/454). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2022/454*

**5. Uncapped daily penalty notices, timing.** FACT: "(7A) A penalty notice imposing a civil penalty that consists of a daily penalty under article 64A(2)(b) (for which there is no maximum) may be given at such intervals as the regulator considers appropriate." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, The Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading Scheme (Amendment) Order 2022 (UK S.I. 2022/454). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2022/454*

**6. New Article 64A liability trigger.** FACT: "(1) A person is liable to a civil penalty where the person fails to comply (or to comply on time) with the requirements of a notice (the “notice to return allowances”) given under article 34V." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, The Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading Scheme (Amendment) Order 2022 (UK S.I. 2022/454). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2022/454*

**7. New Article 64A penalty amounts.** FACT: "(a) £20,000; and (b) a daily penalty at a daily rate of £1,000 for each day that the person fails to comply with the requirements of the notice to return allowances, beginning with the day on which the initial notice is given." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, The Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading Scheme (Amendment) Order 2022 (UK S.I. 2022/454). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2022/454*

*Operational implication:* this is the concrete cost exposure a duty holder faces for failing to return allowances on notice -- a fixed penalty plus an uncapped daily rate running from the day the initial notice is given.

**8. Allowance-surrender deadline floor on permit revocation or surrender.** FACT: "(iii) where the permit is a greenhouse gas emissions permit, on or before a date set out in the notice (which must not be before 30th April in the end year), surrender allowances equal to the sum of" *Source: legislation.gov.uk, The Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading Scheme (Amendment) Order 2022 (UK S.I. 2022/454). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2022/454*

**9. Anti-double-penalty rule.** FACT: "The operator will not be subject to a second “excess emissions penalty” in respect of any failure to comply with this requirement" *Source: legislation.gov.uk, The Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading Scheme (Amendment) Order 2022 (UK S.I. 2022/454). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2022/454*

FACT: "This Order comes into force on the day after the day on which it is made." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, The Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading Scheme (Amendment) Order 2022 (UK S.I. 2022/454). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2022/454*

FACT: "This Order extends to the whole of the United Kingdom." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, The Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading Scheme (Amendment) Order 2022 (UK S.I. 2022/454). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2022/454*

**Qualification accounting.** Per-year trajectory: No phase-in is stated in Articles 1 to 14 and Schedule 6 of this Order. Exceptions and carve-outs: CAPTURED above (obligation 4, the Schedule 5A carve-out). Scope limits: No scope limits are stated in Articles 1 to 14 and Schedule 6 of this Order.

Obligations surveyed: 12; workspace-adjacent: 11; extracted as FACT: 11.

Shortfall: none -- K equals M, and the 15,978-character pool is well under the 200,000-character large-pool threshold. The one surveyed-but-excluded item is the Part 3 procedural re-enactment (Section 4), a correction to how the 2020 Amendment Order's own enforcement changes were adopted, not a duty running to any regulated operator.

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 2022: Enacted (legislation.gov.uk's own instrument-year identifier, UK S.I. 2022/454).
- 13th April 2022: This Order was made.
- 14th April 2022: This Order came into force.

*Source for timeline entries: legislation.gov.uk, UK S.I. 2022/454 (https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2022/454).*
