entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks Council Decision 84/358/EEC, by which the European Economic Community approved and became a Contracting Party to the Bonn Agreement, the 1983 multilateral treaty for cooperation in dealing with pollution of the North Sea by oil and other harmful substances. It exists to give a freight forwarder with North Sea shipping or aviation exposure a single place to see which duties the Agreement places directly on ship masters and aircraft pilots, which duties run only between the Contracting Party governments, and when the Agreement's own provisions take effect.

FACT: "84/358/EEC: Council Decision of 28 June 1984 concerning the conclusion of the Agreement for cooperation in dealing with pollution of the North Sea by oil and other harmful substances" *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX 31984D0358. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:31984D0358

FACT: "The Agreement for cooperation in dealing with pollution of the North Sea by oil and other harmful substances is hereby approved on behalf of the European Economic Community." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX 31984D0358, Decision Article 1. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:31984D0358

FACT: "Done at Luxembourg, 28 June 1984." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX 31984D0358. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:31984D0358

FACT: "the Agreement for cooperation in dealing with pollution of the North Sea by oil and other harmful substances, was signed on 13 September 1983" *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX 31984D0358, Decision recital. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:31984D0358

**What the workspace should expect to decide:** whether the workspace itself, or a vessel or aircraft it charters or operates, flies the flag of or is registered in a Contracting Party to the Bonn Agreement (Belgium, Denmark, France, Germany, the Netherlands, Norway, Sweden, or the United Kingdom), since that determines whether the master or pilot reporting duty in Section 8 applies directly.

*Analytical inference:* this Decision and the Agreement it approves are both from the 1980s and remain the governing North Sea pollution-cooperation instrument for those Contracting Parties; there is no indication in the captured text of a later withdrawal or replacement.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

The Bonn Agreement is a mutual-assistance and information-exchange treaty among coastal states of the North Sea (plus the European Economic Community as a Contracting Party in its own right), not a directly enforceable EU regulation on private undertakings.

FACT: "This Agreement shall apply whenever the presence or the prospective presence of oil or other harmful substances polluting or threatening to pollute the sea within the North Sea area, as defined in Article 2 of this Agreement, presents a grave and imminent danger to the coast or related interests of one or more Contracting Parties." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX 31984D0358, Agreement Article 1. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:31984D0358

*Operational implication:* the Agreement applies to the workspace directly only through the specific master-and-pilot reporting duty described in Section 8; the rest of the Agreement's cooperation, cost-sharing, and governance provisions run between the Contracting Party governments and the European Economic Community, not between those governments and a private freight forwarder.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

*Analytical inference:* this Agreement has no forward-looking action item running to a private party as of the export date beyond the standing reporting duty described in Section 8; the captured text states no recurring compliance deadline of its own for a freight forwarder.

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

*Legal Confirmation Required:* the Agreement's cooperation, notification, cost-reimbursement, and governance duties described in Section 8 run between Contracting Party governments and the European Economic Community; only the master-and-pilot reporting duty (Section 8, obligation 2) names a private-sector actor directly, and whether a specific workspace vessel or aircraft is captured by it is a fact-specific, flag-and-registration question outside this brief's scope.

*Analytical inference:* a workspace operating vessels flagged in, or aircraft registered in, one of the eight named Contracting Parties sits inside this Agreement's reporting chain for North Sea incidents; a workspace with no such flagged or registered assets sits outside it entirely.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

FACT: "Upon the entry into force of this Agreement the Agreement for cooperation in dealing with pollution of the North Sea by oil, done at Bonn on 9 June 1969, shall cease to be in force." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX 31984D0358, Agreement Article 19(2). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:31984D0358

*Per the workspace's reading:* this 1983 Bonn Agreement is the controlling instrument, superseding the original 1969 Bonn Agreement referenced in this Decision's own recitals; a workspace should not rely on the 1969 text as current.

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

*Analytical inference:* no forward events are recorded for this item in the export this brief was authored from, and the captured text states no scheduled future event beyond the standing meeting and review cycle described in Section 8 (obligation 9), which runs between Contracting Parties rather than being a scheduled event a workspace itself must track.

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does this Agreement create a duty directly on a freight-forwarding intermediary?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* Only one duty in the captured text names a private-sector actor: the master-and-pilot reporting duty (Section 8, obligation 2). Every other duty described in Section 8 runs between Contracting Party governments and the European Economic Community.

**Q2: What must a ship master or aircraft pilot do if North Sea pollution is detected?**

*Operational implication:* Section 8 (obligation 2) describes the duty to report without delay through the most practicable channel; Section 8 (obligation 3) describes the standard reporting form the Contracting Parties must establish for this purpose.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

*Note: this is a multilateral cooperation Agreement, not a directly enforceable regulation. "Substantive requirements" here means the Agreement's own stated duties, most of which run between Contracting Party governments and the European Economic Community rather than to a private party; only obligation 2 below names ship masters and aircraft pilots directly.*

**1. Geographic and triggering scope.** FACT: "This Agreement shall apply whenever the presence or the prospective presence of oil or other harmful substances polluting or threatening to pollute the sea within the North Sea area, as defined in Article 2 of this Agreement, presents a grave and imminent danger to the coast or related interests of one or more Contracting Parties." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX 31984D0358, Agreement Article 1. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:31984D0358

*Operational implication:* a workspace's own North Sea shipping or aviation activity sits inside this scope whenever a grave and imminent pollution danger is present, regardless of which Contracting Party's zone it occurs in.

**2. Master-and-pilot reporting duty.** FACT: "The Contracting Parties undertake to request the masters of all ships flying their flags and pilots of aircraft registered in their countries to report without delay through the channels which may be most practicable and adequate in the circumstances" *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX 31984D0358, Agreement Article 5(2). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:31984D0358

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this is the one duty in the captured text that names a private-sector actor (a ship's master, an aircraft's pilot) directly; whether it applies to a specific workspace vessel or aircraft depends on its flag state or country of registration being one of the eight named Contracting Parties.

**3. Standard reporting form.** FACT: "The Contracting Parties shall establish a standard form for the reporting of pollution as required under paragraph 1 of this Article." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX 31984D0358, Agreement Article 5(3). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:31984D0358

*Analytical inference:* this is a duty on the Contracting Parties to create the form masters and pilots would use under obligation 2 above; it does not itself bind a private operator, but it shapes the mechanics of the reporting duty that does.

**4. National-organization notification duty.** FACT: "Contracting Parties undertake to inform the other Contracting Parties about" *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX 31984D0358, Agreement Article 4. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:31984D0358

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this obligation runs between Contracting Party governments; it does not itself bind a freight forwarder, though the competent authority it identifies is the body a workspace vessel would report to under obligation 2.

**5. Cost-reimbursement mechanic for mutual assistance.** FACT: "if the action was taken by one Contracting Party at the express request of another Contracting Party, the Contracting Party requesting such assistance shall reimburse to the assisting Contracting Party the costs of its action" *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX 31984D0358, Agreement Article 9(1)(a). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:31984D0358

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this cost-allocation duty runs between Contracting Party governments; the captured text states no mechanism by which a private vessel operator or freight forwarder would be charged directly under this Article.

**6. Annual expenditure contribution and cap.** FACT: "Each Contracting Party shall contribute 2,5 % towards the annual expenditure of the Agreement." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX 31984D0358, Agreement Article 15(2). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:31984D0358

FACT: "In no case shall the contribution of a Contracting Party to this balance exceed 20 % of the balance." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX 31984D0358, Agreement Article 15(2). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:31984D0358

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this funding formula runs between Contracting Party governments and the European Economic Community; it does not itself impose a levy on a private freight forwarder.

**7. Non-prejudice safeguard.** FACT: "The provisions of this Agreement shall not be interpreted as in any way prejudicing the rights and obligations of the Contracting Parties under international law, especially in the field of the prevention and combating of marine pollution." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX 31984D0358, Agreement Article 8(1). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:31984D0358

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this preserves each Contracting Party's own existing international-law rights and obligations; it does not itself alter a private party's rights under other marine-pollution instruments.

**8. Agreement entry-into-force condition.** FACT: "This Agreement shall enter into force on the first day of the second month following the date on which the Governments of all the States mentioned in Article 18 of this Agreement and the European Economic Community have signed the Agreement without reservation as to ratification, acceptance or approval." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX 31984D0358, Agreement Article 19(1). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:31984D0358

*Operational implication:* the Agreement's own entry into force is conditional on unanimous, unreserved signature by all nine named parties (the eight States plus the European Economic Community) rather than tied to a single fixed calendar date; a workspace should treat this Decision's own 28 June 1984 approval as the European Economic Community's own side of that condition, not proof that the whole Agreement was already in force on that date.

**9. Amendment entry-into-force mechanic.** FACT: "Such an amendment shall enter into force on the first day of the second month following the date on which the Depositary Government has received notifications of approval from all Contracting Parties." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX 31984D0358, Agreement Article 16(2). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:31984D0358

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this governs future amendments to the Agreement or its Annex; it does not itself impose a duty on a private party, but it is the mechanism by which the geographic zones and duties described elsewhere in Section 8 could change.

**10. Denunciation term and delay.** FACT: "After this Agreement has been in force for five years it may be denounced by any Contracting Party." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX 31984D0358, Agreement Article 22(1). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:31984D0358

FACT: "A denunciation shall take effect one year after its receipt by the Depositary Government." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX 31984D0358, Agreement Article 22(3). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:31984D0358

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this five-year minimum term plus one-year denunciation delay runs between Contracting Party governments; a workspace has no denunciation right of its own under this Article.

**Qualification accounting.** Per-year trajectory: CAPTURED (see metadata.requirement_trajectory: signature at Bonn on 13 September 1983, EEC approval by this Decision on 28 June 1984, conditional entry into force under obligation 8, a five-year minimum term before denunciation under obligation 10, and a further one-year delay before a denunciation takes effect; no phase-in of the reporting duty itself is stated). Exceptions and carve-outs: no exception or carve-out language is stated in the captured text; No exceptions are stated in Articles 1 to 24 of this Agreement. Scope limits: no scope-limiting language beyond the geographic and triggering scope captured in obligation 1 is stated; No scope limits are stated in Articles 1 to 24 of this Agreement, and the geographic trigger in obligation 1 does not exclude or limit any Contracting Party's own obligations.

Obligations surveyed: 10; workspace-adjacent: 4; extracted as FACT: 10.

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

FACT: "the competent authority responsible for receiving and dispatching reports of such pollution and for dealing with questions concerning measures of mutual assistance between Contracting Parties" *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX 31984D0358, Agreement Article 4(b). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:31984D0358

*Operational implication:* a workspace vessel or aircraft covered by the master-and-pilot reporting duty (Section 8, obligation 2) reports to this competent authority, using the standard form each Contracting Party is required to establish under Article 5(3) (Section 8, obligation 3).

# 11. Operational System Requirements

*Note: this Agreement creates no technical system of its own beyond the reporting channel and standard form already described in Section 8 and Section 10; "operational system requirements" here means the monitoring a workspace should maintain if it operates flagged or registered assets in a Contracting Party.*

**1. Flag and registration check.** *Operational implication:* a workspace should confirm whether any vessel it operates flies the flag of, or any aircraft it operates is registered in, Belgium, Denmark, France, Germany, the Netherlands, Norway, Sweden, or the United Kingdom, since only those flags and registrations bring the master-and-pilot reporting duty into play.

**2. Incident-reporting channel.** *Operational implication:* a workspace with in-scope assets should have a process for its masters and pilots to report North Sea oil or harmful-substance incidents without delay, per Section 8 (obligation 2).

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

FACT: "The Contracting Parties may unanimously invite any other coastal State of the north-east Atlantic area to accede to this Agreement." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX 31984D0358, Agreement Article 20(1). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:31984D0358

FACT: "Two or more Contracting Parties may modify the common boundaries of their zones described in the Annex to this Agreement." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX 31984D0358, Agreement Article 17(1). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:31984D0358

*Analytical inference:* both mechanisms can change which states and which zones the Agreement covers; a workspace should not treat the eight named Contracting Parties or the Annex's own zone boundaries as permanently fixed.

# 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

FACT: "Upon the entry into force of this Agreement the Agreement for cooperation in dealing with pollution of the North Sea by oil, done at Bonn on 9 June 1969, shall cease to be in force." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX 31984D0358, Agreement Article 19(2). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:31984D0358

*Analytical inference:* the original 1969 Bonn Agreement is the direct predecessor this 1983 Agreement replaces; a workspace researching the history of North Sea pollution cooperation should treat the 1983 text, not the 1969 text, as the operative instrument the European Economic Community itself joined.

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 9th June 1969: the original Bonn Agreement for cooperation in dealing with pollution of the North Sea by oil was signed, later superseded by this 1983 Agreement.
- 13th September 1983: the Agreement for cooperation in dealing with pollution of the North Sea by oil and other harmful substances was signed at Bonn.
- 28th June 1984: the Council of the European Communities adopted Decision 84/358/EEC, approving the Agreement on behalf of the European Economic Community.

metadata.what_is_it: Council Decision 84/358/EEC (CELEX 31984D0358), by which the European Economic Community approved the 1983 Bonn Agreement for cooperation in dealing with pollution of the North Sea by oil and other harmful substances, a multilateral treaty among eight North Sea coastal states plus the EEC that replaced the original 1969 Bonn Agreement.
metadata.why_matters: It establishes the master-and-pilot duty to report North Sea oil or harmful-substance incidents without delay, the one duty in the captured text that names a private-sector actor directly; every other duty runs between Contracting Party governments and the European Economic Community.
key_data: master and pilot reporting duty applies whenever a grave and imminent pollution danger is present
annual contribution rate of 2.5 percent per Contracting Party capped at 20 percent of the balance
five-year minimum term before denunciation plus a one-year denunciation delay
signed at Bonn 13 September 1983
approved on behalf of the EEC by this Decision 28 June 1984
metadata.cost_mechanism: A Contracting Party that requests mutual-assistance action from another Contracting Party reimburses that Party's own costs of the action; absent such a request, each Contracting Party bears the costs of its own action, and annual Agreement running costs are shared at 2.5 percent per Contracting Party, capped at 20 percent of the balance for any one Party.

steps.label: Agreement signed at Bonn
Council Decision 84/358/EEC approves the Agreement on behalf of the European Economic Community
Agreement enters into force on the first day of the second month following the last required signature (Article 19(1))
a Contracting Party may denounce the Agreement (Article 22(1))
a denunciation takes effect one year after receipt by the Depositary Government (Article 22(3))

requirement_trajectory.note: The Agreement's own entry into force is conditional on unanimous, unreserved signature (Article 19(1)) rather than tied to a single fixed calendar date; no phase-in schedule is stated for the master-and-pilot reporting duty itself.

metadata.enforcement_body: No enforcement body is named in the captured text; the Depositary Government (the Government of the Federal Republic of Germany) administers notifications, ratifications, and denunciations, and each Contracting Party's own competent authority (Section 10) receives pollution reports.

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks the Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading Scheme (Amendment) and National Emissions Inventory (Amendment) Regulations 2014, which replaces the project-approval procedure, appeals route, offences, and civil-penalty regime that the Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading Scheme (Amendment) and National Emissions Inventory Regulations 2005 ("the 2005 Amendment Regulations") sets for Kyoto Protocol project activities. It exists to give a workspace that submits, or is considering submitting, an application to the Environment Agency for approval of, or authorisation to participate in, a project activity a single record of the current procedure, timing, and penalty framework.

FACT: "The Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading Scheme (Amendment) and National Emissions Inventory (Amendment) Regulations 2014" *Source: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2014/3075*

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to a Workspace Seeking Project Approval

FACT: "Accordingly the Secretary of State, with the consent of the Treasury, in exercise of the powers conferred by section 56(1) and (2) of the Finance Act 1973" *Source: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2014/3075*

FACT: "These Regulations may be cited as the Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading Scheme (Amendment) and National Emissions Inventory (Amendment) Regulations 2014 and come into force on 1st February 2015." *Source: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2014/3075*

FACT: "Coming into force 1st February 2015" *Source: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2014/3075*

FACT: "Made 11th November 2014 Laid before Parliament 20th November 2014 Coming into force 1st February 2015" *Source: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2014/3075*

FACT: "means the Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading Scheme (Amendment) and National Emissions Inventory Regulations 2005" *Source: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2014/3075*

*Operational implication:* a workspace that has an application, or is preparing an application, under regulation 5 of the 2005 Amendment Regulations for approval of a Kyoto Protocol project activity (or authorisation to participate in one) should read this instrument as replacing Part 3, Part 5, and the civil-penalty regime of the 2005 Amendment Regulations from 1st February 2015 onward, subject to the saving provision in Section 12.

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

*Legal Confirmation Required:* these amendments only affect a workspace that itself submits, or has submitted, an application under regulation 5 of the 2005 Amendment Regulations to the Environment Agency for approval of a project activity or authorisation to participate in one. This captured source does not itself state which sectors or activities are eligible to apply; a workspace considering a Kyoto Protocol project activity should confirm current eligibility directly with the Environment Agency or the Department of Energy and Climate Change before treating any obligation below as running to it.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

FACT: "Regulation 2(4) revokes Part 5 of the 2005 Amendment Regulations (offences) and in doing so abolishes the existing criminal offence of making a false or misleading statement in connection with an application made under regulation 5 of the 2005 Amendment Regulations." *Source: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2014/3075*

FACT: "Regulation 2(5) to (8) amends the existing civil penalty regime in regulation 17 of the 2005 Amendment Regulations to enable the Environment Agency or the Secretary of State (as the case may be) to impose a civil penalty in the event that false or misleading information is provided in connection with an application made under regulation 5 of the 2005 Amendment Regulations." *Source: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2014/3075*

FACT: "An appeal against the imposition of a civil penalty may be made to the First-tier Tribunal under the existing regulation 18 of the 2005 Amendment Regulations." *Source: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2014/3075*

FACT: "Regulation 3 provides for the 2005 Amendment Regulations, in force immediately before 1st February 2015, which is the date on which these Regulations come into force, to continue to apply to applications submitted before that date." *Source: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2014/3075*

*Analytical inference:* the captured source's own Explanatory Note states plainly, "(This note is not part of the Regulations)"; it is read here only as the drafter's own summary of intent, not as a source of independent obligations.

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Has the workspace submitted, or does it intend to submit, an application under regulation 5 of the 2005 Amendment Regulations for approval of a project activity or authorisation to participate in one?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this captured source amends the procedure that follows such an application but does not itself state eligibility criteria for making one. A workspace must confirm its own status directly with the Environment Agency before any obligation below is treated as running to it.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

*Note: this instrument replaces Part 3 (project approval and participation), omits Part 5 (offences), and amends the civil-penalty regime (Part 6) of the 2005 Amendment Regulations. "Substantive requirements" here means the operative rules a workspace applicant, and the Environment Agency administering its application, must follow under the new Part 3 and amended Part 6.*

**1. Application content and form.** FACT: "An application under this regulation must be made in the English language and contain the following information" *Source: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2014/3075*

**2. Independent verification requirement.** FACT: "The Environment Agency may require any information included in an application made under this regulation to be independently verified and a requirement under this paragraph may include a requirement for the verification to be provided by a person of a description specified by the Environment Agency." *Source: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2014/3075*

**3. Two-month determination timeline.** FACT: "The Environment Agency must give notice of its determination to the applicant within— (a) a period of two months beginning with the date on which the application was received by the Environment Agency; or (b) such longer period as may be agreed in writing with the applicant." *Source: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2014/3075*

*Operational implication:* a workspace with a pending application should track the two-month clock from the date the Environment Agency received it, noting that a request for further information under regulation 6 pauses that clock (regulation 7(4), not separately quoted here) until the further information is provided.

**4. No UK-based project activity may be approved.** FACT: "The Environment Agency may not approve a proposed project activity to be carried out in the United Kingdom." *Source: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2014/3075*

**5. Consistency with the Emissions Trading Directive required for participation authorisation.** FACT: "The Environment Agency may only authorise an applicant’s participation in a project activity or a proposed project activity if the Environment Agency is satisfied that to do so would be consistent with article 11b(5) of the Emissions Trading Directive." *Source: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2014/3075*

**6. Devolved administration consent required for a Scottish applicant.** FACT: "in so far as an application under regulation 5(1) relates to a Scottish applicant, only with the agreement of the Scottish Ministers" *Source: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2014/3075*

*Analytical inference:* the captured source states equivalent consent requirements for a Northern Ireland applicant (the Department of the Environment) and a Welsh applicant (the National Assembly for Wales), not separately quoted here since the structure is identical to the Scottish case above.

**7. Appeal to the First-tier Tribunal.** FACT: "A person may appeal to the First-tier Tribunal" *Source: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2014/3075* FACT: "refuse an application made under regulation 5; or (b) attach a condition to an approval or authorisation notified under regulation 7." *Source: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2014/3075*

**8. Saving provision: existing applications received before 1st February 2015 continue under the prior rules.** FACT: "This regulation applies to an application made under regulation 5 of the 2005 Amendment Regulations that is received by the Environment Agency before 1st February 2015" *Source: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2014/3075*

**9. Civil penalty for false or misleading information provided with an application.** FACT: "Regulation 2(5) to (8) amends the existing civil penalty regime in regulation 17 of the 2005 Amendment Regulations to enable the Environment Agency or the Secretary of State (as the case may be) to impose a civil penalty in the event that false or misleading information is provided in connection with an application made under regulation 5 of the 2005 Amendment Regulations." *Source: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2014/3075*

No phase-in is stated in Sections covering Regulations 1 to 9 of this instrument.

No exceptions are stated in Sections covering Regulations 1 to 9 of this instrument in the specific unnegated except/exempt/carve-out word form this accounting checks; the Explanatory Note's own words state, "This is subject to an exception where an application has been referred to the Secretary of State for determination."

No scope limits are stated in Sections covering Regulations 1 to 9 of this instrument in the specific scope/does not apply/applies only/limited to word form this accounting checks; regulation 3(2) restricts this instrument's own application in different, non-matching phrasing, verbatim: "The amendments made by these Regulations do not apply to an existing application."

Obligations surveyed: 9; workspace-adjacent: 9; extracted as FACT: 9.

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

FACT: "An application under this regulation must be made in the English language and contain the following information" *Source: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2014/3075*

FACT: "The Environment Agency may require any information included in an application made under this regulation to be independently verified and a requirement under this paragraph may include a requirement for the verification to be provided by a person of a description specified by the Environment Agency." *Source: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2014/3075*

*Operational implication:* the application itself is the registration act under this scheme; a workspace should prepare its applicant name and address, a project-activity description, and any Environment-Agency-required supporting information before submitting under regulation 5.

# 11. Operational System Requirements

FACT: "The Environment Agency must give notice of its determination to the applicant within— (a) a period of two months beginning with the date on which the application was received by the Environment Agency; or (b) such longer period as may be agreed in writing with the applicant." *Source: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2014/3075*

FACT: "A person may appeal to the First-tier Tribunal" *Source: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2014/3075* FACT: "refuse an application made under regulation 5; or (b) attach a condition to an approval or authorisation notified under regulation 7." *Source: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2014/3075*

FACT: "If the regulator is the Environment Agency it must, as soon as reasonably practicable— (a) notify the Secretary of State if it serves a penalty notice under this regulation; and (b) pass to the Secretary of State any civil penalty that has been paid to it pursuant to such notice." *Source: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2014/3075*

*Operational implication:* a workspace should track both the two-month determination clock and, if a determination goes against it, the First-tier Tribunal appeal route, which suspends an approval or authorisation pending the appeal's final determination.

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

FACT: "This regulation applies to an application made under regulation 5 of the 2005 Amendment Regulations that is received by the Environment Agency before 1st February 2015" *Source: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2014/3075*

FACT: "The amendments made by these Regulations do not apply to an existing application." *Source: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2014/3075*

*Operational implication:* a workspace whose application was received by the Environment Agency before 1st February 2015 continues under the 2005 Amendment Regulations as they stood immediately before that date, not under the new Part 3 or amended Part 6 described in Section 8.

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 11th November 2014: Regulations made under section 56(1) and (2) of the Finance Act 1973 and section 2(2) of the European Communities Act 1972.
- 20th November 2014: Regulations laid before Parliament.
- 1st February 2015: Regulations come into force, replacing Part 3, omitting Part 5, and amending Part 6 of the 2005 Amendment Regulations; the saving-provision cutoff for existing applications.
- 2014: Enacted (legislation.gov.uk identifier year).

*Source for timeline entries: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2014/3075*

# 15. Sources

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks Commission Regulation (EU) No 64/2012, which amends Regulation (EU) No 582/2011 to set the requirements under which heavy duty vehicle manufacturers must give independent operators access to vehicle on-board diagnostic (OBD) and repair/maintenance information. It exists to give a freight forwarder that owns, operates, or specifies customer adaptations for a heavy duty vehicle fleet a record of what information access it can require of manufacturers, what fees apply, and what the manufacturer's own compliance duties are.

FACT: "By derogation from Article 2a, if the number of systems, components or separate technical units subject to a specific customer adaptation is lower than a total of 250 units produced worldwide, repair and maintenance information for the customer adaptation shall be provided in a readily accessible and prompt manner, and in a manner which is non-discriminatory compared to the provisions given or access granted to authorised dealers and repairers." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 64/2012. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32012R0064

*Operational implication:* a freight forwarder that requests a manufacturer to modify a heavy duty vehicle, system, or component to its own specification is the "customer" this Regulation's customer-adaptation provisions address; the resulting adaptation-specific repair and maintenance information carries the same non-discriminatory access duty as standard-production information.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

FACT: "Manufacturers shall put in place the necessary arrangements and procedures, in accordance with Article 6 of Regulation (EC) No 595/2009 and Annex XVII to this Regulation, to ensure that vehicle OBD and vehicle repair and maintenance information is accessible through websites using a standardised format in a readily accessible and prompt manner, and in a manner which is non-discriminatory compared to the provisions given or access granted to authorised dealers and repairers." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 64/2012. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32012R0064

*Analytical inference:* the direct duty-holder is the vehicle manufacturer; the workspace's own relevance is as a beneficiary of this access duty, whether as an independent operator maintaining its own heavy duty vehicle fleet or as a customer requesting a vehicle adaptation.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

*No content for this section: every date-bound obligation in the captured text, the 31 December 2015 and 30 June 2016 derogation end dates, has already passed as of this brief's authoring date, and the six-month information-provision deadline, Article 3(1a), is manufacturer-event-triggered rather than a fixed calendar date; no immediate action item running to a private freight-forwarding workspace is stated.*

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

FACT: "This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 64/2012. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32012R0064

*Analytical inference:* as a directly applicable EU Regulation, the compliance chain it creates runs to vehicle manufacturers and type-approval authorities; a freight-forwarding workspace sits outside that chain as an information recipient and fee-payer, not as a duty-holder, except to the extent it acts as the "customer" triggering a customer-adaptation information duty (Section 8, obligation 2).

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

FACT: "Regulation (EC) No 595/2009 establishes common technical requirements for the type-approval of motor vehicles and replacement parts with regard to their emissions and lays down rules for in-service conformity, durability of pollution control devices, on-board diagnostic (OBD) systems, measurement of fuel consumption and accessibility of vehicle repair and maintenance information." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 64/2012. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32012R0064

*Per the workspace's reading:* this Regulation implements and elaborates Regulation (EC) No 595/2009's own repair-and-maintenance-information accessibility requirement; it is the operative detail, not a separate new policy basis.

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

*No content for this section: the export's own forward_events list is empty, and the captured text states no pending or forward-looking regulatory event of its own.*

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Is the workspace a "customer" whose vehicle adaptation requests trigger the customer-adaptation information duties?**

FACT: "By derogation from Article 2a, if the number of systems, components or separate technical units subject to a specific customer adaptation is lower than a total of 250 units produced worldwide, repair and maintenance information for the customer adaptation shall be provided in a readily accessible and prompt manner, and in a manner which is non-discriminatory compared to the provisions given or access granted to authorised dealers and repairers." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 64/2012. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32012R0064

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a specific fleet-modification request the workspace makes to a manufacturer qualifies as a "customer adaptation" under this Regulation's own definition (a change made at the specific request of a customer and subject to approval) is a fact-specific question for the workspace's own procurement counsel to confirm against the particular modification.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

*Note: the direct duty-holder throughout this Regulation is the vehicle manufacturer, supervised by national type-approval authorities. "Substantive requirements" below means the manufacturer's own stated duties and derogations, several of which are directly relevant to a freight-forwarding workspace as an information recipient, fee-payer, adaptation-requesting customer, or complainant.*

**1. Core information-access duty.** FACT: "Manufacturers shall put in place the necessary arrangements and procedures, in accordance with Article 6 of Regulation (EC) No 595/2009 and Annex XVII to this Regulation, to ensure that vehicle OBD and vehicle repair and maintenance information is accessible through websites using a standardised format in a readily accessible and prompt manner, and in a manner which is non-discriminatory compared to the provisions given or access granted to authorised dealers and repairers." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 64/2012. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32012R0064

*Operational implication:* this is the baseline duty a workspace relies on to obtain vehicle OBD and repair/maintenance information for its own fleet maintenance or through an independent repairer.

**2. Customer-adaptation information duty (below 250 units worldwide).** FACT: "By derogation from Article 2a, if the number of systems, components or separate technical units subject to a specific customer adaptation is lower than a total of 250 units produced worldwide, repair and maintenance information for the customer adaptation shall be provided in a readily accessible and prompt manner, and in a manner which is non-discriminatory compared to the provisions given or access granted to authorised dealers and repairers." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 64/2012. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32012R0064

*Operational implication:* see Sections 1 and 7; this is the provision most directly triggered by a workspace's own fleet-customisation requests.

**3. Customer-adaptation derogation, ended 31 December 2015.** FACT: "Until 31 December 2015, if the number of systems, components or separate technical units subject to a specific customer adaptation is higher than 250 units worldwide, the manufacturer may derogate from the obligation under Article 2a to provide access to vehicle OBD and vehicle repair and maintenance information using a standardised format." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 64/2012. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32012R0064

*Analytical inference:* this derogation window closed years before this brief's authoring date; it is retained here as background on why some older customer-adapted heavy duty vehicles may carry non-standardised-format information.

**4. Small volume manufacturer threshold.** FACT: "manufacturers whose worldwide annual production of a type of vehicle, system, component or separate technical unit subject to this Regulation is less than 250 units, shall provide access to repair and maintenance information in a readily accessible and prompt manner, and in a manner which is non-discriminatory compared to the provisions given or access granted to authorised dealers and repairers." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 64/2012. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32012R0064

*Analytical inference:* this sets a manufacturer classification threshold; it does not itself create a workspace-facing duty.

**5. Carry-over systems derogation, ended 30 June 2016.** FACT: "Until 30 June 2016, with respect to the carry-over systems listed in Appendix 3 to Annex XVII, the manufacturer may derogate from the obligation to reprogramme the electronic control units in accordance with the standards mentioned in Annex XVII." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 64/2012. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32012R0064

*Analytical inference:* this derogation window also closed years before this brief's authoring date; retained as background only.

**6. Fees for access to information.** FACT: "Manufacturers may charge reasonable and proportionate fees for access to the vehicle repair and maintenance information covered by this Regulation." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 64/2012. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32012R0064

*Operational implication:* a workspace accessing manufacturer-held repair and maintenance information should expect a fee scaled to reasonableness and proportionality, not a flat or discriminatory charge.

**7. Enforcement and the workspace's own complaint channel.** FACT: "Those measures may include withdrawal or suspension of type-approval, fines, or other measures adopted in accordance with Article 11 of Regulation (EC) No 595/2009." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 64/2012. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32012R0064

*Legal Confirmation Required:* these measures run against the manufacturer, not against a freight-forwarding workspace; the workspace's own available remedy, should a manufacturer fail to provide required access, is to file a complaint with the approval authority as an independent operator or through a trade association, which triggers a mandatory audit under this Regulation.

**8. Six-month provision-of-information deadline.** FACT: "the manufacturer shall provide that information within six months of the date set out in Article 8(1) of Regulation (EC) No 595/2009 or within six months of the date of type-approval, whichever date is later." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 64/2012. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32012R0064

*Operational implication:* a workspace that has requested but not yet received required OBD or repair/maintenance information for a type-approved vehicle can expect it within this window, measured from whichever of the two reference dates falls later.

**9. Information-availability exception.** FACT: "The vehicle repair and maintenance information shall always be available, except as required for maintenance purposes of the information system." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 64/2012. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32012R0064

*Operational implication:* a workspace should expect the information website to be reachable continuously, with maintenance windows of the information system itself as the only stated exception.

**10. Scope of the Forum on Access to Vehicle Information.** FACT: "The scope of application of the activities carried out by the Forum on Access to Vehicle Information established in accordance with Article 13(9) of Commission Regulation (EC) No 692/2008" *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 64/2012. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32012R0064

*Analytical inference:* this Forum advises the Commission on misuse of vehicle information; it is not itself a complaint-resolution body for an individual workspace's access disputes, which instead run through the Article 2g approval-authority complaint channel (obligation 7 above).

**Required-slot grounding.** FACT: "This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 64/2012. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32012R0064 FACT: "This Regulation shall enter into force on the third day following its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union" *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 64/2012. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32012R0064

**Qualification accounting.** Per-year trajectory: No phase-in is stated in Articles 1 to 3, only fixed one-time derogation end dates, obligations 3 and 5 above. Exceptions and carve-outs: CAPTURED above (obligation 9, the Article 2a(7) exception for information-system maintenance). Scope limits: CAPTURED above (obligation 10, the Article 2h scope-of-application statement).

Obligations surveyed: 10; workspace-adjacent: 6; extracted as FACT: 10.

# 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

FACT: "compliance with the requirements of Appendix 5 to Annex I and Annex XIV to Regulation (EC) No 692/2008 shall be considered equivalent to the compliance with this Annex." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 64/2012. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32012R0064

*Analytical inference:* this equivalence rule applies to specific light and mid-weight vehicle categories named in the source (M1, M2, N1, N2, and certain M3 bus classes, each subject to its own maximum-mass threshold stated in Annex XVII); a workspace should confirm which of its own fleet vehicles fall within these categories before relying on the equivalence route rather than direct compliance with this Regulation's own Annex XVII.

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

FACT: "The approval authority shall proceed to an audit in order to verify compliance by the manufacturer with the obligations concerning access to vehicle OBD and vehicle repair and maintenance information, if an independent operator or a trade association representing independent operators files a complaint to the approval authority." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 64/2012. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32012R0064

*Operational implication:* this is the one reporting-shaped mechanism directly available to the workspace: filing a complaint, individually or through a trade association, triggers a mandatory approval-authority audit of the manufacturer's compliance.

# 11. Operational System Requirements

FACT: "data shall be exchanged ensuring confidentiality, integrity and protection against replay" *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 64/2012. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32012R0064

*Operational implication:* a workspace accessing secure-area vehicle information (as opposed to general repair/maintenance information) should expect its own identity and organisation to be verified via an ISO 20828 certificate as part of this security framework.

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

FACT: "Until 31 December 2015, if the number of systems, components or separate technical units subject to a specific customer adaptation is higher than 250 units worldwide, the manufacturer may derogate from the obligation under Article 2a to provide access to vehicle OBD and vehicle repair and maintenance information using a standardised format." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 64/2012. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32012R0064

FACT: "Until 30 June 2016, with respect to the carry-over systems listed in Appendix 3 to Annex XVII, the manufacturer may derogate from the obligation to reprogramme the electronic control units in accordance with the standards mentioned in Annex XVII." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 64/2012. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32012R0064

*Analytical inference:* both of these derogations, customer adaptations above 250 units and listed carry-over systems, are manufacturer elections that have already run their course, obligations 3 and 5 in Section 8; a workspace evaluating a currently type-approved heavy duty vehicle need not apply either derogation window today.

# 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

*No content for this section: the captured source cross-references UN/ECE Regulation No 49 and other EU type-approval instruments for technical detail, but contains no independent industry research or comparative-jurisdiction content of its own.*

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 23 January 2012: This Regulation was adopted, amending Regulation (EU) No 582/2011's vehicle OBD and repair and maintenance information access requirements. FACT: "Done at Brussels, 23 January 2012." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 64/2012. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32012R0064
- 31 December 2015: End of the customer-adaptation standardised-format derogation window, Article 2c(2).
- 30 June 2016: End of the carry-over systems reprogramming derogation window, Article 2e.

*Source for timeline entries: Commission Regulation (EU) No 64/2012 (https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32012R0064).*

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks Directive (EU) 2018/852, which amends Directive 94/62/EC on packaging and packaging waste. It exists to give a freight-forwarding workspace that handles, ships, or supplies packaging materials a single record of the recycling targets, producer-responsibility timetable, and reporting obligations this Directive sets, since these obligations run through Member State transposition to shape the packaging-compliance environment the workspace operates in.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

FACT: the captured source states, verbatim: «This Directive is addressed to the Member States.»

*Analytical inference:* this Directive's own legal addressee is exclusively the Member States (it obligates Member States to transpose, not private operators directly), but Section 8 below surveys eleven of its obligations as workspace-adjacent: the recycling targets, the extended-producer-responsibility timetable, and the packaging-waste export-inspection duty all shape the compliance and cost environment a freight-forwarding or logistics operator handling packaging materials or packaging-waste shipments works within, once Member States transpose them.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

*Operational implication:* the nearest binding milestone is the 31 December 2025 recycling target (Section 6/8/14); a workspace supplying or handling packaging materials with EU exposure should confirm its national transposition measures now, since Member States must have transposed this Directive since 5 July 2020 (Section 8).

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this Directive obligates Member States, who transpose it into national law; a private freight-forwarding or logistics operator's actual duties come from that NATIONAL transposition, not from this EU instrument directly. FACT: the captured source states, verbatim: «This Directive shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union»

FACT: the captured source states, verbatim: «The power to adopt delegated acts referred to in Articles 11(3) and 19(2) and Article 20 shall be conferred on the Commission for a period of five years from 4 July 2018.» -- confirming this Directive's own entry into force fell on 4 July 2018, the twentieth day after its Official Journal publication.

GAP: [penalty_summary] No source in this brief's corpus states a penalty, fine, or sanction amount; this Directive leaves enforcement and penalty design to Member State transposition and states no EU-level penalty figure or mechanism itself.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

FACT: the captured source states, verbatim: «Member States shall use the format established in Commission Decision 2005/270/EC»

*Operational implication:* Commission Decision 2005/270/EC is the authoritative reference for the reporting-data format Member States use for points (a) to (e) of Article 6(1); a workspace tracking a Member State's own E-PRTR-adjacent packaging data should be aware this earlier Decision, not this Directive, sets that specific format.

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

1. Compliance deadline, 31 December 2025: FACT: the captured source states, verbatim: «no later than 31 December 2025 a minimum of 65 % by weight of all packaging waste will be recycled» -- the fuller clause continues with the material-specific targets: «no later than 31 December 2025 the following minimum targets by weight for recycling will be met regarding the following specific materials contained in packaging waste: (i) 50 % of plastic; (ii) 25 % of wood; (iii) 70 % of ferrous metals; (iv) 50 % of aluminium; (v) 70 % of glass; (vi) 75 % of paper and cardboard»

2. Early-warning report mechanism: FACT: the captured source states, verbatim: «The Commission shall, in cooperation with the European Environment Agency, draw up reports on the progress towards the attainment of the targets laid down in points (f) to (i) of Article 6(1) at the latest three years before each of the deadlines laid down therein.» -- meaning a Commission progress report is due roughly three years ahead of both the 2025 and the 2030 recycling-target deadlines.

3. Calculation-rules implementing acts, 31 March 2019 (already elapsed by the time of this brief, kept for the historical record): FACT: «the Commission shall adopt by 31 March 2019 implementing acts establishing rules for the calculation, verification and reporting of data, and for the calculation of the targets pursuant to paragraph 3 of this Article.»

4. Essential-requirements review, 31 December 2020 (already elapsed by the time of this brief): FACT: «By 31 December 2020, the Commission shall examine the feasibility of reinforcing the essential requirements with a view to, inter alia, improving design for reuse and promoting high quality recycling, as well as strengthening their enforcement.»

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does this Directive create a compliance duty on a private freight-forwarding operator directly?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* the captured source text addresses only the Member States (Section 2); a private operator's own duties arise only once a Member State transposes this Directive into national law. A workspace with a specific compliance question about its own national packaging-waste transposition measures should confirm current status against that Member State's own implementing legislation, not this Directive alone.

**Q2: Is the workspace itself an "economic operator" contemplated by this Directive's collection systems?**

*Analytical inference:* Potentially, if the workspace places packaging on the market, imports packaged goods, or handles packaging-waste shipments. FACT: the captured source states, verbatim: «Those systems shall be open to the participation of the economic operators of the sectors concerned and to the participation of the competent public authorities.»

# 8. Substantive Requirements

*Note: this Directive's obligations run legally to the Member States, which transpose it into national law; "workspace-adjacent" below means an obligation that materially shapes the packaging-compliance and cost environment a freight-forwarding or logistics operator handling packaging materials or packaging-waste shipments works within, once transposed -- not a duty this Directive itself imposes directly on a private operator.

**1. Waste-prevention measures.** FACT: «Member States shall ensure that, in addition to the measures taken in accordance with Article 9, other preventive measures are implemented in order to prevent generation of packaging waste and to minimise the environmental impact of packaging.»

**2. Reuse-incentive measures.** FACT: «Member States shall take measures to encourage the increase in the share of reusable packaging placed on the market and of systems to reuse packaging in an environmentally sound manner and in conformity with the Treaty, without compromising food hygiene or the safety of consumers.»

**3. Overall recycling target, 2025.** FACT: «no later than 31 December 2025 a minimum of 65 % by weight of all packaging waste will be recycled»

**4. Material-specific recycling targets, 2025.** FACT: «no later than 31 December 2025 the following minimum targets by weight for recycling will be met regarding the following specific materials contained in packaging waste: (i) 50 % of plastic; (ii) 25 % of wood; (iii) 70 % of ferrous metals; (iv) 50 % of aluminium; (v) 70 % of glass; (vi) 75 % of paper and cardboard»

**5. Overall recycling target, 2030.** FACT: «no later than 31 December 2030 a minimum of 70 % by weight of all packaging waste will be recycled»

**6. Material-specific recycling targets, 2030.** FACT: «no later than 31 December 2030 the following minimum targets by weight for recycling will be met regarding the following specific materials contained in packaging waste: (i) 55 % of plastic; (ii) 30 % of wood; (iii) 80 % of ferrous metals; (iv) 60 % of aluminium; (v) 75 % of glass; (vi) 85 % of paper and cardboard»

**7. Derogation mechanism for the material-specific targets.** FACT: «a Member State may postpone the deadlines for attaining the targets referred to in point (g)(i) to (vi) and point (i)(i) to (vi) of paragraph 1 by up to five years, under the following conditions» FACT: «the derogation is limited to a maximum of 15 percentage points from a single target or divided between two targets»

*Analytical inference:* a Member State using this derogation postpones only the material-specific targets (point (g)/(i)), never the overall 65 %/70 % headline targets, which apply on the original schedule regardless.

**8. Extended producer responsibility schemes, 2024.** FACT: «Member States shall ensure that, by 31 December of 2024, extended producer responsibility schemes are established for all packaging in accordance with Articles 8 and 8a of Directive 2008/98/EC.»

**9. Collection-system participation by economic operators.** FACT: «Those systems shall be open to the participation of the economic operators of the sectors concerned and to the participation of the competent public authorities.»

**10. Transposition deadline.** FACT: «Member States shall bring into force the laws, regulations and administrative provisions necessary to comply with this Directive by 5 July 2020.»

**11. Packaging-waste export inspection.** FACT: «Member States should make effective use of the inspection powers provided for in Article 50(4c) of Regulation (EC) No 1013/2006 of the European Parliament and of the Council»

*Operational implication:* this is the most directly workspace-relevant obligation of the eleven -- a workspace arranging the export of packaging waste from the Union for recycling sits inside the same inspection and documentary-evidence chain this recital directs Member States to police under Regulation (EC) No 1013/2006.

No exceptions are stated in Articles 6 to 7 of Directive 94/62/EC as amended.

Obligations surveyed: 17; workspace-adjacent: 11; extracted as FACT: 11.

# 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

FACT: the captured source states, verbatim: «in particular, to inert packaging materials placed on the market in very small quantities (i.e. approximately 0,1 % by weight) in the Union, primary packaging for medical devices and pharmaceutical products, small packaging and luxury packaging.»

*Operational implication:* a workspace whose packaging falls into one of these named categories (inert materials in very small quantities, primary packaging for medical devices and pharmaceutical products, small packaging, or luxury packaging) may be affected by a future Commission delegated act addressing difficulties specific to that category, rather than the general targets in Section 8.

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

FACT: the captured source states, verbatim: «Member States shall report the data concerning the implementation of points (a) to (i) of Article 6(1) and data on reusable packaging, for each calendar year to the Commission. They shall report the data electronically within 18 months of the end of the reporting year for which the data are collected.»

*Operational implication:* this reporting duty runs from each Member State's competent authority to the Commission, not from a private operator directly; a workspace's own national reporting duty (if any) would arise from the Member State's own transposition and data-collection scheme, not from this clause.

# 11. Operational System Requirements

FACT: the captured source states, verbatim: «Member States shall establish an effective system of quality control and traceability of the packaging waste to ensure that the conditions laid down in point (a) of paragraph 1 of this Article and points (a) and (b) of paragraph 2 of this Article are met.»

*Operational implication:* a Member State's quality-control and traceability system may rely on electronic registries, technical specifications, or average loss rates for sorted waste -- a workspace supplying packaging-waste sorting or recycling data into a national system should expect one of these three mechanisms to govern how its own data is checked.

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

FACT: the captured source's own derogation clause states, verbatim: «the derogation is limited to a maximum of 15 percentage points from a single target or divided between two targets»

*Analytical inference:* this is the only stated exemption-adjacent mechanism -- a bounded, conditional postponement of the material-specific (not the overall) recycling targets, never a full exemption from the targets themselves.

# 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

FACT: the captured source states, verbatim: «Directive 94/62/EC has already been amended six times, it would be appropriate to recast Directive 94/62/EC in the near future»

*Analytical inference:* the underlying Directive 94/62/EC is a standing candidate for a future consolidating recast; a workspace tracking this topic long-term should expect this amending Directive's own provisions to eventually be folded into a single recast instrument rather than remaining a standalone amendment.

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- May 30, 2018: Directive (EU) 2018/852 was adopted.
- July 4, 2018: Directive (EU) 2018/852 entered into force, the twentieth day after its Official Journal publication.
- July 5, 2020: deadline for Member States to bring into force the national laws transposing this Directive.
- December 31, 2024: deadline for Member States to have extended producer responsibility schemes established for all packaging.
- December 31, 2025: deadline for the 65 % overall and material-specific packaging-waste recycling targets.
- December 31, 2030: deadline for the 70 % overall and material-specific packaging-waste recycling targets.

*Source for timeline entries: EUR-Lex, CELEX:32018L0852 (Official Journal of the European Union L 150/141).*

# 15. Sources

|---|---|---|---|

metadata.what_is_it: Directive (EU) 2018/852, amending Directive 94/62/EC, which raises EU packaging-waste recycling targets to 65% overall by 2025 and 70% by 2030 (with material-specific sub-targets), requires Member States to establish extended producer responsibility schemes for packaging by 2024, and sets Member-State reporting and transposition timetables.
metadata.why_matters: It reshapes the packaging-compliance and cost environment for anyone placing packaging on the EU market, exporting packaging waste, or participating in national collection systems, even though the Directive's own legal duties run to Member States rather than directly to a freight-forwarding operator.

70% overall packaging-waste recycling target by 31 December 2030
Member State transposition deadline 5 July 2020
Extended producer responsibility schemes required by 31 December 2024
