entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks SI 2026/729, a new UK operative regulation requiring operators of permitted waste facilities in England to record, digitally track, and report every load of controlled waste received, backed by a fee, statutory deadlines, criminal offences, and civil sanctions. It exists to give a freight forwarder or transporter moving controlled or hazardous waste into a permitted facility in England a single place to see: what must be recorded about the transporter and the waste, by when, and what happens if it is not.

FACT: "The Digital Waste Tracking (England) Regulations 2026" *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2026/729. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/729

**What the workspace should expect to decide:** whether it, or a counterparty it works with, is "the operator of a permitted facility" for the purposes of this instrument, and separately whether its own transporter details (carrier registration number, mode of transport, vehicle registration number) are the "specified information" an operator must record about it under Schedule 1.

*Analytical inference:* the direct duty-holder under this instrument is the operator of the permitted facility receiving the waste, not the transporter; a freight-forwarding workspace's own compliance exposure runs through being correctly and completely recorded as the transporter in the operator's digital waste record, not through a direct duty of its own under this instrument.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

FACT: "The designated person must establish, maintain and operate an electronic system (“the digital waste tracking system”) for the purpose of tracking controlled waste." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2026/729. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/729

*Operational implication:* the instrument applies to the workspace directly whenever it transports controlled or hazardous waste to a permitted facility in England: Schedule 1 requires the receiving operator to record the transporter's name, address, carrier registration or transporter authorisation number, mode of transport, and (for road transport) vehicle registration number for every load.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

FACT: "These Regulations may be cited as the Digital Waste Tracking (England) Regulations 2026 and come into force on 1st October 2026." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2026/729. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/729

*Operational implication:* the instrument's own commencement date has already passed by the time of this brief's authorship; a workspace transporting controlled waste into an English permitted facility should confirm now, rather than later, that it holds and can supply the carrier registration or transporter authorisation number Schedule 1 requires be recorded about it, since the operator's own compliance deadline (Section 8, obligation 5) runs from the day the load is received, not from any grace period for a transporter to supply missing details.

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

FACT: "The operator must pay the digital waste tracking fee in accordance with regulation 5." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2026/729. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/729

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a specific workspace is itself "the operator of a permitted facility" (and so directly liable for the fee, the specified-steps deadline, and the offences and civil sanctions in Section 8) depends on whether it holds an environmental permit to operate a regulated waste facility under the Environmental Permitting (England and Wales) Regulations 2016 -- a fact-specific determination outside this brief's scope. A workspace that only transports waste to such a facility, without operating one itself, sits in this compliance chain as the source of the "specified information" the operator must record (Schedule 1), not as the direct duty-holder.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

FACT: "Mary Creagh Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs 24th June 2026" *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2026/729. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/729

*Per the workspace's reading:* this instrument is made under section 34CA of the Environmental Protection Act 1990, and cross-references the Hazardous Waste (England and Wales) Regulations 2005 (consignment notes) and the Environmental Permitting (England and Wales) Regulations 2016 (the environmental permit and regulated facility definitions) throughout, rather than replacing either.

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

FACT: "The first report must be published before 1st October 2031." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2026/729. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/729

FACT: "Subsequent reports must be published at intervals not exceeding 5 years." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2026/729. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/729

*Operational implication:* the Secretary of State's own statutory review is the one confirmed future event in this captured text; the first published report is due before 1st October 2031, and subsequent reports at intervals of no more than 5 years thereafter -- a workspace should expect this instrument's own requirements (the fee amount, the specified-steps deadline, the penalty amounts) to be revisited on that cycle, not before.

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Is a freight forwarder itself "the operator of a permitted facility" under this instrument?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* only if it holds an environmental permit to operate a regulated waste facility; see Section 4.

**Q2: Does this instrument apply UK-wide?**

FACT: "These Regulations extend to England and Wales and apply in England." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2026/729. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/729

*Analytical inference:* no. The instrument extends to England and Wales but applies only in England; Scotland and Northern Ireland have their own separate digitally-excluded-number regimes referenced elsewhere in the text (Part 3) but are not directly subject to this instrument's own operative Parts 2, 4, 5, and 6.

**Q3: Is there a grace period for a transporter that lacks a carrier registration number?**

FACT: "If the person who transports the controlled waste has no carrier registration number or no transporter authorisation number, the reason why." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2026/729. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/729

*Analytical inference:* no grace period is stated; the operator must instead record the reason the transporter lacks the number, which does not relieve the transporter of its own separate registration duties under the Waste (England and Wales) Regulations 2011 or the Environmental Authorisations (Scotland) Regulations 2018 (outside this brief's scope).

# 8. Substantive Requirements

*Note: this instrument's own duties run mainly to "the operator of a permitted facility" (a person holding an environmental permit to operate a regulated waste facility), with Schedule 1's specified-information requirements naming the transporter's own registration and transport-mode details as data the operator must record.*

**1. Commencement.** FACT: "These Regulations may be cited as the Digital Waste Tracking (England) Regulations 2026 and come into force on 1st October 2026." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2026/729. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/729

**2. Extent and application.** FACT: "These Regulations extend to England and Wales and apply in England." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2026/729. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/729

**3. Establishment of the digital waste tracking system.** FACT: "The designated person must establish, maintain and operate an electronic system (“the digital waste tracking system”) for the purpose of tracking controlled waste." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2026/729. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/729

**4. Duty to pay the digital waste tracking fee.** FACT: "The operator must pay the digital waste tracking fee in accordance with regulation 5." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2026/729. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/729 FACT: "(1) The digital waste tracking system fee is £26." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2026/729. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/729 FACT: "The digital waste tracking fee is payable to the designated person on the first occasion the obligation to comply with the specified steps under regulation 4(4) arises and then on each anniversary of that occasion." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2026/729. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/729

**5. Duty to complete the specified steps by deadline.** FACT: "The operator must comply with the steps specified (“the specified steps”) in paragraph (5) for each load of controlled waste received at the permitted facility (but see paragraph (7)) by the deadline set out in paragraph (8)." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2026/729. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/729 FACT: "the deadline for completing the specified steps is the end of the second working day after the day on which the load of controlled waste or hazardous controlled waste is received" *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2026/729. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/729

**6. Outage procedure and 7-day catch-up deadline.** FACT: "within 7 days beginning with the day after the day the outage is resolved, ensure the specified information recorded in a written record under sub-paragraph (b) is entered into the digital waste tracking system in accordance with the specified steps." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2026/729. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/729

**7. Correction of errors within one month.** FACT: "The operator of a permitted facility must ensure the correct information is entered into the digital waste tracking system in accordance with the specified steps as soon as reasonably practicable and, in any event, within one month of the date on which the operator of a permitted facility becomes aware of the error." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2026/729. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/729

**8. Digitally excluded operator exemption.** FACT: "is exempt from the requirements in regulations 4 to 7" *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2026/729. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/729

**9. Scope carve-out for local-authority household-waste sites.** FACT: "(2) Paragraph (1) does not apply if— (a) the permitted facility is a place provided under arrangements made by a waste disposal authority" *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2026/729. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/729

*Analytical inference:* this carve-out is narrow (household waste deposited by residents at a local-authority-arranged site); it does not exempt a permitted facility that receives commercial or industrial controlled waste, or hazardous controlled waste, from a transporter.

**10. Criminal offences for specific failures.** FACT: "An operator of a permitted facility who fails to comply with any of the provisions of the regulations specified in paragraph (2) is guilty of an offence." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2026/729. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/729

**11. Criminal penalty: fine.** FACT: "An offence under regulation 16 or 17 is punishable— (a) on conviction on indictment, with a fine; (b) on summary conviction, with a fine." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2026/729. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/729

**12. Fixed monetary penalty amount.** FACT: "The amount of a fixed monetary penalty under these Regulations is £1,000." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2026/729. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/729

**13. Late-payment penalty increase.** FACT: "If the penalty is not paid within the period specified for the purposes of paragraph 5(d), and an appeal is not made, the amount of the penalty is increased by 50%." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2026/729. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/729

**14. Variable monetary penalty (uncapped, case-by-case).** FACT: "variable monetary penalty ” means a penalty of such amount as is determined by the Agency in accordance with Part 2 of Schedule 2." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2026/729. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/729

**15. Appeal window: 2 months.** FACT: "Rule 22 of the 2009 Rules applies to an appeal brought under these Regulations as if rule 22(1)(b) required the notice of appeal to be received by the Tribunal within 2 months of the date on which notice of the decision to which the appeal relates was sent to the appellant." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2026/729. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/729

**16. Public register retention: up to 4 years.** FACT: "Information relating to civil sanctions must be removed from the public register within a period no longer than 4 years after the information was entered on the register." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2026/729. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/729

GAP: this item's captured pool does not state the total number of permitted facilities, transporters, or brokers this instrument's digital waste tracking system is expected to cover, nor any estimate of the aggregate annual fee revenue; only the per-load fee stated in obligation 4 above and the per-contravention penalty amounts (obligations 12 to 14 above) are stated.

No phase-in is stated in Sections 1 to 30 of this instrument.

Obligations surveyed: 16; workspace-adjacent: 16; extracted as FACT: 16.

# 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

FACT: "The operator must comply with the steps specified (“the specified steps”) in paragraph (5) for each load of controlled waste received at the permitted facility (but see paragraph (7)) by the deadline set out in paragraph (8)." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2026/729. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/729

*Operational implication:* product-specific compliance status for a given load of controlled waste turns on whether the operator's digital waste record for that load carries the transporter's carrier registration or transporter authorisation number, the mode of transport, and (for hazardous controlled waste) the consignment note code, all within the second-working-day deadline.

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

FACT: "The name of the person who transported the controlled waste to the permitted facility." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2026/729. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/729

FACT: "their— (i) carrier registration number; or (ii) transporter authorisation number." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2026/729. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/729

FACT: "The mode(s) of transport by which the controlled waste was transported (for example, road, rail, sea, air, inland waterway or pipe)." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2026/729. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/729

FACT: "If road is a mode of transport recorded under paragraph 10, the vehicle registration number for each vehicle used." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2026/729. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/729

*Operational implication:* these Schedule 1 fields are the workspace's own direct reporting exposure as a transporter: the operator records them, but the workspace is the source of the data and bears the consequence (Section 8, obligation 3 of Section 7's Q3 answer) if it cannot supply a carrier registration or transporter authorisation number.

# 11. Operational System Requirements

FACT: "the deadline for completing the specified steps is the end of the second working day after the day on which the load of controlled waste or hazardous controlled waste is received" *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2026/729. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/729

*Operational implication:* a workspace transporting controlled waste to permitted facilities in England on a recurring basis should maintain its own carrier registration or transporter authorisation number, mode-of-transport records, and (for road haulage) vehicle registration details in a form it can supply to a receiving operator promptly, since the operator's own second-working-day deadline leaves little room for a transporter to resolve a missing-detail query after the fact.

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

FACT: "is exempt from the requirements in regulations 4 to 7" *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2026/729. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/729

FACT: "(2) Paragraph (1) does not apply if— (a) the permitted facility is a place provided under arrangements made by a waste disposal authority" *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2026/729. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/729

*Analytical inference:* the two edge cases this captured text defines both concern the RECEIVING OPERATOR's own status (digitally excluded, or a local-authority household-waste site), not the transporter's; no exemption or edge case in this text relieves a transporter or freight forwarder of being correctly recorded under Schedule 1.

- 1st October 2026: this instrument comes into force.

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks Commission Regulation (EU) No 459/2012 of 29 May 2012, which amends Regulation (EC) No 715/2007 and Commission Regulation (EC) No 692/2008 to add a Euro 6 particle-number (PN) emission standard for positive-ignition (petrol) direct-injection light passenger and commercial vehicles. It exists to give a workspace handling type-approval, import, or transport of light vehicles in the EU a single place to see the new direct-injection engine definition, the transitional PN limit, and the entry-into-force date.

*Analytical inference:* this Regulation amends vehicle type-approval and emissions-testing rules that run to vehicle manufacturers and type-approval authorities; it does not itself address freight, transport, or customs duties. A workspace's interest is in the emissions-compliance status of light vehicles it handles as cargo, not in a direct duty running to the workspace as a freight intermediary (see Section 4).

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

FACT: "means an engine which can operate in a mode where the fuel is injected into the intake air after the air has been drawn through the inlet valves." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 459/2012, EUR-Lex CELEX:32012R0459. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32012R0459

*Operational implication:* a workspace transporting or handling type-approval documentation for light passenger or commercial vehicles with positive-ignition direct-injection engines should expect those vehicles' emissions paperwork to reference this new particle-number standard from the dates this brief's Section 8 and Section 14 record.

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

FACT: "in Article 4, paragraph 7 is deleted;" *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 459/2012, EUR-Lex CELEX:32012R0459. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32012R0459

*Legal Confirmation Required:* the duties this Regulation creates run to vehicle manufacturers seeking type approval and to the type-approval authorities that grant it; whether a specific workspace ever occupies a role this Regulation itself regulates (for example, as a manufacturer's authorised representative) is a fact-specific question outside this brief's own corpus and requires counsel review.

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does the direct-injection PN standard apply to every light vehicle the workspace handles?**

FACT: "Positive ignition particulate mass and number limits shall apply only to vehicles with direct injection engines." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 459/2012, EUR-Lex CELEX:32012R0459. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32012R0459

*Analytical inference:* the positive-ignition particulate mass and number limits this Regulation adds apply only to vehicles with direct-injection engines; a positive-ignition vehicle without direct injection is outside this specific standard's reach.

**Q2: Is the transitional particle-number limit still current, or has it been superseded by the full Euro 6 standard?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* the transitional limit in Section 8 runs for three years after dates set by the base Regulation (EC) No 715/2007, which this brief's own corpus does not itself state numerically; confirming whether that three-year window has since closed for a specific vehicle model year requires checking the base Regulation's own Article 10(4) and (5) dates, outside this brief's scope.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

**1. Direct-injection engine definition (Article 1(2), inserting point 18 into Article 3 of Regulation (EC) No 715/2007).** FACT: "means an engine which can operate in a mode where the fuel is injected into the intake air after the air has been drawn through the inlet valves." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 459/2012, EUR-Lex CELEX:32012R0459. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32012R0459

**2. Transitional particle-number limit for direct-injection positive-ignition vehicles (Article 1(3), inserting paragraph 7 into Article 10 of Regulation (EC) No 715/2007).** FACT: "Until three years after the applicable dates set out in paragraphs 4 and 5 for new type approvals and the registration, sale or entry into service of new vehicles and upon the choice of the manufacturer, a particle number emission limit of 6 × 10 12 #/km shall apply to vehicles with a direct injection positive ignition engine." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 459/2012, EUR-Lex CELEX:32012R0459. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32012R0459

**3. Deletion of Article 4(7) of Regulation (EC) No 692/2008 (Article 2(1)).** FACT: "in Article 4, paragraph 7 is deleted;" *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 459/2012, EUR-Lex CELEX:32012R0459. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32012R0459

**4. Grandfathering limit for the previous particulate mass measurement protocol (Annex I, footnote 1).** FACT: "A limit of 5,0 mg/km for the mass of particulate emissions applies to vehicles type approved to the emission limits of this table with the previous particulate mass measurement protocol, before 1.9.2011." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 459/2012, EUR-Lex CELEX:32012R0459. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32012R0459

**5. Scope restriction to direct-injection engines (Annex I, footnote 2).** FACT: "Positive ignition particulate mass and number limits shall apply only to vehicles with direct injection engines." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 459/2012, EUR-Lex CELEX:32012R0459. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32012R0459

**6. Transitional particle-number limit and interim test-method requirement (Annex I, footnote 3).** FACT: "Until three years after the dates specified in Article 10(4) and (5) for new type approvals and new vehicles respectively, a particle number emission limit of 6,0 × 10 12 #/km shall apply to Euro 6 PI direct injection vehicles upon the choice of the manufacturer. Until those dates at the latest a type approval test method ensuring the effective limitation of the number of particles emitted by vehicles under real driving conditions shall be implemented." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 459/2012, EUR-Lex CELEX:32012R0459. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32012R0459

*Operational implication:* until the three-year transitional window closes, a manufacturer may choose to type-approve a direct-injection positive-ignition vehicle against this interim particle-number limit using an interim test method, rather than the full Euro 6 PN standard.

**7. Entry into force (Article 3).** FACT: "This Regulation shall enter into force on the third day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union ." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 459/2012, EUR-Lex CELEX:32012R0459. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32012R0459

*Legal Confirmation Required:* none of the seven obligations above states a fine, sanction, or penalty running to a manufacturer, type-approval authority, or freight-forwarding workspace; this Regulation's own text is silent on enforcement consequences.

No exceptions are stated in Articles 1 to 3.

No scope limits are stated in Articles 1 to 3, beyond the direct-injection restriction already captured as obligation 5 above.

Obligations surveyed: 7; workspace-adjacent: 7; extracted as FACT: 7.

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

FACT: "A limit of 5,0 mg/km for the mass of particulate emissions applies to vehicles type approved to the emission limits of this table with the previous particulate mass measurement protocol, before 1.9.2011." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 459/2012, EUR-Lex CELEX:32012R0459. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32012R0459

*Operational implication:* a vehicle type-approved under the previous particulate mass measurement protocol before 1.9.2011 keeps its grandfathered limit; a workspace reviewing older type-approval documentation should check which measurement protocol the certificate references.

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

FACT: "Positive ignition particulate mass and number limits shall apply only to vehicles with direct injection engines." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 459/2012, EUR-Lex CELEX:32012R0459. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32012R0459

*Analytical inference:* a positive-ignition vehicle without a direct-injection engine is not subject to the particulate mass and number limits this Regulation adds; the edge case this creates is a positive-ignition, non-direct-injection vehicle, which falls outside this specific standard.

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 29 May 2012: Commission Regulation (EU) No 459/2012 adopted.

FACT: "Done at Brussels, 29 May 2012." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 459/2012, EUR-Lex CELEX:32012R0459. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32012R0459

- Third day following publication in the Official Journal of the European Union: entry into force.

FACT: "This Regulation shall enter into force on the third day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union ." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 459/2012, EUR-Lex CELEX:32012R0459. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32012R0459

- Three years after the Article 10(4) and (5) dates for new type approvals and new vehicles respectively: the transitional particle-number limit and interim test method (Section 8, obligation 6) cease to apply.

FACT: "Until three years after the dates specified in Article 10(4) and (5) for new type approvals and new vehicles respectively, a particle number emission limit of 6,0 × 10 12 #/km shall apply to Euro 6 PI direct injection vehicles upon the choice of the manufacturer. Until those dates at the latest a type approval test method ensuring the effective limitation of the number of particles emitted by vehicles under real driving conditions shall be implemented." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 459/2012, EUR-Lex CELEX:32012R0459. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32012R0459

*Source for timeline entries: Commission Regulation (EU) No 459/2012, EUR-Lex CELEX:32012R0459 (https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32012R0459).*

metadata.what_is_it: An EU amendment (Regulation 459/2012) adding a Euro 6 particle-number emission standard, a direct-injection engine definition, and a three-year transitional limit for positive-ignition direct-injection light passenger and commercial vehicles.
metadata.why_matters: It sets the particle-number limits and the transitional test-method rules that light-vehicle manufacturers and type-approval authorities operate under from entry into force through the close of the three-year transitional window tied to the base Regulation's own Article 10(4) and (5) dates.

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks The Carbon Accounting Regulations 2009 (SI 2009/1257), a UK Statutory Instrument made under the Climate Change Act 2008. It establishes the mechanism by which carbon units (assigned amount units, EU allowances, certified emission reductions, emission reduction units, and removal units) are credited to and debited from the "net UK carbon account" for the purposes of the UK's first (2008-2012) carbon budget. It is an internal UK government carbon-accounting mechanism, not a rule that itself binds a freight-forwarding workspace.

FACT: "The Carbon Accounting Regulations 2009" *Source: The Carbon Accounting Regulations 2009, SI 2009/1257, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2009/1257

FACT: "Made 20th May 2009 Coming into force 31st May 2009" *Source: The Carbon Accounting Regulations 2009, SI 2009/1257, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2009/1257

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

This Statutory Instrument implements Part 1 of the Climate Change Act 2008 by defining what counts as a "carbon unit" and setting out the duties of the Secretary of State, the registry administrator (the Environment Agency), and Ministers of the Crown in operating the UK's carbon-budget accounting.

**Jurisdictional scope slot:**

FACT: the UK assigned amount is defined by reference to Commission Decision 2006/944/EC, which determines "the respective emission levels allocated to the Community and each of its "Member States under the Kyoto Protocol pursuant to Council Decision 2002/358/EC" *Source: The Carbon Accounting Regulations 2009, SI 2009/1257, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2009/1257

*Analytical inference:* this cross-reference is definitional background (how the UK's own Kyoto-era assigned amount was set at EU level); it is not a scope statement of who this Instrument itself reaches -- the Instrument's own duty-holders are named individually in Section 8 below, and none of them is a private freight-forwarding operator.

FACT: "No Impact Assessment has been prepared for this Order as no impact on the private or voluntary sectors is foreseen." *Source: The Carbon Accounting Regulations 2009, SI 2009/1257, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2009/1257

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this Instrument's own Explanatory Note states directly that it has no foreseen impact on the private or voluntary sectors. A freight-forwarding workspace should treat this Regulation as background to UK carbon-budget accounting mechanics, not as a source of any direct compliance obligation.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

*No content for this section -- this Instrument's own deadlines (Section 14) all fall within the 2008-2012 first carbon budget period and its 2013-2014 close-out window, all of which have already passed as of the current review; no current-action item for the workspace is stated in the captured text.*

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

FACT: "These Regulations may be cited as the Carbon Accounting Regulations 2009 and come into force on 31st May 2009." *Source: The Carbon Accounting Regulations 2009, SI 2009/1257, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2009/1257

FACT: before laying the draft instrument, the Secretary of State "consulted the Scottish Ministers, the Welsh Ministers and the Department of the Environment in Northern Ireland, in accordance with section 28(4)(a) of the Act" and, per the Explanatory Note's preamble, "in exercise of the powers conferred by sections 26(1) and (2), 27 and 90(3) of the Act, makes the following Regulations" *Source: The Carbon Accounting Regulations 2009, SI 2009/1257, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2009/1257

*Legal Confirmation Required:* every duty and power in this Instrument runs among UK central government bodies (the Secretary of State, Ministers of the Crown, the devolved administrations consulted here, the Committee on Climate Change, and the registry administrator). No duty in this Instrument's own text is addressed to, or runs from, a private freight-forwarding workspace, carrier, or logistics intermediary.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

FACT: "It is the duty of the Secretary of State, as soon as is reasonably practicable after these regulations come into force, to instruct the registry administrator to open an account (“the credit account”) in the UK registry for the purpose of holding carbon units which are to be credited to the net UK carbon account in accordance with regulation 5." *Source: The Carbon Accounting Regulations 2009, SI 2009/1257, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2009/1257

FACT: "Under this regulation, carbon units may be transferred to the credit account by any person but are only credited to the net UK carbon account if a Minister of the Crown makes a declaration to that effect. There are limits on the circumstances in which a declaration can be made." *Source: The Carbon Accounting Regulations 2009, SI 2009/1257, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2009/1257

**Primary deadline slot (recurring annual calculation cycle).**

FACT: "Calculations under this regulation are to be performed annually, and must be performed— (a) in respect of 2008, by 15th June 2009; and (b) in respect of any subsequent year of the 2008–2012 budgetary period (“Year X”), by 31st May in Year X+1." *Source: The Carbon Accounting Regulations 2009, SI 2009/1257, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2009/1257

*Analytical inference:* this recurring 15th June 2009 / 31 May in Year X+1 calculation cycle is the closest thing in this Instrument to a per-year trajectory, but it is a Secretary-of-State-internal accounting calendar for the 2008-2012 UK carbon budget, not a compliance deadline reaching any private duty-holder.

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

*No content for this section -- the captured text states no further pending regulatory event beyond this Instrument's own 2008-2012 budgetary-period mechanics described in Section 14; no forward-dated guidance document or scheduled event is stated in the pool.*

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does this Instrument create any duty running directly to a freight-forwarding workspace?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* No. Every duty and power in this Instrument runs among UK central government bodies (Section 4 above), and the Instrument's own Explanatory Note states that no impact on the private or voluntary sectors is foreseen.

**Q2: Could a workspace ever interact with the "credit account" mechanism this Instrument creates?**

*Analytical inference:* regulation 5 states that carbon units "may be transferred to the credit account by any person," but crediting to the net UK carbon account itself requires a Ministerial declaration, and the underlying carbon units (assigned amount units, EU allowances, certified emission reductions, emission reduction units, removal units) are Kyoto-Protocol and EU ETS market instruments, not instruments a freight-forwarding workspace would ordinarily hold or transact directly.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

*Note: this Instrument is an internal UK government carbon-accounting mechanism. Its own Explanatory Note states plainly that "no impact on the private or voluntary sectors is foreseen" (Section 2 above). "Substantive requirements" here means the duties this Instrument places on UK government bodies; none of the obligations surveyed below reaches a freight-forwarding workspace directly.*

The obligations surveyed span: the duty to open a credit account (regulation 4), the power to credit carbon units on Ministerial declaration (regulation 5), the annual EU ETS credit/debit calculation duty with its 15th June 2009 first deadline (regulation 6, detailed in Section 5), the debit-for-disposal duty (regulation 7), the duty to cancel carbon units by 15th May 2014 (regulation 8, detailed in Section 10), the duty to maintain a register (regulation 9), the definition of what counts as a carbon unit (regulation 3), and the pre-laying consultation duties on the Secretary of State (the preamble, Section 4 above).

No phase-in is stated in sections 26(1) and (2), 27 and 90(3) of the Climate Change Act 2008, the enabling provisions under which these Regulations were made.

No exceptions are stated in sections 26(1) and (2), 27 and 90(3) of the Climate Change Act 2008.

No scope limits are stated in sections 26(1) and (2), 27 and 90(3) of the Climate Change Act 2008.

Obligations surveyed: 8; workspace-adjacent: 0; extracted as FACT: 0.

# 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

*No content for this section -- this Instrument concerns UK carbon-budget accounting mechanics, not product-specific compliance status.*

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

FACT: "It is the duty of the Secretary of State, in respect of each year of the 2008–2012 budgetary period, to calculate whether an amount of carbon units is to be credited to or debited from the net UK carbon account as a result of the operation of the EU ETS." *Source: The Carbon Accounting Regulations 2009, SI 2009/1257, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2009/1257

FACT: "It is the duty of the Secretary of State, during a period beginning with 1st January 2013 and ending with 15th May 2014, to ensure that carbon units have been cancelled in accordance with this regulation." *Source: The Carbon Accounting Regulations 2009, SI 2009/1257, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2009/1257

*Analytical inference:* both duties above run to the Secretary of State alone; there is no registration or reporting duty in this Instrument's own text running to a private freight-forwarding operator.

# 11. Operational System Requirements

FACT: "It is the duty of the Secretary of State to maintain a register containing information about the carbon units credited to and debited from the net UK carbon account under these Regulations." *Source: The Carbon Accounting Regulations 2009, SI 2009/1257, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2009/1257

*Operational implication:* this register is the UK registry's own internal transaction record, maintained by the Secretary of State; a freight-forwarding workspace has no operational system obligation of its own arising from this Instrument.

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

*No content for this section -- no exemption, carve-out, or scope-limiting clause of comparable substance is stated in this Instrument's own regulations (the only word-boundary-clean "except" occurrence in the captured pool is the hosting website's own content-licence notice, not a clause of the Instrument itself).*

# 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

FACT: "For the purposes of Part 1 of the Climate Change Act 2008 the following are carbon units— (a) assigned amount units; (b) European Union allowances; (c) certified emission reductions; (d) emission reduction units; and (e) removal units." *Source: The Carbon Accounting Regulations 2009, SI 2009/1257, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2009/1257

FACT: "Each carbon unit has a value of 1 tonne of carbon dioxide equivalent." *Source: The Carbon Accounting Regulations 2009, SI 2009/1257, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2009/1257

*Analytical inference:* this definitional foundation ties the Instrument to the wider Kyoto Protocol and EU ETS carbon-market family (Decision No 280/2004/EC, the Emissions Trading Directive 2003/87/EC, the Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading Scheme Regulations 2005, and the Registries Regulation (EC) No 2216/2004); a workspace researching the UK's own carbon-market instruments should treat those instruments, not this internal accounting mechanism, as the substantive research target.

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 20th May 2009: The Carbon Accounting Regulations 2009 made.
- 31st May 2009: The Carbon Accounting Regulations 2009 come into force.
- 15th June 2009: first annual EU ETS credit or debit calculation deadline, in respect of 2008.
- 1st January 2013 to 15th May 2014: window for the Secretary of State's duty to see that carbon units have been cancelled for the 2008-2012 budgetary period.

# 15. Sources

| # | Source | Type | URL |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | The Carbon Accounting Regulations 2009, SI 2009/1257, legislation.gov.uk | Tier 1, primary UK legislative portal | https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2009/1257 |

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks Commission Regulation (EU) 2015/830, which replaces Annex II to the REACH Regulation ((EC) No 1907/2006) with a new safety data sheet (SDS) content and format standard. It exists to give a freight-forwarding workspace that receives, reads, or forwards safety data sheets for chemical substances and mixtures it transports (by road, rail, sea, inland waterways, or air) a single record of what this Regulation changed, its own commencement dates, and what remains outside this brief's own captured source.

FACT: "Annex II to Regulation (EC) No 1907/2006, as amended by Article 59(5) of Regulation (EC) No 1272/2008 and by Regulation (EU) No 453/2010, is replaced by the text set out in the Annex to this Regulation." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2015/830, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32015R0830

**What the workspace should expect to decide:** whether its own SDS-handling processes (checking Section 14 Transport Information on every SDS it receives before moving a chemical shipment) already reflect this Regulation's own Annex II content standard.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

FACT: "SECTION 14: Transport information This section of the safety data sheet shall provide basic classification information for the transport/shipment of substances or mixtures mentioned in Section 1 by road, rail, sea, inland waterways or air." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2015/830, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32015R0830

*Operational implication:* this is the single most directly workspace-relevant part of this Regulation: it names road, rail, sea, and inland-waterway and air transport explicitly as the modes an SDS's own Section 14 must address, which is the section a freight forwarder consults to classify and move a chemical shipment safely and in compliance with dangerous-goods transport rules.

FACT: "14.1. UN number The UN number (i.e. the four-figure identification number of the substance, mixture or article preceded by the letters “UN”) from the UN Model Regulations shall be provided." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2015/830, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32015R0830

*Analytical inference:* the UN number this subsection requires on every SDS is the same identifier a freight forwarder's own dangerous-goods declaration and transport documentation already carries; this Regulation is the source of the SDS-side requirement to state it.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

*No content for this section: this Regulation's own transitional period (Section 8, Article 2) expired 31 May 2017; no currently-active transitional deadline remains in this brief's own captured text.*

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

*Legal Confirmation Required:* the duty to compile an SDS meeting this Annex II standard runs to the substance or mixture's manufacturer, importer, or downstream formulator under REACH Article 31, not to a freight forwarder as such; a freight forwarder's own relationship to this Regulation is as a RECIPIENT and USER of the SDS (particularly its Section 14 Transport Information), not as the party who must compile it. Whether the workspace itself also acts as a distributor or downstream user with its own SDS-provision duty under REACH Article 31 is a fact-specific question outside this brief's own captured source.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

FACT: "as provided on the label in the official language(s) of the Member State(s) where the substance or mixture is placed on the market, unless the Member State(s) concerned provide(s) otherwise." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2015/830, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32015R0830

*Analytical inference:* this confirms the SDS's own product-identifier labeling language requirement varies by the destination Member State where the substance or mixture is placed on the market, unless that Member State agrees otherwise.

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

*No content for this section: this record's export carries no forward events, and this Regulation's own dated provisions (application from 1 June 2015; the transitional deadline of 31 May 2017) are already historical relative to today.*

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does the workspace itself compile safety data sheets, or only receive and act on them?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this brief's own captured text does not state which role any specific workspace occupies; a freight forwarder that only receives and forwards SDSs as part of moving chemical shipments has no direct Annex II compilation duty, but a workspace that is also a distributor, importer, or downstream formulator under REACH Article 31 may have its own SDS-provision duty.

**Q2: Are any SDSs still in circulation in the pre-2015 format?**

*Analytical inference:* no. The Article 2 transitional period (Section 8) ended 31 May 2017; every SDS a workspace receives today should already comply with this Regulation's own Annex II content standard.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

*Note: this Regulation's own duties run primarily to the manufacturer, importer, or downstream formulator who compiles a safety data sheet under REACH Article 31; a freight-forwarding workspace's own relevance is chiefly as the reader of a compliant SDS's Section 14 Transport Information, marked below where the two roles diverge.*

**1. Annex II replacement (Article 1).** FACT: "Annex II to Regulation (EC) No 1907/2006, as amended by Article 59(5) of Regulation (EC) No 1272/2008 and by Regulation (EU) No 453/2010, is replaced by the text set out in the Annex to this Regulation." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2015/830, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32015R0830

**2. Transitional period, now expired (Article 2; primary_deadline).** FACT: "Without prejudice to Article 31(9) of Regulation (EC) No 1907/2006, safety data sheets provided to any recipient before 1 June 2015 may continue to be used and need not comply with the Annex to this Regulation until 31 May 2017." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2015/830, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32015R0830

*Analytical inference:* the 31 May 2017 deadline named here is this Regulation's own stated compliance date; it has passed relative to today, so it is recorded as historical rather than as a currently-active deadline (Section 3).

**3. Entry into force and application date (Article 3; effective_date).** FACT: "This Regulation shall enter into force on the third day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union . It shall apply from 1 June 2015." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2015/830, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32015R0830

FACT: "Done at Brussels, 28 May 2015." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2015/830, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32015R0830

**4. SDS label-language requirement, varies by Member State (jurisdictional_scope).** FACT: "as provided on the label in the official language(s) of the Member State(s) where the substance or mixture is placed on the market, unless the Member State(s) concerned provide(s) otherwise." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2015/830, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32015R0830

**5. Registration-number disclosure to the enforcement authority, 7-day window (due date).** FACT: "this supplier provides the full registration number to the Member State authority responsible for enforcement (the enforcement authority) within 7 days upon request, received either directly from the enforcement authority or forwarded by his recipient" *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2015/830, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32015R0830

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this duty runs to a "supplier" (which can include a distributor or downstream user) who has chosen to omit the individual registrant's full registration number from an SDS; whether a specific freight-forwarding workspace occupies that role requires direct assessment.

**6. Transport Information section requirement (Section 14 of the SDS itself).** FACT: "SECTION 14: Transport information This section of the safety data sheet shall provide basic classification information for the transport/shipment of substances or mixtures mentioned in Section 1 by road, rail, sea, inland waterways or air." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2015/830, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32015R0830

FACT: "This subsection only applies when cargoes are intended to be carried in bulk according to the following IMO instruments: Annex II of Marpol and the IBC Code." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2015/830, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32015R0830

*Operational implication:* subsection 14.7's own bulk-carriage scope limit (Marpol Annex II and the IBC Code) is directly relevant to an ocean-freight workspace moving bulk chemical cargo.

**7. Toxicological-properties reporting exception (not workspace-adjacent).** FACT: "the data should describe the toxicological properties of the mixture as a whole, except if Article 6(3) of Regulation (EC) No 1272/2008 applies." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2015/830, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32015R0830

*Analytical inference:* this exception governs how the SDS compiler assesses and reports toxicological data; it is a compilation-side drafting rule, not a duty running to a freight forwarder reading the finished SDS.

**8. Property-not-applicable reporting rule (not workspace-adjacent).** FACT: "If it is stated that a particular property does not apply or if information on a particular property is not available, the reasons shall be given." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2015/830, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32015R0830

*Analytical inference:* this is a completeness rule for the SDS compiler (state a reason when a property does not apply, rather than leaving the field blank); it is not itself a duty running to a freight forwarder reading the SDS.

*Qualification accounting.* Per-year trajectory: CAPTURED via `metadata.requirement_trajectory` (the 1 June 2015 application date and the 31 May 2017 transitional-compliance deadline). Exceptions and carve-outs: CAPTURED above (item 7, the toxicological-properties exception). Scope limits: CAPTURED above (item 8, the property-not-applicable rule; also item 6's bulk-carriage scope limit).

Obligations surveyed: 8; workspace-adjacent: 6; extracted as FACT: 8.

# 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

*No content for this section: this Regulation's own captured text applies generally to any substance or mixture requiring a safety data sheet under REACH Article 31; it states no separate product-specific compliance status.*

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

FACT: "this supplier provides the full registration number to the Member State authority responsible for enforcement (the enforcement authority) within 7 days upon request, received either directly from the enforcement authority or forwarded by his recipient" *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2015/830, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32015R0830

*Operational implication:* this is the only registration-number-shaped reporting duty in this brief's own captured text, and it runs to a supplier (potentially including a distributor or downstream user), not generically to every freight forwarder.

# 11. Operational System Requirements

*Operational implication:* a freight-forwarding workspace handling chemical shipments should maintain a process for checking Section 14 Transport Information (Section 8, item 6) on every SDS it receives before movement, since this is the section this Regulation requires to state UN number, proper shipping name, transport hazard class, packing group, environmental hazards, special precautions, and bulk-carriage applicability under Marpol Annex II / the IBC Code.

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

FACT: "This subsection only applies when cargoes are intended to be carried in bulk according to the following IMO instruments: Annex II of Marpol and the IBC Code." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2015/830, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32015R0830

*Analytical inference:* the bulk-carriage subsection of Section 14 (subsection 14.7) applies only to cargoes intended to be carried in bulk under Marpol Annex II or the IBC Code; a workspace moving packaged (non-bulk) chemical cargo has no direct overlap with this specific subsection.

# 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

FACT: "Annex II to Regulation (EC) No 1907/2006, as amended by Article 59(5) of Regulation (EC) No 1272/2008 and by Regulation (EU) No 453/2010, is replaced by the text set out in the Annex to this Regulation." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2015/830, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32015R0830

*Analytical inference:* this Regulation amends Annex II of the parent REACH Regulation ((EC) No 1907/2006) itself, and Annex II had already been amended once before by Regulation (EU) No 453/2010; a workspace tracking REACH SDS format history should treat REACH itself, not this amending Regulation alone, as the standing instrument to monitor going forward.

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 28 May 2015: Commission Regulation (EU) 2015/830 adopted.
- 1 June 2015: This Regulation applies from this date (Article 3).
- 31 May 2017: The Article 2 transitional period ends; safety data sheets provided before 1 June 2015 may no longer be used without complying with the new Annex II.

*Source for timeline entries: Commission Regulation (EU) 2015/830, EUR-Lex (https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32015R0830).*

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks Commission Decision 2011/389/EU, which fixes the Union-wide quantities of aviation allowances under the EU Emissions Trading System (Directive 2003/87/EC) — the total number of allowances to be auctioned, placed in the special reserve, and distributed for free to aircraft operators, for the 2012 trading period and for each year from 2013 onward.

FACT: "COMMISSION DECISION of 30 June 2011 on the Union-wide quantity of allowances referred to in Article 3e(3)(a) to (d) of Directive 2003/87/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council establishing a scheme for greenhouse gas emission allowances trading within the Community (Text with EEA relevance) (2011/389/EU)" *Source: Commission Decision 2011/389/EU, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32011D0389

FACT: "Done at Brussels, 30 June 2011." *Source: Commission Decision 2011/389/EU, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32011D0389

FACT: "This Decision shall enter into force on the third day following its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union ." *Source: Commission Decision 2011/389/EU, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32011D0389

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

This Decision is a Commission implementing act that fixes numeric allowance quantities under the aviation EU ETS; it does not itself create a duty on any single aircraft operator or freight forwarder, but the totals it fixes are the ceiling from which each aircraft operator's own free allocation and auction share are ultimately derived. It applies to the workspace indirectly: a lower Union-wide free-allocation total (Section 8) generally means airlines face a larger allowance shortfall to buy or offset, a cost that can be passed through to air freight capacity and pricing.

FACT: "Article 3e(3)(a) to (d) of Directive 2003/87/EC provides for a decision by the Commission, before the start of each trading period, fixing the total quantity of allowances to be created, auctioned, placed in the special reserve provided for in Article 3f(1) of Directive 2003/87/EC, and distributed for free to aircraft operators." *Source: Commission Decision 2011/389/EU, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32011D0389

*Analytical inference:* because Article 3e(3)(a) to (d) of Directive 2003/87/EC requires this fixing to happen "before the start of each trading period," this Decision is itself a scheduled, recurring Commission act rather than a one-off; a workspace tracking aviation-ETS cost exposure should expect a successor Decision before each future trading period.

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

*Legal Confirmation Required:* This Decision's obligations, described in Section 8, run from the Commission fixing Union-wide totals to the mechanics of Directive 2003/87/EC's own allocation and auctioning provisions (Articles 3c, 3d, 3e and 3f); no source in this brief's corpus names an aircraft operator, airline, or freight forwarder as a direct addressee of THIS Decision (unlike Directive 2003/87/EC itself, which does address aircraft operators). No express "this Decision is addressed to..." clause appears anywhere in the captured text.

*Analytical inference:* Because this Decision only fixes the Union-wide totals rather than any individual operator's allocation, a workspace's practical exposure runs through its air carriers' own EU ETS compliance costs, not through any duty of this Decision running to the workspace directly.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

FACT: "These quantities are to be determined arithmetically from the figure on the historical aviation emissions which has been set by Commission Decision 2011/149/EU of 7 March 2011 on historical aviation emissions pursuant to Article 3c(4) of Directive 2003/87/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council establishing a scheme for greenhouse gas emission allowances trading within the Community ( 2 ) , at 219 476 343 tonnes of CO 2 ." *Source: Commission Decision 2011/389/EU, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32011D0389

FACT: "Following its adaptation on incorporation into the EEA Agreement by Decision of the EEA Joint Committee No 6/2011 of 1 April 2011 amending Annex XX (Environment) to the EEA Agreement" *Source: Commission Decision 2011/389/EU, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32011D0389

FACT: "Pursuant to Article 3e(3)(e) and the third subparagraph of Article 3f(5) of Directive 2003/87/EC (inserted on incorporation into the EEA Agreement), the Commission is to decide on the EEA-wide benchmark, which needs to be based on the EEA-wide quantities of allowances fixed by the EEA Joint Committee." *Source: Commission Decision 2011/389/EU, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32011D0389

*Per the workspace's reading:* the Union-wide quantities in Section 8 are derived arithmetically from this historical-emissions baseline decision, and the EEA-wide benchmark this Decision references depends in turn on figures the EEA Joint Committee had not yet fixed at the time of this Decision's own adoption.

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does this Decision create a direct compliance duty on a freight-forwarding workspace?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* No. This Decision fixes Union-wide allowance totals under Directive 2003/87/EC's aviation provisions; no source in this brief's corpus names a freight forwarder, or even an individual aircraft operator, as a direct addressee of this Decision.

**Q2: Does this Decision state what happens to these quantities after the periods it names?**

*Analytical inference:* No. The captured text fixes totals only for the 2012 period and "each year of the period beginning on 1 January 2013"; no source in this brief's corpus states a further phase-down, sunset, or renewal date beyond that open-ended 2013-onward figure.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

*Note: this Decision's content is almost entirely numeric fixings under Directive 2003/87/EC's aviation-allowance provisions. "Substantive requirements" here means each Article's own stated Union-wide allowance total plus the operational implications those totals carry for a workspace exposed to air-carrier EU ETS compliance costs.*

**1. Free-allocation-linked total, Article 3c(1), 2012.** FACT: "The Union-wide total number of allowances referred to in Article 3c(1) of Directive 2003/87/EC relating to the period from 1 January 2012 to 31 December 2012 is 212 892 053." *Source: Commission Decision 2011/389/EU, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32011D0389

**2. Free-allocation-linked total, Article 3c(2), from 2013.** FACT: "The Union-wide total number of allowances referred to in Article 3c(2) of Directive 2003/87/EC relating to each year of the period beginning on 1 January 2013 is 208 502 526." *Source: Commission Decision 2011/389/EU, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32011D0389

**3. Auctioned-allowance total, Article 3d(1), 2012.** FACT: "The Union-wide total number of allowances referred to in Article 3d(1) of Directive 2003/87/EC relating to the period from 1 January 2012 to 31 December 2012 is 31 933 808." *Source: Commission Decision 2011/389/EU, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32011D0389

**4. Auctioned-allowance total, Article 3d(2), from 2013.** FACT: "The Union-wide total number of allowances referred to in Article 3d(2) of Directive 2003/87/EC relating to each year of the period beginning on 1 January 2013 is 31 275 379." *Source: Commission Decision 2011/389/EU, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32011D0389

**5. Special-reserve total, Article 3f(1).** FACT: "The Union-wide total number of allowances referred to in Article 3f(1) of Directive 2003/87/EC relating to the special reserve is 50 040 608." *Source: Commission Decision 2011/389/EU, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32011D0389

**6. Free-allocation total, Article 3e(3)(d), 2012.** FACT: "The Union-wide total number of allowances referred to in Article 3e(3)(d) of Directive 2003/87/EC relating to the period from 1 January 2012 to 31 December 2012 is 180 958 245." *Source: Commission Decision 2011/389/EU, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32011D0389

**7. Free-allocation total, Article 3e(3)(d), from 2013.** FACT: "The Union-wide total number of allowances referred to in Article 3e(3)(d) of Directive 2003/87/EC relating to each year of the period beginning on 1 January 2013 is 170 972 071." *Source: Commission Decision 2011/389/EU, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32011D0389

*Operational implication:* the 2013-onward totals (obligations 2, 4 and 7) are each lower than their 2012 counterparts, so a workspace exposed to air-carrier EU ETS costs should expect the free/auctioned allowance pool to tighten from 2013 rather than hold steady.

**8. Historical-emissions baseline these totals are derived from.** FACT: "These quantities are to be determined arithmetically from the figure on the historical aviation emissions which has been set by Commission Decision 2011/149/EU of 7 March 2011 on historical aviation emissions pursuant to Article 3c(4) of Directive 2003/87/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council establishing a scheme for greenhouse gas emission allowances trading within the Community ( 2 ) , at 219 476 343 tonnes of CO 2 ." *Source: Commission Decision 2011/389/EU, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32011D0389

No exceptions are stated in Articles 1 to 5 of this Decision.

No scope limits are stated in Articles 1 to 5 of this Decision.

Obligations surveyed: 9; workspace-adjacent: 8; extracted as FACT: 8.

# 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

FACT: "Following its adaptation on incorporation into the EEA Agreement by Decision of the EEA Joint Committee No 6/2011 of 1 April 2011 amending Annex XX (Environment) to the EEA Agreement" *Source: Commission Decision 2011/389/EU, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32011D0389

*Analytical inference:* this Decision's own incorporation into the EEA Agreement (adjacent to, but procedurally distinct from, its EU-internal effect) is the relevant adjacent-framework context for a workspace tracking whether EEA states outside the EU (Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway) apply the same aviation-allowance totals.

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 30 June 2011: Commission Decision 2011/389/EU adopted (the instrument's own dateline, "Done at Brussels").
- 1 January 2012: start of the first trading period this Decision fixes allowance totals for.
- 1 January 2013: start of the ongoing annual period this Decision's other allowance totals apply to.

*Source for timeline entries: Commission Decision 2011/389/EU, EUR-Lex (https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32011D0389).*

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks an EU Commission Decision adopting the sectoral reference document (SRD) on best environmental management practices for the waste management sector under the EMAS Regulation (EC) No 1221/2009. It is a voluntary reference toolkit, not a general regulatory instrument, and this brief gives a freight-forwarding workspace with reverse-logistics, reuse, or EMAS-registration exposure a single place to see who it reaches and what it contains.

FACT: "COMMISSION DECISION (EU) 2020/519 of 3 April 2020 on the sectoral reference document on best environmental management practices, sector environmental performance indicators and benchmarks of excellence for the waste management sector under Regulation (EC) No 1221/2009 on the voluntary participation by organisations in a Community eco-management and audit scheme (EMAS)" *Source: EUR-Lex, Commission Decision (EU) 2020/519 (CELEX 32020D0519). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32020D0519*

FACT: "Done at Brussels, 3 April 2020." *Source: EUR-Lex, Commission Decision (EU) 2020/519 (CELEX 32020D0519). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32020D0519*

*Analytical inference:* this Decision's own legal effect is narrow: it formally adopts the Annex (the SRD itself) under the EMAS Regulation's Article 46(1) mandate; the SRD's own content is a best-practice reference, not a set of directly enforceable emission or discharge limits.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

FACT: "This Sectoral Reference Document addresses two types of organisations of the waste management sector: waste management companies (public and private), including companies implementing producer responsibility schemes, and waste authorities (public administrations in charge of waste management, mainly at local level)." *Source: EUR-Lex, Commission Decision (EU) 2020/519 (CELEX 32020D0519). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32020D0519*

*Operational implication:* a freight-forwarding workspace is neither a "waste management company" nor a "waste authority" by default; this document reaches a workspace only if it itself operates waste-management, recycling, or producer-responsibility-scheme functions, or is registered (or preparing to register) with EMAS (Section 4).

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

FACT: "This Decision shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union" *Source: EUR-Lex, Commission Decision (EU) 2020/519 (CELEX 32020D0519). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32020D0519*

*Operational implication:* this Decision has already been in force and applicable for several years; there is no future compliance date for a workspace within the duty-holder class (Section 4) to calendar.

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

*Legal Confirmation Required:* the SRD's own duty-holder class (Section 8, obligation 1) is EMAS-registered or EMAS-registering organisations, and, within that, organisations falling in the waste management sector's two named organisation types (Section 2). Whether a specific freight-forwarding workspace's own reverse-logistics, reuse, or recycling operation falls within either category, or whether the workspace is itself EMAS-registered, is a fact-specific question this brief's captured text does not resolve for any specific workspace.

*Analytical inference:* the most direct freight-adjacent link is the reuse/repair best environmental management practice (Section 8, obligation 6), which by its own terms names garments, furniture, and electrical and electronic equipment -- product categories a freight forwarder handling reverse logistics, returns, or take-back programmes for luxury goods, apparel, or consumer electronics would recognise directly.

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does this Decision create a binding duty on freight forwarders as such?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* No. The only stated duty-holder class (Section 8, obligation 1) is organisations registered or preparing to register with EMAS; freight forwarders, carriers, and customs brokers are not named, and participation in EMAS itself is voluntary under Regulation (EC) No 1221/2009's own title.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

*Note: this is a voluntary sectoral reference document, not a binding regulatory instrument with direct compliance duties on the wider freight sector. "Substantive requirements" here means the SRD's own stated duty on EMAS-registered organisations (obligation 1) plus its own scope and content statements, which reach a freight-forwarding workspace only when that workspace itself falls within the duty-holder class or subject-matter scope described below.*

**1. EMAS-registered-organisation duty to take the SRD into account.** FACT: "Organisations registered or preparing to become registered under the eco-management and audit scheme established by Regulation (EC) No 1221/2009 are required to take those documents into account when developing their environmental management system and when assessing their environmental performance in their environmental statement, or updated environmental statement, prepared in accordance with Annex IV to that Regulation." *Source: EUR-Lex, Commission Decision (EU) 2020/519 (CELEX 32020D0519). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32020D0519*

**2. Article 1 operative incorporation of the Annex.** FACT: "HAS ADOPTED THIS DECISION: Article 1 The sectoral reference document on best environmental management practices, sector environmental performance indicators and benchmarks of excellence for the waste management sector is set out in the Annex to this Decision" *Source: EUR-Lex, Commission Decision (EU) 2020/519 (CELEX 32020D0519). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32020D0519*

**3. Application date, distinct from entry into force.** FACT: "It shall apply from 12 August 2020." *Source: EUR-Lex, Commission Decision (EU) 2020/519 (CELEX 32020D0519). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32020D0519*

**4. Subject-matter scope, two organisation types.** FACT: "This Sectoral Reference Document addresses two types of organisations of the waste management sector: waste management companies (public and private), including companies implementing producer responsibility schemes, and waste authorities (public administrations in charge of waste management, mainly at local level)." *Source: EUR-Lex, Commission Decision (EU) 2020/519 (CELEX 32020D0519). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32020D0519*

**5. Waste-treatment scope limitation.** FACT: "the scope of this Sectoral Reference Document is limited to facilities performing treatments outside the scope of the Industrial Emissions Directive" *Source: EUR-Lex, Commission Decision (EU) 2020/519 (CELEX 32020D0519). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32020D0519*

**6. Reuse/repair best environmental management practice, named product categories.** FACT: "This BEMP applies to all waste management organisations that handle any type of reusable items, in particular garments, furniture and electrical and electronic equipment." *Source: EUR-Lex, Commission Decision (EU) 2020/519 (CELEX 32020D0519). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32020D0519*

*Operational implication:* this is the practice most directly relevant to a freight-forwarding workspace operating reverse logistics for garments, furniture, or electronics; it is a recommended practice for organisations within the SRD's own scope, not a mandatory technical standard.

**7. Economic-instrument disincentives waste authorities may adopt.** FACT: "taxes and tax modulation, e.g. waste disposal tax, landfill tax, incineration tax" *Source: EUR-Lex, Commission Decision (EU) 2020/519 (CELEX 32020D0519). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32020D0519*

*Legal Confirmation Required:* obligation 7 describes policy tools a national or local waste authority MAY adopt; it is not a penalty this Decision itself imposes on any organisation, and no source in this brief's corpus states a fine or penalty running from this Decision directly to a freight-forwarding workspace.

**Qualification accounting.** Per-year trajectory: No phase-in is stated in Articles 1 to 2 and Sections 2 to 3 of the Annex to this Decision. Exceptions and carve-outs: No exceptions are stated in Articles 1 to 2 and Sections 2 to 3 of the Annex to this Decision. Scope limits: CAPTURED above (obligation 5, the Industrial Emissions Directive exclusion).

Obligations surveyed: 7; workspace-adjacent: 7; extracted as FACT: 7.

Shortfall: none -- K equals M, and the 124,815-character pool is under the 200,000-character large-pool threshold, so the forced five-claim floor is not independently triggered (K already clears it regardless).

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 3 April 2020: Commission Decision (EU) 2020/519 adopted at Brussels.
- Twentieth day following Official Journal publication: This Decision enters into force.
- 12 August 2020: This Decision applies from this date.

*Source for timeline entries: EUR-Lex, Commission Decision (EU) 2020/519 (https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32020D0519).*

# 15. Sources
