entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks the Deposit Scheme for Drinks Containers (England and Northern Ireland) Regulations 2025 (UK SI 2025/67), the deposit return scheme (DRS) instrument for single-use drinks containers in England and Northern Ireland. It exists to give a freight forwarder, warehouse operator, or reverse-logistics provider handling drinks containers in this scheme area a single place to see who this instrument binds, what its penalty and reporting mechanics are, and when its provisions take effect.

FACT: "The Deposit Scheme for Drinks Containers (England and Northern Ireland) Regulations 2025" *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK Statutory Instrument 2025 No. 67. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2025/67

FACT: "Made 23rd January 2025 Coming into force in accordance with regulation 1" *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK Statutory Instrument 2025 No. 67. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2025/67

FACT: "The Secretary of State makes these Regulations in exercise of the powers conferred by sections 54 and 143(1) of, and Schedule 8 to, the Environment Act 2021" *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK Statutory Instrument 2025 No. 67. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2025/67

**What the workspace should expect to decide:** whether the workspace, or a client whose goods it moves, is itself a "scheme producer" (a manufacturer or importer of deposit items), a "scheme retailer" or "in-scope retailer" operating a return point, or a warehouse/logistics provider handling deposit items or returnable items in England or Northern Ireland, since that determines which of the duties in Section 8 apply.

*Analytical inference:* this instrument was made in January 2025 with a main commencement date over two and a half years later (Section 8, obligation 1), giving affected businesses a long lead time; a small number of provisions, mainly registration and interpretation provisions, come into force far earlier, the day after the Regulations were made.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

This instrument establishes a deposit return scheme: producers and importers of single-use drinks containers pay a deposit into a central deposit management organisation (DMO), retailers charge that deposit to consumers and must generally operate or arrange a return point, and consumers get the deposit back when they return an empty container.

*Operational implication:* a pure freight-forwarding intermediary with no role as a producer, importer, retailer, or return-point operator of deposit items is not itself named as a duty-holder anywhere in the captured text; a workspace that imports, warehouses, or distributes drinks in scheme-covered containers, or that operates or services a return point on behalf of a retail client, sits inside the duties described in Section 8.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

*Analytical inference:* the main commencement date (1st October 2027, Section 8 obligation 1) and the registration and reporting deadlines described in Section 8 are all more than a year out from this instrument's own January 2025 making date; the immediate action for an in-scope workspace is confirming its own classification (producer, retailer, return-point operator, or none of these) ahead of the early-commencing registration provisions.

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the workspace itself is a "scheme producer", a "scheme retailer", an "in-scope retailer", or a party otherwise named in Section 8 is a fact-specific question outside this brief's scope; the duties described there run to those defined classes, not to a freight-forwarding intermediary generically.

*Analytical inference:* a workspace acting purely as a carrier or forwarder of goods that happen to include deposit items, with no producer, retailer, or return-point role of its own, sits outside this instrument's duty-holder classes even though the goods it moves are themselves covered by the scheme.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

*Per the workspace's reading:* the Environment Act 2021 (Section 1, sections 54 and 143(1) and Schedule 8) is the parent statute this instrument is made under; a workspace with a broader question about the deposit-scheme power itself, beyond this instrument's own detailed rules, should treat the 2021 Act as the controlling authority.

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

**1. National enforcement authority monitoring-plan deadline.** FACT: "no later than 1st September 2027 and, in each subsequent year no later than 31st December of that year," *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK Statutory Instrument 2025 No. 67, regulation 106(1). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2025/67

*Analytical inference:* this is the recurring deadline by which each national enforcement authority (the Environment Agency for England, or DAERA for Northern Ireland) must provide its proposed monitoring plan to the Secretary of State or DAERA, as appropriate; it runs between public authorities, not to a private workspace, but it is the clearest scheduled recurring event the captured text states (see Section 8, obligation 10, for the fuller sentence this is drawn from).

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does this instrument create a duty directly on a freight-forwarding intermediary?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* Not by that description. Every duty in Section 8 runs to a defined class: registered scheme producers, groceries retailers, in-scope retailers, the deposit management organisation, or national enforcement authorities. A workspace should confirm which, if any, of these classes it or its client falls into.

**Q2: What happens if a scheme producer or retailer fails to comply with a duty in Section 8?**

*Operational implication:* Section 8 (obligation 8) describes the enforcement authority's power to impose a fixed or variable monetary penalty, recoverable as a civil debt or by court order; Section 8 (obligation 9) describes the right to appeal a final notice.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

*Note: this is a large, multi-part regulatory instrument. "Substantive requirements" here means a representative set of the obligation-shaped statements the captured 249,010-character text contains, spanning commencement, jurisdictional scope, producer and retailer duties, and the enforcement and appeal mechanism; it is not an exhaustive obligation-by-obligation restatement of every one of this instrument's many regulations.*

**1. Commencement.** FACT: "Except as provided in paragraph (3), these Regulations come into force on 1st October 2027." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK Statutory Instrument 2025 No. 67, regulation 1(2). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2025/67

*Operational implication:* a small set of provisions, mainly registration, interpretation, and the deposit management organisation's own appointment, come into force the day after the Regulations were made (23rd January 2025), well ahead of the 1st October 2027 main commencement date; a workspace should not assume every duty in this instrument waits until 2027.

**2. Extent and jurisdictional application.** FACT: "These Regulations extend to England and Wales and Northern Ireland." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK Statutory Instrument 2025 No. 67, regulation 2(1). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2025/67

FACT: "These Regulations apply only in England and Northern Ireland." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK Statutory Instrument 2025 No. 67, regulation 2(2). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2025/67

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this instrument's legal extent (England, Wales, and Northern Ireland) is broader than where its duties actually apply (England and Northern Ireland only); a workspace operating solely in Wales or Scotland is outside the scheme this instrument creates, which is a deliberate design choice given Wales and Scotland's own separate deposit-scheme arrangements.

**3. Export-shop and existing-container-drinks exclusion.** FACT: "the supply of container drinks in export shops or the supply of existing container drinks" *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK Statutory Instrument 2025 No. 67, regulation 2(3). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2025/67

*Operational implication:* a workspace handling export-bound drinks consignments through an export shop, or drinks already in the supply chain before the relevant cutover, should confirm whether this exclusion applies before assuming a deposit item duty attaches.

**4. Producer registration fee duty.** FACT: "A registered scheme producer must pay any registration fee, or any instalment of such a fee, to the deposit management organisation." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK Statutory Instrument 2025 No. 67, regulation 21. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2025/67

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this duty runs to a "registered scheme producer"; whether a workspace acting as an importer of packaged drinks itself qualifies as a scheme producer under this instrument's own registration provisions is a fact-specific question outside this brief's scope.

**5. Deposit payment duty.** FACT: "A registered scheme producer must pay to the deposit management organisation an amount equivalent to the deposit for each deposit item which the scheme producer supplies to any person." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK Statutory Instrument 2025 No. 67, regulation 22(1). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2025/67

*Operational implication:* a workspace that itself supplies deposit items as a registered scheme producer should treat this as its core recurring financial obligation under the scheme, separate from the registration fee in obligation 4 above.

**6. Return-point operating duty for in-scope retailers.** FACT: "A groceries retailer who supplies deposit items to consumers at, on or from MRP premises must operate a return point in respect of those premises." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK Statutory Instrument 2025 No. 67, regulation 34(1). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2025/67

*Legal Confirmation Required:* "MRP premises" is this instrument's own defined term for mandatory-return-point premises; whether a specific workspace-operated or workspace-serviced retail premises falls within that definition is a fact-specific question outside this brief's scope.

**7. Return-point exemption.** FACT: "But paragraph (1) does not apply if an exemption has effect in respect of the MRP premises" *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK Statutory Instrument 2025 No. 67, regulation 34(2). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2025/67

*Operational implication:* a workspace servicing a small urban groceries retailer should check whether a return-point exemption is in effect before assuming obligation 6 above applies to that retailer's premises.

**8. Enforcement authority monetary penalty powers.** FACT: "impose a fixed monetary penalty in accordance with Part 3 of Schedule 6" *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK Statutory Instrument 2025 No. 67, Part 9 (enforcement). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2025/67

FACT: "An enforcement authority may recover a fixed monetary penalty or variable monetary penalty as a civil debt or on the order of a court, as if payable under a court order." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK Statutory Instrument 2025 No. 67, Part 9 (enforcement). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2025/67

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this instrument's own compliance and sanctions table (Schedule 6) sets specific fixed and variable monetary penalty amounts per regulation breached; those specific figures are not restated as verbatim FACT claims in this brief because the currency symbol preceding each amount is rendered as a corrupted character in this capture (see the discovery note for this batch), not because the amounts are absent from the source.

**9. Appeal right against a final notice.** FACT: "A person who receives a final notice may appeal against it." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK Statutory Instrument 2025 No. 67, regulation 13(1). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2025/67

FACT: "(a) that the decision was based on an error of fact; (b) that the decision was wrong in law; (c) that the decision was unreasonable for any other reason." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK Statutory Instrument 2025 No. 67, appeal grounds provision. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2025/67

*Operational implication:* a workspace served a final notice under this instrument's enforcement provisions should treat these three grounds as its available appeal routes.

**10. National enforcement authority monitoring-plan deadline.** FACT: "no later than 1st September 2027 and, in each subsequent year no later than 31st December of that year," *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK Statutory Instrument 2025 No. 67, regulation 106(1). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2025/67

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this recurring deadline runs to the national enforcement authority (the Environment Agency or DAERA), not to a private workspace; it is surveyed and used to ground the required primary_deadline slot because it is the clearest recurring, dated obligation the captured text states, but it does not itself bind a freight forwarder.

**11. Internal review-application window.** FACT: "within a period of 28 days beginning with the date on which the affected person receives notice of the decision, or such longer period as the deposit management organisation may specify under regulation 77 (1) (a) , the affected person applies to the deposit management organisation for review of the decision." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK Statutory Instrument 2025 No. 67, deposit management organisation review provisions. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2025/67

*Operational implication:* a workspace, as an "affected person" under a deposit management organisation decision, has 28 days from receiving notice of that decision (or such longer period as the deposit management organisation specifies) to apply for internal review before any further appeal route.

**Qualification accounting.** Per-year trajectory: no multi-year phase-in schedule is stated in this instrument beyond the early-commencement carve-out already captured in obligation 1; No phase-in is stated in Sections covering Regulations 1 to 106 of this instrument. Exceptions and carve-outs: CAPTURED above (obligation 7, the return-point exemption). Scope limits: CAPTURED above (obligation 7, "does not apply" language, and obligation 2's own "apply only" jurisdictional limit).

Obligations surveyed: 11; workspace-adjacent: 10; extracted as FACT: 14.

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

FACT: "A registered scheme producer must pay any registration fee, or any instalment of such a fee, to the deposit management organisation." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK Statutory Instrument 2025 No. 67, regulation 21. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2025/67

*Operational implication:* registration with the deposit management organisation is the gateway obligation for a scheme producer; the registration provisions in Chapter 1 of Part 4 are among the small set of provisions that came into force the day after this instrument was made (23rd January 2025), well ahead of the main 1st October 2027 commencement date.

# 11. Operational System Requirements

*Note: "operational system requirements" here means the monitoring a workspace should maintain if it is a scheme producer, retailer, or return-point operator; this instrument's own technical reporting systems (the DMO's registration and returns-data systems) are the deposit management organisation's responsibility to build, not the workspace's.*

**1. Duty-holder classification.** *Operational implication:* a workspace should determine, before the early-commencing registration provisions apply, whether it or a client is a scheme producer, an in-scope retailer, or neither, since that classification drives every duty in Section 8.

**2. Return-point and reporting monitoring.** *Operational implication:* a workspace servicing a return point should track both the return-point operating duty (Section 8, obligation 6) and any applicable exemption (obligation 7), since an exemption can change without notice under the deposit management organisation's own review powers (Section 8, obligation 11).

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

FACT: "But paragraph (1) does not apply if an exemption has effect in respect of the MRP premises" *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK Statutory Instrument 2025 No. 67, regulation 34(2). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2025/67

FACT: "the supply of container drinks in export shops or the supply of existing container drinks" *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK Statutory Instrument 2025 No. 67, regulation 2(3). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2025/67

*Analytical inference:* these are the two clearest edge cases in the captured text: a return-point exemption for specific MRP premises, and a blanket exclusion for export-shop and existing-container-drink supply; a workspace should check both before assuming a duty applies to a specific consignment or premises.

# 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

*Analytical inference:* the captured text itself notes that these Regulations extend to, but do not apply the scheme's duties in, Wales (Section 8, obligation 2); a workspace with UK-wide drinks-container logistics should research Wales's and Scotland's own, separately administered deposit return scheme arrangements rather than assuming this instrument's England-and-Northern-Ireland scheme covers the whole of Great Britain.

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 23rd January 2025: the Regulations were made.
- 24th January 2025: the day after making, on which the early-commencing provisions (this Part, Part 2 interpretation, and specified registration, exemption, and deposit-management-organisation provisions) come into force.
- 1st September 2027: first deadline for each national enforcement authority's own proposed monitoring plan, due to the Secretary of State or DAERA.
- 1st October 2027: main commencement date for the Regulations.
- 31st December each year from 2027: recurring annual deadline for each national enforcement authority's monitoring-plan provision and publication duties.

*Source for timeline entries: legislation.gov.uk, UK Statutory Instrument 2025 No. 67 (https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2025/67).*

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks the Waste (Miscellaneous Provisions) (Wales) Regulations 2011, a Welsh Statutory Instrument that amends several existing Welsh waste-related instruments (chiefly the Hazardous Waste (Wales) Regulations 2005, via its own Schedule) to transpose Directive 2008/98/EC in relation to Wales, and revokes one Welsh instrument entirely. It exists to give a workspace that holds, transports, or deals in waste (including hazardous waste) in Wales a record of these amendments.

FACT: "The Waste (Miscellaneous Provisions) (Wales) Regulations 2011" *Source: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/wsi/2011/971*

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to a Workspace Handling Waste in Wales

FACT: "The Welsh Ministers make these Regulations in exercise of the powers conferred by section 2(2) of the European Communities Act 1972." *Source: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/wsi/2011/971*

FACT: "Made 28 March 2011 Laid before the National Assembly for Wales 28 March 2011 Coming into force 29 March 2011" *Source: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/wsi/2011/971*

FACT: "These Regulations— (a) come into force on 29 March 2011; and (b) apply in relation to Wales." *Source: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/wsi/2011/971*

*Operational implication:* a workspace that holds, transports, deals in, or brokers waste subject to the Hazardous Waste (Wales) Regulations 2005, the Landfill Allowances Scheme (Wales) Regulations 2004, or the other amended instruments below, and that operates in Wales, should treat these amendments as current from 29 March 2011.

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

*Legal Confirmation Required:* these amendments only affect a workspace that itself holds, transports, deals in, or brokers waste (including hazardous waste) covered by the Hazardous Waste (Wales) Regulations 2005 or the other Welsh instruments this SI amends, in relation to Wales. This captured source does not itself restate the full underlying duties of those amended instruments (only the specific amendments); a workspace with an actual Welsh waste operation should confirm current, consolidated text of the amended instruments directly.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

FACT: "These Regulations are supplementary to the Waste (England and Wales) Regulations 2011" *Source: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/wsi/2011/971*

*Analytical inference:* the captured source's own Explanatory Note states plainly, "(This note is not part of the Regulations)"; it is read here only as the drafter's own summary of intent, not as a source of independent obligations.

FACT: "Reg. 4 revoked (20.7.2015) by The Hazardous Waste (Miscellaneous Amendments) (Wales) Regulations 2015 (S.I. 2015/1417)" *Source: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/wsi/2011/971*

*Analytical inference:* this is the legislation.gov.uk editorial record's own note that regulation 4 of this 2011 instrument was itself later revoked; a workspace should treat regulation 4's amendment (originally to the List of Wastes (Wales) Regulations 2005) as no longer in force since the date stated in the FACT quote above, while the rest of this instrument's amendments remain unaffected by that later change.

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does the workspace hold, transport, deal in, or broker waste (including hazardous waste) in relation to Wales, under any of the instruments this SI amends?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this captured source amends specific definitions and procedures in several existing Welsh waste instruments but does not itself restate their full underlying duties. A workspace with an actual Welsh waste operation should confirm current status directly against the amended instruments' consolidated text.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

*Note: this is a multi-instrument amending SI. "Substantive requirements" here means the amendments this instrument itself makes, each of which is workspace-adjacent only for a workspace already subject to the amended instrument in question.*

**1. Territorial and temporal application.** FACT: "These Regulations— (a) come into force on 29 March 2011; and (b) apply in relation to Wales." *Source: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/wsi/2011/971*

**2. Schedule amendments to the Hazardous Waste (Wales) Regulations 2005 take effect.** FACT: "The Schedule, which provides for amendment of the Hazardous Waste (Wales) Regulations 2005" *Source: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/wsi/2011/971*

**3. Revocation of the Environmental Protection (Duty of Care) (Amendment) (Wales) Regulations 2003.** FACT: "The Environmental Protection (Duty of Care) (Amendment) (Wales) Regulations 2003 M7 are revoked." *Source: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/wsi/2011/971*

**4. Revised meaning of "waste" under the Hazardous Waste (Wales) Regulations 2005.** FACT: "is waste within the meaning of Article 3(1) of the Waste Directive; and (ii) subject to regulation 15, is not excluded from the scope of that Directive by Article 2(1), (2) or (3)." *Source: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/wsi/2011/971*

**5. Non-hazardous determination does not apply to diluted or mixed waste.** FACT: "The power at paragraph (1) to decide that waste be treated as non-hazardous does not apply to waste which has been diluted or mixed with the aim of lowering the initial concentrations of hazardous substances to a level below the thresholds for defining waste as hazardous." *Source: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/wsi/2011/971*

**6. Conditions on the mixing of waste oil.** FACT: "Paragraph (1) applies to the mixing of waste oil— (a) only to the extent that the prohibition in that paragraph is technically feasible and economically viable; and (b) only where such mixing would impede the treatment of the waste oil." *Source: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/wsi/2011/971*

**7. Five-year consignment-note retention for a landfill-permit holder.** FACT: "the period for retention of a consignment note required to be kept by regulation 51(2)(a) is— (a) for 5 years after the deposit of the waste; or (b) if the permit authorises disposal of waste in a landfill, until the permit is surrendered or revoked." *Source: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/wsi/2011/971*

**8. Three-year record-retention duty after waste is transferred.** FACT: "Any person required to keep a record by paragraph (1) must preserve it— (a) while the person is a holder of the waste or (if not a holder) has control of the waste; and (b) for 3 years after the date on which the waste is transferred to another person." *Source: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/wsi/2011/971*

**9. Six-month transitional election right for carriers.** FACT: "Until the end of the period of 6 months beginning with the day on which the Waste (Miscellaneous Provisions) (Wales) Regulations 2011 are made— (a) a carrier may elect to use the multiple collection procedure which applied immediately before the coming into force of those Regulations; and (b) the forms set out in these Regulations as originally enacted, or forms requiring the same information is substantially the same format, may be used instead of those substituted by the Waste (Miscellaneous Provisions) (Wales) Regulations 2011." *Source: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/wsi/2011/971*

*Operational implication:* a carrier already using the pre-2011 multiple collection procedure had until the end of the six-month period following 28 March 2011 (the date these Regulations were made) to continue relying on the prior forms and procedure before the new Part 3 forms and definitions applied.

No exceptions are stated in Sections covering Regulations 1 to 7 and the Schedule of this instrument, in the specific unnegated except/exempt/carve-out word form this accounting checks.

Obligations surveyed: 9; workspace-adjacent: 9; extracted as FACT: 9.

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

FACT: "the period for retention of a consignment note required to be kept by regulation 51(2)(a) is— (a) for 5 years after the deposit of the waste; or (b) if the permit authorises disposal of waste in a landfill, until the permit is surrendered or revoked." *Source: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/wsi/2011/971*

FACT: "Any person required to keep a record by paragraph (1) must preserve it— (a) while the person is a holder of the waste or (if not a holder) has control of the waste; and (b) for 3 years after the date on which the waste is transferred to another person." *Source: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/wsi/2011/971*

*Operational implication:* a workspace holding a waste permit, or otherwise required to keep a consignment-note record under the amended Hazardous Waste (Wales) Regulations 2005, should retain those records for the durations above, measured from the deposit, disposal, recovery, or transfer event as applicable.

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

FACT: "Until the end of the period of 6 months beginning with the day on which the Waste (Miscellaneous Provisions) (Wales) Regulations 2011 are made— (a) a carrier may elect to use the multiple collection procedure which applied immediately before the coming into force of those Regulations; and (b) the forms set out in these Regulations as originally enacted, or forms requiring the same information is substantially the same format, may be used instead of those substituted by the Waste (Miscellaneous Provisions) (Wales) Regulations 2011." *Source: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/wsi/2011/971*

FACT: "Reg. 4 revoked (20.7.2015) by The Hazardous Waste (Miscellaneous Amendments) (Wales) Regulations 2015 (S.I. 2015/1417)" *Source: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/wsi/2011/971*

*Operational implication:* both are time-bound edge cases: the six-month carrier transition window (Section 8, obligation 9) and regulation 4's own subsequent 2015 revocation (Section 5), each narrowing which version of this instrument's own text currently applies.

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 28 March 2011: Regulations made and laid before the National Assembly for Wales.
- 29 March 2011: Regulations come into force, applying in relation to Wales.
- 2011: Enacted (legislation.gov.uk identifier year).

*Source for timeline entries: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/wsi/2011/971*

# 15. Sources

| # | Source | Type | URL |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | The Waste (Miscellaneous Provisions) (Wales) Regulations 2011 (Welsh S.I. 2011 No. 971 (W. 141)) | Welsh Statutory Instrument, legislation.gov.uk | https://www.legislation.gov.uk/wsi/2011/971 |

*Referenced in the captured text but not independently captured or verified in this pool: the Hazardous Waste (Wales) Regulations 2005 (S.I. 2005/1806 (W.138)); the Landfill Allowances Scheme (Wales) Regulations 2004 (S.I. 2004/1490 (W.155)); the Waste (England and Wales) Regulations 2011; Directive 2008/98/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council on waste.*

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks Council Decision (EU) 2020/1580, which amends an earlier Council Decision to set the European Union's negotiating position at two International Maritime Organization (IMO) committee sessions in November 2020, concerning a Model agreement for the authorization of recognized organizations (classification societies) acting on behalf of flag Administrations. It exists to give a freight forwarder with ocean freight exposure a record of what EU position was taken and what, if anything, it requires of the workspace directly.

*Analytical inference:* this is a procedural, position-setting Decision internal to EU external representation at the IMO; it creates no direct compliance duty on a private freight-forwarding workspace, but its subject matter, recognized-organization (classification society) authorization standards, bears on the ship-safety and pollution-prevention framework that governs ocean carriers.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

FACT: "The Council should therefore authorise the Member States to express the position of the Union." *Source: Council Decision (EU) 2020/1580. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32020D1580

*Legal Confirmation Required:* because the Union itself is neither an IMO member nor a contracting party to the relevant conventions, this Decision authorises Member States, not the workspace, to express the EU position; whether the underlying IMO instruments (the MSC-MEPC.5 circular, MARPOL Annex VI amendments, SOLAS Chapter II-1 amendments) ever create a duty on the workspace's own ocean carriers is a separate, fact-specific question requiring review of those instruments once adopted and transposed.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

*No content for this section: the only dated events in the captured text, the November 2020 IMO committee sessions, have already passed as of this brief's authoring date; no immediate action item running to a private freight-forwarding workspace is stated.*

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

FACT: "Member States are hereby authorised to give their consent to be bound, in the interests of the Union, by the amendments and the circular referred to in Articles 1 and 2, to the extent that those amendments and that circular fall under the exclusive competence of the Union." *Source: Council Decision (EU) 2020/1580. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32020D1580

*Analytical inference:* the compliance chain this Decision creates runs from the Union, through the Council's authorisation, to Member States, who express the position and give consent to be bound at the IMO; it does not run to a private freight-forwarding workspace, whose own ocean carriers would instead be bound, if at all, by the resulting IMO instruments once those instruments are adopted and take effect under applicable flag-state law.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

FACT: "during its 75th session to be held from 16 to 20 November 2020" *Source: Council Decision (EU) 2020/1580. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32020D1580

*Per the workspace's reading:* the authoritative instrument this Decision positions the EU toward is the MSC-MEPC.5 circular itself (a Model agreement for the authorization of recognized organizations), which this Decision's own corpus does not include in full; a workspace with a specific question about recognized-organization authorization standards should consult the IMO's own published circular once approved.

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

*No content for this section: the export's own forward_events list is empty, and the captured text's own dated events, the MEPC 75 and MSC 102 sessions, both fall in November 2020 and have already occurred as of this brief's authoring date.*

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does this Decision create a direct regulatory obligation on a private freight-forwarding workspace?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* No. FACT: "The Council should therefore authorise the Member States to express the position of the Union." *Source: Council Decision (EU) 2020/1580. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32020D1580 This Decision's own obligations run to Member States as the Union's representatives at the IMO; any eventual duty on an ocean carrier would arise from the resulting IMO instrument itself, not from this positioning Decision.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

*Note: this Decision is a procedural, position-setting instrument for EU external representation at two IMO committees, not a standalone instrument creating a schedule of private-party duties. "Substantive requirements" below means the Decision's own stated positions and authorisations.*

**1. EU position at MEPC 75 (Marine Environment Protection Committee).** FACT: "during its 75th session to be held from 16 to 20 November 2020" *Source: Council Decision (EU) 2020/1580. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32020D1580

*Operational implication:* the EU position at this session was to support adoption of amendments to MARPOL Annex VI regulations 2, 14 and 18 and appendices I and VI, and approval of the MSC-MEPC.5 circular; a workspace tracking pollution-prevention standards for its own ocean carriers should treat this session's outcome as the relevant IMO-level event.

**2. EU position at MSC 102 (Maritime Safety Committee).** FACT: "during its 102nd session to be held from 4 to 11 November 2020" *Source: Council Decision (EU) 2020/1580. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32020D1580

*Operational implication:* the EU position at this session was to approve the MSC-MEPC.5 circular and to support adoption of amendments to SOLAS Chapter II-1, the International Code of Safety for Ships Using Gases or Other Low-flashpoint Fuels, and resolution A.658(16) on retro-reflective materials on life-saving appliances; a workspace tracking ship-safety standards for its own ocean carriers should treat this session's outcome as the relevant IMO-level event.

**3. Member State consent-to-be-bound authorisation.** FACT: "Member States are hereby authorised to give their consent to be bound, in the interests of the Union, by the amendments and the circular referred to in Articles 1 and 2, to the extent that those amendments and that circular fall under the exclusive competence of the Union." *Source: Council Decision (EU) 2020/1580. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32020D1580

*Analytical inference:* this authorises Member States, not the Union itself, to give binding consent at the IMO; it is an internal EU competence mechanism, not a workspace-facing duty.

**4. Jurisdictional basis for Member State representation.** FACT: "The Council should therefore authorise the Member States to express the position of the Union." *Source: Council Decision (EU) 2020/1580. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32020D1580

*Analytical inference:* this confirms the Decision's authorisation runs to Member States because the Union itself holds no IMO membership; it creates no separate duty on a private operator.

**5. Scope limitation of this Decision.** FACT: "The scope of this Decision should be limited to the content of the MSC-MEPC.5 circular proposed, to the extent that that circular falls under the exclusive competence of the Union and may affect Union common rules." *Source: Council Decision (EU) 2020/1580. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32020D1580

*Analytical inference:* this Decision's own scope is expressly limited to the MSC-MEPC.5 circular's content, and only to the extent that content falls under exclusive Union competence; it does not extend to the full substance of either IMO committee's broader agenda.

**Required-slot grounding.** FACT: "This Decision shall enter into force on the date of its adoption." *Source: Council Decision (EU) 2020/1580. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32020D1580

**Qualification accounting.** Per-year trajectory: No phase-in is stated in Articles 1 to 4, only the two fixed November 2020 committee session dates, obligations 1 and 2 above. Exceptions and carve-outs: No exceptions are stated in Articles 1 to 4. Scope limits: CAPTURED above (obligation 5, the Decision's own scope-limitation recital).

Obligations surveyed: 5; workspace-adjacent: 2; extracted as FACT: 5.

# 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

*No content for this section: the captured source addresses an EU negotiating position at the IMO, not any product-specific compliance status.*

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

*No content for this section: every authorisation stated in the captured source, obligation 3 above, runs from the Union to Member States, not from a private freight-forwarding workspace to any authority.*

# 11. Operational System Requirements

*No content for this section: the captured source states no technical, reporting, or monitoring system requirement running to a private freight-forwarding workspace.*

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

*No content for this section: no exception or edge case running to a private freight-forwarding workspace is stated in Articles 1 to 4; the Decision's own scope limitation, obligation 5 in Section 8, addresses EU-internal competence division, not a workspace-facing carve-out.*

# 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

*No content for this section: the captured source is a single Council Decision text with no adjacent research, industry body, or alternative-mechanism content.*

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 23 October 2020: This Decision was adopted. FACT: "Done at Luxembourg, 23 October 2020." *Source: Council Decision (EU) 2020/1580. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32020D1580
- 4 to 11 November 2020: The IMO Maritime Safety Committee's 102nd session, at which the EU position set by this Decision was to be taken.
- 16 to 20 November 2020: The IMO Marine Environment Protection Committee's 75th session, at which the EU position set by this Decision was to be taken.

*Source for timeline entries: Council Decision (EU) 2020/1580 (https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32020D1580).*

# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks Commission Regulation (EU) No 493/2012, which lays down the detailed methodology and annual reporting rules for recyclers of waste batteries and accumulators calculating and reporting recycling efficiencies under Directive 2006/66/EC. It exists to give a freight-forwarding workspace with an active waste-battery logistics or recycling relationship a single record of this Regulation's recurring compliance cycle, since its own duty holder is the recycler, not a freight-forwarding operator.

*Analytical inference:* the discussion below reads this Regulation's own duties as running to the defined "recycler" role (Article 2), not to a freight-forwarding operator, unless the workspace itself operates a battery-recycling process.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

FACT: the captured source states, verbatim: «This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States.»

*Analytical inference:* as a Regulation (not a Directive), this instrument binds directly in every Member State without national transposition -- but its own operative duties (Section 8) run specifically to "recyclers" of waste batteries and accumulators, a defined duty-holder class distinct from a freight-forwarding operator. A workspace is relevant to this instrument as a logistics counterpart to a recycling facility, not as the facility itself, unless the workspace operates its own battery-recycling process.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

*Operational implication:* none identified as current. Both dated milestones this Regulation sets (1 January 2014 applicability; 30 April 2015 first annual report, Section 14) are already elapsed as of this brief; a workspace with an active waste-battery-recycling relationship should confirm that counterpart's ongoing ANNUAL reporting compliance (the four-month post-calendar-year deadline recurs every year, Section 8/10), not treat this as a one-time historical filing.

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this Regulation's operative duties run to recyclers of waste batteries and accumulators, as defined in Article 2; the captured source text states no duty running to a freight-forwarding operator directly. FACT: the captured source states, verbatim: «This Regulation shall enter into force on the day of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union»

GAP: [penalty_summary] No source in this brief's corpus states a penalty, fine, or sanction amount; this Regulation states no EU-level penalty figure or mechanism anywhere in the captured text.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

FACT: the captured source states, verbatim: «Directive 2006/66/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council of 6 September 2006 on batteries and accumulators and waste batteries and accumulators and repealing Directive 91/157/EEC»

*Operational implication:* Directive 2006/66/EC (and its own Annex III, Part B) is the parent instrument setting the minimum recycling-efficiency targets this Regulation only supplies the CALCULATION method for; a workspace tracking the underlying targets themselves should track that Directive, not only this Regulation.

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

*No content for this section -- the only dated milestones this Regulation itself sets (Article 1's 1 January 2014 applicability date and Article 3(4)'s 30 April 2015 first-report deadline, both in Section 14) are already elapsed as of this brief; no forward-looking guidance or pending event is stated in the captured source text.*

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does this Regulation create a compliance duty on a freight-forwarding operator directly?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* the captured source text's operative duties (Section 8) run to "recyclers" as defined in Article 2 -- a defined technical duty-holder class -- not to a freight-forwarding operator. A workspace with a specific compliance question about a battery-recycling counterpart's own reporting status should confirm directly with that counterpart or the relevant Member State's competent authority.

**Q2: Is the workspace itself a "recycler" under this Regulation?**

*Analytical inference:* Generally no, unless the workspace itself operates a waste-battery recycling process as defined in Article 2(1); a freight-forwarding workspace that only arranges TRANSPORT of waste batteries to a recycling facility is not itself the recycler this Regulation's reporting duty (Section 10) addresses.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

*Note: this Regulation's operative duties run to "recyclers" of waste batteries and accumulators, a defined technical duty-holder class, not to a freight-forwarding operator directly. "Substantive requirements" here surveys those duties for workspace relevance rather than assuming they apply.*

**1. Applicability date and scope.** FACT: «Article 1 Scope This Regulation shall apply to the recycling processes carried out to waste batteries and accumulators from 1 January 2014.»

**2. Recycling-efficiency calculation method (lead-acid, nickel-cadmium and other batteries).** FACT: «The method set out in Annex I shall be used to calculate the recycling efficiency of a process for recycling waste lead-acid, nickel-cadmium and other batteries and accumulators.»

**3. Recycled-lead-content calculation method.** FACT: «The method set out in Annex II shall be used to calculate the rate of recycled lead content for any recycling process.»

**4. Multi-facility reporting responsibility.** FACT: «Where a recycling process is carried out at more than one facility, the first recycler is responsible for submitting the information required under point 4 to the Member State’s competent authorities.»

**5. Technological adaptation period (recital).** FACT: «Recyclers of waste batteries and accumulators need at least 18 months to adapt their technological processes to the new recycling efficiencies calculation requirements.»

*Analytical inference:* this recital explains why Article 1 set the applicability date at 1 January 2014, roughly 18 months after this Regulation's own adoption (Section 14) -- the trajectory recorded in this entry's own metadata.

No exceptions are stated in Articles 1 to 4.

Obligations surveyed: 11; workspace-adjacent: 0; extracted as FACT: 5.

# 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

FACT: the captured source states, verbatim: «‘recycling process’ means any reprocessing operation as referred to in Article 3(8) of Directive 2006/66/EC which is carried out on waste lead-acid, nickel-cadmium and other batteries and accumulators and results in the production of output fractions as defined in point 5 of this Article.»

*Operational implication:* this Regulation's calculation methodology is battery-chemistry-specific -- Annex I covers all three named types generally, Annex II applies only to the recycled-lead rate for lead-acid batteries, and Annex III applies only to the recycled-cadmium rate for nickel-cadmium batteries; a workspace tracking a specific battery chemistry's recycling compliance should confirm which Annex its counterpart's own reporting is measured against.

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

FACT: the captured source states, verbatim: «Recyclers shall report the information shown in Annex IV, Annex V and Annex VI, as applicable, on an annual basis and shall send it to the Member State’s competent authorities by no later than four months from the end of a calendar year concerned.»

FACT: the captured source states, verbatim: «Recyclers shall send their first annual reports no later than the 30 April 2015.»

FACT: the captured source states, verbatim: «Reporting on the recycling efficiency shall cover all individual steps of recycling and all corresponding output fractions.»

*Operational implication:* this reporting duty runs from the recycler to the Member State's competent authority, on a recurring annual cycle (four months after each calendar year's end); it is not a duty this Regulation places on a freight-forwarding operator.

# 11. Operational System Requirements

*No content for this section -- the operational systems this Regulation describes (Annexes I to III's recycling-efficiency calculation formulas) are internal to a battery-recycling facility's own process, not a system a freight-forwarding workspace itself operates or maintains.*

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

*No content for this section -- no exemption or edge case running to a freight-forwarding operator is stated in the captured source text (see Section 8's qualification accounting).*

# 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

*No content for this section -- the captured pool contains only this Regulation's own operative text and technical Annexes, with no adjacent research or alternative body referenced.*

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- June 11, 2012: Commission Regulation (EU) No 493/2012 was adopted.
- January 1, 2014: this Regulation becomes applicable to waste-battery recycling processes.
- April 30, 2015: deadline for recyclers' first annual recycling-efficiency reports.

*Source for timeline entries: EUR-Lex, CELEX:32012R0493 (Official Journal of the European Union L 151/9).*

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2025/1482, which sets new, tiered concentration limits for five brominated flame-retardant chemicals (the "listed PBDE") in mixtures and articles, with a stricter limit for toys and childcare products made from recovered material. It exists to give a freight forwarder moving plastics, consumer goods, toys, or childcare products into or within the EU a single place to see: what the concentration limits are, when each tier takes effect, and what is excluded.

FACT: "COMMISSION DELEGATED REGULATION (EU) 2025/1482 of 24 July 2025 amending Regulation (EU) 2019/1021 of the European Parliament and of the Council as regards the persistent organic pollutants tetrabromodiphenyl ether, pentabromodiphenyl ether, hexabromodiphenyl ether, heptabromodiphenyl ether and decabromodiphenyl ether (Text with EEA relevance)" *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX:32025R1482. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32025R1482

**What the workspace should expect to decide:** whether any product it moves that is made from or contains recovered/recycled plastic material -- particularly toys or childcare products -- could contain the listed PBDE above the applicable tier's limit, and by which date the stricter limit for that product category takes effect.

*Analytical inference:* the direct duty-holder under the amended Regulation (EU) 2019/1021 is the manufacturer or person placing the product on the market or using it, per Article 3(1) of that Regulation (Section 8); a freight forwarder's own exposure is indirect, through the compliance status of the goods it moves.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

FACT: "the manufacturing, placing on the market and use, whether on their own, in mixtures or in articles, of substances listed in Annex I to that Regulation are prohibited, subject to Article 4 of that Regulation." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX:32025R1482. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32025R1482

FACT: "Particular attention should be given to childcare products and toys in view of potential exposure to listed PBDE contained in them." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX:32025R1482. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32025R1482

*Operational implication:* the instrument applies to the workspace whenever it handles a product made from or containing recovered material that could carry the listed PBDE as an unintentional trace contaminant -- most acutely toys and childcare products, which the instrument's own recitals single out for a stricter limit tier.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

FACT: "(a) 10 mg/kg upon entry into force of this Regulation where they are present in mixtures or articles, except for food contact materials subject to Regulation (EC) No 1935/2004 of the European Parliament and of the Council" *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX:32025R1482. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32025R1482

*Operational implication:* the general 10 mg/kg limit (excluding food contact materials) applies from this Regulation's own entry into force (Section 6); a workspace moving mixtures or articles not made from recovered material should confirm against this limit now, since it carries no later phase-in date of its own.

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

*Legal Confirmation Required:* the amended Regulation (EU) 2019/1021's own Article 3(1) prohibition runs to the manufacturing, placing on the market, and use of the listed substances; whether a specific freight-forwarding workspace's own handling of a shipment (as opposed to the manufacturer or importer placing the product on the market) falls within that prohibition's reach for a specific product is a fact-specific question outside this brief's scope.

*Analytical inference:* the workspace's practical position is as a mover of goods whose own manufacturer or importer bears the direct compliance duty; the workspace's exposure is to handling non-compliant goods it did not itself produce or place on the market.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

FACT: "reduces the concentration limit in waste for the sum of tetraBDE, pentaBDE, hexaBDE, heptaBDE and decaBDE to 500 mg/kg as of 10 June 2023, to 350 mg/kg from 30 December 2025 and to 200 mg/kg from 30 December 2027." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX:32025R1482. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32025R1482

*Per the workspace's reading:* this schedule is stated in this instrument's own recitals as background from a DIFFERENT, already-adopted instrument (Regulation (EU) 2022/2400, cited in recital 4) governing the concentration limit in WASTE, not in mixtures or articles placed on the market; it is not itself amended or restated as an operative provision of this 2025/1482 Regulation, but is directly relevant background for a workspace also handling PBDE-containing waste streams.

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

FACT: "This Regulation shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union" *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX:32025R1482. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32025R1482

*Operational implication:* the recovered-material and toys/childcare tiers (Section 8, obligations 5 and 6) both step down further on 30 December 2025 and again on 30 December 2027 (recovered material) or 17 May 2027 (toys); a workspace should calendar these dates now, since the toys/childcare tier's final step (10 mg/kg) is markedly stricter than the general tier's own flat 10 mg/kg limit reached immediately on entry into force.

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does this Regulation apply to food contact materials?**

FACT: "should be excluded from this Regulation as listed PBDE should in principle not be present in food contact materials" *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX:32025R1482. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32025R1482

*Analytical inference:* no. Food contact materials subject to Regulation (EC) No 1935/2004 are excluded from every tier of this Regulation's own limit values (Section 8, obligations 4 to 6).

**Q2: Does the Regulation apply uniformly across all Member States?**

FACT: "This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX:32025R1482. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32025R1482

*Analytical inference:* yes, directly and without need for national transposition, since this is an EU Regulation (as distinct from a Directive).

**Q3: Is the toys/childcare limit the same as the general recovered-material limit?**

*Analytical inference:* no. Both start at 500 mg/kg upon entry into force and step to 350 mg/kg on 30 December 2025, but the recovered-material tier's final step (200 mg/kg, 30 December 2027) is less strict than the toys/childcare tier's final step (10 mg/kg, 17 May 2027) -- see Section 8, obligations 5 and 6.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

*Note: this instrument amends Annex I to Regulation (EU) 2019/1021; its own duties (the concentration limits) run to the manufacturing, placing on the market, and use of the listed substances under that Regulation's Article 3(1) and 4(1), not to a freight forwarder directly.*

**1. Prohibition baseline under the amended Regulation.** FACT: "the manufacturing, placing on the market and use, whether on their own, in mixtures or in articles, of substances listed in Annex I to that Regulation are prohibited, subject to Article 4 of that Regulation." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX:32025R1482. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32025R1482

**2. Prior UTC limit being superseded.** FACT: "Tetrabromodiphenyl ether (tetraBDE), pentabromodiphenyl ether (pentaBDE), hexabromodiphenyl ether (hexaBDE), heptabromodiphenyl ether (heptaBDE) and decabromodiphenyl ether (decaBDE) (together ‘listed polybrominated diphenyl ethers’, ‘listed PBDE’) are listed in Annex I to Regulation (EU) 2019/1021 with an unintentional trace contaminant (UTC) limit value of 500 mg/kg for the sum of the concentrations of the five substances where they are present in mixtures or articles." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX:32025R1482. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32025R1482

*Analytical inference:* this obligation states the PRE-amendment limit (500 mg/kg, under review); it is surveyed as background context, not counted as workspace-adjacent below, since it is superseded by obligations 4 to 6 rather than itself a currently operative limit.

**3. Waste concentration limit schedule (cited context from Regulation (EU) 2022/2400).** FACT: "reduces the concentration limit in waste for the sum of tetraBDE, pentaBDE, hexaBDE, heptaBDE and decaBDE to 500 mg/kg as of 10 June 2023, to 350 mg/kg from 30 December 2025 and to 200 mg/kg from 30 December 2027." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX:32025R1482. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32025R1482

**4. General concentration limit: 10 mg/kg, excluding food contact materials.** FACT: "(a) 10 mg/kg upon entry into force of this Regulation where they are present in mixtures or articles, except for food contact materials subject to Regulation (EC) No 1935/2004 of the European Parliament and of the Council" *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX:32025R1482. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32025R1482

**5. Recovered-material tier: 500 to 350 to 200 mg/kg.** FACT: "500 mg/kg upon entry into force of this Regulation, 350 mg/kg as of 30 December 2025 and 200 mg/kg as of 30 December 2027 where they are present in mixtures or articles containing or made of recovered material containing tetra-, penta-, hexa-, hepta- or decaBDE, except for food contact materials subject to Regulation (EC) No 1935/2004" *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX:32025R1482. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32025R1482

**6. Toys and childcare-products tier: 500 to 350 to 10 mg/kg.** FACT: "500 mg/kg upon entry into force of this Regulation, 350 mg/kg as of 30 December 2025 and 10 mg/kg as of 17 May 2027, where they are present in toys subject to Directive 2009/48/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council" *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX:32025R1482. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32025R1482

**7. Food contact materials exclusion.** FACT: "should be excluded from this Regulation as listed PBDE should in principle not be present in food contact materials" *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX:32025R1482. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32025R1482

**8. Entry into force.** FACT: "This Regulation shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union" *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX:32025R1482. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32025R1482

**9. Direct applicability across Member States.** FACT: "This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX:32025R1482. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32025R1482

**10. Amendment mechanism.** FACT: "Annex I to Regulation (EU) 2019/1021 is amended in accordance with the Annex to this Regulation." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX:32025R1482. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32025R1482

GAP: no source in this item's captured pool states a fine, penalty, or sanction running to a manufacturer, importer, or freight-forwarding operator for exceeding these concentration limits; this Delegated Regulation itself only sets the limit values and their effective dates, leaving enforcement and penalties to Member States' own implementation of Regulation (EU) 2019/1021, which is outside this brief's captured pool.

No scope limits are stated in Articles 1 to 2.

Obligations surveyed: 10; workspace-adjacent: 9; extracted as FACT: 10.

# 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

FACT: "(a) 10 mg/kg upon entry into force of this Regulation where they are present in mixtures or articles, except for food contact materials subject to Regulation (EC) No 1935/2004 of the European Parliament and of the Council" *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX:32025R1482. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32025R1482

FACT: "500 mg/kg upon entry into force of this Regulation, 350 mg/kg as of 30 December 2025 and 10 mg/kg as of 17 May 2027, where they are present in toys subject to Directive 2009/48/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council" *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX:32025R1482. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32025R1482

*Operational implication:* product-specific compliance status turns on which of the three tiers a specific product falls into (general mixtures/articles; recovered-material mixtures/articles; toys and childcare products from recovered material) and the date checked against, since each tier has its own step-down schedule.

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

*No content for this section is grounded in the item's captured source pool.*

# 11. Operational System Requirements

*Note: because this is a substance concentration-limit amendment rather than a reporting framework, "operational system requirements" here means the product-testing and supplier-verification practice a workspace should maintain, not a technical system this Regulation itself requires.*

FACT: "Particular attention should be given to childcare products and toys in view of potential exposure to listed PBDE contained in them." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX:32025R1482. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32025R1482

*Operational implication:* a workspace sourcing or moving toys or childcare products made from recovered plastic material should confirm supplier testing data against the toys/childcare tier's own step-down schedule (Section 8, obligation 6), given the instrument's own stated concern for children's potential exposure.

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

FACT: "should be excluded from this Regulation as listed PBDE should in principle not be present in food contact materials" *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX:32025R1482. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32025R1482

*Analytical inference:* the one exclusion this instrument states is food contact materials subject to Regulation (EC) No 1935/2004, which applies across all three concentration-limit tiers (Section 8, obligations 4 to 6); no other product category is excluded in the captured text.

# 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

*No content for this section is grounded in the item's captured source pool.*

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 24 July 2025: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2025/1482 adopted (signed at Brussels).
- 28.10.2025: published in the Official Journal of the European Union, EN L series 2025/1482.
- 30 December 2025: recovered-material and toys/childcare tiers both step to 350 mg/kg.
- 17 May 2027: toys/childcare tier steps to its final 10 mg/kg limit.
- 30 December 2027: recovered-material tier steps to its final 200 mg/kg limit.

*Source for timeline entries: EUR-Lex, CELEX:32025R1482 (https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32025R1482).*

metadata.what_is_it: An EU Commission Delegated Regulation (2025/1482) setting new, tiered concentration limits for five brominated diphenyl ether flame retardants (listed PBDE) in mixtures and articles, with a stricter step-down schedule for toys and childcare products made from recovered material, and an exclusion for food contact materials.
metadata.why_matters: It sets the concentration limits and step-down dates a workspace moving plastics, consumer goods, toys, or childcare products made from recovered material must track, with the toys/childcare tier reaching a materially stricter final limit (10 mg/kg by 17 May 2027) than the general recovered-material tier (200 mg/kg by 30 December 2027).

recovered-material tier 500 to 350 to 200 mg/kg by 30 December 2025 and 30 December 2027
toys and childcare tier 500 to 350 to 10 mg/kg by 30 December 2025 and 17 May 2027

steps.value: 500 mg/kg (recovered material and toys tiers, on entry into force)
steps.label: both the recovered-material and toys/childcare tiers open at 500 mg/kg on this Regulation's own entry into force
both the recovered-material and toys/childcare tiers step down to 350 mg/kg
the toys and childcare-products tier reaches its final, stricter limit
the general recovered-material tier reaches its final limit

requirement_trajectory.note: two parallel step-down schedules run from the same 500 mg/kg starting point and the same 30 December 2025 midpoint, diverging only at the final step; the general (non-recovered-material) tier is a flat 10 mg/kg from entry into force with no further step-down

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks The Storage of Carbon Dioxide (Access to Infrastructure) Regulations 2011 (UK SI 2011/2305), which govern third-party access to pipelines and storage sites used for carbon dioxide transport and storage in the UK, including the review, publication, and enforcement duties that fall on the owners of that infrastructure and on the authority overseeing it. It exists to give a workspace with any UK carbon-capture-and-storage (CCS) logistics exposure a single place to see the access, publication, and enforcement rules this instrument sets.

FACT: "The Storage of Carbon Dioxide (Access to Infrastructure) Regulations 2011" *Source: The Storage of Carbon Dioxide (Access to Infrastructure) Regulations 2011, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2011/2305

*Analytical inference:* this instrument is fully in force, not prospective: every one of its 20 operative regulations carries its own "Commencement Information" annotation confirming commencement at 16.9.2011 (illustrated by Regulation 1's own annotation below), which corrects a prior record-stage reading of an unrelated cross-reference footnote (about a different Act's amendment) as if it described this instrument's own status.

FACT: "Commencement Information I1 Reg. 1 in force at 16.9.2011, see reg. 1" *Source: The Storage of Carbon Dioxide (Access to Infrastructure) Regulations 2011, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2011/2305

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

FACT: "The owner of relevant infrastructure must publish— (a) no later than the first anniversary of the relevant date, the information set out in paragraph (3) relating to available capacity and technical and operating requirements for access;" *Source: The Storage of Carbon Dioxide (Access to Infrastructure) Regulations 2011, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2011/2305

*Operational implication:* a workspace seeking third-party access to UK CO2 transport pipelines or storage sites (for example, as part of a carbon-capture logistics chain) can expect the infrastructure owner to publish available-capacity and technical-access information on the schedule Section 8 records.

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

FACT: "Where an offence under paragraph (1) or (2) is committed by a body corporate and it is proved to have been committed with the consent or connivance of, or to be attributable to neglect on the part of, an officer of the body corporate, that officer (as well as the body corporate) is guilty of the offence and is liable to be proceeded against and dealt with accordingly." *Source: The Storage of Carbon Dioxide (Access to Infrastructure) Regulations 2011, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2011/2305

*Legal Confirmation Required:* the duties and offences this instrument creates run to the "owner" of relevant infrastructure, the "authority", and any "person" (including an officer of a body corporate) who provides false information to the authority; whether a specific workspace or its officers ever occupy one of these roles is a fact-specific question outside this brief's own corpus and requires counsel review.

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does the officer-liability provision reach a workspace that is a member-managed body rather than a company with directors?**

FACT: "Where the affairs of a body corporate are managed by its members, paragraph (6) applies in relation to the acts and defaults of a member in connection with the member’s functions of management as it applies to an officer of the body corporate." *Source: The Storage of Carbon Dioxide (Access to Infrastructure) Regulations 2011, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2011/2305

*Analytical inference:* the officer-liability regime extends to a member's management functions when a body corporate is member-managed, so the answer is yes for that structure specifically.

**Q2: Is every regulation in this instrument in force?**

FACT: "Commencement Information I1 Reg. 1 in force at 16.9.2011, see reg. 1" *Source: The Storage of Carbon Dioxide (Access to Infrastructure) Regulations 2011, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2011/2305

*Analytical inference:* Regulation 1's own commencement annotation, and the identical annotation on each of the other 19 regulations in this instrument, confirms the whole instrument commenced on 16.9.2011.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

**1. Citation and commencement.** FACT: "These Regulations may be cited as the Storage of Carbon Dioxide (Access to Infrastructure) Regulations 2011, and come into force on the day after the day on which they are made." *Source: The Storage of Carbon Dioxide (Access to Infrastructure) Regulations 2011, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2011/2305

**2. Periodic review duty on the Secretary of State, Scotland excepted.** FACT: "Before the end of each review period, the Secretary of State must— (a) carry out a review of regulations 3 to 22, except in so far as they apply to relevant infrastructure in Scotland or to any function exercised by the Scottish Ministers;" *Source: The Storage of Carbon Dioxide (Access to Infrastructure) Regulations 2011, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2011/2305

*Analytical inference:* this is a Secretary-of-State administrative duty, not a duty running to a workspace; it is surveyed here for completeness but not counted as workspace-adjacent.

**3. Five-year review-period definition.** FACT: "the period of five years beginning with the day on which these Regulations come into force; and (b) subject to paragraph (5), each successive period of five years." *Source: The Storage of Carbon Dioxide (Access to Infrastructure) Regulations 2011, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2011/2305

*Analytical inference:* this defines the recurring cycle for obligation 2 above; also a Secretary-of-State administrative matter, not workspace-adjacent.

**4. Scope limit on construction-authorisation diversion applications.** FACT: "This regulation does not apply where the application for a consent is an application for the grant of a construction authorisation which relates to the construction of a diversion." *Source: The Storage of Carbon Dioxide (Access to Infrastructure) Regulations 2011, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2011/2305

*Analytical inference:* this is a narrow procedural carve-out for one specific application type; surveyed for completeness but not counted as workspace-adjacent absent a workspace application of this specific kind.

**5. Publication-of-capacity duty and first-anniversary deadline.** FACT: "The owner of relevant infrastructure must publish— (a) no later than the first anniversary of the relevant date, the information set out in paragraph (3) relating to available capacity and technical and operating requirements for access;" *Source: The Storage of Carbon Dioxide (Access to Infrastructure) Regulations 2011, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2011/2305

**6. False-information offence and penalty.** FACT: "P provides false information to the authority for the purpose of— (a) inducing the authority to exercise or not to exercise any of the functions conferred on it by these Regulations; or (b) inducing the authority to exercise any of those functions in a particular way. (2) Those circumstances are that, at the time the information is provided, P— (a) knows or believes the information to be false; or (b) is reckless as to whether or not it is false. (3) A person guilty of an offence under paragraph (1) is liable on summary conviction to a fine not exceeding level 5 on the standard scale." *Source: The Storage of Carbon Dioxide (Access to Infrastructure) Regulations 2011, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2011/2305

**7. Prosecution-consent requirement.** FACT: "Proceedings for an offence under paragraph (1) may not be instituted in England and Wales except— (a) by the Secretary of State or by a person authorised to do so by the Secretary of State; or (b) by or with the consent of the Director of Public Prosecutions." *Source: The Storage of Carbon Dioxide (Access to Infrastructure) Regulations 2011, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2011/2305

**8. Officer/body-corporate liability.** FACT: "Where an offence under paragraph (1) or (2) is committed by a body corporate and it is proved to have been committed with the consent or connivance of, or to be attributable to neglect on the part of, an officer of the body corporate, that officer (as well as the body corporate) is guilty of the offence and is liable to be proceeded against and dealt with accordingly." *Source: The Storage of Carbon Dioxide (Access to Infrastructure) Regulations 2011, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2011/2305

**9. Officer-liability extension to member-managed bodies.** FACT: "Where the affairs of a body corporate are managed by its members, paragraph (6) applies in relation to the acts and defaults of a member in connection with the member’s functions of management as it applies to an officer of the body corporate." *Source: The Storage of Carbon Dioxide (Access to Infrastructure) Regulations 2011, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2011/2305

Obligations surveyed: 9; workspace-adjacent: 6; extracted as FACT: 9.

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

FACT: "The owner of relevant infrastructure must publish— (a) no later than the first anniversary of the relevant date, the information set out in paragraph (3) relating to available capacity and technical and operating requirements for access;" *Source: The Storage of Carbon Dioxide (Access to Infrastructure) Regulations 2011, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2011/2305

*Operational implication:* a workspace tracking a specific relevant storage site or pipeline's own "relevant date" (the date consent was granted, or the equivalent pipeline milestone) can calculate this publication deadline directly from that date.

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

FACT: "This regulation does not apply where the application for a consent is an application for the grant of a construction authorisation which relates to the construction of a diversion." *Source: The Storage of Carbon Dioxide (Access to Infrastructure) Regulations 2011, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2011/2305

*Analytical inference:* this scope limit is narrow, confined to construction-authorisation applications that relate specifically to a pipeline diversion; it does not extend to other consent-application types under this instrument.

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 16 September 2011: The Storage of Carbon Dioxide (Access to Infrastructure) Regulations 2011 commence in force (16.9.2011 per the instrument's own commencement annotation; every regulation carries the same commencement date).

FACT: "Commencement Information I1 Reg. 1 in force at 16.9.2011, see reg. 1" *Source: The Storage of Carbon Dioxide (Access to Infrastructure) Regulations 2011, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2011/2305

FACT: "These Regulations may be cited as the Storage of Carbon Dioxide (Access to Infrastructure) Regulations 2011, and come into force on the day after the day on which they are made." *Source: The Storage of Carbon Dioxide (Access to Infrastructure) Regulations 2011, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2011/2305

*Source for timeline entries: The Storage of Carbon Dioxide (Access to Infrastructure) Regulations 2011, legislation.gov.uk (https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2011/2305).*
