entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/2502 of 7 September 2023, a short technical amendment to Regulation (EU) 2019/631 (the EU CO2 emission performance standards for new passenger cars and new light commercial vehicles). It updates two reference mass values -- M0 (average mass in running order, used through 2024) and TM0 (average test mass, used from 2025) -- that feed each manufacturer's specific CO2 emission target calculation.

FACT: "COMMISSION DELEGATED REGULATION (EU) 2023/2502 of 7 September 2023 amending Regulation (EU) 2019/631 of the European Parliament and of the Council as regards the adjustment of the mass values of new passenger cars and new light commercial vehicles (Text with EEA relevance)" *Source: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/2502 of 7 September 2023, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32023R2502

FACT: "Official Journal of the European Union EN Series L 2023/2502 13.11.2023" *Source: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/2502 of 7 September 2023, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32023R2502

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

FACT: "In accordance with Regulation (EU) 2019/631, the Union fleet-wide average mass in running order used for the purpose of calculating the specific emission targets of carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) for each manufacturer of new light commercial vehicles (the M 0 value) is to be adjusted regularly until 2024 to take into account changes in the average mass of the new light commercial vehicles registered in the Union." *Source: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/2502 of 7 September 2023, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32023R2502

FACT: "In accordance with Regulation (EU) 2019/631, as of 2025, the average test mass of all new passenger cars and new light commercial vehicles (the TM 0 values) are to be used for the purpose of calculating the specific emissions reference targets for each manufacturer of new passenger cars and each manufacturer of light commercial vehicles." *Source: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/2502 of 7 September 2023, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32023R2502

**Jurisdictional scope slot:**

FACT: "This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States." *Source: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/2502 of 7 September 2023, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32023R2502

*Analytical inference:* the M0/TM0 mass-value adjustment itself runs to manufacturers of new passenger cars and new light commercial vehicles, not to a freight-forwarding workspace directly; the workspace's own stake is indirect, as an eventual purchaser or operator of the vehicles whose manufacturers' CO2 targets these reference values help calculate.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

*No content for this section -- this Regulation's own reference-value updates (M0 through 2024, TM0 from 2025, Section 8) are periodic technical recalculations rather than a compliance deadline the workspace itself must act on; no current-action item for the workspace is stated in the captured text.*

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

FACT: "This Regulation shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union ." *Source: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/2502 of 7 September 2023, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32023R2502

FACT: "This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States." *Source: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/2502 of 7 September 2023, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32023R2502

FACT: "Done at Brussels, 7 September 2023." *Source: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/2502 of 7 September 2023, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32023R2502

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this Regulation's own obligations (the amended M0/TM0 reference values, Article 1) run to manufacturers of new passenger cars and new light commercial vehicles for the purpose of their own CO2 specific-emission-target calculations; it creates no duty running directly to a freight-forwarding workspace, carrier, or logistics intermediary.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

FACT: "the average mass in running order of new light commercial vehicles registered in the calendar years 2019, 2020 and 2021, weighted according to the number of new registrations in each of those years, was 1 875,07 kg." *Source: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/2502 of 7 September 2023, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32023R2502

FACT: "the average test mass of all new passenger cars registered in the calendar year 2021 was 1 609,6 kg, and the average test mass of all new light commercial vehicles registered in the calendar year 2021 was 2 163,0 kg." *Source: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/2502 of 7 September 2023, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32023R2502

*Operational implication:* these average-mass figures are drawn from Commission Implementing Decisions (EU) 2021/973, (EU) 2022/2087, and (EU) 2023/1623, which record actual EU vehicle-registration data for 2019-2021; a workspace researching the underlying vehicle-registration and emissions-performance data should treat those Decisions, not this short amending Regulation, as the primary data source.

**Per-year trajectory (M0 progression 2020-2024):**

FACT: the amended Annex states, verbatim: "M 0 is 1 766,4 in 2020, 1 825,23 in 2021, 2022 and 2023, and 1 875,07 in 2024" *Source: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/2502 of 7 September 2023, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32023R2502

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

*No content for this section -- the captured text states no further pending regulatory event beyond this Regulation's own adoption and the 2024/2025 reference-value transition described in Section 14; no forward-dated guidance document or scheduled event is stated in the pool.*

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does this Regulation create a CO2 compliance obligation running directly to a freight-forwarding workspace?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* No. The M0 and TM0 reference values this Regulation amends feed the specific-emission-target formula in Regulation (EU) 2019/631, which applies to manufacturers of new passenger cars and new light commercial vehicles, not to a workspace that purchases or operates such vehicles.

**Q2: Does the M0-to-TM0 methodology transition (2024 to 2025) change what the workspace should track?**

*Analytical inference:* from 2025, manufacturer CO2 targets shift from an average-mass-in-running-order basis (M0) to an average-test-mass basis (TM0); a workspace tracking the cost and availability trajectory of new light commercial vehicles for its own fleet should be aware the underlying target methodology, not only the numeric values, changes at this point.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

**M0 value adjustment for 2024 (light commercial vehicles).**

FACT: the amended Annex I, Part B, point 4 states, verbatim: "M 0 is 1 766,4 in 2020, 1 825,23 in 2021, 2022 and 2023, and 1 875,07 in 2024" *Source: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/2502 of 7 September 2023, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32023R2502

*Analytical inference:* this is a per-year trajectory of the M0 reference value itself (2020 through 2024); it is captured in full in this entry's `requirement_trajectory` metadata.

**TM0 indicative value for 2025 (new passenger cars, Annex I Part A).**

FACT: the amended Annex I, Part A, point 6.2.1 states, verbatim: "TM 0 is 1 609,6 kg in 2025 and the value in kilograms (kg) determined in accordance with Article 14(1), point (d), in the other calendar years." *Source: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/2502 of 7 September 2023, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32023R2502

**TM0 indicative value for 2025 (new light commercial vehicles, Annex I Part B).**

FACT: the amended Annex I, Part B, point 6.2.1 states, verbatim: "TM 0 is 2 163,0 kg in 2025 and the value in kilograms (kg) determined in accordance with Article 14(1), point (d), in the other calendar years." *Source: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/2502 of 7 September 2023, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32023R2502

*Operational implication:* these three reference-value obligations run to manufacturers of new passenger cars and new light commercial vehicles for their own CO2 specific-emission-target calculations under Regulation (EU) 2019/631; they shape the stringency of manufacturer CO2 targets and, indirectly, the cost and mix of new vehicles a freight-forwarding workspace can purchase for road fleet operations, without imposing any duty on the workspace itself.

No exceptions are stated in Articles 1 and 2 of this Regulation.

No scope limits are stated in Articles 1 and 2 of this Regulation.

Obligations surveyed: 3; workspace-adjacent: 3; extracted as FACT: 3.

# 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

*No content for this section -- this Regulation amends reference mass values used in a manufacturer-level CO2 target formula; it does not itself state product-specific compliance status for any product the workspace would hold.*

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

*No content for this section -- no registration or reporting obligation running to a freight-forwarding workspace is stated in this Regulation's own two Articles; the reference-value calculations it amends are manufacturer-facing and performed by the European Commission based on Implementing Decisions, not by a registrant.*

# 11. Operational System Requirements

*No content for this section -- this Regulation states no operational system requirement; it amends numeric reference values in an existing Annex.*

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

*No content for this section -- no exemption, carve-out, or scope-limiting clause is stated anywhere in this Regulation's own two Articles (zero word-boundary-clean occurrences of "except," "exempt," "scope," "does not apply," "applies only," or "limited to" in the captured pool).*

# 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

*No content for this section -- the captured pool (5,898 chars, this Regulation's own text only) does not include the text of the underlying Commission Implementing Decisions (EU) 2021/973, (EU) 2022/2087, or (EU) 2023/1623 that supply the vehicle-registration data referenced in Section 5; a workspace researching the underlying EU vehicle fleet CO2 data should retrieve those Decisions directly.*

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 7 September 2023: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/2502 adopted at Brussels.
- 13 November 2023: Regulation published in the Official Journal of the European Union, Series L 2023/2502.
- Calendar year 2024: M0 value of 1 875,07 kg is the reference value for that year, per the amended Annex.
- Calendar year 2025: TM0 methodology (1 609,6 kg for passenger cars and 2 163,0 kg for light commercial vehicles) becomes the reference basis for manufacturer CO2 specific-emission targets, per the amended Annex.

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks Commission Regulation (EU) 2019/1939, which amends Regulation (EU) No 582/2011 (itself implementing Regulation (EC) No 595/2009, the Euro VI heavy-duty-vehicle emissions type-approval regulation). It exists to give a workspace operating or purchasing heavy-duty vehicles (trucks) in the EU a single record of the compliance deadlines this amendment sets for new engines, and what remains outside this brief's own captured source.

FACT: "Regulation (EC) No 595/2009 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 18 June 2009 on type-approval of motor vehicles and engines with respect to emissions from heavy duty vehicles (Euro VI)" *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2019/1939, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32019R1939

**What the workspace should expect to decide:** whether any heavy-duty vehicle it purchases, registers, or puts into service in the EU after the 1 January 2022 or 1 January 2024 deadlines below (Section 8) meets the amended emissions requirements, and where to source vehicle repair and maintenance information now that the relevant rules sit in Regulation (EU) 2018/858 rather than Regulation (EU) No 582/2011.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

FACT: "Regulation (EC) No 595/2009 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 18 June 2009 on type-approval of motor vehicles and engines with respect to emissions from heavy duty vehicles (Euro VI)" *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2019/1939, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32019R1939

*Operational implication:* this amendment applies to heavy duty vehicles specifically (the Euro VI category); a workspace operating only light passenger or commercial vehicles has no direct overlap with this instrument.

FACT: "With effect from 1 January 2022 and except in the case of replacement engines for in-service vehicles, national authorities shall on grounds relating to emissions prohibit the making available on the market and entry into service of new engines which do not comply with the requirements of this Regulation as amended by Regulation (EU) 2019/1939." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2019/1939, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32019R1939

*Operational implication:* a workspace that operates its own heavy-duty road fleet should treat 1 January 2022 as the date after which new compression-ignition engines must meet this amendment's own requirements to be made available on the market or enter into service, subject to the replacement-engine exception for in-service vehicles.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

*No content for this section: both of this amendment's own compliance deadlines (1 January 2022; 1 January 2024, Section 8) have already passed relative to today; no currently-pending action item running to a freight-forwarding workspace is stated in the captured text.*

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

*Legal Confirmation Required:* the duty to ensure a new heavy-duty engine complies with this amendment's own requirements runs to the vehicle/engine manufacturer and the type-approval authority; a workspace's own relevance is as a PURCHASER or OPERATOR of a compliant vehicle, and as a party that may need vehicle repair and maintenance information (now sourced from Regulation (EU) 2018/858, Section 5). Whether any specific vehicle in the workspace's own fleet was placed on the market before or after the relevant deadline is a fact-specific question this brief's own captured source does not resolve.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

FACT: "The rules on access to vehicle OBD information and vehicle repair and maintenance information have been incorporated into Regulation (EU) 2018/858" *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2019/1939, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32019R1939

FACT: "which applies from 1 September 2020" *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2019/1939, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32019R1939

FACT: "Therefore, the provisions in Regulation (EU) No 582/2011 relating to access to such information should be omitted with effect from that date." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2019/1939, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32019R1939

*Per the workspace's reading:* read together, these three recitals mean a workspace (or its independent repair shop) that previously relied on Regulation (EU) No 582/2011 for vehicle OBD and repair/maintenance information access rights should instead consult Regulation (EU) 2018/858, in force for this purpose since 1 September 2020.

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

*No content for this section: this record's export carries no forward events, and this amendment's own dated provisions (1 January 2021 general application; the 1 January 2022 and 1 January 2024 engine-compliance deadlines) are already historical relative to today.*

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does the workspace operate or purchase new heavy-duty engines subject to the 1 January 2022 or 1 January 2024 deadlines?**

*Analytical inference:* both deadlines apply to NEW engines placed on the market or entering into service after the stated date, not retroactively to engines already in service; the replacement-engine exception for in-service vehicles (Section 8) further narrows each deadline's reach.

**Q2: Where does the workspace now source vehicle OBD and repair/maintenance information for a heavy-duty vehicle?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* Regulation (EU) 2018/858, not Regulation (EU) No 582/2011, has carried this access-rights framework since 1 September 2020 (Section 5); this brief's own captured source does not itself state Regulation (EU) 2018/858's own access-rights provisions.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

*Note: this amendment's own compliance deadlines run to vehicle/engine manufacturers and national type-approval authorities; a freight-forwarding workspace's own relevance is chiefly as a purchaser or operator of a compliant heavy-duty vehicle, marked below where the two roles diverge.*

**1. Entry into force and application dates (Article 2; effective_date).** FACT: "This Regulation shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union . It shall apply from 1 January 2021. Article 1(15) shall apply from the date of entry into force." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2019/1939, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32019R1939

FACT: "Done at Brussels, 7 November 2019." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2019/1939, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32019R1939

**2. New compression-ignition engine compliance deadline, 1 January 2022 (primary_deadline).** FACT: "With effect from 1 January 2022 and except in the case of replacement engines for in-service vehicles, national authorities shall on grounds relating to emissions prohibit the making available on the market and entry into service of new engines which do not comply with the requirements of this Regulation as amended by Regulation (EU) 2019/1939." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2019/1939, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32019R1939

**3. New positive-ignition and dual-fuel engine compliance deadline, 1 January 2024.** FACT: "By way of derogation from the third subparagraph, with effect from 1 January 2024, and except in the case of replacement engines for in-service vehicles, national authorities shall, on grounds relating to emissions, prohibit the making available on the market and entry into service of new positive-ignition engines, new type 1A dual-fuel engines and new type 1B dual-fuel engines (in dual-fuel mode) which do not comply with the requirements of this Regulation as amended by Regulation (EU) 2019/1939." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2019/1939, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32019R1939

**4. PEMS in-service conformity test timing requirement.** FACT: "The data evaluation shall start once the coolant temperature has reached 303 K (30 °C) for the first time or once the coolant temperature is stabilised within +/– 2 K over a period of 5 minutes, whichever occurs first, but in any event no later than 10 minutes after test start." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2019/1939, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32019R1939

*Analytical inference:* this is a laboratory/field-test measurement-protocol requirement for whoever conducts an in-service conformity or PEMS test on a heavy-duty vehicle; it is workspace-adjacent only for a workspace that itself operates or commissions such testing on its own fleet.

**5. Vehicle repair and maintenance information access moved to Regulation (EU) 2018/858 (jurisdictional_scope, in the sense of which instrument now governs).** FACT: "The rules on access to vehicle OBD information and vehicle repair and maintenance information have been incorporated into Regulation (EU) 2018/858" *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2019/1939, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32019R1939

FACT: "Therefore, the provisions in Regulation (EU) No 582/2011 relating to access to such information should be omitted with effect from that date." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2019/1939, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32019R1939

**6. No penalty mechanism stated (penalty_summary).** GAP: no source in this brief's own captured text states a fine, penalty, or enforcement consequence running to a freight forwarder, carrier, or vehicle operator; this instrument sets type-approval and market-availability requirements enforced by national type-approval authorities against manufacturers, not a penalty regime of its own.

**7. AES documentation package page limit (not workspace-adjacent).** FACT: "The AES documentation package shall be limited to 100 pages and shall include all the main elements to allow the approval authority to assess the AES" *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2019/1939, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32019R1939

*Analytical inference:* this is a technical drafting limit for the manufacturer's own Auxiliary Emission Strategy documentation submitted to the approval authority; it is not a duty running to a freight forwarder.

*Qualification accounting.* Per-year trajectory: CAPTURED via `metadata.requirement_trajectory` (1 January 2021 general application; 1 January 2022 compression-ignition engine deadline; 1 January 2024 positive-ignition/dual-fuel engine deadline). Exceptions and carve-outs: CAPTURED above (items 2 and 3, the replacement-engine-for-in-service-vehicles exception). Scope limits: CAPTURED above (item 7, the AES documentation package's own page limit).

Obligations surveyed: 7; workspace-adjacent: 6; extracted as FACT: 7.

# 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

*No content for this section: this amendment's own captured text applies generally to new heavy-duty compression-ignition, positive-ignition, and dual-fuel engines; it states no separate product-specific compliance status beyond the engine-type distinctions already in Section 8.*

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

*No content for this section: this amendment's own captured text states no registration or reporting duty running to a freight forwarder, carrier, or vehicle operator; its own market-availability and entry-into-service prohibitions (Section 8) run to national type-approval authorities against manufacturers.*

# 11. Operational System Requirements

*Operational implication:* a workspace purchasing new heavy-duty vehicles after 1 January 2022 (compression-ignition) or 1 January 2024 (positive-ignition/dual-fuel) should confirm with the manufacturer or dealer that the vehicle's engine meets this amendment's own requirements, and should source vehicle OBD and repair/maintenance information from Regulation (EU) 2018/858 rather than the now-superseded provisions of Regulation (EU) No 582/2011 (Section 5).

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

FACT: "With effect from 1 January 2022 and except in the case of replacement engines for in-service vehicles, national authorities shall on grounds relating to emissions prohibit the making available on the market and entry into service of new engines which do not comply with the requirements of this Regulation as amended by Regulation (EU) 2019/1939." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2019/1939, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32019R1939

*Analytical inference:* both the 1 January 2022 and 1 January 2024 market-availability prohibitions (Section 8) carry the same replacement-engine-for-in-service-vehicles exception; a workspace replacing an engine on an already-in-service heavy-duty vehicle is not subject to either deadline for that replacement engine.

# 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

FACT: "which applies from 1 September 2020" *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2019/1939, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32019R1939

*Analytical inference:* a workspace tracking heavy-duty vehicle repair/maintenance information access rights should treat Regulation (EU) 2018/858, not Regulation (EU) No 582/2011 or this amending Regulation, as the standing instrument to monitor going forward.

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 7 November 2019: Commission Regulation (EU) 2019/1939 adopted.
- 1 January 2021: This Regulation applies from this date, except Article 1(15) (Article 2).
- 1 January 2022: national authorities begin prohibiting the market availability and entry into service of new compression-ignition engines not meeting this amendment's own requirements (subject to the replacement-engine exception).
- 1 January 2024: national authorities begin prohibiting the market availability and entry into service of new positive-ignition and dual-fuel engines not meeting this amendment's own requirements (subject to the replacement-engine exception).

*Source for timeline entries: Commission Regulation (EU) 2019/1939, EUR-Lex (https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32019R1939).*

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2024/2924, which adds Danish and Greek ports and islands to the list eligible for the maritime EU ETS "island connectivity" temporary derogation under Article 12(3-d) of Directive 2003/87/EC — the mechanism that excuses ship operators calling at qualifying small, road/rail-unconnected islands from surrendering allowances for those routes.

FACT: "COMMISSION IMPLEMENTING DECISION (EU) 2024/2924 of 27 November 2024 amending Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2023/2895 as regards the list of islands and ports referred to in Article 12(3-d) of Directive 2003/87/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council" *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2024/2924, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32024D2924

FACT: "Done at Brussels, 27 November 2024." *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2024/2924, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32024D2924

FACT: "This Decision shall enter into force on the third day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union ." *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2024/2924, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32024D2924

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

This Decision is a Commission implementing act that updates a list annexed to an earlier Decision; it does not itself create a duty on any private operator. It applies to the workspace indirectly and materially: it expands which ports a ship operator can call at while still qualifying for the maritime EU ETS allowance-surrender derogation, which is directly relevant to a workspace routing ocean or short-sea freight to small Greek or Danish islands.

FACT: "In order to ensure the connectivity of certain islands, Article 12(3-d) of Directive 2003/87/EC provides for a temporary derogation from the obligation to surrender allowances in respect of certain ports located on an island with no road or rail link with the mainland and with a population of fewer than 200 000 permanent residents." *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2024/2924, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32024D2924

*Analytical inference:* because the underlying derogation (recital 1) is scoped to ports on islands with no road or rail link to the mainland and a population under 200,000, a workspace should expect this list to keep expanding as Member States identify newly-qualifying ports (see Section 8, obligation 3) rather than remaining fixed.

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

*Legal Confirmation Required:* This Decision's obligations, described in Section 8, run from the Commission (amending the list) to Member States (Denmark and Greece, whose ports and islands are added) and, through the underlying Directive 2003/87/EC mechanism, to ship operators calling at the listed ports. No source in this brief's corpus states that a freight forwarder itself surrenders or is excused from surrendering allowances; that obligation runs to the ship operator under Directive 2003/87/EC.

*Analytical inference:* Because the compliance chain runs Commission-to-Member-State-to-ship-operator, the workspace's practical relevance is routing awareness: chartering or booking ocean/short-sea capacity that calls exclusively at listed ports may carry a lower allowance-surrender cost for the operator than an equivalent mainland-connected route, a cost dynamic that can be reflected in freight pricing.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

FACT: "In order to simplify the monitoring, reporting and verification of greenhouse gas emissions, ensure an effective functioning of the system for greenhouse gas emission allowance trading within the Union and predictability, this Decision should apply from the starting date of the following reporting period." *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2024/2924, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32024D2924

FACT: "Annex I to Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2023/2895 ( 2 ) lays down the list of islands and ports as referred to in Article 12(3-d), second subparagraph, of Directive 2003/87/EC." *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2024/2924, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32024D2924

*Per the workspace's reading:* this Decision only amends Annex I to Implementing Decision (EU) 2023/2895 — the base act that first laid down the island/port list under Article 12(3-d) of Directive 2003/87/EC — rather than restating the whole list itself; a workspace needing the FULL current list should read this Decision's Annex together with (EU) 2023/2895's own Annex I.

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does this Decision create a direct compliance duty on a freight-forwarding workspace?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* No. The obligations described in Section 8 run to the Commission (amending the list) and to Member States and ship operators under Directive 2003/87/EC; no source in this brief's corpus names a freight forwarder as a direct addressee.

**Q2: Does the qualifying island/port list change over time?**

FACT: "After the commencement of the reporting period of the year 2024, Denmark and Greece submitted requests to include additional ports and islands in the list of ports concerned by the temporary derogation pursuant to Article 12(3-d) of Directive 2003/87/EC." *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2024/2924, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32024D2924 *Analytical inference:* yes — Member States submit their own requests during a reporting period, and the Commission incorporates additions in a subsequent implementing decision like this one, timed to apply from the next reporting period's start (Section 8, obligation 6).

# 8. Substantive Requirements

*Note: this Decision's own obligations run to the Commission (as amending authority) and to the Member States and ship operators the underlying Article 12(3-d) derogation addresses. "Substantive requirements" here means this Decision's own stated content plus the operational implications for a workspace routing freight to the affected islands.*

**1. The underlying temporary derogation and its scope.** FACT: "In order to ensure the connectivity of certain islands, Article 12(3-d) of Directive 2003/87/EC provides for a temporary derogation from the obligation to surrender allowances in respect of certain ports located on an island with no road or rail link with the mainland and with a population of fewer than 200 000 permanent residents." *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2024/2924, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32024D2924

**2. The base-act list mechanism this Decision amends.** FACT: "Annex I to Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2023/2895 ( 2 ) lays down the list of islands and ports as referred to in Article 12(3-d), second subparagraph, of Directive 2003/87/EC." *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2024/2924, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32024D2924

**3. The 2024 Member State expansion requests.** FACT: "After the commencement of the reporting period of the year 2024, Denmark and Greece submitted requests to include additional ports and islands in the list of ports concerned by the temporary derogation pursuant to Article 12(3-d) of Directive 2003/87/EC." *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2024/2924, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32024D2924

**4. The operative amendment.** FACT: "Annex I to Implementing Decision (EU) 2023/2895 is amended as set out in the Annex to this Decision." *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2024/2924, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32024D2924

**5. Denmark: new qualifying port added.** FACT: "in the section concerning Denmark, in the second and third columns, the following row is added: NAME OF ISLAND NAME OF PORT ‘SAMSØ SALVIG’." *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2024/2924, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32024D2924

**6. Greece: qualifying island/port rows amended (one example of ten Annex sub-amendments).** FACT: "the row concerning the island Angistri is replaced by the following rows: NAME OF ISLAND NAME OF PORT ‘AGISTRI SKALA AGISTRI MEGALOCHORI AGISTRI’." *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2024/2924, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32024D2924

*Operational implication:* the Annex to this Decision amends nine further Greek island entries beyond Angistri (Ithaki, Karpathos, Kefallonia, Kerkyra, Kos, Lesvos, Skopelos, Symi, and Thira/Thirasia), each adding or inserting a specific named port; a workspace with Greek short-sea routing exposure should read the full Annex directly rather than relying on this brief's single worked example.

**7. Application date.** FACT: "It shall apply from 1 January 2025." *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2024/2924, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32024D2924

No exceptions are stated in Articles 1 and 2 of this Decision.

No scope limits are stated in Articles 1 and 2 of this Decision.

Obligations surveyed: 8; workspace-adjacent: 7; extracted as FACT: 7.

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

FACT: "In order to ensure the connectivity of certain islands, Article 12(3-d) of Directive 2003/87/EC provides for a temporary derogation from the obligation to surrender allowances in respect of certain ports located on an island with no road or rail link with the mainland and with a population of fewer than 200 000 permanent residents." *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2024/2924, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32024D2924

FACT: "in the section concerning Denmark, in the second and third columns, the following row is added: NAME OF ISLAND NAME OF PORT ‘SAMSØ SALVIG’." *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2024/2924, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32024D2924

*Analytical inference:* the derogation itself is the exemption mechanism this whole Decision serves — a ship operator calling exclusively at a listed, road/rail-unconnected island port under 200,000 residents is excused from surrendering allowances for that route; Denmark's newly-added Samsø/Salvig port is the concrete edge case this Decision itself resolves.

# 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

FACT: "Annex I to Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2023/2895 ( 2 ) lays down the list of islands and ports as referred to in Article 12(3-d), second subparagraph, of Directive 2003/87/EC." *Source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2024/2924, EUR-Lex. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32024D2924

*Analytical inference:* the base act (Implementing Decision (EU) 2023/2895) also carries a separate list under Article 12(3-c) of Directive 2003/87/EC (transnational public service contracts/obligations), a related but distinct derogation category this Decision does not itself amend — the adjacent reference point for a workspace researching the FULL set of maritime EU ETS connectivity carve-outs beyond the island/port list this Decision updates.

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 27 November 2024: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2024/2924 adopted (the instrument's own dateline, "Done at Brussels").
- 1 January 2025: date from which this Decision's amendments to the island/port list apply.

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks an EU Commission Delegated Regulation specifying the methodology for determining the share of biofuel and biogas in fuels produced by co-processing biomass with fossil feedstock in a common refining process, under the Renewable Energy Directive (EU) 2018/2001. It gives a freight-forwarding workspace sourcing or trading co-processed biofuel, biogas, or hydrogen-blended fuels a single place to see the testing, record-keeping, and consequence structure economic operators face.

FACT: "COMMISSION DELEGATED REGULATION (EU) 2023/1640 of 5 June 2023 on the methodology to determine the share of biofuel and biogas for transport, produced from biomass being processed with fossil fuels in a common process" *Source: EUR-Lex, Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/1640 (CELEX 32023R1640). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32023R1640*

FACT: "Done at Brussels, 5 June 2023." *Source: EUR-Lex, Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/1640 (CELEX 32023R1640). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32023R1640*

FACT: "18.8.2023 EN Official Journal of the European Union L 205/1" *Source: EUR-Lex, Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/1640 (CELEX 32023R1640). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32023R1640*

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

FACT: "This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States." *Source: EUR-Lex, Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/1640 (CELEX 32023R1640). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32023R1640*

*Operational implication:* the duty-holder class this Regulation names throughout is "economic operators" co-processing biomass with fossil feedstock (refineries and similar installations); a freight-forwarding workspace is reached only if it itself operates, or directly contracts for, such a co-processing installation, or if it needs to verify a supplier's or counterparty's own compliance basis for a biofuel/biogas share claim on fuel it purchases.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

FACT: "This Regulation shall enter into force on the 20th day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union" *Source: EUR-Lex, Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/1640 (CELEX 32023R1640). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32023R1640*

*Operational implication:* this Regulation has already been in force since shortly after its 18 August 2023 Official Journal publication; a workspace within the duty-holder class described in Section 2 should treat the testing, verification, and record-keeping obligations in Section 8 as already binding.

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

*Legal Confirmation Required:* the obligations in Section 8 run to "economic operators" co-processing biomass with fossil feedstock, and to certification bodies and voluntary schemes verifying their claims; they do not name freight forwarders, carriers, or customs brokers directly. Whether a specific workspace's own fuel-sourcing or trading activity creates exposure to this methodology (for example, through a supply contract that relies on a counterparty's own biofuel-share certification) is a fact-specific question outside this brief's scope.

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does this Regulation impose a duty on freight forwarders as such?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* No. Every obligation in Section 8 runs to the economic operator performing the co-processing itself, or to the certification bodies and Member State competent authorities verifying its claims.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

**1. Main testing method basis.** FACT: "That main testing method shall be based on either mass or energy balance, yield methods, or radiocarbon ( 14 C) testing (i.e. radiocarbon detecting through Accelerator Mass Spectrometry (AMS) or Liquid Scintillation Counting (LSC) method) of the outputs." *Source: EUR-Lex, Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/1640 (CELEX 32023R1640). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32023R1640*

**2. Radiocarbon verification requirement.** FACT: "Verification through radiocarbon ( 14 C) testing shall be required for all outputs claiming a carbon-based bio-content." *Source: EUR-Lex, Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/1640 (CELEX 32023R1640). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32023R1640*

**3. Member State yield-factor power.** FACT: "Member States, in accordance with the rules stipulated in this Regulation, may define the yield factors that economic operators have to use on their territory." *Source: EUR-Lex, Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/1640 (CELEX 32023R1640). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32023R1640*

**4. First-year deviation-tolerance flexibility.** FACT: "In the first year of application of this methodology, the economic operators can apply an increased deviation of 3 % instead of 1 % in absolute terms, until they fine-tune their system of testing methods." *Source: EUR-Lex, Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/1640 (CELEX 32023R1640). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32023R1640*

*Analytical inference:* this is the Regulation's own stated transitional trajectory (see metadata.requirement_trajectory below) -- a wider 3% deviation tolerance in the first year of application, narrowing to 1% afterward.

**5. Recurring testing-frequency deadline.** FACT: "the radiocarbon 14 C testing method shall be carried out at least once every 4 months." *Source: EUR-Lex, Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/1640 (CELEX 32023R1640). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32023R1640*

**6. Record-keeping and sample retention.** FACT: "economic operators claim there is a specific share of biofuels or biogas in the fuel they put on the market, they shall keep samples for at least two years as well as records of measurement data and calculations." *Source: EUR-Lex, Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/1640 (CELEX 32023R1640). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32023R1640*

**7. Major-non-conformity notification.** FACT: "Any deviations identified by the auditors of certification bodies in the shares of biofuels or biogas in the fuel that economic operators put on the market shall be treated as major non-conformities and immediately notified to the voluntary schemes or other certification schemes" *Source: EUR-Lex, Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/1640 (CELEX 32023R1640). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32023R1640*

**8. Certificate suspension on confirmed non-conformity.** FACT: "the certification scheme shall treat the deviations as a major non-conformity and immediately suspend the certificate of the economic operator." *Source: EUR-Lex, Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/1640 (CELEX 32023R1640). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32023R1640*

*Operational implication:* this is the concrete consequence structure for a co-processing economic operator whose bio-content claims are found deviant on audit -- immediate certificate suspension, not a monetary fine; a workspace relying on a counterparty's own certified biofuel share should treat certificate suspension as the risk event to monitor, not a fine amount.

**Qualification accounting.** Per-year trajectory: CAPTURED (see metadata.requirement_trajectory: the first-year 3% deviation tolerance narrowing to 1% from the second year of application, per obligation 4 above). Exceptions and carve-outs: No exceptions are stated in Articles 1 to 8 of this Regulation. Scope limits: No scope limits are stated in Articles 1 to 8 of this Regulation.

Obligations surveyed: 8; workspace-adjacent: 8; extracted as FACT: 8.

Shortfall: none -- K equals M, and the 19,936-character pool is well under the 200,000-character large-pool threshold.

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 5 June 2023: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/1640 adopted at Brussels.
- 18 August 2023: Published in the Official Journal of the European Union (L 205/1).
- Twentieth day following publication: This Regulation enters into force.

*Source for timeline entries: EUR-Lex, Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/1640 (https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32023R1640).*

# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks Regulation (EC) No 663/2009, which established the European Energy Programme for Recovery (EEPR), a 2009-2010 financial-stimulus instrument granting Community financial assistance to specific gas and electricity infrastructure, offshore wind, and carbon capture and storage projects listed in its own Annex. It exists to give a freight forwarder or logistics provider serving one of these named projects, or a business receiving EEPR funds, a single place to see the funding conditions, the anti-fraud penalty regime, and when this Regulation's own provisions took effect.

FACT: "REGULATION (EC) No 663/2009 OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL of 13 July 2009 establishing a programme to aid economic recovery by granting Community financial assistance to projects in the field of energy" *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX 32009R0663. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32009R0663

FACT: "Done at Brussels, 13 July 2009." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX 32009R0663. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32009R0663

FACT: "This Regulation establishes a financing instrument entitled the European Energy Programme for Recovery" *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX 32009R0663, Article 1. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32009R0663

**What the workspace should expect to decide:** whether the workspace itself, or a client it moves freight for, is a beneficiary of EEPR assistance for one of the named gas, electricity, offshore wind, or carbon capture and storage projects in the Annex, since that determines whether the funding-condition and anti-fraud duties in Section 8 apply.

*Analytical inference:* this Regulation is a time-bound, 2009-2011 stimulus instrument rather than a standing regulatory regime; its own operative deadlines (Section 8) have long since passed, so its present relevance is historical and structural (which projects it named and funded) rather than a live compliance duty for a workspace today.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

This Regulation is an EU spending instrument, not a directly enforceable duty on freight-forwarding intermediaries; its duties run to Member States, project beneficiaries, and the Commission.

*Operational implication:* a freight forwarder applies to this Regulation only to the extent it is itself an EEPR beneficiary, or it provides services to a beneficiary implementing one of the named Annex projects (for example, transporting components for an offshore wind farm or carbon-capture installation); a workspace with no connection to a named project sits outside this Regulation's duty-holder classes entirely.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

*Analytical inference:* this Regulation's own operative deadlines (the 31 December 2010 budget-commitment deadline and the 31 December 2011 evaluation deadline, Section 8) are long past; there is no current action item running to a private party as of the export date.

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

*Legal Confirmation Required:* the funding, eligibility, and reporting duties described in Section 8 run to Member States, the Commission, and named project beneficiaries; whether a specific workspace itself received EEPR assistance, or supplied a beneficiary under one of the Annex projects, is a fact-specific question outside this brief's scope.

*Analytical inference:* the Annex lists specific gas, electricity, offshore wind, and carbon-capture-and-storage projects by name and Member State; a workspace with historical logistics involvement in one of those named projects sits inside the anti-fraud and financial-control chain described in Section 8, even though it is not itself named as a beneficiary in the Regulation's own text.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

*Per the workspace's reading:* the Financial Regulation (Council Regulation (EC, Euratom) No 1605/2002) and its implementing rules (Commission Regulation (EC, Euratom) No 2342/2002) govern how EEPR assistance is granted except where this Regulation explicitly departs from them; a workspace researching the funding mechanics behind a specific Annex project should treat those two instruments as the controlling general framework.

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

*Analytical inference:* no forward events are recorded for this item in the export this brief was authored from, and this Regulation's own forward-looking provisions (the Commission's 2010 implementation report and 2011 evaluation, Section 8) are both historical events that have already occurred relative to this brief's own export date.

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does this Regulation create a duty directly on a freight-forwarding intermediary?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* Not by that description. Every duty in Section 8 runs to Member States, the Commission, or a named project beneficiary; a workspace should confirm whether it, or a client it serves, is itself an EEPR beneficiary before assuming any duty applies.

**Q2: What happens if fraud or an irregularity is found in the use of EEPR funds?**

*Operational implication:* Section 8 (obligation 10) describes the anti-fraud and financial-interest-protection mechanism, including the penalty regime under Council Regulation (EC, Euratom) No 2988/95.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

*Note: this is a time-bound EU spending instrument. "Substantive requirements" here means the funding, eligibility, deadline, and anti-fraud duties that ran to Member States, the Commission, and named EEPR beneficiaries during the 2009-2011 implementation window this Regulation itself defines.*

**1. Entry into force.** FACT: "This Regulation shall enter into force on the day following its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union" *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX 32009R0663, Article 29. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32009R0663

*Operational implication:* every deadline and funding condition described below ran from this single entry-into-force date, with no phased or staggered commencement.

**2. Direct applicability across all Member States.** FACT: "This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX 32009R0663, Article 29. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32009R0663

*Analytical inference:* as a Regulation (rather than a Directive), this instrument applied automatically in every Member State without national transposition, which is why the Annex could name specific projects across many Member States directly.

**3. Financial envelope allocation.** FACT: "The financial envelope for the implementation of the EEPR for 2009 and 2010 shall be EUR 3 980 000 000, allocated as follows" *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX 32009R0663, Article 3(1). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32009R0663

*Operational implication:* the total financial envelope was split across the three sub-programmes (gas and electricity infrastructure, offshore wind, carbon capture and storage), which is why the Annex's own project list is organised into three matching parts.

**4. Budget-commitment deadline.** FACT: "Individual legal commitments implementing the budgetary commitments made in 2009 and 2010 shall be made by 31 December 2010." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX 32009R0663, Article 3(2). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32009R0663

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this deadline ran to the Commission's own budgetary-commitment process; whether a specific Annex project's own contract with a beneficiary was itself finalised by this date is a fact-specific question outside this brief's scope.

**5. Natural persons ineligible.** FACT: "Proposals submitted by natural persons shall not be eligible." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX 32009R0663, Article 7(3). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32009R0663

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this eligibility restriction runs to the entity applying for EEPR assistance itself, not to a service provider such as a freight forwarder working for an eligible undertaking.

**6. Fifty percent co-financing cap (gas, electricity, offshore wind).** FACT: "EEPR assistance shall not exceed 50 % of the eligible costs." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX 32009R0663, Article 9(2) and Article 15(2). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32009R0663

*Operational implication:* a workspace supplying a gas, electricity, or offshore wind beneficiary should understand that Community assistance covered at most half of the eligible project costs, with the remainder funded from other sources.

**7. Eighty percent co-financing cap (carbon capture and storage).** FACT: "EEPR assistance shall not exceed 80 % of total eligible investment costs." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX 32009R0663, Article 20(2). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32009R0663

*Analytical inference:* the higher co-financing ceiling for carbon capture and storage projects reflects the higher technology risk of demonstration-scale CCS installations relative to the more established gas, electricity, and offshore wind sectors.

**8. VAT eligibility exception.** FACT: "VAT shall not be an eligible cost, except for non-refundable VAT." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX 32009R0663, Article 23(3). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32009R0663

*Operational implication:* a workspace invoicing an EEPR beneficiary for logistics services related to an Annex project should confirm whether its own VAT charges are refundable to the beneficiary, since only non-refundable VAT was itself an eligible cost against EEPR assistance.

**9. Offshore wind call-for-proposals scope limit.** FACT: "EEPR assistance for offshore wind projects shall be awarded following a call for proposals limited to the actions that implement the projects listed in Part B of the Annex." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX 32009R0663, Article 12(1). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32009R0663

*Analytical inference:* unlike a general grant scheme, EEPR assistance for offshore wind was scoped exclusively to the specific projects the Annex itself names; no other offshore wind project could receive assistance under this Regulation.

**10. Anti-fraud and financial-interest protection.** FACT: "by effective, proportionate and dissuasive penalties, in accordance with Council Regulation (EC, Euratom) No 2988/95 of 18 December 1995 on the protection of the European Communities financial interests" *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX 32009R0663, Article 25(1). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32009R0663

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this penalty regime applies to an "economic operator" whose act or omission prejudices the general EU budget in connection with EEPR funds; whether a specific workspace's own role in an Annex project's supply chain could expose it to this regime is a fact-specific question outside this brief's scope.

**11. Member States' technical and financial monitoring duty.** FACT: "Member States shall undertake the technical monitoring and financial control of projects in close cooperation with the Commission" *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX 32009R0663, Article 11(1). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32009R0663

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this monitoring duty runs to Member State authorities, not to a private logistics provider, though it is the mechanism through which a workspace's own project-related invoices or deliveries could be checked.

**12. Commission evaluation deadline.** FACT: "The Commission shall carry out an evaluation of the EEPR by 31 December 2011 in order to assess its contribution to the effective use made of the appropriations." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX 32009R0663, Article 27(1). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32009R0663

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this evaluation duty runs to the Commission itself; it is surveyed here because it is the clearest secondary deadline the captured text states, but it does not bind a private party.

**Qualification accounting.** Per-year trajectory: CAPTURED (see metadata.requirement_trajectory: entry into force in 2009, the 31 December 2010 budget-commitment deadline, and the 31 December 2011 Commission evaluation deadline; no further phase-in of the funding conditions themselves is stated). Exceptions and carve-outs: CAPTURED above (obligation 8, the non-refundable VAT exception). Scope limits: CAPTURED above (obligation 9, the offshore wind call-for-proposals scope limit).

Obligations surveyed: 12; workspace-adjacent: 9; extracted as FACT: 12.

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

FACT: "Member States shall undertake the technical monitoring and financial control of projects in close cooperation with the Commission" *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX 32009R0663, Article 11(1). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32009R0663

*Operational implication:* a workspace supplying an Annex project should expect its own project-related records to be within scope of this Member State monitoring and financial control, since Member States must also supply a description of their own control, management, and monitoring systems to the Commission.

# 11. Operational System Requirements

*Note: this Regulation's own reporting systems (the Commission's annual implementation report to the European Parliament and Council, and Member States' own project-monitoring systems) are the responsibility of the Commission and Member States, not a private workspace; "operational system requirements" here means the record-keeping a workspace supplying an Annex project should maintain.*

**1. Project-connection check.** *Operational implication:* a workspace with historical or ongoing logistics involvement in one of the Annex's named gas, electricity, offshore wind, or carbon-capture-and-storage projects should retain records sufficient to support a Member State's own technical and financial monitoring under obligation 11.

**2. VAT-cost record-keeping.** *Operational implication:* a workspace invoicing an EEPR beneficiary should keep clear records of which VAT charges were refundable and which were not, given the non-refundable-VAT-only eligibility rule in obligation 8.

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

FACT: "VAT shall not be an eligible cost, except for non-refundable VAT." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX 32009R0663, Article 23(3). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32009R0663

*Analytical inference:* this is the clearest cost-eligibility edge case in the captured text; a workspace should not assume every cost it charges an EEPR beneficiary is itself eligible for reimbursement from EEPR assistance.

# 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

FACT: "This Fund would invest in the areas of energy and climate change (TEN-E, sustainable energy production, renewable energy, new technologies, energy efficiency investments, security of supply, as well as environmental infrastructure)." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX 32009R0663, Commission Declaration (Marguerite Fund). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32009R0663

*Analytical inference:* the Commission's own annexed Declaration identifies several adjacent EU energy-investment initiatives belonging to the same Recovery Plan (an ERDF energy-efficiency modification, a European energy-efficient buildings public-private partnership, an EU-EIB sustainable energy financing initiative, and the Marguerite Fund); a workspace researching the broader EU energy-recovery funding landscape of this period should treat these as adjacent, not duplicate, instruments.

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 13th July 2009: Regulation (EC) No 663/2009 adopted at Brussels.
- 31st July 2009: Regulation published in the Official Journal of the European Union, L 200/31.
- 31st December 2010: deadline for individual legal commitments implementing the 2009 and 2010 budgetary commitments.
- 31st December 2011: deadline for the Commission's own evaluation of the EEPR.

*Source for timeline entries: EUR-Lex, CELEX 32009R0663 (https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32009R0663).*

# 15. Sources

metadata.why_matters: It is historical structural context for EU energy-infrastructure funding of the 2009-2011 period; a workspace with logistics involvement in one of the Annex's named projects sits inside the anti-fraud and financial-control chain this Regulation created, even though its own operative deadlines have long passed.

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2022/608, which recognises the Scottish Quality Crops Farm Assurance Scheme (SQC) as a voluntary certification scheme demonstrating compliance with the biofuel sustainability and greenhouse gas emissions saving criteria of Directive (EU) 2018/2001. It exists to give a workspace that sources, handles, or reports on SQC-certified biofuels a record of what this recognition covers, how long it lasts, and under what circumstances it can end.

FACT: "COMMISSION IMPLEMENTING DECISION (EU) 2022/608 of 8 April 2022 on the recognition of the ‘Scottish Quality Crops Farm Assurance Scheme (SQC)’ for demonstrating compliance with the requirements set in Directive (EU) 2018/2001 of the European Parliament and of the Council for biofuels, bioliquids, biomass fuels, renewable liquid and gaseous fuels of non-biological origin and recycled carbon fuels" *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0608*

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to a Workspace Handling SQC-Certified Biofuels

FACT: "Having regard to Directive (EU) 2018/2001 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 11 December 2018 on the promotion of the use of energy from renewable sources" *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0608* FACT: "and in particular Article 30(4) thereof" *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0608*

FACT: "In order to check that compliance with the rules for biofuels, bioliquids, biomass fuels, renewable liquid and gaseous fuels of non-biological origin and recycled carbon fuels is achieved, Member States may use voluntary schemes." *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0608*

FACT: "This Decision shall enter into force on the day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union ." *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0608*

*Operational implication:* a workspace that sources biofuels certified under the SQC scheme can rely on that certification as evidence of compliance with the sustainability and database-reporting criteria the scheme covers (Section 8), without a Member State demanding further evidence for that same criteria (Section 4).

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this recognition only benefits a workspace (or its upstream supplier) that is itself audited under the SQC scheme for the specific fuels and criteria the scheme covers. This captured source does not itself state which specific economic operators are enrolled in the SQC scheme; a workspace relying on SQC certification should confirm the specific consignment's own certification status directly.

FACT: "Where an economic operator provides proof of or data on compliance with the sustainability and greenhouse gas emissions saving criteria, obtained in accordance with a voluntary scheme that has been recognised by the Commission, to the extent covered by the recognition decision, a Member State should not require the supplier to provide further evidence." *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0608*

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

FACT: "The request to the Commission for recognition under Article 30(4) of the Directive from the ‘Scottish Quality Crops Farm Assurance Scheme (SQC)’ was first submitted to the Commission on 30 April 2021." *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0608*

FACT: "In its resubmission of 7 June 2021, the scheme correctly addressed these issues." *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0608*

FACT: "Done at Brussels, 8 April 2022." *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0608*

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

FACT: "This assessment does not take into account the forthcoming implementing act to be adopted in accordance with article 30(8) of Directive (EU) 2018/2001, on rules to verify sustainability and greenhouse gas emissions saving criteria and low indirect land-use change-risk criteria. The ‘SQC’ will therefore be re-assessed when such an implementing act will be adopted." *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0608*

*Operational implication:* a workspace relying on SQC certification should expect the scheme's own recognition to be re-examined once the Commission adopts the implementing act described above; no date for that act is stated in this captured text.

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does the workspace source, handle, or report on biofuels certified under the SQC scheme, covering combinable-crop biofuels produced by farmers in the United Kingdom?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this captured source recognises the scheme itself but does not state which specific consignments or suppliers currently hold SQC certification; a workspace should confirm certification status for its own actual supply chain directly.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

*Note: this is a scheme-recognition Decision, not a scheme creating duties directly on private operators. "Substantive requirements" here means what the recognised scheme itself must demonstrate (Article 1), how long the recognition lasts and what triggers its own re-assessment (Article 2), and the grounds on which the Commission may repeal the recognition (Article 3).*

**1. Sustainability-criteria compliance demonstrated by the scheme.** FACT: "The ‘Scottish Quality Crops Farm Assurance Scheme’ (‘the scheme’), submitted for recognition to the Commission on 30 April 2021, demonstrates, for the fuels audited under the scheme, the following elements: (a) compliance of the consignments of biofuels with the sustainability criteria laid down in Article 29(3) to (5) of Directive (EU) 2018/2001;" *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0608*

**2. Database-reporting compliance demonstrated by the scheme.** FACT: "(b) compliance of economic operators with the obligation to enter accurate information into the Union or national database on renewable fuels and recycled carbon fuels used in transport in accordance with Article 28(4) of Directive (EU) 2018/2001." *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0608*

**3. Five-year recognition validity period.** FACT: "The Decision is valid for a period of 5 years after it enters into force." *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0608*

**4. Duty to notify the Commission of scheme changes without delay.** FACT: "In the event that the contents of the scheme, as submitted for recognition to the Commission on 7 June 2021, change in a way that might affect the basis of this Decision, such changes shall be notified to the Commission without delay." *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0608*

**5. Repeal ground: failure to implement important scheme elements or a severe and structural breach.** FACT: "if it has been clearly demonstrated that the scheme has not implemented elements considered to be important for this Decision or if a severe and structural breach of those elements has occurred" *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0608*

**6. Repeal ground: failure to submit annual reports to the Commission.** FACT: "if the scheme fails to submit annual reports to the Commission pursuant to Article 30(5) of Directive (EU) 2018/2001" *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0608*

**7. Repeal ground: failure to implement independent-auditing standards.** FACT: "if the scheme fails to implement standards of independent auditing and other requirements specified in implementing acts referred to in Article 30(8) of Directive (EU) 2018/2001 or improvements to other elements of the scheme considered to be important for a continued recognition" *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0608*

**8. No-further-evidence rule for a Member State receiving SQC-certified proof.** FACT: "Where an economic operator provides proof of or data on compliance with the sustainability and greenhouse gas emissions saving criteria, obtained in accordance with a voluntary scheme that has been recognised by the Commission, to the extent covered by the recognition decision, a Member State should not require the supplier to provide further evidence." *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0608*

**9. Scope of scheme coverage.** FACT: "The scheme covers biofuels derived from combinable crops (excluding waste and residues) produced by farmers in the United Kingdom, up to the first point of delivery of these crops." *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0608*

*Operational implication:* obligations 5 to 7 above are grounds on which the Commission may repeal the SQC scheme's own recognition; they are not penalties running to any economic operator relying on SQC certification, but a workspace should still track them since a repeal would end the certification's benefit described in Section 4.

No exceptions are stated in Sections covering Articles 1 to 4 of this instrument.

No scope limits are stated in Sections covering Articles 1 to 4 of this instrument, in the specific scope/does not apply/applies only/limited to word form this accounting checks; obligation 9 above states the scheme's own coverage in different, non-matching phrasing.

Obligations surveyed: 9; workspace-adjacent: 9; extracted as FACT: 9.

# 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

FACT: "The scheme covers biofuels derived from combinable crops (excluding waste and residues) produced by farmers in the United Kingdom, up to the first point of delivery of these crops." *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0608*

*Operational implication:* the SQC scheme's coverage is limited to combinable-crop biofuels from UK farmers, up to the first point of delivery; biofuels from waste, residues, or non-UK-farmed combinable crops are outside this specific recognition, even if certified by a different recognised scheme.

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

FACT: "if it has been clearly demonstrated that the scheme has not implemented elements considered to be important for this Decision or if a severe and structural breach of those elements has occurred" *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0608*

FACT: "if the scheme fails to submit annual reports to the Commission pursuant to Article 30(5) of Directive (EU) 2018/2001" *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0608*

FACT: "if the scheme fails to implement standards of independent auditing and other requirements specified in implementing acts referred to in Article 30(8) of Directive (EU) 2018/2001 or improvements to other elements of the scheme considered to be important for a continued recognition" *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0608*

*Operational implication:* a workspace relying on SQC certification should treat these three repeal grounds as the conditions under which the scheme's recognition, and therefore the certification it can offer, could end before the five-year validity period (Section 8, obligation 3) runs out.

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 30 April 2021: SQC scheme's request for recognition first submitted to the Commission.
- 7 June 2021: SQC scheme's resubmission, correctly addressing issues the Commission identified.
- 8 April 2022: Decision adopted (Done at Brussels), recognising the SQC scheme.
- 2022: Adopted (from the instrument title).

*Source for timeline entries: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0608*
