entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2020/1208, which sets the structure, format, and submission processes for Member State reporting to the European Commission under the Energy Union Governance Regulation (EU) 2018/1999: national greenhouse gas inventories, climate adaptation actions, auctioning revenue use, and policies and measures projections. It exists to give a freight forwarder with EU exposure a record of what this Regulation requires of Member States and whether it creates any direct duty on a private workspace.

FACT: "Scope This Regulation applies to the reports submitted by the Member States containing data required for the year 2021 onwards." *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2020/1208. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32020R1208

*Analytical inference:* every substantive obligation in this Regulation runs from a Member State to the European Commission; it is government-to-government reporting infrastructure, not a private-party compliance instrument, so its relevance to the workspace is as background on the EU climate-governance data pipeline, not as a source of a direct duty.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

FACT: "This Regulation establishes rules implementing Regulation (EU) 2018/1999 as regards the following" *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2020/1208. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32020R1208

*Legal Confirmation Required:* none of the five reporting streams this Regulation implements, national adaptation actions, greenhouse gas inventories, national inventory systems, the comprehensive review, and policies/measures projections, names a private freight-forwarding operator as a reporting party; whether any specific national inventory ever requires activity-level data from a workspace's own operations is a separate, fact-specific question for the relevant national inventory authority.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

*No content for this section: every obligation in the captured text runs to Member States, not to a private freight-forwarding workspace, and no workspace-facing deadline is stated.*

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

FACT: "This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States." *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2020/1208. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32020R1208

*Analytical inference:* as a directly applicable EU Regulation, the compliance chain it creates runs from the Union to Member States and their national inventory authorities; a freight-forwarding workspace sits outside that chain entirely, as neither a reporting party nor a named data source.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

FACT: "Member States and the Commission shall cooperate and coordinate in preparing the Union greenhouse gas inventory and of the Union inventory report in accordance with the timescales set out in Annex XXI." *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2020/1208. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32020R1208

*Per the workspace's reading:* this Regulation is itself the operative implementing detail for Regulation (EU) 2018/1999's own reporting framework; a workspace with a specific question about a Member State's own climate reporting timetable should consult the relevant national inventory authority directly.

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

*No content for this section: the export's own forward_events list is empty, and the captured text states no pending or forward-looking regulatory event beyond the annual reporting cycles already described in Section 8.*

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does this Regulation create a direct regulatory obligation on a private freight-forwarding workspace?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* No. FACT: "Scope This Regulation applies to the reports submitted by the Member States containing data required for the year 2021 onwards." *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2020/1208. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32020R1208 Every reporting duty in this Regulation runs from a Member State to the Commission; no provision names a private operator as a duty-holder.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

*Note: every duty-holder in this Regulation is a Member State reporting to the European Commission. "Substantive requirements" below means the Regulation's own stated Member State reporting obligations and timescales, none of which runs directly to a private freight-forwarding workspace.*

**1. Subject matter: five reporting streams implemented.** FACT: "This Regulation establishes rules implementing Regulation (EU) 2018/1999 as regards the following" *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2020/1208. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32020R1208

*Analytical inference:* these five streams, adaptation actions and auctioning revenue use, greenhouse gas inventories, national inventory systems, the comprehensive review, and policies/measures projections, together define this Regulation's full operative scope.

**2. Scope in time.** FACT: "Scope This Regulation applies to the reports submitted by the Member States containing data required for the year 2021 onwards." *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2020/1208. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32020R1208

*Analytical inference:* this Regulation's own reporting formats apply only to data required for the year 2021 onward; earlier reporting years are governed by the transitional rule (obligation 8 below).

**3. Monthly compiled-information availability deadline.** FACT: "the information received pursuant to this paragraph shall be made available, in electronic form and no later than at the end of the month referred to above." *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2020/1208. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32020R1208

*Analytical inference:* this deadline governs the Commission's own compilation and electronic publication of Member State-submitted data; it is not a submission deadline running to a private party.

**4. Annex-specific due date and verification window.** FACT: "The data reported here shall be consistent with verified emissions as accounted for in the EU transaction log referred to in Article 20 of Directive 2003/87/EC five working days before the due date for the submission of this Annex." *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2020/1208. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32020R1208

*Analytical inference:* this ties a specific Annex's own reporting content to the EU Emissions Trading System transaction log, five working days ahead of that Annex's due date; both the transaction log and the due date are Member State-facing.

**5. Reporting on use of Effort Sharing Regulation transfer revenues.** FACT: "Member States shall report the information on the use of revenues in accordance with Article 5(6) of Regulation (EU) 2018/842 referred to in point (n) of Part 1 of Annex V to Regulation (EU) 2018/1999 in accordance with the format set out in Annex XIX to this Regulation." *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2020/1208. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32020R1208

*Analytical inference:* this is a Member State reporting duty on how proceeds from Effort Sharing Regulation allocation transfers are used; it does not create a reporting duty on a private operator.

**6. Reporting on accounted greenhouse gas emissions and removals.** FACT: "Member States shall report accounted greenhouse gas emissions and removals pursuant to Article 26(5) of Regulation (EU) 2018/1999 in accordance with the format set out in Annex XX." *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2020/1208. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32020R1208

*Analytical inference:* this is a Member State reporting duty under the LULUCF accounting framework (Regulation (EU) 2018/1999, Article 26(5)); no private-party reporting duty attaches.

**7. Cooperation and coordination timescales for the Union inventory.** FACT: "Member States and the Commission shall cooperate and coordinate in preparing the Union greenhouse gas inventory and of the Union inventory report in accordance with the timescales set out in Annex XXI." *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2020/1208. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32020R1208

*Analytical inference:* this is a Member State-Commission coordination duty for preparing the aggregated Union-level greenhouse gas inventory; no private-party role is stated.

**8. Transitional rule for 2019 and 2020 reporting data.** FACT: "Implementing Regulation (EU) No 749/2014 shall continue to have effect for the reports containing the data required for the years 2019 and 2020." *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2020/1208. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32020R1208

*Analytical inference:* this is why obligation 2's own 2021-onward scope statement does not create a gap for the two preceding reporting years; the predecessor Implementing Regulation continues to govern them.

**Required-slot grounding.** FACT: "This Regulation shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union" *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2020/1208. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32020R1208

**Qualification accounting.** Per-year trajectory: No phase-in is stated in Articles 1 to 41, only a one-time transition from Implementing Regulation (EU) No 749/2014, obligation 8 above. Exceptions and carve-outs: No exceptions are stated in Articles 1 to 41. Scope limits: CAPTURED above (obligation 2, the Article 2 scope-in-time statement).

Obligations surveyed: 8; workspace-adjacent: 0; extracted as FACT: 8.

# 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

*No content for this section: the captured source addresses Member State reporting formats, not any product-specific compliance status.*

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

*No content for this section: every registration and reporting duty stated in the captured source, Section 8 above, runs from Member States to the European Commission, not from a private freight-forwarding workspace to any authority.*

# 11. Operational System Requirements

*No content for this section: the technical and system requirements stated in the captured source (national inventory system arrangements, the e-platform referred to in Article 28 of Regulation (EU) 2018/1999) are Member State obligations, not requirements running to a private freight-forwarding workspace.*

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

*No content for this section: no exception or edge case running to a private freight-forwarding workspace is stated in Articles 1 to 41; the transitional rule, obligation 8 in Section 8, addresses Member State reporting-year coverage, not a workspace-facing carve-out.*

# 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

*No content for this section: the captured source is a single EU Implementing Regulation and its reporting-template annexes, with no adjacent industry research or comparative-jurisdiction content of its own.*

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 7 August 2020: This Regulation was adopted. FACT: "Done at Brussels, 7 August 2020." *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2020/1208. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32020R1208
- 1 January 2021: The date from which this Regulation applies. FACT: "It shall apply from 1 January 2021." *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2020/1208. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32020R1208

*Source for timeline entries: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2020/1208 (https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32020R1208).*

# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks Regulation (EU) 2023/435, which amends the Recovery and Resilience Facility Regulation (EU) 2021/241 to add "REPowerEU chapters" -- funded partly through auctioned EU emissions-allowance revenue -- letting Member States fund energy-security, energy-efficiency and zero-emission-transport-infrastructure measures within their national recovery and resilience plans. It exists to give a freight-forwarding workspace a single record of this funding mechanism, since its own legal duties run to Member States and the Commission, not to a private operator directly.

*Analytical inference:* the discussion below reads this Regulation as a Member-State funding-and-planning instrument; Section 8 surveys four of its measures as workspace-adjacent because they shape available funding for zero-emission transport infrastructure (including rail) and SME energy-cost relief, not because any clause here creates a direct duty on a freight-forwarding operator.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

FACT: the captured source states, verbatim: «This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States.»

**1. REPowerEU chapter requirement.** FACT: «Recovery and resilience plans submitted to the Commission after 1 March 2023 that require the use of additional funding under Articles 14, 21a or 21b, shall include a REPowerEU chapter containing measures and their corresponding milestones and targets.»

Stakeholder consultation on recovery and resilience plans.** FACT: the captured source states, verbatim: «the Member States should provide a summary of the consultation process, conducted in accordance with national legal frameworks, of local and regional authorities, social partners and other relevant stakeholders concerned with the implementation of their recovery and resilience plans.»

*Analytical inference:* a freight or logistics trade association could be one of the "other relevant stakeholders" a Member State consults when finalising its REPowerEU chapter, giving the sector an input channel into which transport-infrastructure measures get funded.

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks SI 2001/662, a UK Climate Change Levy instrument that defines the technical eligibility test and energy-calculation rules for a facility to be included in a climate change agreement (CCA) -- a reduced Climate Change Levy rate scheme for energy-intensive installations. It exists to give a freight forwarder that operates, or serves, an energy-intensive facility a single place to see: the 90% eligibility test, how "reckonable energy" is calculated, and which generation types are calculated differently.

FACT: "The Climate Change Agreements (Eligible Facilities) Regulations 2001" *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2001/662. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2001/662

**What the workspace should expect to decide:** whether any facility it operates, or any counterparty facility whose Climate Change Levy status affects its own costs, meets the 90% reckonable-energy threshold this instrument sets, and if so, which of the three energy-calculation rules (general, dedicated electricity generation plant, or combined heat and power) applies to it.

*Analytical inference:* this instrument is a technical eligibility-definition regulation, not a rate-setting or penalty-creating one; its own duties run to the determination of facility eligibility for a climate change agreement, not to a freight forwarder directly.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

FACT: "These Regulations provide that a facility is to be eligible for inclusion in a climate change agreement only where it is likely that at least 90% of the energy supplied to the facility will be used within an energy intensive installation." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2001/662. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2001/662

*Operational implication:* the instrument applies to the workspace indirectly, through any energy-intensive facility (its own, or a counterparty's) whose Climate Change Levy discount depends on meeting this 90% threshold -- the calculation method (Section 8) determines whether that facility retains its lower-levy eligible status.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

*No content for this section is grounded in the item's captured source pool.*

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this instrument's own eligibility test (Section 8) is applied "in connection with concluding or varying a climate change agreement" between the facility operator and the relevant sector association or the Environment Agency (under the Finance Act 2000 Schedule 6 framework, outside this brief's captured pool); whether a specific workspace itself holds or benefits from such an agreement is a fact-specific question outside this brief's scope.

*Analytical inference:* the workspace's practical exposure is indirect -- as an operator of, or party dealing with, a facility whose Climate Change Levy rate depends on this instrument's own eligibility calculation, not as a direct duty-holder under this instrument itself.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

FACT: "Made 2nd March 2001 Laid before Parliament 9th March 2001 Coming into force 1st April 2001" *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2001/662. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2001/662

*Per the workspace's reading:* this instrument is made under the Secretary of State's powers in paragraphs 50(3) to (5) and 146 of Schedule 6 to the Finance Act 2000 (the Climate Change Levy framework), and does not itself create the levy or the agreement mechanism -- it only defines the eligibility test and calculation rules referenced within that framework.

FACT: "“the Act” means the Finance Act 2000;" *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2001/662. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2001/662

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

*No content for this section is grounded in the item's captured source pool.*

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does this instrument state its own geographic extent?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* no explicit extent clause appears anywhere in this captured pool -- see Section 8's own jurisdictional_scope GAP note. This is consistent with the drafting style of many pre-2000s UK statutory instruments, which often relied on the parent Act's own extent rather than stating a separate extent clause.

**Q2: Does the same energy-calculation rule apply to all generation types?**

FACT: "This regulation does not apply to electricity generated by a combined heat and power station." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2001/662. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2001/662

*Analytical inference:* no. Regulation 5's dedicated-electricity-generation-plant rule expressly does not apply to combined heat and power stations, which instead use Regulation 6's own separate formulae.

**Q3: Is the 2.6 electricity conversion factor applied uniformly?**

FACT: "there are exceptions to this rule in the case of dedicated electricity generation plants (regulation 5) and combined heat and power stations (regulation 6)." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2001/662. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2001/662

*Analytical inference:* no. The Explanatory Note itself confirms the 2.6 conversion factor (Section 8, obligation 6) carries exceptions for dedicated electricity generation plants and combined heat and power stations, each of which uses its own gross-calorific-value-based calculation instead.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

*Note: this instrument's own requirements are technical eligibility and calculation rules applied when determining whether a facility qualifies for inclusion in a climate change agreement, not duties running directly to a freight forwarder.*

**1. Commencement.** FACT: "These Regulations may be cited as the Climate Change Agreements (Eligible Facilities) Regulations 2001 and shall come into force on 1st April 2001." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2001/662. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2001/662

**2. Purpose of the eligibility test.** FACT: "This regulation specifies the circumstances in which an installation or site is to be taken to be a facility for the purposes of determining in connection with concluding or varying a climate change agreement whether the facility is to be, or is to continue to be, identified in the agreement as a facility to which the agreement applies." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2001/662. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2001/662

**3. Installation 90% eligibility test.** FACT: "The condition referred to in paragraph (2)(b) is that it is likely that in the relevant 12 month period at least 90% of the reckonable energy supplied to the installation will be used within the installation." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2001/662. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2001/662

**4. Site 90% eligibility test.** FACT: "The condition referred to in paragraph (3)(b) is that it is likely that in the relevant 12 month period at least 90% of the reckonable energy supplied to the site (whether or not to the installations or parts of installations) will be used within the installation or parts of installations (as the case may be)." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2001/662. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2001/662

**5. General reckonable-energy definition.** FACT: "Energy supplied to the relevant premises is reckonable only if, and to the extent that, it is produced from relevant commodities which are, or are deemed to be, burned within the relevant premises." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2001/662. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2001/662

**6. Electricity conversion factor: 2.6.** FACT: "Subject to regulations 5 and 6, the quantity of energy produced from electricity is to be multiplied by a factor of 2.6 to convert it into reckonable energy." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2001/662. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2001/662

**7. Dedicated electricity generation plant calculation and its combined-heat-and-power exclusion.** FACT: "Subject to paragraph (2), where electricity is generated in plant which is located, and intended for supplying electricity primarily for use, within the relevant premises or any other part of the site, the reckonable energy in respect of such use shall be calculated by reference to the gross calorific value of the relevant commodity burned to produce the electricity." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2001/662. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2001/662 FACT: "This regulation does not apply to electricity generated by a combined heat and power station." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2001/662. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2001/662 FACT: "there are exceptions to this rule in the case of dedicated electricity generation plants (regulation 5) and combined heat and power stations (regulation 6)." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2001/662. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2001/662

**8. Combined heat and power station calculation.** FACT: "Reckonable energy from a combined heat and power station shall be calculated by reference to the gross calorific value of the relevant commodity burned to produce it." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2001/662. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2001/662

**9. Steam calculation.** FACT: "The reckonable energy in respect of steam supplied to any place within the relevant premises shall be calculated by taking the enthalpy of the steam and by dividing it by the efficiency of the system which generates the steam and supplies it to the place where it is used." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2001/662. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2001/662

GAP: this item's captured pool contains no verbatim jurisdictional-extent statement (no "extend to" or equivalent clause appears anywhere in the text) and no fine, penalty, or sanction language of any kind -- this instrument is a technical eligibility-calculation instrument with no enforcement provisions of its own.

No phase-in is stated in Sections 1 to 7 of this instrument.

No exceptions are stated in Sections 1 to 7 of this instrument.

Obligations surveyed: 9; workspace-adjacent: 9; extracted as FACT: 9.

# 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

*No content for this section is grounded in the item's captured source pool.*

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

*No content for this section is grounded in the item's captured source pool.*

# 11. Operational System Requirements

*Note: because this instrument sets a calculation methodology rather than a reporting system, "operational system requirements" here means the record-keeping a facility operator should maintain to support its own 90% eligibility determination.*

FACT: "Determinations are to be made in respect of the likely supply and use of energy over the twelve months which follow the supply of taxable commodities to the facility." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2001/662. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2001/662

*Operational implication:* a facility operator (or a workspace assessing a counterparty facility's Climate Change Levy status) should maintain records of taxable-commodity supply and use over the relevant 12-month determination window, including past supply and use data, since the instrument requires past supply or use to be taken into account when determining likely future use.

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

FACT: "This regulation does not apply to electricity generated by a combined heat and power station." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2001/662. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2001/662

FACT: "there are exceptions to this rule in the case of dedicated electricity generation plants (regulation 5) and combined heat and power stations (regulation 6)." *Source: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2001/662. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2001/662

*Analytical inference:* the two edge cases this text defines are the same generation-type divergence noted in Section 7: combined heat and power stations are excluded from Regulation 5's dedicated-plant rule and instead follow Regulation 6's own formulae, and both dedicated electricity generation plants and combined heat and power stations are excluded from the general 2.6 conversion-factor rule.

# 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

*No content for this section is grounded in the item's captured source pool.*

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 2nd March 2001: The Climate Change Agreements (Eligible Facilities) Regulations 2001 made and signed by the Minister of State, Department of the Environment, Transport and the Regions.
- 9th March 2001: laid before Parliament.
- 1st April 2001: this instrument comes into force.

*Source for timeline entries: legislation.gov.uk, UK SI 2001/662 (https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2001/662).*

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks the Commission Decision of 26 July 2022 instructing the Central Administrator of the European Union Transaction Log to enter changes to the national allocation tables of 20 named Member States into the European Union Transaction Log (the EU Emissions Trading System's Union Registry). It exists to give a workspace that tracks EU ETS free-allocation registry changes a single place to see what this Decision instructs, and why: it corrects and updates national allocation tables previously entered by an earlier Commission Decision, not a first-time entry.

*Analytical inference:* this is an inter-institutional administrative act running from the Commission to its own Central Administrator; it does not itself create a duty running to a private freight-forwarding workspace. A workspace's interest is in tracking EU ETS free-allocation registry corrections generally, not in a direct obligation this specific Decision places on it (see Section 4).

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

FACT: "By Commission Decision 2021/C 302/01 ( 4 ) , the Commission instructed the Central Administrator of the European Union Transaction Log to enter the national allocation tables of Belgium, Bulgaria, Czechia, Denmark, Germany, Estonia, Ireland, Greece, Spain, France, Croatia, Italy, Cyprus, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Hungary, the Netherlands, Austria, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovenia, Slovakia, Finland and Sweden into the European Union Transaction Log." *Source: Commission Decision of 26 July 2022, EUR-Lex CELEX:32022D1130(01). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D1130(01)

*Operational implication:* a workspace tracking a specific EU ETS-covered installation's free-allocation entitlement should treat this Decision as a CORRECTION to the prior Decision (2021/C 302/01), not a fresh allocation cycle; the underlying national allocation tables for the fourth trading period (Section 8) are being adjusted, not replaced wholesale.

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

FACT: "Having regard to Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2019/331 of 19 December 2018 determining transitional Union-wide rules for harmonised free allocation of emission allowances pursuant to Article 10a of Directive 2003/87/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council ( 1 ) , and in particular Article 23(4) thereof," *Source: Commission Decision of 26 July 2022, EUR-Lex CELEX:32022D1130(01). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D1130(01)

*Legal Confirmation Required:* the notification duty this Decision references (Article 23(2) of Delegated Regulation (EU) 2019/331) runs from a Member State to the Commission, and the entry duty this Decision itself creates (Section 8, obligation 1) runs from the Commission to its own Central Administrator; neither runs to a private freight-forwarding workspace directly. Whether a specific workspace operates an installation whose own national allocation table entry is affected by this Decision is a fact-specific question outside this brief's own corpus and requires review of the installation-level Annex data against the workspace's own EU ETS compliance records.

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does this Decision itself grant or reduce free allocation, or only instruct a registry entry?**

*Analytical inference:* the Sole Article (Section 8, obligation 1) instructs the Central Administrator to ENTER changes into the registry; the underlying free-allocation decisions were made under Article 23(2) of Delegated Regulation (EU) 2019/331 by each Member State, and this Decision's own role is to operationalise those already-decided changes in the Union Registry.

**Q2: Is Belgium's own notification representative of how every named Member State's change entered this Decision?**

FACT: "Pursuant to Article 23(2) of Delegated Regulation (EU) 2019/331, Belgium notified to the Commission, by letter dated 7 July 2022, changes to its national allocation table to provide free allocation of emission allowances to new entrants and to adjust free allocation of emission allowances for incumbent installations following activity level changes or other changes related to their operations." *Source: Commission Decision of 26 July 2022, EUR-Lex CELEX:32022D1130(01). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D1130(01)

*Analytical inference:* yes, structurally: each of the 20 named Member States has its own materially identical recital in this Decision, differing only in the state's name and the notification letter date(s) (Germany's own recital, quoted in Section 8, is a second worked example).

# 8. Substantive Requirements

**1. Central administrator's registry-entry duty (Sole Article).** FACT: "HAS DECIDED AS FOLLOWS: Sole Article The central administrator shall enter the changes to the national allocation tables of Belgium, Bulgaria, Czechia, Denmark, Germany, Estonia, Greece, Spain, France, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Hungary, the Netherlands, Austria, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Finland and Sweden set out in the Annex into the European Union Transaction Log." *Source: Commission Decision of 26 July 2022, EUR-Lex CELEX:32022D1130(01). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D1130(01)

**2. Belgium's Article 23(2) notification (representative recital, one of 20).** FACT: "Pursuant to Article 23(2) of Delegated Regulation (EU) 2019/331, Belgium notified to the Commission, by letter dated 7 July 2022, changes to its national allocation table to provide free allocation of emission allowances to new entrants and to adjust free allocation of emission allowances for incumbent installations following activity level changes or other changes related to their operations." *Source: Commission Decision of 26 July 2022, EUR-Lex CELEX:32022D1130(01). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D1130(01)

**3. Germany's Article 23(2) notification (second representative recital).** FACT: "Pursuant to Article 23(2) of Delegated Regulation (EU) 2019/331, Germany notified to the Commission, by letter dated 11 July 2022, changes to its national allocation table to provide free allocation of emission allowances to new entrants and to adjust free allocation of emission allowances for incumbent installations following activity level changes or other changes related to their operations." *Source: Commission Decision of 26 July 2022, EUR-Lex CELEX:32022D1130(01). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D1130(01)

*Analytical inference:* obligations 2 and 3 are surveyed here to illustrate the pattern this Decision's recitals repeat 20 times (once per named Member State); neither is itself a duty running to a freight-forwarding workspace.

**4. Fourth trading period scope (2021 to 2030).** FACT: "Delegated Regulation (EU) 2019/331 lays down the transitional Union-wide rules for harmonised free allocation of emission allowances pursuant to Article 10a of Directive 2003/87/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council ( 2 ) for the fourth trading period from 2021 until 2030." *Source: Commission Decision of 26 July 2022, EUR-Lex CELEX:32022D1130(01). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D1130(01)

**5. Prior registry-entry Decision being corrected.** FACT: "By Commission Decision 2021/C 302/01 ( 4 ) , the Commission instructed the Central Administrator of the European Union Transaction Log to enter the national allocation tables of Belgium, Bulgaria, Czechia, Denmark, Germany, Estonia, Ireland, Greece, Spain, France, Croatia, Italy, Cyprus, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Hungary, the Netherlands, Austria, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovenia, Slovakia, Finland and Sweden into the European Union Transaction Log." *Source: Commission Decision of 26 July 2022, EUR-Lex CELEX:32022D1130(01). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D1130(01)

**6. Legal basis and Commission empowerment (Article 23(4) of Delegated Regulation (EU) 2019/331).** FACT: "Having regard to Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2019/331 of 19 December 2018 determining transitional Union-wide rules for harmonised free allocation of emission allowances pursuant to Article 10a of Directive 2003/87/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council ( 1 ) , and in particular Article 23(4) thereof," *Source: Commission Decision of 26 July 2022, EUR-Lex CELEX:32022D1130(01). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D1130(01)

*Legal Confirmation Required:* none of the six obligations above states a fine, sanction, or penalty running to a Member State, an installation operator, or a freight-forwarding workspace; this Decision's own text is silent on enforcement consequences, and it carries no explicit entry-into-force clause of its own beyond its adoption date (Section 14).

No phase-in is stated in Article 1 of this Decision.

No exceptions are stated in Article 1 of this Decision.

No scope limits are stated in Article 1 of this Decision.

Obligations surveyed: 6; workspace-adjacent: 2; extracted as FACT: 6.

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

FACT: "Member State: Belgium Installation ID Installation ID (Union registry) Installation name Operator name" *Source: Commission Decision of 26 July 2022, EUR-Lex CELEX:32022D1130(01). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D1130(01)

*Operational implication:* the Annex records each affected installation's identity (Union registry Installation ID, installation name, operator name) alongside its Member State; a workspace checking whether one of its own EU ETS-covered installations is affected by this correction should look up that installation's own Union registry ID in the Annex's per-Member-State table.

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

*No content for this section as of the export date; this Decision's own text states no exemption, carve-out, or edge case beyond the per-Member-State allocation changes already captured in Section 8.*

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 26 July 2022: Commission Decision adopted, instructing the Central Administrator to enter the changes.

FACT: "Done at Brussels, 26 July 2022." *Source: Commission Decision of 26 July 2022, EUR-Lex CELEX:32022D1130(01). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D1130(01)

*Source for timeline entries: Commission Decision of 26 July 2022, EUR-Lex CELEX:32022D1130(01) (https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D1130(01)).*

# 15. Sources

| # | Source | Type | URL |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Commission Decision of 26 July 2022, EUR-Lex CELEX:32022D1130(01) | EU institutional decision, Official Journal (C series) | https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D1130(01) |

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks The Environmental Protection (Amendment) (Northern Ireland) (EU Exit) Regulations 2019 (SI 2019/289), a Brexit "fixing" instrument that amends a wide range of Northern Ireland environmental legislation (waste, air quality, and industrial emissions law) so it continues to operate correctly once EU law no longer applies directly. It does not create new substantive environmental obligations of its own; it replaces EU-specific references (chiefly "Member State") in already-existing Northern Ireland regulations so those regulations keep functioning post-EU-exit.

FACT: "The Environmental Protection (Amendment) (Northern Ireland) (EU Exit) Regulations 2019" *Source: The Environmental Protection (Amendment) (Northern Ireland) (EU Exit) Regulations 2019, SI 2019/289, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2019/289

FACT: "Made 15th February 2019 Laid before Parliament 19th February 2019 Coming into force in accordance with regulation 1" *Source: The Environmental Protection (Amendment) (Northern Ireland) (EU Exit) Regulations 2019, SI 2019/289, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2019/289

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

**Jurisdictional scope slot:**

FACT: "These Regulations extend to Northern Ireland only." *Source: The Environmental Protection (Amendment) (Northern Ireland) (EU Exit) Regulations 2019, SI 2019/289, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2019/289

*Analytical inference:* this Instrument's own textual amendments apply only within Northern Ireland; a freight-forwarding workspace with Northern Ireland waste, air-quality, or industrial-emissions exposure sits within its scope, while operations solely in Great Britain do not.

FACT: the core mechanism this Instrument applies across the amended Regulations is that a reference to a "Member State shall be read as a reference to a duty or function of the Department" *Source: The Environmental Protection (Amendment) (Northern Ireland) (EU Exit) Regulations 2019, SI 2019/289, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2019/289

*Operational implication:* this single substitution rule (Member State to Department) is how this Instrument keeps the underlying Northern Ireland waste, air-quality, and industrial-emissions Regulations legally operative post-EU-exit; the underlying obligations on carriers, producers, and operators are preserved, not created or removed, by this Instrument.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

*No content for this section -- this Instrument's own commencement point (IP completion day, Section 14) has already passed as of the current review, and no current-action item for the workspace is stated in the captured text.*

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

FACT: "The Secretary of State makes these Regulations in exercise of the powers conferred by section 8 of, and paragraph 21 of Schedule 7 to, the European Union (Withdrawal) Act 2018" *Source: The Environmental Protection (Amendment) (Northern Ireland) (EU Exit) Regulations 2019, SI 2019/289, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2019/289

FACT: "These Regulations may be cited as the Environmental Protection (Amendment) (Northern Ireland) (EU Exit) Regulations 2019 and come into force on [ F1 IP completion day ] ." *Source: The Environmental Protection (Amendment) (Northern Ireland) (EU Exit) Regulations 2019, SI 2019/289, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2019/289

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this Instrument does not itself create a new duty running to a freight-forwarding workspace; it preserves the pre-existing duties in the eight Waste Provisions, two Air and Environmental Quality Provisions, and twelve further instruments its three Schedules amend (Section 8 below). Whether a specific underlying duty (for example, waste carrier registration) reaches the workspace is a question for that underlying Regulation, not for this amending Instrument.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

FACT: "Schedule 1 amends the Waste Provisions." *Source: The Environmental Protection (Amendment) (Northern Ireland) (EU Exit) Regulations 2019, SI 2019/289, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2019/289

FACT: "Schedule 2 amends the Air and Environmental Quality Provisions." *Source: The Environmental Protection (Amendment) (Northern Ireland) (EU Exit) Regulations 2019, SI 2019/289, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2019/289

FACT: "Schedule 3 modifies specified EU Directives for the purposes of these Regulations" *Source: The Environmental Protection (Amendment) (Northern Ireland) (EU Exit) Regulations 2019, SI 2019/289, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2019/289

*Operational implication:* this Instrument's own three Schedules are the authoritative map of which underlying Northern Ireland environmental Regulations were kept operative post-EU-exit; a workspace researching a specific underlying duty (waste carrier registration, packaging producer responsibility, industrial emissions permitting) should read the amended text of the named underlying Regulation itself, not this amending Instrument, for the substantive rule.

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

*No content for this section -- the captured text states no further pending regulatory event beyond this Instrument's own IP-completion-day commencement described in Section 14; no forward-dated guidance document or scheduled event is stated in the pool.*

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does this Instrument itself create a new environmental compliance duty for a freight-forwarding workspace?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* No. This Instrument's own function is to substitute "Department" for "Member State" (and similar EU-specific terminology) in already-existing Northern Ireland Regulations, so those Regulations remain operative after EU exit. Any substantive duty a workspace carries (waste carrier registration, packaging producer responsibility, industrial emissions permitting) arises under the underlying, amended Regulation, not under this Instrument.

**Q2: Does the waste-definition exception and scope-exclusion language in Schedule 3 (Section 8 below) change what counts as "waste" for a Northern Ireland operation?**

*Analytical inference:* Schedule 3's modifications to the retained Waste Framework Directive definitions state specific exclusions (gaseous effluents, in-situ land, uncontaminated excavated soil, among others) from the scope of the general "waste" definition, and a specific exception for how "waste" itself is defined when the Asbestos Directive's own definition applies instead. A workspace handling material that might fall into one of these excluded or exceptionally-defined categories in Northern Ireland should check the amended underlying Regulation's own text directly.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

**Waste Provisions amendment (Schedule 1, eight Northern Ireland waste Regulations).**

FACT: "Schedule 1 amends the Waste Provisions." *Source: The Environmental Protection (Amendment) (Northern Ireland) (EU Exit) Regulations 2019, SI 2019/289, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2019/289

*Operational implication:* the eight amended Regulations include the Controlled Waste (Registration of Carriers and Seizure of Vehicles) Regulations (Northern Ireland) 1999 and the Producer Responsibility Obligations (Packaging Waste) Regulations (Northern Ireland) 2007 (Section 5 above); a freight-forwarding workspace that carries controlled waste, or places packaging on the Northern Ireland market, may carry duties under those underlying Regulations, preserved (not created) by this amendment.

**Air and Environmental Quality Provisions amendment (Schedule 2, two Northern Ireland Regulations).**

FACT: "Schedule 2 amends the Air and Environmental Quality Provisions." *Source: The Environmental Protection (Amendment) (Northern Ireland) (EU Exit) Regulations 2019, SI 2019/289, legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2019/289

**Retained EU Directive modification (Schedule 3, twelve further Northern Ireland instruments).**
